He asks the Lord of Thanigai, the deity Murugan who rides a great peacock, to arrive and wipe away this sorrow. If God shows sudden grace to someone so undeserving, true devotees will not object: they will simply rejoice.

tamil: யாரை யுந்துணை கொண்டிலேன் நின்அடி இணைதுணை அல்லால்நின்
பேரை உன்னிவாழ்ந் திடும்படி செய்வையோ பேதுறச் செய்வாயோ
பாரை யும்உயிர்ப் பரப்பையும் படைத்தருள் பகவனே உலகேத்தும்
சீரை உற்றிடும் தணிகைஅம் கடவுள்நின் திருவுளம் அறியேனே.
translit: yārai yuntuṇai koṇṭilēṉ niṉaṭi iṇaituṇai allālniṉ pērai uṉṉivāḻn tiṭumpaṭi ceyvaiyō pētuṟac ceyvāyō pārai yumuyirp parappaiyum paṭaittaruḷ pakavaṉē ulakēttum cīrai uṟṟiṭum taṇikai-am kaṭavuḷniṉ tiruvuḷam aṟiyēṉē.
translation: I have taken no one else as my refuge, relying only on your two feet. Will you make me live contemplating your name, or will you leave me to suffer in confusion? O God who gracefully created the earth and the vast multitude of souls! O God of beautiful Thanigai holding greatness praised by the world! I do not know your divine will.
commentary: Complete surrender is the only path left to the speaker. Relying on no other refuge, he places his fate entirely at the feet of God. He asks the creator of the world whether his destiny is to live focused on the divine name or to be left in confusion, admitting he cannot guess the divine will.

tamil: உளங்கொள் வஞ்சக நெஞ்சர்தம் இடம்இடர் உழந்தகம் உலைவுற்றேன்
வளங்கொள் நின்பத மலர்களை நாள்தொறும் வாழ்த்திலேன் என்செய்கேன்
குளங்கொள் கண்ணனும் கண்ணனும் பிரமனும் குறிக்கரும் பெருவாழ்வே
தளங்கொள் பொய்கைசூழ் தணிகைஅம் பதியில்வாழ் தனிப்பெரும் புகழ்த்தேவே.
translit: uḷaṅkoḷ vañcaka neñcartam iṭamiṭar uḻantakam ulaivuṟṟēṉ vaḷaṅkoḷ niṉpata malarkaḷai nāḷtoṟum vāḻttilēṉ eṉceykēṉ kuḷaṅkoḷ kaṇṇaṉum kaṇṇaṉum piramaṉum kuṟikkarum peruvāḻvē taḷaṅkoḷ poykaicūḻ taṇikai-am patiyilvāḻ taṉipperum pukaḻttēvē.
translation: Enduring hardship among deceitful-hearted people, my inner being is completely agitated. I have not praised your fertile lotus feet every day. What shall I do? O great life difficult to be comprehended by Vishnu, Siva, and Brahma! O uniquely renowned God living in the beautiful town of Thanigai surrounded by ponds full of blooming leaves!
commentary: Living among deceitful people causes the speaker deep emotional turmoil. He feels helpless and guilty for failing to offer praise every single day. He addresses the Lord of Thanigai as a supreme reality that even the great cosmic gods Vishnu, Siva, and Brahma struggle to comprehend.

tamil: தேவர் நாயகன் ஆகியே என்மனச் சிலைதனில் அமர்ந்தோனே
மூவர் நாயகன் எனமறை வாழ்த்திடும் முத்தியின் வித்தேஇங்
கேவ ராயினும் நின்திருத் தணிகைசென் றிறைஞ்சிடில் அவரேஎன்
பாவ நாசம்செய் தென்றனை ஆட்கொளும் பரஞ்சுடர் கண்டாயே.
translit: tēvar nāyakaṉ ākiyē eṉmaṉac cilaitaṉil amarntōṉē mūvar nāyakaṉ eṉamaṟai vāḻttiṭum muttiyiṉ vittē-iṅ kēva rāyiṉum niṉtirut taṇikaiceṉ ṟiṟaiñciṭil avarē-eṉ pāva nācamcey teṉṟaṉai āṭkoḷum parañcuṭar kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O Lord of the celestial gods who sits upon the mountain of my mind! O seed of liberation praised by the Vedas as the Lord of the cosmic trinity! Whoever they may be in this world, if they go to your holy Thanigai and worship, they become the very supreme light that destroys my sins and takes me as its own.
commentary: The Lord of the celestial gods sits right upon the mountain of the devotee's own mind. The poem declares that anyone at all who visits the holy town of Thanigai to worship becomes a form of that supreme light. Seeing these fellow pilgrims is enough to destroy his own sins and bring him salvation.

tamil: கண்ட னேகவா னவர்தொழும் நின்திருக் கழல்இணை தனக்காசை
கொண்ட னேகமாய்த் தெண்டன்இட் டானந்தக் கூத்தினை உகந்தாடித்
தொண்ட னேனும்நின் அடியரில் செறிவனோ துயர்உழந் தலைவேனோ
அண்ட னேதிருத் தணிகைவாழ் அண்ணலே அணிகொள்வேல் கரத்தோனே
translit: kaṇṭa ṉēkavā ṉavartoḻum niṉtiruk kaḻaliṇai taṉakkācai koṇṭa ṉēkamāyt teṇṭaṉiṭ ṭāṉantak kūttiṉai ukantāṭit toṇṭa ṉēṉumniṉ aṭiyaril ceṟivaṉō tuyaruḻan talaivēṉō aṇṭa ṉētirut taṇikaivāḻ aṇṇalē aṇikoḷvēl karattōṉē
translation: Desiring your holy anklet-wearing feet worshipped by countless heavenly beings, I fall in prostration many times and joyfully dance the dance of bliss. Will I, your mere servant, join the gathering of your devotees, or will I wander enduring sorrow? O Lord of the universe! O master living in holy Thanigai! O Lord holding the beautiful spear in your hand!
commentary: The speaker is caught between joyful devotion and deep insecurity. Out of love for the Lord, he falls to the ground in worship and dances in pure bliss. Yet he still wonders if he will finally be allowed to join the close gathering of true devotees, or if he is doomed to wander the world in sorrow.

tamil: ஊணே உடையே பொருளேஎன் றுருகி மனது தடுமாறி
வீணே துயரத் தழுந்துகின்றேன் வேறோர் துணைநின் அடிஅன்றிக்
காணேன் அமுதே பெருங்கருணைக் கடலே கனியே கரும்பேநல்
சேணேர் தணிகை மலைமருந்தே தேனே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: ūṇē uṭaiyē poruḷē-eṉ ṟuruki maṉatu taṭumāṟi vīṇē tuyarat taḻuntukiṉṟēṉ vēṟōr tuṇainiṉ aṭi-aṉṟik kāṇēṉ amutē peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭalē kaṉiyē karumpēnal cēṇēr taṇikai malaimaruntē tēṉē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: Melting and faltering in mind over food, clothing, and wealth, I sink into sorrow in vain. I see no support other than your feet. O nectar, O ocean of great compassion, O fruit, O sugarcane, O medicine of the good Thanigai mountain reaching the high heavens, O honey, O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: The anxiety of trying to secure material needs like food, clothing, and wealth creates pointless suffering. The human mind falters under these constant pressures. Relief from this worldly sickness only comes from taking refuge in God, who serves as the ultimate healing medicine and the true source of nourishment.

tamil: பாரும் விசும்பும் அறியஎனைப் பயந்த தாயும் தந்தையும்நீ
ஒரும் போதிங் கெனில்எளியேன் ஒயாத் துயருற் றிடல்நன்றோ
யாரும் காண உனைவாதுக் கிழுப்பேன் அன்றி என்செய்கேன்
சேரும் தணிகை மலைமருந்தே தேனே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: pārum vicumpum aṟiya-eṉaip payanta tāyum tantaiyumnī orum pōtiṅ keṉileḷiyēṉ oyāt tuyaruṟ ṟiṭalnaṉṟō yārum kāṇa uṉaivātuk kiḻuppēṉ aṉṟi eṉceykēṉ cērum taṇikai malaimaruntē tēṉē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: The earth and sky know you are the mother and father who bore me. Since this is so, is it right for this poor one to suffer ceaseless sorrow here? I will drag you into a public dispute for everyone to see. What else can I do? O medicine of the gathering Thanigai mountain, O honey, O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: A child has the natural right to demand care from their parents. Since God is both mother and father to all life, leaving a devotee to suffer ceaseless sorrow is fundamentally unjust. The poet boldly threatens to drag the divine into a public dispute if this neglect continues, claiming the right to hold God accountable.

tamil: கஞ்சன் துதிக்கும் பொருளேஎன் கண்ணே நின்னைக் கருதாத
வஞ்சர் கொடிய முகம்பார்க்க மாட்டேன் இனிஎன் வருத்தம்அறுத்
தஞ்சல் எனவந் தருளாயேல் ஆற்றேன் கண்டாய் அடியேனே
செஞ்சந் தனம்சேர் தணிகைமலைத் தேனே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: kañcaṉ tutikkum poruḷē-eṉ kaṇṇē niṉṉaik karutāta vañcar koṭiya mukampārkka māṭṭēṉ iṉi-eṉ varuttamaṟut tañcal eṉavan taruḷāyēl āṟṟēṉ kaṇṭāy aṭiyēṉē ceñcan taṉamcēr taṇikaimalait tēṉē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: O Truth praised by Brahma, O my eye. I will not look at the cruel faces of the deceitful who do not think of you. If you do not come now to end my sorrow, tell me to fear not, and bestow your grace, know that your servant cannot endure it. O honey of Thanigai mountain abundant with red sandalwood, O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: Surrounding oneself with deceitful people who ignore the divine only deepens spiritual misery. The poet resolves to turn away from their cruelty entirely. The only cure for this worldly distress is God's direct assurance of grace, bringing comfort to a servant who can no longer endure the pain alone.

tamil: மின்நேர் உலக நடைஅதனால் மேவும் துயருக் காளாகிக்
கல்நேர் மனத்தேன் நினைமறந்தென் கண்டேன் கண்டாய் கற்பகமே
பொன்னே கடவுள் மாமணியே போதப் பொருளே பூரணமே
தென்னேர் தணிகை மலைஅரசே தேவே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: miṉnēr ulaka naṭai-ataṉāl mēvum tuyaruk kāḷākik kalnēr maṉattēṉ niṉaimaṟanteṉ kaṇṭēṉ kaṇṭāy kaṟpakamē poṉṉē kaṭavuḷ māmaṇiyē pōtap poruḷē pūraṇamē teṉṉēr taṇikai malai-aracē tēvē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: Subjected to the sorrow born of worldly ways as fleeting as lightning, I, with a heart of stone, forgot you. What have I gained? See this, O wish-fulfilling tree. O gold, O great divine gem, O essence of wisdom, O absolute perfection. O king of the beautiful southern Thanigai mountain, O God, O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: Chasing the fleeting trends of the world hardens the heart and brings no real reward. Forgetting the divine for the sake of temporary worldly gains is a deep mistake. True wealth is found only in the absolute perfection of spiritual wisdom, which provides a lasting treasure beyond earthly ambitions.

tamil: வளைத்தே வருத்தும் பெருந்துயரால் வாடிச் சவலை மகவாகி
இளைத்தேன் தேற்றும் துணைகாணேன் என்செய் துய்கேன் எந்தாயே
விளைத்தேன் ஒழுகும் மலர்த்தருவே விண்ணே விழிக்கு விருந்தேசீர்
திளைத்தோர் பரவும் திருத்தணிகைத் தேவே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: vaḷaittē varuttum peruntuyarāl vāṭic cavalai makavāki iḷaittēṉ tēṟṟum tuṇaikāṇēṉ eṉcey tuykēṉ entāyē viḷaittēṉ oḻukum malarttaruvē viṇṇē viḻikku viruntēcīr tiḷaittōr paravum tiruttaṇikait tēvē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: Withered by the great sorrow that surrounds and torments me, I grew frail like a sickly infant. I see no companion to comfort me. What shall I do to survive, my mother? O flowering tree dripping with abundant honey, O sky, O feast for the eyes. O God of holy Thanigai praised by those steeped in excellence, O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: Worldly suffering leaves the soul feeling as helpless as a sick and abandoned infant. In this state of total exhaustion, there is no human companion who can offer adequate comfort. The poet cries out to God as a nurturing mother and a generous flowering tree, pleading for the nourishment needed to survive.

tamil: அடுத்தே வருத்தும் துயர்க்கடலில் அறியா தந்தோ விழுந்திட்டேன்
எடுத்தே விடுவார் தமைக்காணேன் எந்தாய் எளியேன் என்செய்கேன்
கடுத்தேர் கண்டத் தெம்மான்தன் கண்ணே தருமக் கடலேஎன்
செடித்தீர் தணிகை மலைப்பொருளே தேனே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: aṭuttē varuttum tuyarkkaṭalil aṟiyā tantō viḻuntiṭṭēṉ eṭuttē viṭuvār tamaikkāṇēṉ entāy eḷiyēṉ eṉceykēṉ kaṭuttēr kaṇṭat temmāṉtaṉ kaṇṇē tarumak kaṭalē-eṉ ceṭittīr taṇikai malaipporuḷē tēṉē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: Alas, I fell unknowingly into the sea of sorrow that endlessly afflicts me. I see no one to lift me out. My mother, what will I, this poor wretch, do? O eye of our Lord whose throat holds dark poison! O ocean of virtue! O Reality of Mount Thanigai who removes my flaws! O honey! O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: The poet feels completely helpless, drowning in a sea of worldly sorrow with no one to pull him out. He turns to the divine as his only rescue, calling God both his mother and the eye of Siva, the Lord whose throat holds dark poison.

tamil: உண்டால் குறையும் எனப்பசிக்கும் உலுத்தர் அசுத்த முகத்தைஎதிர்
கண்டால் நடுங்கி ஒதுங்காது கடைகாத் திரந்து கழிக்கின்றேன்
கொண்டார் அடியர் நின்அருளை யானோ ஒருவன் குறைபட்டேன்
திண்டார் அணிவேல் தணிகைமலைத் தேவே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: uṇṭāl kuṟaiyum eṉappacikkum uluttar acutta mukattai-etir kaṇṭāl naṭuṅki otuṅkātu kaṭaikāt tirantu kaḻikkiṉṟēṉ koṇṭār aṭiyar niṉaruḷai yāṉō oruvaṉ kuṟaipaṭṭēṉ tiṇṭār aṇivēl taṇikaimalait tēvē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: I see the impure faces of misers who go hungry thinking their wealth will diminish if they eat. Seeing them, I do not tremble and back away. Instead I waste my time waiting at their gates and begging. Your devotees have received your grace. Am I the only one left lacking? O God of Mount Thanigai holding the beautiful spear adorned with strong garlands! O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: The poet paints a sharp picture of human greed: misers who are so obsessed with money that they starve themselves so their wealth will not shrink. He feels ashamed that instead of seeking divine grace like other true devotees, he wastes his life waiting at the doors of such selfish people. He begs God to tell him why he alone is left lacking.

tamil: வேட்டேன் நினது திருஅருளை வினையேன் இனிஇத் துயர்பொறுக்க
மாட்டேன் மணியே அன்னேஎன் மன்னே வாழ்க்கை மாட்டுமனம்
நாட்டேன் அயன்மால் எதிர்வரினும் நயக்கேன் எனக்கு நல்காயோ
சேட்டேன் அலரும் பொழில்தணிகைத் தேவே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: vēṭṭēṉ niṉatu tiru-aruḷai viṉaiyēṉ iṉi-it tuyarpoṟukka māṭṭēṉ maṇiyē aṉṉē-eṉ maṉṉē vāḻkkai māṭṭumaṉam nāṭṭēṉ ayaṉmāl etirvariṉum nayakkēṉ eṉakku nalkāyō cēṭṭēṉ alarum poḻiltaṇikait tēvē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: I desired your holy grace. I, this wretch bound by karma, can no longer bear this sorrow. O gem! O mother! O my king! I do not fix my mind on worldly life. Even if Brahma and Vishnu appear before me, I will not desire them. Will you not bestow your grace upon me? O God of Thanigai with groves blooming with honey-filled flowers! O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: True devotion means desiring divine grace above all else. The poet says he has lost all interest in worldly life and would refuse even the presence of the great creator and preserver gods, Brahma and Vishnu. Only the grace of the divine flame matters to him now.

tamil: கல்லா நாயேன் எனினும்எனைக் காக்கும் தாய்நீ என்றுலகம்
எல்லாம் அறியும் ஆதலினால் எந்தாய் அருளா திருத்திஎனில்
பொல்லாப் பழிவந் தடையும்உனக் கரசே இனியான் புகல்வதென்னே
செல்லார் பொழில்சூழ் திருத்தணிகைத் தேவே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: kallā nāyēṉ eṉiṉumeṉaik kākkum tāynī eṉṟulakam ellām aṟiyum ātaliṉāl entāy aruḷā tirutti-eṉil pollāp paḻivan taṭaiyumuṉak karacē iṉiyāṉ pukalvateṉṉē cellār poḻilcūḻ tiruttaṇikait tēvē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: Even though I am an ignorant dog, the whole world knows you are the mother who protects me. Because of this, my mother, if you remain without granting grace, a terrible blame will fall upon you. O King, what more is there for me to say? O God of holy Thanigai surrounded by cloud-capped groves! O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: The poet uses a familiar devotional argument to demand grace. He says the whole world already recognizes the divine as his protecting mother. Therefore, if God lets him suffer, the world will blame God for failing in a mother's most basic duty.

tamil: என்னே சற்றும் இரங்கிலைநீ என்நெஞ் சோநின் நல்நெஞ்சம்
மன்னே ஒளிகொள் மாணிக்க மணியே குணப்பொன் மலையேநல்
தென்னேர் பொழில்சூழ் திருத்தணிகைத் தேவே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: aṉṉē appā eṉaniṉtāṭkārvam kūrntiṅ kalaikiṉṟēṉ eṉṉē caṟṟum iraṅkilainī eṉneñ cōniṉ nalneñcam maṉṉē oḷikoḷ māṇikka maṇiyē kuṇappoṉ malaiyēnal teṉṉēr poḻilcūḻ tiruttaṇikait tēvē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: Crying out "O Mother, O Father," I wander here with deep yearning for your feet. What is this? You show no pity at all. Is your good heart just like my own heart? O King! O radiant ruby! O golden mountain of virtues! O God of holy Thanigai surrounded by fine beautiful groves! O rich flame of wisdom.
commentary: Wandering in deep yearning, the poet wonders why his cries to a mother and father go completely unanswered. He asks a striking question: is God's heart just as hard and unyielding as his own human heart?

tamil: நடைஏய் துயரால் மெலிந்து நினை நாடா துழலும் நான்நாயில்
கடையேன் எனினும் காத்தல்என்றன் கண்ணே நினது கடன்அன்றோ
தடையேன் வருவாய் வந்துன்அருள் தருவாய் இதுவே சமயம்காண்
செடிதீர்த் தருளும் திருத்தணிகைத் தேவே ஞானச் செழுஞ்சுடரே.
translit: naṭai-ēy tuyarāl melintu niṉai nāṭā tuḻalum nāṉnāyil kaṭaiyēṉ eṉiṉum kāttaleṉṟaṉ kaṇṇē niṉatu kaṭaṉaṉṟō taṭaiyēṉ varuvāy vantuṉaruḷ taruvāy ituvē camayamkāṇ ceṭitīrt taruḷum tiruttaṇikait tēvē ñāṉac ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: Lord of Thanigai who removes faults and bestows grace, O rich flame of wisdom. I grow weak from constant sorrow and wander without seeking you. Even if I am lower than a dog, my very eye, is it not your duty to protect me? Why is there a delay? Come and bestow your grace. See, this is the perfect time.
commentary: The poet pleads for divine protection by reminding God of his duty to save even the most unworthy souls. He admits he is distracted by worldly sorrow and feels lower than a dog for failing to seek the divine. Yet he claims a deeply intimate bond, calling the Lord his own eye. Because of this vital closeness, he argues that God has an absolute responsibility to step in and offer grace without delay.

translit: cīrpūtta aruṭkaṭalē karumpē tēṉē cempākē eṉatukulat teyva mēnal kūrpūtta vēlmalarkkai aracē cānta kuṇakkuṉṟē taṇikaimalaik kōvē ñāṉap pērpūtta niṉpukaḻaik karuti ēḻai piḻaikka-aruḷ ceyvāyō piḻaiyai nōkkip pārpūtta pavattiluṟa viṭileṉ ceykēṉ pāviyēṉ antōvaṉ payamtī rēṉē.
translation: O ocean of grace flourishing with excellence, O sugarcane, O honey, O sweet syrup, O deity of my lineage! O King holding a sharp spear in your lotus hand, O mountain of peaceful qualities, O Lord of Thanigai hill! Considering your fame renowned for wisdom, will you grant grace for this poor one to survive? If you look at my faults and let me fall into the earthly cycle of birth, what will I do? Alas, I am a sinner and I cannot be freed from this cruel fear.
commentary: The poet appeals to the Lord's reputation for deep wisdom, asking to be saved by grace rather than judged by merit. He fears that if God looks only at his personal flaws, he will be thrown right back into the endless, painful cycle of earthly birth.

translit: tīrāta tuyarkkaṭalil aḻunti nāḷum tiyaṅki-aḻu tēṅkumintac cēykku nīkaṇ pārāta ceyaleṉṉē entāy entāy pāvi-eṉa viṭṭaṉaiyō paṉṉā ḷāka ērāya aruḷtaruvāy eṉṟē ēmān tiruntēṉē eṉceykēṉ yārum illēṉ cīrārun taṇikaivarai amutē āti teyvamē niṉkaruttait teḷinti lēṉē.
translation: Sinking in the endless ocean of sorrow, I despair, cry, and pine away every day. Why do you not look upon this child? My father, my father! Have you abandoned me as a sinner? For many days I waited in eager hope, believing you would grant your beautiful grace. What will I do? I have no one else. O nectar of the excellent Thanigai mountain, O primal deity, I do not understand your intention.
commentary: Comparing himself to a weeping child waiting for a father's attention, the poet sinks under the weight of his own sorrow. He wonders if he has been cast aside for so long simply because he is a sinner.

translit: teḷikkumaṟaip poruḷē-eṉ aṉpē eṉṟaṉ celvamē tiruttaṇikait tēvē aṉpar kaḷikkummaṟaik karuttēmeyñ ñāṉa nītik kaṭavuḷē niṉaruḷaik kāṇēṉ iṉṉum cuḷikkummiṭit tuyarumyamaṉ kayiṟum īṉat toṭarpummalat taṭarpummaṉac cōrvum antō aḷikkumeṉai eṉceyumō aṟiyēṉ niṉṟaṉ aṭittuṇaiyē uṟutuṇaimaṟ ṟaṉṟi uṇṭō.
translation: O clear meaning of the Vedas, O my love, O my wealth, O God of holy Thanigai! O Vedic truth delighting devotees, O God of true wisdom and justice! I still have not seen your grace. The tormenting sorrow of poverty, the rope of Yama, base attachments, the affliction of impurities, and the exhaustion of my mind press upon me. Alas, I do not know what these will do to me. Is there any firm support for me other than your twin feet?
commentary: The poet describes the crushing weight of daily life, from the exhaustion of the mind and the pain of poverty to the terrifying approach of Yama, the god of death. He declares that the Lord's feet are his only reliable defense against these overwhelming worldly afflictions.

translit: uṇṭāya ulakuyirkaḷ tammaik kākka oḷittiruntav vuyirviṉaikaḷ oruṅkē nāḷum kaṇṭāyē ivvēḻai kalaṅkum taṉmai kāṇāyō paṉṉiraṇṭu kaṇkaḷ koṇṭōy taṇṭāta niṉaruṭkut takumō viṭṭāl tarumamō taṇikaivarait talattiṉ vāḻvē viṇṭāti tēvartoḻum mutalē mutti vittēcoṟ patamkaṭanta vēṟkai yāṉē.
translation: To protect the lives in this world, you remain hidden and observe all their deeds every day. Do you not see the bewildered state of this poor one, O Lord with twelve eyes? Does it suit your unfailing grace? Is it just if you abandon me, O life of the Thanigai mountain shrine? O primal Lord worshiped by celestial gods, O seed of liberation, O spear-wielding Lord who transcends all words!
commentary: The Lord is addressed as the god with twelve eyes, a traditional description of Murugan, who secretly watches all deeds to protect all beings. The poet asks how an all-seeing God can witness his desperate confusion and still leave him without help.

translit: kaiyāta aṉpuṭaiyār aṅkai mēvum kaṉiyē-eṉ uyirē-eṉ kaṇṇē eṉṟum poyyāta pūraṇamē taṇikai ñāṉap poruḷēniṉ poṉaruḷip pōtiyāṉ peṟṟāl uyyāta kuṟai-uṇṭō tuyarcol lāmal ōṭumē yamaṉpācam ōyntu pōmeṉ aiyāniṉ aṭiyaroṭu vāḻku vēṉiṅ kāruṉai-al lāleṉakkiṉ ṟaruḷcey vāyē.
translation: O fruit resting in the palms of those with unflagging love! O my life, O my eyes, O ever-true perfection, O profound wisdom of Thanigai! If I receive your golden grace now, will I fall short of salvation? Sorrow will flee without a word and Yama's noose will fall away. O my Lord, I will live among your devotees. Who else is there for me but you? Grant me your grace today!
commentary: The promise of divine grace brings absolute freedom from suffering and the fear of death. The poet knows that the moment he receives this golden grace, Yama's deadly rope will simply fall away, allowing him to live in peace among true devotees.

translit: vāykkumuṉa taruḷeṉṟē antō nāḷum vaḻipārttiṅ kiḷaikkiṉṟēṉ varuttum pollā nōykkumuṟu tuyarkkumilak kāṉēṉ māḻki nontēṉniṉ aruḷkāṇēṉ nuvalum pācat tēykkumavaṉ varilavaṉuk kiyātu colvēṉ eṉceykēṉ tuṇai-aṟiyā ēḻai yēṉē tūykkumara kuruvēteṉ taṇikai mēvum cōtiyē iraṅkāyō toḻumpā ḷarkkē.
translation: Believing that your grace will come to me, alas, I watch the path every day and grow weary. I have become a target for cruel, tormenting diseases and intense sorrow. I languish and suffer, yet I do not see your grace. If the one who severs these worldly bonds arrives, what will I say to him? What will I do, a poor soul who knows no other support? O pure Kumara Guru! O Jothi residing in southern Thanigai! Will you not show pity on this servant?
commentary: The poet waits in physical and emotional pain for a grace that seems endlessly delayed. He worries that death will arrive before he achieves this spiritual connection. Stripped of all other comfort, he begs the divine light (Jothi) for mercy.

translit: āḷāyō tuyaraḷakkar vīḻntu māḻki aiyāvō eṉummuṟaiyai antō caṟṟum kēḷāyō eṉceykēṉ entāy aṉpar kiḷattumuṉa taruḷeṉakkuk kiṭaiyā tākil nāḷāyōr naṭuvaṉvaril eṉcey vāṉō nāyiṉēṉ eṉcolvēṉ nāṇu vēṉō tōḷā-ōr maṇiyēteṉ taṇikai mēvum cuṭarē-eṉ aṟivēciṟ cukaṅkoḷ vāḻvē.
translation: Will you not save me? Falling and languishing in the ocean of sorrow, I cry out, "O Lord!" Alas, will you not listen to my plea even a little? What will I do, my father? If your grace, spoken of by your devotees, is denied to me, what will the impartial arbiter do when my final day comes? What will I, lower than a dog, say? Will I stand ashamed? O flawless gem! O flame residing in southern Thanigai! My true knowledge! O life of supreme bliss!
commentary: The fear of facing the end of life without spiritual shelter continues here. He wonders how he can stand before the arbiter of death if he is denied the grace that other devotees possess. Feeling entirely helpless, he turns to God as his only source of true knowledge and lasting joy.

translit: vāḻvēnaṟ poruḷēnal maruntē ñāṉa vāritiyē taṇikaimalai vaḷḷa lēyāṉ pāḻvēlai eṉuṅkoṭiya tuyaruḷ māḻkip pataittaiyā muṟaiyōniṉ patattuk keṉṟē tāḻvēṉī taṟintilaiyē nāyēṉ maṭṭum tayavilaiyō nāṉpāvi tāṉō pārkkuḷ āḻvēṉeṉ ṟayalviṭṭāl nīti yēyō accō-iṅ keṉceykēṉ aṇṇāl aṇṇāl.
translation: O life! O supreme reality! O good medicine! O ocean of wisdom! O benefactor of the Thanigai hills! Languishing and trembling in the cruel ocean of sorrow, I cry out, "O Lord, is this right?" I bow down at your feet alone. Do you not know this? Do you lack compassion only for me, who am like a dog? Am I indeed a sinner? If you forsake me to sink into the earth as a stranger, is that justice? Alas, what will I do here, O Lord! O Lord!
commentary: Calling God the ultimate medicine for his suffering, the poet openly questions divine justice. He asks if it is right to be abandoned when he has surrendered completely. He wonders if he is uniquely sinful to be left alone in his sorrow while longing for compassion.

translit: aṇṇāvē niṉaṭiyai aṉṟi vēṟōr ātaraviṅ kaṟiyēṉneñ caḻintu tuṉpāl puṇṇāvēṉ taṉṉai-iṉṉum vañcar pāṟpōyp pulantumuka vāṭṭamuṭaṉ pulampi niṟkap paṇṇātē yāvaṉivaṉ pāvik kuḷḷum paṭupāvi eṉṟeṉṉaip parintu taḷḷa eṇṇātē yāṉmikavum ēḻai kaṇṭāy icaikkariya taṇikaiyilvīṟ ṟirukkum kōvē.
translation: O Lord! I know no other support here but your feet. My heart is shattered and wounded by sorrow. Do not make me go to deceitful people, lamenting with a withered face and weeping before them. Do not push me away thinking, "Who is this man? He is the worst sinner among sinners." See that I am utterly helpless, O King enthroned in indescribable Thanigai!
commentary: True devotion means refusing to beg for worldly favors from deceitful people. The poet asks God not to force him into that humiliation by withholding divine support. He begs not to be rejected as a ruined sinner, asking God to see his absolute helplessness instead.

translit: kōvēnal taṇikaivarai amarnta ñāṉa kulamaṇiyē kukaṉēcaṟ kuruvē yārkkum tēvē-eṉ viṇṇappam oṉṟu kēṇmō cintaitaṉil niṉaikka-aruḷ ceyvāy nāḷum pūvēyum ayaṉtirumāl pulavar muṟṟum pōṟṟumeḻil purantaraṉep puviyum ōṅkac cēvēṟum perumāṉiṅ kivarkaḷ vāḻttal ceytuvakkum niṉiraṇṭu tiruttāḷ cīrē.
translation: O King! O gem of wisdom seated on the good mountain of Thanigai! O Guhan! O True Guru! O God of all! Hear my one request. Grant me the grace to meditate daily in my mind on the glory of your two holy feet. Brahma seated on his flower, Vishnu, beautiful Indra extolled by all the wise, and Lord Siva riding the bull who makes all worlds flourish all praise your feet with joy.
commentary: The poet strips away all his desperate complaints to make a single request. He asks only for the grace to constantly remember the divine presence in his mind. He notes that even the greatest gods of the Hindu tradition, such as Brahma, Vishnu, and Siva, find their ultimate joy in praising this exact same supreme reality.

sections.title: The Garland of the Soul's Witness

translit: paṇēṟum moḻi-aṭiyar paravi vāḻttum pātamalar aḻakiṉai-ip pāvi pārkkil kaṇēṟu paṭumeṉṟō kaṉavi lēṉum kāṭṭeṉṟāl kāṭṭukilāy karuṇai ītō viṇēṟum arimutalōrk kariya ñāṉa viḷakkē-eṉ kaṇṇēmey vīṭṭiṉ vittē taṇēṟu poḻiltaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: O lamp of wisdom, rare even to Vishnu who ascends to the heavens and others! My eye, the seed of the true home! O gem of Thanigai with cool, flourishing groves! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul! When I ask you to show the beauty of your lotus feet, praised and worshipped by devotees whose words rise like music, you do not show them even in a dream. Is it because you fear this sinner's evil eye will fall upon them? Is this your grace?
commentary: The speaker asks playfully why the divine hides its beautiful feet even in dreams. He wonders if God is afraid that a flawed human gaze might cast an "evil eye" on them. This opening verse sets the tone, praising the lord as the rare light of wisdom and the true, natural witness within every living being.

translit: paṇṭumaṉa tuvantukuṇam ciṟitum illāp pāviyēṉ taṉai-āṇṭāy parivāl iṉṟu koṇṭukulam pēcutalpōl eḷiyēṉ kuṟṟam kuṟittuviṭil eṉceykēṉ koṭiya ṉēṉaik kaṇṭutirut toṇṭarnakai ceyvār entāy kaiviṭēl uṉāṇai kāṇmuk kālum taṇtuḷavaṉ pukaḻtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: In the past, you gladly and affectionately ruled over this sinner who has no good qualities. But today, if you point out the faults of this poor one, like someone who accepts a person and then questions their lineage, what will I do? Seeing me, a cruel man, the holy devotees will laugh. My father, do not abandon me! I swear on your command for all time. O gem of Thanigai praised by the god wearing cool tulasi! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: A plea is made not to be abandoned after being accepted by grace. The speaker compares God pointing out his worldly flaws to someone welcoming a person into their life and only later questioning their background. He fears the shame of being cast away in front of pure devotees.

translit: puṉpulaiya vañcakarpāl ceṉṟu vīṇē pukaḻntumaṉam ayarntuṟukaṇ poruntip poyyām vaṉpulaiya vayiṟōmpip piṟavi nōykku maruntāya niṉaṭiyai maṟantēṉ antō iṉpulaiya uyirkoḷvāṉ varileṉ pālav viyamaṉukkiṅ keṉcolkēṉ eṉcey kēṉē taṉpukaḻkāṇ aruntaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Going to base, deceitful people, vainly praising them and exhausting my mind, experiencing sorrow, and nurturing this false, strong, base stomach, I forgot your feet, the medicine for the disease of birth. Alas! When the god of death comes to take this sweet life, what will I say to him here, what will I do? O renowned gem of Thanigai! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: This verse captures the painful trap of living purely for physical survival. The speaker regrets wasting his energy flattering deceitful people merely to feed his stomach. By forgetting the divine presence, which is the only real cure for the endless cycle of birth, he fears he will have absolutely no defense when death finally comes.

translit: peruṅkaḷapa mulaimaṭavār eṉṉum pollāp pēykkōṭpaṭ ṭāṭukiṉṟa pitta ṉēṉuk kirumpulavark kariyatiru aruḷī vāyēl eṉcolāraṭiyarataṟ kentāy entāy karumpiṉiḻin toḻukumaruḷ cuvaiyē mukkaṇ kaṉikaṉinta tēṉē-eṉ kaṇṇē ñāṉam tarumpuṉitar pukaḻtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: If you grant your holy grace, which is rare even for great sages, to this madman who dances while caught by the evil ghost of women with large, sandal-smeared breasts, what will the devotees not say about it? My father, my father! O taste of grace flowing from sugarcane! O sweet honey ripened in the three-eyed fruit! My eye! O gem of Thanigai praised by pure ones who bestow wisdom! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The text confesses how deeply the human mind can be distracted by physical lust, describing it as an evil ghost that makes a person mad. The speaker wonders aloud what true sages will think if God grants the highest grace to someone so flawed. Despite his sense of unworthiness, he appeals directly to God's sweetness and boundless mercy.

translit: kalaḷavām neñcameṉa vañca mātar kaṇmāyam eṉumkayiṟṟāl kaṭṭu vittuc colaḷavāt tuṉpameṉum kaṭalil vīḻttac cōrkiṉṟēṉ antōnal tuṇai-ōṉ ṟillēṉ malaḷavāyp pavammāykkum maruntām uṉṟaṉ malarppātap puṇaitantāl mayaṅkēṉ entāy callam ulāt tarumtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: My heart has become hard as stone. Bound by the rope of the visual illusions of deceitful women and cast into a sea of indescribable sorrow, I grow faint. Alas, I have no good companion! My father, if you give me the raft of your lotus feet, the powerful medicine that destroys worldly births, I will not be bewildered. O gem of Thanigai where clouds wander! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Overwhelmed by worldly illusions, the speaker feels his heart has hardened into stone. He finds himself drowning in a sea of sorrow with no companion to help him. He asks the divine for the raft of its lotus feet, calling it the only medicine powerful enough to destroy the illusion of worldly existence and bring him safely across.

translit: aṉṉaimuta lāmpantat taḻuṅki nāḷum alaintuvayi ṟōmpimaṉam ayarntu nāyēṉ muṉṉaiviṉai yāṟpaṭumpā ṭellām colli muṭiyēṉcey piḻaikaruti muṉiyēl aiyā poṉṉainikar aruṭkuṉṟē oṉṟē mukkaṭ pūmaṇamē naṟavēnaṟ pulavar pōṟṟat taṉṉainikar tarumtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Daily plunged into worldly bonds beginning with my mother, wandering to feed my stomach, my mind exhausted, I am like a dog. I cannot finish recounting all the sufferings I endure due to past karma. O Lord, do not be angry with me for the mistakes I make. O hill of grace resembling gold, O supreme One, O fragrance of the three-eyed Lord's flower, O honey praised by good poets, O gem of Thanigai that has no equal, O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The daily struggle to survive and care for a family exhausts the mind. The burden of karma (the accumulated results of past actions) brings endless suffering and mistakes. The poet begs the divine presence at Thanigai (a sacred hill town) to look past these flaws and grant grace instead of anger.

translit: paṉṉarumvaṉ tuyarālneñ caḻintu nāḷum pataitturuki niṉaruṭpāl parukak kiṭṭā tuṉṉarumpoy vāḻkkai-eṉum kāṉat tinta ūrnakaikkap pāvi-aḻal uṇarnti lāyō eṉṉarumai appā-eṉ aiyā eṉṟaṉ iṉṉuyirkkut talaivā-iṅ kevarkkum tēvā taṉṉiyalcīr vaḷartaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: My heart destroyed by unspeakable harsh sorrow, I throb and melt every day, unable to drink the milk of your grace. In this forest of approaching false life, as this town laughs at me, do you not perceive the weeping of this sinner? My precious father, my Lord, master of my sweet life, God to everyone here, O gem of Thanigai flourishing with natural excellence, O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Worldly life often feels like a false forest where society mocks true spiritual longing. Surrounded by a laughing town, the seeker feels completely isolated and heartbroken. He asks God to hear his weeping and grant him the nourishment of divine grace.

translit: kōvēniṉ patamtutiyā vañca neñcak koṭiyōrpāl maṉavaruttam koṇṭāḻ kiṉṟēṉ cāvēṉum allaṉniṉpoṉ aruḷaik kāṇēṉ tamiyēṉai uyyumvaṇṇam taruva teṉṟō cēvēṟum civaperumāṉ aritiṉ īṉṟa celvamē aruḷñāṉat tēṉē aṉpar tāvētam teṟumtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: O King, feeling mental sorrow among cruel and deceitful-hearted people who do not praise your feet, I sink down. I do not die, yet I do not see your golden grace. When will you grant a way to save this lonely one? O treasure preciously begotten by Lord Siva who mounts the bull, O honey of graceful wisdom, O gem of Thanigai who destroys the sorrows of devotees, O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Living among cruel and deceitful people brings deep sorrow to the spiritual seeker. Trapped in a painful middle ground, he is unable to die but also unable to find divine grace in life. He asks when a path to salvation will finally open for a lonely soul.

translit: ōyātu varummiṭiyāṉ vañcar pālceṉ ṟuḷaṅkalaṅki nāṇi-iran tuḻaṉṟen nāḷum māyāta tuyaraṭaintu varuntit teyva maruntāya niṉaṭiyai maṟantiṭ ṭēṉē tāyākit tantaiyāyt tamarāy ñāṉa caṟkuruvāyt tēvākit taḻaitta oṉṟē cāyāta pukaḻttaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Afflicted by ceaseless poverty, I approach deceitful people. My heart confused and ashamed, I beg and wander every day. Suffering unending sorrow, I forgot your feet which are the divine medicine. O One who flourishes as mother, father, relative, true guru of wisdom, and God, O gem of Thanigai with unfading fame, O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Poverty forces people to beg from those who are deceitful and cruel. This daily humiliation brings deep shame and confusion to the heart. The exhausting struggle to survive makes a person forget the divine, which is the only true medicine for human sorrow.

translit: miṉṉāḷum iṭaimaṭavār alku lāya veṅkuḻiyil vīḻntāḻntu melintēṉ allāl ennāḷum uṉaippōṟṟi aṟiyēṉ eṉṉē ēḻaimati koṇṭēṉiṅ keṉcey kēṉē aṉṉāyeṉa appā-eṉ ṟaraṟṟum aṉpark kāramutē aruṭkaṭalē amarar kōvē taṉṉārvat tamartaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Falling and sinking into the hot pit of lust for lightning-waisted women, I became weak. I have never known how to praise you. I possess such an impoverished mind. What shall I do here? O precious nectar to the devotees who cry out to you as mother and father, O ocean of grace, O king of the immortals, O gem of Thanigai cherished by loving devotees, O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Sensual desires and lust drain a person of their vital energy. Wasting strength on physical attraction leaves the mind impoverished and unable to focus on the divine. Realizing this weakness, the seeker cries out to God, who responds like a loving parent to those who ask for help.

translit: vaṉcoliṉār iṭai-aṭaintu māḻkum inta māpāvi yēṉkuṟaiyai vakuttu nāḷum eṉcoliṉum iraṅkāmal antō vāḷā irukkiṉṟāy eṉṉēniṉ irakkam entāy iṉcelaṭi yavarmakiḻum iṉpa mē-uḷ iruḷakaṟṟum ceḻuñcuṭarē evarkkum kōvē taṉcolvaḷar tarumtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Caught among those who speak harsh words, I, this great sinner, languish. Though I detail my grievances every day, whatever I say, you show no pity. Alas, you remain silent. What kind of compassion is yours, my Father? O bliss that delights the devotees who walk the sweet path. O rich flame that dispels inner darkness. O King of all. O Gem of Thanigai where sacred words flourish. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The feeling of divine silence is one of the most painful stages of spiritual life. Surrounded by cruel voices, the poet pours out his heart daily, only to meet what feels like absolute indifference. Even in his deep frustration, he still knows God as the inner light that clears away darkness and stands as the silent witness of his soul.

translit: mīḷāta vaṉtuyarkoṇ ṭīṉar tammāl melintuniṉai aḻaittalaṟi vimmā niṉṟēṉ kēḷāta kēḷvi-elām kēṭpip pāynī kēṭkilaiyō eṉaḷavil kēḷvi iṉṟō māḷāta teṇṭaraka iruḷai nēkkum matiyēciṟ cukañāṉa maḻaipey viṇṇē tāḷāḷar pukaḻtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Suffering inescapable deep sorrow caused by base people, I grew weak. I called out to you, cried aloud and sobbed. You make us hear all unheard wisdom. Do you not hear me? Do you have no ears for me? O moon that dispels the unending inner darkness of true devotees. O sky that rains the wisdom of supreme bliss. O Gem of Thanigai praised by people of great effort. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: God is the source of all wisdom and the ultimate hearer, yet the speaker feels completely ignored. The sorrow here comes from dealing with base and cruel people, an exhaustion that leaves the devotee sobbing. He pictures divine grace as a cool moon that chases away deep inner darkness, hoping that this soothing light will finally reach him.

translit: maṇṇiṉāl maṅkaiyarāl poruḷāl antō varuntimaṉam mayaṅkimika vāṭi niṉṟēṉ puṇṇiyā niṉaruḷai iṉṉum kāṇēṉ poṟuttumuṭi yēṉtuyaram pukalva teṉṉē eṇṇiṉāl aḷappariya periya mōṉa iṉpamē aṉpartama titayat tōṅkum taṇṇiṉāl poḻiltaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Alas, distressed by attachments to land, women, and wealth, my mind was deluded and I languished greatly. O virtuous Lord, I have not yet seen your grace. I cannot bear this sorrow any longer. What more can I say? O great bliss of silence, immeasurable by thought, rising high in the hearts of devotees. O Gem of Thanigai surrounded by cool groves. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Worldly attachments to property, physical desire, and wealth create a deep mental fog. Caught in these relentless distractions, the mind exhausts itself and loses its way. The poet contrasts this worldly noise with the deep, silent bliss that God places in the hearts of true devotees. He begs to experience that quiet grace before his sorrow breaks him completely.

translit: vañcakarām kāṉiṉiṭai aṭaintē neñcam varunti-uṟu kaṇveyilāl māḻān tantō tañcameṉpār iṉṟi-oru pāvi nāṉē taṉittaruḷnīrt tākamuṟṟēṉ tayaicey vāyō ceñcolmaṟai muṭiviḷakkē uṇmai ñāṉat tēṟalē muttoḻilcey tēvar tēvē cañcalamnīt taruḷtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Entering the forest of deceitful people, my heart suffered. Struck by the harsh sun of affliction, alas, I languished. I, a sinner, have no one to call a refuge. Left completely alone, I thirst for the water of your grace. Will you show mercy? O lamp at the summit of the scriptures of righteous words. O honey of true wisdom. O God of the gods who perform the three cosmic functions. O Gem of Thanigai who removes sorrow and bestows grace. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The world often feels like a barren forest filled with deceit, beating down on the soul like a harsh sun. Completely alone and exhausted, the speaker thirsts for a single drop of divine grace. He recognizes this grace as the ultimate truth standing high above all scriptures, higher even than the traditional gods who create, maintain, and destroy the universe.

translit: vāḻāta vaṇṇameṉaik keṭukkum pollā vañcakaneñ cālulakil māḻān tantō pāḻāṉa maṭantaiyarpāl cintai vaikkum pāviyēṉ mukampārkkap paṭuva tēyō ēḻāya vaṉpavattai nīkkum ñāṉa iṉpamē eṉaracē iṟaiyē caṟṟum tāḻāta pukaḻttaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Ruined by my wicked and deceitful heart that keeps me from living righteously, I languished in the world, alas. Will you even look at the face of this sinner who sets his mind on vain women? O bliss of wisdom that removes the fierce cycle of sevenfold births. O my King. O Lord. O Gem of Thanigai of unwaning fame. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Deep spiritual longing often brings a crushing sense of personal unworthiness. The poet looks at his own wandering mind and his lingering worldly desires, wondering how a pure God could even bear to look at his face. He places his hope in the divine wisdom that has the power to break the endless cycle of birth and rebirth, trusting it can save him no matter how flawed he feels.

translit: uḷantaḷara viḻicurukkum vañcar pālceṉ ṟuttamaniṉ aṭiyaimaṟan tōyā veyyil iḷantaḷirpōl nalintirantiṅ kuḻalum inta ēḻaimukam pārttiraṅkāy eṉṉē eṉṉē vaḷantarucaṟ kuṇamalaiyē mukkaṭ cōti maṇiyiṉirun toḷiroḷiyē mayilūr maṉṉē taḷantarumpūm poḻiltaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: I go to deceitful people who glare at me and make my heart sink. I forget your supreme feet. I wilt like a tender shoot in the relentless sun, begging and wandering here. You do not look at the face of this poor one and show mercy. What is this, what is this! O mountain of good qualities that grants prosperity! O light shining from the three-eyed jewel of Jothi! O king who rides the peacock! O jewel of Thanigai with its lush flowering groves! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The poet describes the deep humiliation of seeking help from cruel, worldly people while forgetting God. He compares his suffering to a fragile plant withering under a scorching sun. He pleads with the divine, addressed here as Murugan, the lord of Thanigai, to finally look at his face and grant him mercy.

translit: kallāta vañcakarpāl ceṉṟu vīṇāḷ kaḻittu niṟkum kaṭaiyaṉivaṉ karuṇai illāp pollāta pāvi-eṉa eṇṇi eṉṉaip puṟampōkkil aiyāyāṉ puriva teṉṉē ellāmcey vallavaṉē tēvar yārkkum iṟaivaṉē mayilēṟum empi rāṉē callāpa vaḷattaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: "This lowest of men wastes his days going to ignorant deceivers. He is a wicked sinner devoid of compassion." If you think of me this way and cast me out, O Lord, what will I do? O omnipotent one! O God to all the celestials! O our Lord who mounts the peacock! O jewel of Thanigai rich in delightful abundance! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The poet's greatest fear is divine rejection. He worries that God will look at his wasted life and his lack of compassion for others, and cast him aside as a sinner. If the all-powerful Lord abandons him, he has nowhere else to turn.

translit: kaṉṉēya neñcakarmāṭ ṭaṇuki aiyō karainturuki entāyniṉ karuṇai kāṇā teṉṉē-eṉ ṟēṅki-aḻum pāvi yēṉuk kirukka-iṭam ilaiyōniṉ itayaṅ kallō poṉṉē-eṉ uyirkkuyirāyp poruntu ñāṉa pūraṇamē puṇṇiyamē puṉita vaippē taṉṉēril teṉtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Alas, I approach people with stone-like hearts, and I melt and weep. O my mother, I do not see your compassion. Is there no place for this sinner who pines and cries out, "What is this?" Is your heart a stone? O gold! O perfection of wisdom that exists as the life of my life! O merit! O sacred treasure! O jewel of beautiful Thanigai that has no equal! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Having suffered at the hands of stony-hearted people, the poet now directs his frustration at the divine. Addressing God intimately as a mother, he asks a daring question: if there is no mercy for his tears, is God's heart also made of stone? He pleads for refuge, reminding God that the divine presence is the very life of his own soul.

translit: pāvaviṉaik kōriṭamām maṭavār taṅkaḷ pāḻṅkuḻikkaṇ vīḻamaṉam paṟṟi antō māvalviṉai yuṭaṉmelintiṅ kuḻalkiṉ ṟēṉniṉ malaraṭiyaip pōṟṟēṉeṉ matitāṉ eṉṉē tēvartoḻum poruḷē-eṉ kulattuk kellām teyvamē aṭiyaruḷam ceḻikkum tēṉē tāvakaṉṟōr pukaḻtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Alas, my mind is intent on falling into the ruinous pit of women, the very dwelling place of sinful deeds. I wander here, withered by great and cruel karma. I do not praise your flower-like feet. What is the state of my mind? O reality worshipped by the celestials! O God of my entire lineage! O honey that makes the hearts of devotees flourish! O jewel of Thanigai praised by those freed from sorrow! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The poet confesses his distraction by lust and physical desires, describing them as a trap that leads to spiritual ruin. He sees this obsession as a cruel burden of past actions (karma) that keeps him wandering aimlessly in the world. He questions his own sanity for chasing these fleeting attachments instead of praising the divine.

translit: kaṉṉiyartam mārpiṭaṅkoṇ ṭalaikkum puṉcīḻk kaṭṭikaḷaik karutimaṉam kalaṅki vīṇē aṉṉiyaṉāy alaikiṉṟēṉ mayakkam nīkki aṭimaikoḷal ākātō aruṭpoṟ kuṉṟē ceṉṉimicaik kaṅkaivaittōṉ aritil peṟṟa celvamē eṉpurukkum tēṉē eṅkum taṉṉiyalkoṇ ṭuṟumtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: I obsess over the vile, pus-filled lumps swaying on the chests of young women. My mind is confused, and I wander in vain as an alienated stranger. Will you not dispel my delusion and take me as your servant? O golden hill of grace! O wealth rarely obtained by the Lord who bears the Ganges on his head! O honey that melts my bones! O jewel of Thanigai, whose true nature pervades everywhere! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: To break the spell of lust, the poet uses blunt, graphic language to strip away the illusion of physical beauty. By describing the human body in terms of decay, he forces his mind to see the emptiness of his worldly obsessions. He begs the Lord to dispel this intense delusion and finally accept him as a devoted servant.

translit: uḷḷamaṉak kuraṅkāṭṭit tiriyum eṉṟaṉ uḷavaṟintō aiyānī uṉṉaip pōṟṟār kaḷḷamaṉak kuraṅkukaḷai āṭṭa vaittāy kaṭaiyaṉēṉ poṟuttumuṭi killēṉ kaṇṭāy teḷḷamutap peruṅkaṭalē tēṉē ñāṉat teḷivē-eṉ teyvamē tēvar kōvē taḷḷariya pukaḻttaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: O Lord, knowing my wandering state of making the monkey of my inner mind dance, you made the deceitful mind-monkeys of those who do not praise you dance. I, the lowest one, cannot bear this. Look at me! O great ocean of clear ambrosia! O honey! O clarity of wisdom! O my God! O King of the gods! O gem of Thanigai of inseparable fame! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The restless human mind is like a dancing monkey. Vallalar tells God that he is already struggling to control his own thoughts, and it is exhausting to watch the deceitful minds of others dance wildly around him. He calls out to the divine as a sweet, calming ocean of grace that alone can settle his soul.

translit: vantāḷvāy aiyāvō vañcar tampāl varuntukiṉṟēṉ eṉṟalaṟum māṟṟam kēṭṭum entāynī iraṅkāmal irukkiṉ ṟāyāl eṉmaṉampōl niṉmaṉamum irunta tēyō kantā-eṉ ṟuraippavartam karuttuḷ ūṟum kaṉiracamē karumpēkaṟ kaṇṭē naṟcīr tantāḷum tiruttaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: "Come and rule me, O Lord! I suffer among deceitful people!" Even after hearing my crying words, you remain without pity, my father. Has your heart become just like my heart? O fruit juice, sugarcane, and rock candy welling up in the thoughts of those who call out "O Kanda"! O gem of sacred Thanigai who bestows excellent glory and rules! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: God seems to be ignoring these desperate cries for help. Surrounded by deceitful people, Vallalar wonders aloud if God's heart has become as hard and cold as his own. Yet he still trusts that for those who chant the name Kanda, a name for the youthful god Murugan, the divine presence wells up inside them as sweet as rock candy and sugarcane.

translit: ūrāti ikaḻmāyak kayiṟṟāl kaṭṭuṇ ṭōyntalaṟi maṉamkuḻaintiṅ kuḻalu kiṉṟēṉ pārāti aṇṭamelām kaṇattil kāṇpōy pāviyēṉ mukavāṭṭam pārtti lāyō cīrāti pakavaṉaruṭ celva mē-eṉ cintaimalarn tiṭa-ūṟun tēṉē iṉpam cārāti malaittaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Bound by the illusory rope despised by the townspeople and others, I wander here exhausted, crying, and broken-hearted. You who see the earth and all the universes in a single instant, have you not seen the withered face of this sinner? O wealth of the glorious primal Lord's grace! O honey welling up to make my mind blossom! O gem of the primordial mountain Thanigai where joy abounds! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The distractions of the world act like ropes that tie the soul down and leave it exhausted. Vallalar asks a painful question: how can a God who sees the entire universe in a single instant fail to notice one tired, sorrowful face? He pleads for the grace of the divine to flow like honey and make his closed mind blossom.

translit: vā-eṉpār iṉṟi-uṉa taṉpar eṉṉai vañcakaṉeṉ ṟēmaṟuttu vaṉka ṇānī pō-eṉpār ākileṅkup pōvēṉ antō poyyaṉēṉ tuṇai-iṉṟip pulampu vēṉē kō-eṉpārk karuḷtarumak kuṉṟē oṉṟē kuṇaṅkuṟi-aṟ ṟiṭa-aruḷum kuruvē vāḻkkait tā-eṉpār pukaḻttaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Without anyone to welcome me, your devotees reject me as a deceiver. If they say to me, "You hard-hearted man, go away!" where will I go? Alas, I, a liar, will lament without any companion. O mountain of dharma who grants grace to those who call you King! O Supreme One! O Guru who bestows grace to eradicate qualities and marks! O gem of Thanigai praised by those who ask for the gift of life! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The deepest fear here is total isolation and rejection by other spiritual seekers. If the true devotees of God drive him away as a fraud, he will have absolutely nowhere left to turn. He prays to the divine as the supreme teacher who looks past outward flaws and grants grace beyond all human judgments.

translit: māyaineṟi yāmulaka vāḻkkai taṉṉil varuntiniṉai aḻaittalaṟi māḻkā niṉṟēṉ tāyai-aṟi yātuvarum cūluṇ ṭō-eṉ cāminī aṟiyāyō tayai-il lāyō pēyainikar pāvi-eṉa niṉaintu viṭṭāl pētaiyēṉ eṉceykēṉ peruñcīrk kuṉṟē cāyaikaṭal ceṟitaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Suffering in this worldly life of illusory paths, calling you and crying out, I stand perishing. Is there any child in the womb unknown to the mother? O my Lord, do you not know me? Do you have no mercy? If you consider me a sinner equal to a demon, what will I, a fool, do? O mountain of great glory! O gem of Thanigai surrounded by an ocean of shade! O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: A mother always knows the child growing inside her own womb. Vallalar uses this intimate bond to ask why God, the parent of all souls, seems unaware of his suffering in this confusing world. He says plainly that if the divine abandons him as a hopeless sinner, he is completely lost.

translit: miṉṉainikarn taḻivāḻkkait tuyarāl neñcam melintuniṉa taruḷparuka vēṭṭuniṉṟēṉ eṉṉai-ivaṉ perumpāvi eṉṟē taḷḷil eṉceykēṉ tāṉpeṟumcēy iyaṟṟum kuṟṟam aṉṉaipoṟut tiṭalnīti alla vō-eṉ aiyāvē nīpoṟukkal ākā tōtāṉ taṉṉainikar tarumtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: My heart has weakened from the sorrow of this perishing life that flashes and fades like lightning. I stand yearning to drink your grace. If you reject me, calling me a great sinner, what will I do? Is it not right for a mother to forgive the faults of the child she bore? My Lord, can you not forgive me? O gem of Thanigai, peerless and absolute. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Life in this world perishes as quickly as a flash of lightning. Knowing how fleeting everything is, the poet yearns deeply for divine grace. He appeals to God exactly as a child appeals to a mother, reasoning that a mother naturally forgives her child's mistakes. He trusts entirely in the Lord of Thanigai, who dwells within as the silent witness of every living soul.

translit: muntaiviṉai yālniṉatu vaḻiyil cellā mūṭaṉēṉ taṉai-aṉpar muṉintu peṟṟa tantaivaḻi nillāta pāvi eṉṟē taḷḷiviṭil talaicāyttut tayaṅku vēṉē entainiṉa taruḷcaṟṟē aḷittāl vēṟōr eṇṇamilēṉ ēkāntat tiruntu vāḻvēṉ cantaṉavāṉ poḻiltaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Bound by past karma, I am a fool who does not walk your path. If your devotees scold and reject me, calling me a sinner who abandons the path of the father who begot him, I will hang my head in despair. My father, if you grant me just a little of your grace, I will have no other thought and will live in solitude. O gem of Thanigai with great sandalwood groves. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: The weight of past actions (karma) can make a person lose their way and stray from the spiritual path. The poet fears that true devotees will scold and reject him for abandoning God, his true father. To save him from this despair, he asks for just a small measure of grace. With that grace alone, he says he will live a life of quiet devotion, needing absolutely nothing else.

translit: paṉṉakanon tuṟuvañca ulakil niṉṟu paratavittuṉ aruṭketirpōyp pārkkiṉ ṟēṉniṉ poṉṉaruḷaip puṇarntumaṉa makiḻntu vāḻap puṇṇiyaṉē nāyēṟkup poruttam iṉṟō piṉṉai-oru tuṇai-aṟiyēṉ taṉiyē viṭṭāl perumaniṉak kaḻakēyō pētai yāmeṉ taṉṉai-aḷit taruḷtaṇikai maṇiyē jīva cāṭciyāy niṟaintaruḷum cakaca vāḻvē.
translation: Suffering like a wounded snake in this deceitful world, I struggle and look eagerly for your grace. O virtuous Lord, am I, a lowly dog, not fit to unite with your golden grace and live with a joyful heart? I know no other support. O great Lord, if you abandon me to be alone, is it fair to your majesty? Please protect and grace my ignorant self. O gem of Thanigai. O natural life that fills and graces as the witness of the soul!
commentary: Worldly deception causes a suffering so sharp that the poet compares it to a wounded snake writhing in pain. He declares that he has no support anywhere else, leaving him entirely dependent on the divine. He asks if it is fitting for a supreme Lord to abandon a helpless soul. Despite feeling totally unworthy, he begs to be united with God's golden grace so his heart can finally find joy.

translit: viṇa ṟātuvāḻ vēntaṉ ātiyar vēṇṭi ēṅkavum viṭṭeṉ neñcakak kaṇa ṟātunī kalantu niṟpataik kaḷḷa nāyiṉēṉ kaṇṭu koṇṭilēṉ eṇa ṟāttuyark kaṭaluḷ mūḻkiyē iyaṅki māḻkuvēṉ yātu ceykuvēṉ taṇa ṟāppoḻil kulavum pōrivāḻ cāmi yētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: Even as the king of the endless heavens and other gods long and pine for you, you set them aside and stand unceasingly mingled in the eye of my heart. I am a deceitful dog and did not realize this. Sinking in a boundless ocean of sorrow, I wander and waste away. What shall I do? O Lord dwelling in Pori where unfailingly cool groves flourish, O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: God ignores the high gods of heaven to dwell intimately in the human heart, but we fail to notice. The tragedy here is wandering through life drowning in sorrow, completely blind to the divine presence already resting unceasingly within us.

translit: vāṭkaṇ ēḻaiyar mayalil paṭṭakam mayaṅki mālayaṉ vaḻuttum niṉtirut tāṭkaṇ nēyamaṟ ṟulaka vāḻkkaiyil cañca rittuḻal vañca ṉēṉiṭam āṭka ṇēcuḻal anta kaṉvaril añcu vēṉalāl yātu ceykuvēṉ nāṭka ṇērmalarp poḻilkoḷ pōrivāḻ nāya kātirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: Caught in infatuation for women with sword-like eyes, my heart is bewildered. I have no love for your holy feet praised by Vishnu and Brahma. I am a deceitful person wandering aimlessly in worldly life. If the god of death comes to claim me with fierce, rolling eyes, I will be terrified. What else can I do? O Master dwelling in Pori surrounded by groves of fresh blooming flowers, O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: Worldly obsessions blind the mind to the divine until it is too late. The poet admits to wasting his life on fleeting physical infatuations, warning that a life lived without spiritual love offers nothing but sheer terror when the moment of death finally arrives.

translit: eṇṇil puṉtoḻil eyti aiyavō iyalpiṉ vāḻkkaiyil iyaṅki māḻkiyē kaṇṇiṉ uṇmaṇi yāya niṉtaṉaik karuti ṭātuḻal kapaṭa ṉēṟkaruḷ naṇṇi vantivaṉ ēḻai yāmeṉa nalki āṇṭiṭal niyāya mēcolāy taṇi rumpoḻil cūḻum pōrivāḻ cāmi yētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: Alas, performing countless base deeds, I wander and waste away in worldly life. I am a hypocrite roaming without a thought of you, the very pupil of my eye. Tell me, is it not right for you to approach with grace and claim me, taking pity on this helpless one? O Lord dwelling in Pori surrounded by cool, vast groves, O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: The poet asks God to step in and save him purely out of pity, because he cannot save himself. He calls God the very pupil of his eye. This shows that the divine is the core of our own vision and life, even when we live as hypocrites who forget to look inward.

translit: kūvi ēḻaiyar kuṟaikaḷ tīra-āṭ koḷḷum vaḷḷalē kuṟukum vāḻkkaiyil pāvi yēṉpaṭum pāṭa ṉaittaiyum pārtti runtumnī parintu vantilāy cēvi yēṉ eṉil taḷḷal nītiyō tiruva ruṭkoru cintu vallaiyō tāvi ērvaḷaip payilcey pōrivāḻ cāmi yētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: O bountiful Lord who calls out to the helpless and claims them to end their sorrows! Though you watch all the suffering this sinner undergoes in this fleeting life, you do not come to me with compassion. Is it justice to cast me away because I have not served you? Are you not the singular ocean of divine grace? O Lord dwelling in Pori where beautiful conches leap and thrive, O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: Divine grace cannot depend on what we have earned. The poet challenges God directly, asking if it is truly justice to abandon someone simply because they failed to serve. If God is an ocean of grace, that compassion must extend to the helpless precisely when they lack merit.

translit: cantai nērnaṭai taṉṉil ēṅkuvēṉ cāmi niṉtirut tāḷuk kaṉpilēṉ entai nīmakiḻn teṉṉai āḷvaiyēl eṉṉai aṉparkaḷ eṉcol vārkaḷō nintai ēṟpiṉum karuṇai ceytiṭal nitta niṉaruḷ nīti ākumāl tantai tāyeṉa vantu cīrtarum talaiva ṉētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: I pine away, wandering a path like a bustling marketplace. O Lord, I have no love for your holy feet. My Father, if you joyfully claim me, what will your true devotees say? Even if you accept blame for it, showing mercy is the very justice of your eternal grace. O Master who comes as father and mother to bestow greatness, O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: Showing mercy to an unloving person might scandalize the strictly devoted, but it is the true nature of God. The poet begs God to act as a loving parent and accept the blame of the pious. In this view, divine justice is not about punishing the wicked or rewarding the good; it is the act of showing limitless grace to everyone.

translit: cellum vāḻkkaiyil tiyaṅka viṭṭuniṉ ceyya tāḷtuti ceyti ṭātuḻal kallum venniṭak kaṇṭu miṇṭucey kaḷḷa neñciṉēṉ kavalai tīrppaiyō collum iṉpavāṉ cōti yē-aruḷ tōṟṟa mēcuka corupa vaḷḷalē calli yaṅkeṭa aruḷcey pōrivāḻ cāmi yētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: I wander in this fleeting life without praising your red feet, left to languish in confusion. Will you cure the sorrow of my deceitful heart? My heart acts so stubbornly that even a stone would shrink back in fear upon seeing it. O heavenly Jothi of bliss! O manifestation of Grace! O generous Lord whose very form is bliss! Grant your grace so that my afflictions perish. O Lord dwelling in Porur! O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: The speaker laments that his heart is so hardened by worldly distractions that even a stone would be frightened by its stubbornness. He turns to the divine light (Jothi) as the only force capable of breaking through this deceit and granting relief from suffering.

translit: ētu ceykuva ṉēṉum eṉṟaṉai īṉṟa nīpoṟut tiṭutal allatai ītu ceytavaṉ eṉṟiv vēḻaiyai enta vaṇṇamnī eṇṇi nīkkuvāy vātu ceyvaṉip pōtu vaḷḷalē vaṟiya ṉēṉeṉa matittu niṉṟiṭēl tātu ceymalarp poḻilkoḷ pōrivāḻ cāmi yētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: Whatever I might do, you who brought me into this world must forgive me. How can you consider rejecting this poor soul by saying, "He has committed this fault"? I will argue with you now, O generous Lord. Do not stand aloof by dismissing me as a destitute man. O Lord dwelling in Porur with its groves of pollen-rich flowers! O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: Vallalar speaks to God with the fierce intimacy of a child demanding forgiveness from a parent. He argues that since the divine brought him into the world, it is God's absolute duty to overlook his mistakes and never abandon him.

translit: pēyum añcuṟum pētai yārkaḷaip pēṇum ipperum pēya ṉēṟkoru tāyum appaṉum tamarum naṭpumāyt taṇa ruṭkaṭal tanta vaḷḷalē nīyum nāṉumōr pālum nīrumāy niṟka vēṇṭiṉēṉ nīti ākumō cāyum vaṉpavam taṉṉai nīkkiṭum cāmi yētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: I am a great demon who cherishes ignorant women whom even demons would fear. Yet you became a mother, a father, relatives, and friends to me. O generous Lord who gave me the cool ocean of Grace! I begged that you and I should stand united like milk and water. Is this a just request? O Lord who removes the harsh karma that brings ruin! O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: The poet contrasts his own deep sense of unworthiness with the boundless generosity of God, who steps in to be his mother, father, and entire family. Emboldened by this grace, he asks for absolute union with the divine, blending together completely like milk mixed with water.

translit: poyyar tammaṉam pukutal iṉṟeṉap puṉita nūlelām pukalva tātalāl aiya niṉtiru aruṭki rappa-iṅ kañci niṉṟeṉiv viñcu vañcaṉēṉ meyyar uḷḷuḷē viḷaṅkum cōtiyē vitti lātavāṉ viḷainta iṉpamē taiya lāriru vōrum mēvutōḷ cāmi yētirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: All the sacred texts declare that you do not enter the minds of liars. Therefore, O Sire, I stand here terrified to beg for your holy grace, for I am overflowing with deceit. O Jothi shining within the hearts of the truthful! O bliss that flourishes in the great space without a seed! O Lord whose shoulders are embraced by your two consorts! O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: Scriptures warn that the divine presence will not enter a deceitful mind. Knowing his own flaws, the poet stands terrified to ask for grace, praising God as the light that naturally shines within those who are deeply truthful.

translit: māliṉ vāḻkkaiyiṉ mayaṅki niṉpatam maṟantu ḻaṉṟiṭum vañca neñciṉēṉ pāliṉ nīreṉa niṉa ṭikkaṇē paṟṟi vāḻntiṭap paṇṇu vāykolō cēliṉ vāṭkaṇār tīya māyaiyil tiyaṅki niṉṟiṭac ceyku vāykolō cāla niṉuḷam tāṉev vaṇṇamō cāṟṟi ṭāytirut taṇikai nātaṉē.
translation: I am a deceitful-hearted man wandering in bewilderment through this life of delusion, entirely forgetting your feet. Will you make me hold fast to your feet and live, united like water in milk? Or will you abandon me to stand bewildered in the wicked illusion of women with sharp, carp-like eyes? What is the true intention of your heart? Tell me, O Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: Vallalar asks for a direct answer about his spiritual fate. He wants to know if God will finally pull him out of worldly illusions into an inseparable union, or leave him to wander in endless confusion.

tamil: நாளை ஏகியே வணங்குதும் எனத்தினம் நாளையே கழிக்கின்றோம்
ஊளை நெஞ்சமே என்னையோ என்னையோ உயர்திருத் தணிகேசன்
தாளை உன்னியே வாழ்ந்திலம் உயிர்உடல் தணந்திடல் தனைஇந்த
வேளை என்றறி வுற்றிலம் என்செய்வோம் விளம்பரும் விடையோமே.
translit: nāḷai ēkiyē vaṇaṅkutum eṉattiṉam nāḷaiyē kaḻikkiṉṟōm ūḷai neñcamē eṉṉaiyō eṉṉaiyō uyartirut taṇikēcaṉ tāḷai uṉṉiyē vāḻntilam uyiruṭal taṇantiṭal taṉai-inta vēḷai eṉṟaṟi vuṟṟilam eṉceyvōm viḷamparum viṭaiyōmē.
translation: "We will go and worship tomorrow," we say, and we waste our days day by day. O base heart, what is this, what is this! We have not lived meditating on the feet of the exalted Lord of sacred Thanigai. We do not realize that the soul may part from the body at this very moment. What will we do, we who are unspeakably foolish?
commentary: The habit of putting off spiritual practice until tomorrow is a fatal mistake. Life is fragile, and the soul can leave the body at any second. Waiting for the right time to seek God only wastes the short time we actually have.

tamil: விடைய வாழ்க்கையை விரும்பினன் நின்திரு விரைமலர்ப் பதம்போற்றேன்
கடைய நாயினேன் எவ்வணம் நின்திருக் கருணைபெற் றுய்வேனே
விடையில் ஏறிய சிவபரஞ் சுடர்உளே விளங்கிய ஒளிக்குன்றே
தடையி லாதபேர் ஆனந்த வெள்ளமே தணிகைஎம் பெருமானே.
translit: viṭaiya vāḻkkaiyai virumpiṉaṉ niṉtiru viraimalarp patampōṟṟēṉ kaṭaiya nāyiṉēṉ evvaṇam niṉtiruk karuṇaipeṟ ṟuyvēṉē viṭaiyil ēṟiya civaparañ cuṭaruḷē viḷaṅkiya oḷikkuṉṟē taṭaiyi lātapēr āṉanta veḷḷamē taṇikai-em perumāṉē.
translation: I desired a worldly life. I do not praise your sacred, fragrant, flower-like feet. I am the lowest dog. How will I receive your sacred grace and be saved? O hill of light shining within the supreme flame of Siva who mounts the bull! O unobstructed flood of supreme bliss! Our Lord of Thanigai!
commentary: The distraction of worldly desires keeps us from experiencing divine grace. The poet feels deep regret over his worldly choices, contrasting his own lowly state with the boundless, unobstructed bliss of God. He describes this divine presence as a brilliant light shining within the supreme flame of Siva.

tamil: பெருமை வேண்டிய பேதையில் பேதையேன் பெருந்துயர் உழக்கின்றேன்
ஒருமை ஈயும்நின் திருப்பதம் இறைஞ்சிலேன் உய்வதெப் படியேயோ
அருமை யாம்தவத் தம்மையும் அப்பனும் அளித்திடும் பெருவாழ்வே
தரும வள்ளலே குணப்பெருங் குன்றமே தணிகைமா மலையானே.
translit: perumai vēṇṭiya pētaiyil pētaiyēṉ peruntuyar uḻakkiṉṟēṉ orumai īyumniṉ tiruppatam iṟaiñcilēṉ uyvatep paṭiyēyō arumai yāmtavat tammaiyum appaṉum aḷittiṭum peruvāḻvē taruma vaḷḷalē kuṇapperuṅ kuṉṟamē taṇikaimā malaiyāṉē.
translation: A fool among fools who desires worldly greatness, I suffer immense sorrow. I do not bow to your sacred feet that grant oneness. How am I to be saved? O great life bestowed by the mother and father of rare penance! O generous giver of dharma! Great hill of virtues! Lord of the great Thanigai mountain!
commentary: Chasing worldly status and greatness brings only deep sorrow. True relief comes from seeking the divine, which grants a deep sense of oneness. The verse addresses the deity as the embodiment of virtue and dharma (righteous duty).

tamil: மலையும் வேற்கணார் மையலில் அழுந்தியே வள்ளல்நின் பதம்போற்றா
தலையும் இப்பெருங் குறையினை ஐயகோ யாவரோ டுரைசெய்கேன்
நிலைகொள் ஆனந்த நிருத்தனுக் கொருபொருள் நிகழ்த்திய பெருவாழ்வே
தலைமை மேவிய சற்குரு நாதனே தணிகையம் பதியானே.
translit: malaiyum vēṟkaṇār maiyalil aḻuntiyē vaḷḷalniṉ patampōṟṟā talaiyum ipperuṅ kuṟaiyiṉai aiyakō yāvarō ṭuraiceykēṉ nilaikoḷ āṉanta niruttaṉuk koruporuḷ nikaḻttiya peruvāḻvē talaimai mēviya caṟkuru nātaṉē taṇikaiyam patiyāṉē.
translation: Sinking into infatuation for women with eyes like battling spears, I wander without praising your feet, O generous Lord. Alas, to whom shall I tell this great flaw? O great life who imparted the unique truth to the dancer of eternal bliss! O true Guru Lord of supreme eminence! Lord of the beautiful city of Thanigai!
commentary: Sensual infatuation causes the mind to wander endlessly and forget its spiritual purpose. The poet appeals to the Lord as the supreme Guru, recalling the mythological tradition where the young god Murugan imparted the ultimate truth to his own father, Siva, the cosmic dancer.

tamil: பதியும் அப்பனும் அன்னையும் குருவும்நற் பயன்தரு பொருளாய
கதியும் நின்திருக் கழல்அடி அல்லது கண்டிலன் எளியேனே
விதியும் மாலும்நின் றேத்திடும் தெய்வமே விண்ணவர் பெருமானே
வதியும் சின்மய வடிவமே தணிகைமா மலைஅமர்ந் திடுவாழ்வே.
translit: patiyum appaṉum aṉṉaiyum kuruvumnaṟ payaṉtaru poruḷāya katiyum niṉtiruk kaḻalaṭi allatu kaṇṭilaṉ eḷiyēṉē vitiyum mālumniṉ ṟēttiṭum teyvamē viṇṇavar perumāṉē vatiyum ciṉmaya vaṭivamē taṇikaimā malai-amarn tiṭuvāḻvē.
translation: Home, father, mother, guru, the substance that yields good fruit, and the ultimate refuge: I, a poor wretch, have found nothing but your sacred feet adorned with anklets. O Deity praised by Brahma and Vishnu! Lord of the celestials! O abiding form of pure consciousness! The great life seated on the great Thanigai mountain!
commentary: Complete surrender means seeing the divine as everything: home, mother, father, teacher, and ultimate refuge. The poet recognizes God as a heavenly ruler praised by other deities, and in the end as the abiding form of pure consciousness itself.

tamil: வாழும் நின்திருத் தொண்டர்கள் திருப்பதம் வழுத்திடா துலகத்தே
தாழும் வஞ்சர்பால் தாழும்என் தன்மைஎன் தன்மைவன் பிறப்பாய
ஏழும் என்னதே ஆகிய தையனே எவர்எனைப் பொருகின்றோர்
ஊழும் நீக்குறும் தணிகைஎம் அண்ணலே உயர்திரு வருள்தேனே.
translit: vāḻum niṉtirut toṇṭarkaḷ tiruppatam vaḻuttiṭā tulakattē tāḻum vañcarpāl tāḻumeṉ taṉmai-eṉ taṉmaivaṉ piṟappāya ēḻum eṉṉatē ākiya taiyaṉē evareṉaip porukiṉṟōr ūḻum nīkkuṟum taṇikai-em aṇṇalē uyartiru varuḷtēṉē.
translation: I do not praise the holy feet of your living devotees in this world. Instead I bow down before lowly deceivers. What is this nature of mine? O Lord, all seven cruel births have become my lot. Who is there to fight me? O our Lord of Thanigai who dispels past karma! O honey of supreme divine grace!
commentary: The poet questions his own character, wondering why he flatters deceitful people instead of honoring true devotees of God. He says this worldly attachment keeps him trapped in the painful cycle of repeated births. He turns to the divine, asking the Lord to wipe away the burden of his past actions (karma) and offer the sweetness of grace.

tamil: தேனும் தெள்ளிய அமுதமும் கைக்கும்நின் திருவருள் தேன்உண்டே
யானும் நீயுமாய்க் கலந்துற வாடும்நாள் எந்தநாள் அறியேனே
வானும் பூமியும் வழுத்திடும் தணிகைமா மலைஅமர்ந் திடுதேவே
கோனும் தற்பர குருவுமாய் விளங்கிய குமாரசற் குணக்குன்றே.
translit: tēṉum teḷḷiya amutamum kaikkumniṉ tiruvaruḷ tēṉuṇṭē yāṉum nīyumāyk kalantuṟa vāṭumnāḷ entanāḷ aṟiyēṉē vāṉum pūmiyum vaḻuttiṭum taṇikaimā malai-amarn tiṭutēvē kōṉum taṟpara kuruvumāy viḷaṅkiya kumāracaṟ kuṇakkuṉṟē.
translation: Drinking the honey of your divine grace makes ordinary honey and clear nectar taste bitter. I do not know when the day will come for you and me to mingle and rejoice together. O God seated on the great mountain of Thanigai praised by heaven and earth! O Kumara, mountain of noble virtues shining as the Sovereign and the supreme Guru!
commentary: Divine grace is so sweet that it makes ordinary honey and heavenly nectar taste bitter by comparison. The poet longs for the day when he will experience total union with the divine. He addresses God as the supreme teacher (guru) and sovereign who holds all noble virtues.

tamil: குன்று பொய்உடல் வாழ்வினை மெய்எனக் குறித்திவண் அலைகின்றேன்
இன்று நின்திரு வருள்அடைந் துய்வனோ இல்லைஇவ் வுலகத்தே
என்றும் இப்படிப் பிறந்திறந் துழல்வனோ யாதும்இங் கறிகில்லேன்
நன்று நின்திருச் சித்தம்என் பாக்கியம் நல்தணி கையில்தேவே.
translit: kuṉṟu poyuṭal vāḻviṉai meyeṉak kuṟittivaṇ alaikiṉṟēṉ iṉṟu niṉtiru varuḷaṭain tuyvaṉō illai-iv vulakattē eṉṟum ippaṭip piṟantiṟan tuḻalvaṉō yātumiṅ kaṟikillēṉ naṉṟu niṉtiruc cittameṉ pākkiyam naltaṇi kaiyiltēvē.
translation: I wander here taking this decaying false bodily life to be real. Will I attain your divine grace today and be saved? Or will I endlessly wander in this world, continually being born and dying like this? I know nothing of this. Your divine will is my good fortune. O Lord in beautiful Thanigai!
commentary: The poet admits he has spent his life treating his temporary physical body as a permanent reality. Feeling deeply uncertain, he wonders if he will be saved by grace today or forced to endure the endless cycle of birth and death. With no answers of his own, he surrenders completely to the divine will.

tamil: தேவ ரும்தவ முனிவரும் சித்தரும் சிவன்அரி அயன்ஆகும்
மூவ ரும்பணி முதல்வநின் அடியில்என் முடிஉற வைப்பாயேல்
ஏவ ரும்எனக் கெதிர்இலை முத்திவீ டென்னுடை யதுகண்டாய்
தாவ ரும்பொழில் தணிகையம் கடவுளே சரவண பவகோவே.
translit: tēva rumtava muṉivarum cittarum civaṉari ayaṉākum mūva rumpaṇi mutalvaniṉ aṭiyileṉ muṭi-uṟa vaippāyēl ēva rumeṉak ketirilai muttivī ṭeṉṉuṭai yatukaṇṭāy tāva rumpoḻil taṇikaiyam kaṭavuḷē caravaṇa pavakōvē.
translation: O Primal Lord worshipped by celestial beings, ascetic sages, realized mystics, and the trinity of Siva, Vishnu, and Brahma! If you let my head rest at your feet, no one can stand against me. The mansion of liberation will belong entirely to me. O God of Thanigai surrounded by unfading groves! O King Saravanabhava!
commentary: The Lord is addressed as the supreme source worshipped even by the highest gods and realized mystics. The poet declares that total surrender at the feet of the divine brings absolute spiritual protection. With this backing, nothing can stop him from reaching the ultimate freedom of liberation.

tamil: வேயை வென்றதோள் பாவையர் படுகுழி விழுந்தலைந் திடும்இந்த
நாயை எப்படி ஆட்கொளல் ஆயினும் நாதநின் செயல்அன்றே
தாயை அப்பனைத் தமரினை விட்டுனைச் சார்ந்தவர்க் கருள்கின்றோய்
மாயை நீக்குநல் அருள்புரி தணிகைய வந்தருள் இந்நாளே.
translit: vēyai veṉṟatōḷ pāvaiyar paṭukuḻi viḻuntalain tiṭuminta nāyai eppaṭi āṭkoḷal āyiṉum nātaniṉ ceyalaṉṟē tāyai appaṉait tamariṉai viṭṭuṉaic cārntavark karuḷkiṉṟōy māyai nīkkunal aruḷpuri taṇikaiya vantaruḷ innāḷē.
translation: I am a dog wandering after falling into the trap of women whose shoulders are smoother than bamboo. However you choose to redeem me, O Lord, is that not your doing? You bestow grace on those who have abandoned mother, father, and kindred to take refuge in you. Grant your pure grace to remove my illusion. O Lord of Thanigai, come and bless me this very day.
commentary: The poet confesses that he has wasted time chasing physical desires. He asks God to rescue him, noting that the divine readily grants grace to those who leave behind family ties and worldly attachments. He prays for this pure grace to shatter his worldly illusions (maya) immediately.

translit: caṅka pāṇiyaic catumu kattaṉaic ceṅkaṇ āyirat tēvar nātaṉai maṅka lampeṟa vaitta vaḷḷalē taṅka ruḷtirut taṇikai aiyaṉē.
translation: O benevolent Lord who established Vishnu holding the conch, four-faced Brahma, and Indra the thousand-red-eyed lord of the devas, so they might attain auspiciousness. O Lord of holy Thanigai of abiding grace!
commentary: The supreme divine grace gives the traditional gods their power and position. By naming Vishnu, Brahma, and Indra, the verse makes it clear that the Lord of Thanigai is the ultimate source behind them all.

translit: aiya ṉēniṉai aṉṟi eṅkaṇum poyya ṉēṟkoru pukali lāmaiyāl veyya ṉēṉeṉa veṟuttu viṭṭiṭēl meyya ṉētirut taṇikai vēlaṉē.
translation: O Lord, I am a man of falsehood. Since I have no refuge anywhere other than You, do not forsake me in disgust by thinking I am cruel. O embodiment of Truth, O Velan of holy Thanigai!
commentary: The speaker begs the divine for shelter, confessing to a life of falsehood and cruelty. He appeals to God as the very embodiment of truth, asking not to be rejected for his flaws because he has nowhere else to turn.

translit: vēlaṉ mātavaṉ vētaṉ ēttiṭum mēlaṉ māmayil mēlaṉ aṉparuḷ cāla niṉṟavaṉ taṇikai nāyakaṉ vāla naṟpatam vaippeṉ neñcamē.
translation: He is Velan, the Supreme One praised by Vishnu and Brahma. He rides the great peacock. He dwells firmly in the hearts of his devotees. I will place the pure, good feet of the Lord of Thanigai in my heart.
commentary: Even though the highest gods worship Him, the supreme Lord Velan (a name for Murugan, the wielder of the spear) chooses to live firmly inside the hearts of His devotees. Knowing this, the speaker resolves to hold the divine presence within his own heart.

translit: neñca mē-iḵ teṉṉai niṉmati vañca vāḻviṉil mayaṅku kiṉṟaṉai tañcam eṉṟaruḷ taṇikai cārttiyēl kañca māmalark kaḻalki ṭaikkumē.
translation: O heart, what is this? Your mind is deluded by this deceitful life. If you seek refuge in graceful Thanigai, you will attain His holy feet that resemble great lotus flowers.
commentary: The mind is easily tricked by the false promises of everyday worldly life. The speaker tells his own heart to wake up from this confusion and seek true safety in divine grace.

translit: kiṭaikkuḷ māḻkiyē kilamcey antakaṉ paṭaikkuḷ paṭṭiṭum pāṉmai eytiṭēṉ taṭaikkuḷ paṭṭiṭāt taṇikai yāṉpatat taṭaikka lampukun taruḷce ḻippaṉē.
translation: I will not perish in worldly ties and fall prey to the army of the destructive God of Death. I have taken refuge at the feet of the Lord of Thanigai who is beyond all limitations, and I will flourish in His grace.
commentary: Taking refuge in divine grace is the only way to escape the destructive forces of mortality and worldly attachment. The speaker trusts that the Lord's limitless power will protect him from the God of Death and allow him to flourish.

translit: ceḻikkum cīrtirut taṇikait tēvaniṉ koḻikkum nallaruḷ koḷḷai koḷḷavē taḻikkoṇ ṭaṉparaic cārnti lēṉivaṇ paḻikkuḷ ākumeṉ pāṉmai eṉṉaiyō.
translation: O Lord of flourishing and renowned Thanigai. I have not joined your devotees to seize the abundance of your overflowing good grace. What is this nature of mine that falls into blame here?
commentary: Spiritual progress is rarely a solitary road. Vallalar wonders why he has not sought out the company of fellow seekers. He sees the gathering of devotees as a place where God's grace overflows and can be shared by all, and he regrets being stuck in his own flawed habits away from that shared spiritual wealth.

translit: eṉṉai eṉṉai-ī teṉṟaṉ mātavam muṉṉai naṉṉeṟi muyaṉṟi lēṉainiṉ poṉṉai aṉṉatāḷ pōṟṟa vaittaṉai aṉṉai eṉṉumnal taṇikai aṇṇalē.
translation: O Lord of good Thanigai who is like a mother. I did not strive in the good path of old. Yet you have made me praise your golden feet. What is this, what is this great penance of mine?
commentary: This verse expresses pure wonder at unearned grace. Vallalar admits he did nothing to deserve this blessing, having entirely neglected the spiritual path in the past. Yet God, acting with the unprompted love of a mother, has drawn him in and given him the gift of devotion anyway.
