translit: aṇṇi lēṉniṉai aiya niṉaṭi eṇṇi lēṉitaṟ kiyātu ceykuvēṉ puṇṇi ṉēṉpiḻai poṟuttuk kōṭiyāl taṇṇiṉ nīḷpoḻil taṇikai appaṉē.
translation: I have not drawn near you, O Lord. I have not meditated on your feet. What will I do about this? Please forgive the faults of this flawed one, O Father of Thanigai surrounded by cool and expansive groves.
commentary: A direct plea for forgiveness. Vallalar confesses that he has kept his distance and failed to fix his mind on the divine. Aware of his own mistakes, he asks God to look past these flaws with a father's patient mercy.

translit: appaṉ eṉṉuṭai aṉṉai tēcikaṉ ceppaṉ eṉkulat teyvam āṉavaṉ tuppaṉ eṉuyirt tuṇaivaṉ yātumōr tappil aṉparcēr taṇikai vaḷḷalē.
translation: You are my father, my mother, and my guiding master. You are the righteous one and the deity of my lineage. You are my strength and the companion of my life, O patron of Thanigai where flawless devotees gather.
commentary: Vallalar describes the divine as every meaningful relationship combined into one. God is a mother, a father, a guiding teacher, and a lifelong companion. By listing these bonds, he shows that total intimacy and strength are found entirely in the divine.

translit: vaḷḷal uṉaṭi vaṇaṅkip pōṟṟa-eṉ uḷḷam eṉvacat tuṟṟa tillaiyāl eḷḷal aiyavō ēḻai-eṉ ceykēṉ taḷḷa rumpoḻil taṇikai veṟpaṉē.
translation: O patron, my heart is not under my control to bow down and praise your feet. This is a disgrace, alas. What will this poor soul do, O Lord of the Thanigai hill surrounded by dense groves?
commentary: The greatest obstacle in spiritual practice is often a wandering mind. Vallalar laments that even when he wants to worship, his own heart refuses to obey him. He captures the helpless frustration of wanting to be perfectly devoted but finding his own mind rebelling against him.

translit: veṟpa ṉētirut taṇikai vēlaṉē poṟpa ṉētirup pōri nātaṉē kaṟpa mēlpala kālam cellumāl aṟpa ṉēṉtuyark kaḷavu cāṟṟavē.
translation: Lord of the hill. Velan of holy Thanigai. Beautiful Lord of holy Tirupporur. Many eons would pass just to tell the full measure of this lowly one's sorrow.
commentary: The sorrow of being separated from the divine is so vast that it would take countless ages to describe it. God is addressed here as Velan, the Lord who carries the sacred spear, residing in the holy temple towns of Thanigai and Tirupporur. The poet expresses a deep, exhausting sadness that spans lifetimes, humbling himself completely before the Lord of the hills.

translit: cāṟu cērtirut taṇikai entainiṉ āṟu māmukat taḻakai moṇṭukoṇ ṭūṟil kaṇkaḷāl uṇṇa eṇṇiṉēṉ īṟil eṉṉuṭai eṇṇam muṟṟumō.
translation: My Father of holy Thanigai abundant with festivals. I yearned to scoop up the beauty of your six great faces and drink it in through faultless eyes. Will my endless desire be fulfilled?
commentary: The desire to see God is felt as a physical thirst. The Lord of Thanigai is traditionally depicted with six faces. The poet longs to gather up the sheer beauty of those faces and drink it in through pure, faultless eyes. He wonders if this endless, burning yearning will ever finally be satisfied.

translit: muṟṟu mōmaṉam muṉṉi niṉpatam paṟṟu mōviṉaip pakuti eṉpavai vaṟṟu mōcuka vāḻvu vāykkumō caṟṟum ōrkilēṉ taṇikai attaṉē.
translation: Lord of Thanigai, I do not know in the slightest. Will my mind mature and hold fast to your feet? Will the divisions of my karma dry up? Will a joyful life be granted to me?
commentary: True spiritual surrender requires a steady mind and freedom from past burdens. Karma refers to the accumulated weight of past actions that keep a soul bound to suffering. The poet feels entirely uncertain about his own readiness. He wonders aloud if his past karma will ever completely dry up, allowing him to achieve the joyful life of resting securely with God.

translit: atta ṉētaṇi kāca lattaruḷ vitta ṉēmayil mēṟkoḷ vēlaṉē pitta ṉēṉperum piḻaipo ṟuttiṭil cutta aṉparkaḷ colvar ētamē.
translation: Father. Seed of grace in the Thanigai hills. Velan who rides the peacock. If you forgive the massive faults of this madman, would your pure devotees ever call it a flaw?
commentary: Divine grace is absolute, and true devotees rejoice when it is given to anyone. God is pictured here riding a peacock, a classic symbol of spiritual victory. The poet calls himself a madman burdened with massive faults, asking if God's pure followers would ever complain if such a broken person were forgiven. The unspoken truth is that pure love never resents mercy shown to others.

translit: ēti lāreṉa eṇṇik kaiviṭil nīti yō-eṉai nilaikka vaittavā cāti vāṉpoḻil taṇikai nātaṉē īti niṉaruḷ eṉṉum piccaiyē.
translation: Lord of Thanigai surrounded by great jasmine groves. If you consider me a stranger and abandon me, is that justice, O Lord who established me firmly? Bestow upon me the alms of your grace.
commentary: Grace is a pure gift that cannot be earned, only begged for like alms. The poet appeals directly to God's sense of justice. Since God has already brought him this far and set his feet on the path, abandoning him now as a stranger would be deeply unfair. He asks the Lord to simply hand down the free gift of grace.

translit: piccai ēṟṟavaṉ piḷḷai nī-eṉil iccai ēṟṟavark kiyātu ceykuvāy paccai māmayil parama nātaṉē kacci nērtaṇi kaikka ṭampaṉē.
translation: If you are the son of the Lord who took alms, what will you do for those who harbor desire for you? Supreme Lord on the great green peacock! O wearer of Kadamba flowers in Thanigai, a city that rivals Kanchi.
commentary: The poem makes a playful challenge based on divine family history. The Lord who took alms is Siva, who is celebrated in sacred lore as a wandering beggar. The poet playfully asks what a beggar's son can possibly give to those who long for his grace.

translit: kaṭappa māmalark kaṇṇi mārpaṉē taṭappe rumpoḻil taṇikait tēvaṉē iṭappa ṭācciṟi yēṉai aṉparkaḷ toṭappa ṭāteṉil colva teṉkolō.
translation: O Lord whose chest is adorned with a garland of great Kadamba flowers! God of Thanigai surrounded by vast magnificent groves! If your devotees do not associate with this lowly one who has no place, what is there to say?
commentary: The poet expresses a deep sense of unworthiness. He appeals directly to God, asking what hope he has if the true devotees refuse to accept him.

translit: piccai ēṟṟavaṉ piḷḷai nī-eṉil iccai ēṟṟavark kiyātu ceykuvāy paccai māmayil parama nātaṉē kacci nērtaṇi kaikka ṭampaṉē.
translation: If you are the son of the Lord who took alms, what will you do for those who harbor desire for you? Supreme Lord on the great green peacock! O wearer of Kadamba flowers in Thanigai, a city that rivals Kanchi.
commentary: The verse repeats the teasing question. It contrasts the Lord's majestic appearance on a green peacock with his simple lineage as the son of a mendicant.

translit: kaṭappa māmalark kaṇṇi mārpaṉē taṭappe rumpoḻil taṇikait tēvaṉē iṭappa ṭācciṟi yēṉai aṉparkaḷ toṭappa ṭāteṉil colva teṉkolō.
translation: O Lord whose chest is adorned with a garland of great Kadamba flowers! God of Thanigai surrounded by vast magnificent groves! If your devotees do not associate with this lowly one who has no place, what is there to say?
commentary: Repeating his heartfelt plea, the poet emphasizes his total reliance on the community of believers. Without their fellowship, he feels entirely lost and without a place in the world.

translit: eṉcol kēṉitai eṇṇil aṟputam vaṉco lēṉpiḻai matitti ṭātuvan tiṉco lālivaṇ irutti eṉṟaṉaṉ taṉcol cepparum taṇikait tēvaṉē.
translation: What can I say? When I think of this, it is a wonder. Not weighing the faults of my harsh speech, he came and with sweet words said, 'Stay here.' He is the God of Thanigai, whose own words are beyond description.
commentary: God responds to the poet's challenging words with total forgiveness. Overlooking all faults, the deity offers sweet words of welcome, an act of grace that fills the poet with wonder.

translit: tēva nēcaṉē ciṟakkum īcaṉē pāva nācaṉē parama tēcaṉē cāva kācaṉē taṇikai vācaṉē kōva pācaṉē kuṟikkoḷ eṉṉaiyē.
translation: O friend of the gods, O glorious Lord, O destroyer of sins, O Supreme Teacher, O tranquil Lord, O resident of Thanigai, O King free of bonds, please accept me as your own.
commentary: This verse is a direct, urgent plea for acceptance. God is praised as the ultimate teacher and the one who wipes away past wrongs, establishing a bond of complete surrender.

translit: kuṟikkoḷ aṉparaik kūṭu ṟāta-iv veṟikkoḷ nāyiṉai vēṇṭi aiyanī muṟikkoḷ vāykolō muṉikoḷ vāykolō neṟikkoḷ vōrpukaḻ taṇikai nittaṉē.
translation: O eternal Lord of Thanigai, praised by those who follow the righteous path. I am a mad dog who does not join the devotees focused on you. O Lord, will you desire me and break my bonds, or will you cast your anger upon me?
commentary: A sense of deep unworthiness drives this verse. The speaker compares himself to a wild, wandering dog that stays away from true devotees. He wonders aloud if God will choose to step in and break his worldly attachments, or simply reject him.

translit: taṇikai mēviya cāmi yēniṉai eṇikai viṭṭiṭēl eṉṟu tōttiram aṇikai niṉaṭik kayarntu niṉṟuvīṇ kaṇikai pōleṉaik kalakkiṟ ṟuḷḷamē.
translation: O Lord residing in Thanigai, my mind agitates me like a worthless courtesan. I grow weary at your feet, failing to sing your praises and beg you never to forget me.
commentary: The human mind is shown as the greatest obstacle to devotion. It is compared to a distracting courtesan who scatters a person's attention and leaves them exhausted, unable to properly hold onto God's presence.

translit: uḷḷam nekkuviṭ ṭurukum aṉpartam naḷa kattiṉil naṭikkum cōtiyē taḷa runtiṟal taṇikai āṉanta veḷḷa mēmaṉam viḷḷac ceyvaiyē.
translation: O Jothi who dances in the deep core of devotees whose hearts soften and melt. O flood of bliss in Thanigai possessing unsurpassed power, make my mind blossom open.
commentary: God is a divine light (Jothi) that dances actively inside the hearts of those who melt with love. The prayer here is for this powerful flood of bliss to crack a closed mind wide open so it can finally blossom.

translit: ceyva taṉṟavaṉ ciṟiya ṉēṉṟaṉai vaivar aṉparkaḷ eṉṉil mattaṉēṉ uyva tevvaṇam uraicey attaṉē caiva nātaṉē taṇikai maṉṉaṉē.
translation: I am a lowly one who commits wrongful deeds. If your devotees scorn me, how will a madman like me find salvation? Tell me, O Father, O Lord of the Saiva path, O King of Thanigai.
commentary: The focus shifts from God's judgment to the judgment of the spiritual community. There is a deep anxiety that if good and devoted people reject him for his faults, a confused and flawed person will have no path left to salvation.

translit: maṉṉum niṉaruḷ vāyppa tiṉṟiyē iṉṉum ittuyar ēykkil eṉceykēṉ poṉṉiṉ ampuyaṉ pōṟṟum pātaṉē taṉṉil niṉṟiṭum taṇikai mēlaṉē.
translation: If this sorrow continues to torment me without my attaining your enduring grace, what will I do? O Lord whose feet are praised by Brahma born on the golden lotus! O Lord who dwells upon unique Thanigai!
commentary: The poet feels completely helpless against his sorrow without divine grace. He wonders how he can possibly survive if the Lord of Thanigai does not intervene. Even Brahma, the creator god in Hindu tradition who is said to be born on a golden lotus, worships this supreme divine presence.

translit: mēlai vāṉavar vēṇṭum niṉtiruk kālai eṉciram kaḷikka vaippaiyō cālai ōṅkiya taṇikai veṟpaṉē vēlai ēntukai vimala nātaṉē.
translation: Will you place your holy feet, desired by the highest celestial gods, upon my head so it may rejoice? O Lord of the Thanigai mountain with its towering halls! O pure Lord holding a spear in your hand!
commentary: Placing the divine feet on a devotee's head is the ultimate sign of blessing and spiritual initiation in Tamil tradition. The poet asks for this supreme gift so his mind can rejoice. He notes that even the highest celestial gods beg for this exact blessing.

translit: vēta māmuṭi viḷaṅkum niṉtirup pātam ēttiṭāp pāvi yēṉtaṉak kītal iṉṟupō eṉṉil eṉceykēṉ cātal pōkkumnal taṇikai nēyaṉē.
translation: I am a sinner who does not praise your holy feet that shine at the supreme crown of the Vedas. If you tell me to go away today without granting me anything, what will I do? O beloved Lord of good Thanigai who dispels death!
commentary: The poet fears being turned away empty-handed because he feels he has failed to properly praise the divine. He seeks a grace that goes beyond his own flawed efforts. He appeals to a Lord whose power conquers death itself and whose presence is the true peak of the Vedas, the ancient sacred scriptures.

translit: nēyam niṉpuṭai niṉṟi ṭāta-eṉ māya neñciṉuḷ vanti ruppaiyō pēya ṉēṉperum piḻaipo ṟuttiṭat tāya niṉkaṭaṉ taṇikai vāṇaṉē.
translation: Will you come and reside in my illusory heart that lacks steadfast love for you? Forgiving the great faults of this mad fool is your maternal duty, O dweller of Thanigai!
commentary: It is a bold request to ask God to live in a heart that is distracted and lacking in steady love. To bridge this gap, the poet appeals to the divine's maternal nature. Just as a mother instinctively forgives her child's mistakes, he asks the Lord to overlook his flaws and enter his life anyway.

translit: vāṇu talperu māṭṭi māroṭu kāṇu taṟkuṉaik kātal koṇṭaṉaṉ ēṇu taṟkeṉa teṇṇam muṟṟumō māṇu taṟpukaḻt taṇikai vaṇṇaṉē.
translation: I fell in love, desiring to see you alongside your great goddesses with radiant foreheads. Will my intention to attain you be fulfilled? O beautiful Lord of Thanigai of glorious and excellent fame!
commentary: The desire here is for a complete, joyous vision of the divine. The poet longs to see the Lord of Thanigai accompanied by his traditional consorts, the goddesses Valli and Deivanai. He wonders if his intense love will be enough to finally bring this spiritual longing to reality.

translit: vaṇṇa ṉē-aruḷ vaḻaṅkum paṉṉiru kaṇṇa ṉē-ayil karaṅkoḷ aiyaṉē taṇṇa ṉērtirut taṇikai vēlaṉē tiṇṇam ītaruḷ ceyyum kālamē.
translation: O beautiful one! O twelve-eyed Lord who bestows grace! O Master holding the sharp spear in your hand! O Velan of cool and holy Thanigai! This is certainly the time for you to grant your grace.
commentary: The speaker calls upon Lord Murugan to grant his grace without delay. He addresses the deity by his traditional forms, mentioning the twelve eyes of his six faces and the sharp spear or vel in his hand. Murugan is praised as the lord of Thanigai, a sacred hill temple known for its peaceful coolness. The verse rests on a deep certainty that the perfect moment for grace has finally come.

translit: kālku ṟitta-eṉ karuttu muṟṟiyē cālva ḷattirut taṇikai cārvaṉeṉ mālpa kaippiṇi māṟi ōṭavē mēlku ṟippaṉāl veṟṟic caṅkamē.
translation: Fulfilling my determined intention, I will set out and reach abundantly fertile and holy Thanigai. As my delusion, hostility, and disease turn and flee, I will loudly sound the conch of victory.
commentary: The climb to the holy hill of Thanigai represents a total victory over both physical and mental suffering. The speaker declares that stepping into the divine presence will force all sickness, hatred, and spiritual delusion to flee. Blowing the conch shell is a traditional way to announce a triumph, marking the end of worldly struggles and the fulfillment of a firm resolve.

sections.title: A Petition of the Garland of Delusion

tamil: சொல்லும் பொருளு மாய்நிறைந்த சுகமே அன்பர் துதிதுணையே
புல்லும் புகழ்சேர் நல்தணிகைப் பொருப்பின் மருந்தே பூரணமே
அல்லும் பகலும் நின்நாமம் அந்தோ நினைந்துன் ஆளாகேன்
கல்லும் பொருவா வன்மனத்தால் கலங்கா நின்றேன் கடையேனே.
translit: collum poruḷu māyniṟainta cukamē aṉpar tutituṇaiyē pullum pukaḻcēr naltaṇikaip poruppiṉ maruntē pūraṇamē allum pakalum niṉnāmam antō niṉaintuṉ āḷākēṉ kallum poruvā vaṉmaṉattāl kalaṅkā niṉṟēṉ kaṭaiyēṉē.
translation: O bliss who fills all things as word and meaning! O help to praising devotees! O medicine of good Thanigai mountain which gathers embracing fame! O perfect one! Alas, I do not think of your name night and day and become your servant. I stand bewildered by a hard heart that even stone cannot equal. I am the lowest of all.
commentary: The poet laments that his heart is harder than stone because it refuses to focus on the divine. He looks to the deity of Thanigai mountain as the ultimate medicine for this spiritual sickness, regretting that he wastes his days without remembering the one who gives meaning to all words.

tamil: கடையேன் வஞ்ச நெஞ்சகத்தால் கலுழ்கின் றேன்நின் திருக்கருணை
அடையேன் அவமே திரிகின்றேன் அந்தோ சிறிதும் அறிவில்லேன்
விடையே றீசன் புயம்படும்உன் விரைத்தாள் கமலம் பெறுவேனோ
கொடைஏர் அருளைத் தருமுகிலே கோவே தணிகைக் குலமணியே.
translit: kaṭaiyēṉ vañca neñcakattāl kaluḻkiṉ ṟēṉniṉ tirukkaruṇai aṭaiyēṉ avamē tirikiṉṟēṉ antō ciṟitum aṟivillēṉ viṭaiyē ṟīcaṉ puyampaṭumuṉ viraittāḷ kamalam peṟuvēṉō koṭai-ēr aruḷait tarumukilē kōvē taṇikaik kulamaṇiyē.
translation: I am the lowest. I weep through my deceitful heart. I do not attain your holy grace. I wander in vain. Alas, I have no wisdom at all. Will I ever reach your fragrant lotus feet that rest upon the shoulders of the Lord who rides the bull? O cloud pouring forth the grace of beautiful bounty! O king! O crowning gem of Thanigai!
commentary: Deep sorrow over a distracted mind takes center stage here. The poet feels lost in empty pursuits and wonders if he will ever be worthy of grace. He asks if he will ever reach the divine feet that are tenderly held upon the shoulders of Siva, the Lord who rides the bull.

tamil: மணியே அடியேன் கண்மணியே மருந்தே அன்பர் மகிழ்ந்தணியும்
அணியே தணிகை அரசேதெள் அமுதே என்றன் ஆருயிரே
பிணிஏய் துயரால் வருந்திமனப் பேயால் அலைந்து பிறழ்கின்றேன்
தணியேன் தாகம் நின்அருளைத் தருதல் இலையேல் தாழ்வேனே.
translit: maṇiyē aṭiyēṉ kaṇmaṇiyē maruntē aṉpar makiḻntaṇiyum aṇiyē taṇikai aracēteḷ amutē eṉṟaṉ āruyirē piṇi-ēy tuyarāl varuntimaṉap pēyāl alaintu piṟaḻkiṉṟēṉ taṇiyēṉ tākam niṉaruḷait tarutal ilaiyēl tāḻvēṉē.
translation: O gem! O pupil of your servant's eye! O medicine! O ornament worn joyfully by devotees! O king of Thanigai! O clear ambrosia! O my precious life! I suffer the sorrow of disease. Driven by the ghost of my mind, I wander and stray. My thirst does not cool. If you do not grant your grace, I will fall low.
commentary: The restless human mind is described here as a haunting ghost that drives the soul into sickness and confusion. The poet cries out to the Lord of Thanigai as his precious life and medicine, warning that without the cooling drink of divine grace, his deep spiritual thirst will ruin him.

tamil: தாழ்வேன் வஞ்ச நெஞ்சகர்பால் சார்வேன் தனக்குன் அருள்தந்தால்
வாழ்வேன் இலையேல் என்செய்கேன் வருத்தம் பொறுக்க மாட்டேனே
ஏழ்வே தனையும் கடந்தவர்தம் இன்பப் பெருக்கே என்உயிரே
போழ்வேல் கரங்கொள் புண்ணியனே புகழ்சேர் தணிகைப் பொருப்பரசே.
translit: tāḻvēṉ vañca neñcakarpāl cārvēṉ taṉakkuṉ aruḷtantāl vāḻvēṉ ilaiyēl eṉceykēṉ varuttam poṟukka māṭṭēṉē ēḻvē taṉaiyum kaṭantavartam iṉpap perukkē eṉuyirē pōḻvēl karaṅkoḷ puṇṇiyaṉē pukaḻcēr taṇikaip porupparacē.
translation: I will fall low and join with the deceitful-hearted. If you grant me your grace, I will live. If not, what will I do? I cannot bear this sorrow. O flood of bliss for those who have crossed the seven torments! O my life! O virtuous one holding the piercing spear in your hand! O king of Thanigai mountain which gathers fame!
commentary: Without divine help, the poet fears he will fall into the company of deceitful people. He looks to the Lord holding the spear as the only true joy for those who have successfully crossed the torments of ordinary life.

tamil: அரைசே அடியர்க் கருள்குகனே அண்ணா தணிகை ஐயாவே
விரைசேர் கடம்ப மலர்ப்புயனே வேலா யுதக்கை மேலோனே
புரைசேர் மனத்தால் வருந்திஉன்றன் பூம்பொற் பதத்தைப் புகழ்கில்லேன்
தரைசேர் வாழ்வில் தயங்குகின்றேன் அந்தோ நின்று தனியேனே.
translit: araicē aṭiyark karuḷkukaṉē aṇṇā taṇikai aiyāvē viraicēr kaṭampa malarppuyaṉē vēlā yutakkai mēlōṉē puraicēr maṉattāl varunti-uṉṟaṉ pūmpoṟ patattaip pukaḻkillēṉ taraicēr vāḻvil tayaṅkukiṉṟēṉ antō niṉṟu taṉiyēṉē.
translation: O king! O Guha who grants grace to devotees! O elder brother! O master of Thanigai! O one whose shoulders wear fragrant kadamba flowers! O supreme one holding the spear weapon in your hand! Suffering with a flawed mind, I fail to praise your beautiful golden feet. I languish in this earthly life. Alas, I stand entirely alone.
commentary: The pain of spiritual isolation is the focus of this plea. The poet addresses the deity Guha as an elder brother and master. He confesses that a flawed mind keeps him tied to the struggles of earthly life, leaving him entirely alone and unable to offer praise.

tamil: தனியே துயரில் வருந்திமனம் சாம்பி வாழ்க்கைத் தளைப்பட்டிங்
கினிஏ துறுமோ என்செய்கேன் என்றே நின்றேற் கிரங்காயோ
கனியே பாகே கரும்பேஎன் கண்ணே தணிகைக் கற்பகமே
துனிஏய் பிறவி தனைஅகற்றும் துணையே சோதிச் சுகக்குன்றே.
translit: taṉiyē tuyaril varuntimaṉam cāmpi vāḻkkait taḷaippaṭṭiṅ kiṉi-ē tuṟumō eṉceykēṉ eṉṟē niṉṟēṟ kiraṅkāyō kaṉiyē pākē karumpē-eṉ kaṇṇē taṇikaik kaṟpakamē tuṉi-ēy piṟavi taṉai-akaṟṟum tuṇaiyē cōtic cukakkuṉṟē.
translation: Alone and suffering in sorrow, my mind withered, bound by the shackles of worldly life, I stand wondering what will happen now and what I should do. Will you not pity me? O fruit, sweet syrup, sugarcane, my very eyes, the wish-fulfilling tree of Thanigai, the companion who dispels the sorrow of birth, the mountain of blissful Jothi!
commentary: The burden of ordinary life leaves the mind exhausted and bound by worldly attachments. Seeking relief, the speaker turns to the divine, describing God with terms of intense sweetness like fruit, syrup, and sugarcane. This divine presence is the only true companion capable of breaking the painful cycle of birth and death. It is a direct plea for the blissful light of Jothi to replace earthly sorrow.

tamil: குன்றே மகிழ்ந்த குணக்குன்றே கோவே தணிகைக் குருபரனே
நன்றே தெய்வ நாயகமே நவிலற் கரிய நல்உறவே
என்றே வருவாய் அருள்தருவாய் என்றே புலம்பி ஏங்குற்றேன்
இன்றே காணப் பெறில்எந்தாய் இறவேன் பிறவேன் இருப்பேனே.
translit: kuṉṟē makiḻnta kuṇakkuṉṟē kōvē taṇikaik kuruparaṉē naṉṟē teyva nāyakamē navilaṟ kariya naluṟavē eṉṟē varuvāy aruḷtaruvāy eṉṟē pulampi ēṅkuṟṟēṉ iṉṟē kāṇap peṟilentāy iṟavēṉ piṟavēṉ iruppēṉē.
translation: O mountain of virtues who rejoices on the hill, king, supreme Guru of Thanigai, good Lord of the gods, noble kinship hard to describe. I lament and yearn, crying out to know when you will come and grant your grace. If I attain your vision today, my father, I will not die, I will not be born again. I will remain eternally.
commentary: The ultimate promise of this spiritual path is a life completely free from both death and rebirth. The speaker cries out in deep yearning for a direct vision of God. He declares that experiencing this divine reality today will conquer physical death itself. Complete liberation means remaining eternally in the state of grace.

tamil: இருப்பேன் துயர்வாழ் வினில்எனினும் எந்தாய் நினது பதங்காணும்
விருப்பேன் அயன்மால் முதலோரை வேண்டேன் அருள வேண்டாயோ
திருப்பேர் ஒளியே அருட்கடலே தெள்ளார் அமுதே திருத்தணிகைப்
பொருப்பே மகிழ்ந்த புண்ணியமே புனித ஞான போதகமே.
translit: iruppēṉ tuyarvāḻ viṉileṉiṉum entāy niṉatu pataṅkāṇum viruppēṉ ayaṉmāl mutalōrai vēṇṭēṉ aruḷa vēṇṭāyō tiruppēr oḷiyē aruṭkaṭalē teḷḷār amutē tiruttaṇikaip poruppē makiḻnta puṇṇiyamē puṉita ñāṉa pōtakamē.
translation: Even if I remain in this sorrowful life, my father, I desire only to see your feet. I do not beg Brahma, Vishnu, or the other gods. Will you not grant me your grace? O great holy light, ocean of grace, clear nectar, embodiment of merit who rejoices on the Thanigai hill, teacher of pure wisdom!
commentary: True devotion requires an undivided focus. The speaker explicitly refuses to pray to the traditional Hindu deities like Brahma or Vishnu, desiring only the grace of the one supreme holy light. Worldly sorrow loses its sting as long as this pure connection to the divine teacher is maintained.

tamil: போதா நந்த அருட்கனியே புகலற் கரிய பொருளேஎன்
நாதா தணிகை மலைஅரசே நல்லோர் புகழும் நாயகனே
ஓதா தவமே வருந்துயரால் உழன்றே பிணியில் உலைகின்றேன்
ஏதாம் உனதின் அருள்ஈயா திருந்தால் அந்தோ எளியேற்கே.
translit: pōtā nanta aruṭkaṉiyē pukalaṟ kariya poruḷē-eṉ nātā taṇikai malai-aracē nallōr pukaḻum nāyakaṉē ōtā tavamē varuntuyarāl uḻaṉṟē piṇiyil ulaikiṉṟēṉ ētām uṉatiṉ aruḷīyā tiruntāl antō eḷiyēṟkē.
translation: O fruit of grace of blissful wisdom, reality hard to describe, my Lord, king of the Thanigai hill, Lord praised by the virtuous. Having performed no true austerities, I suffer in sorrow and perish in disease. Alas, what will happen to this poor one if you do not grant your grace?
commentary: Physical disease and mental anguish weigh heavily on the human experience. The speaker admits to lacking the spiritual merit or strength to perform traditional austerities. Without personal achievements to rely on, the only hope left is the absolute necessity of divine grace to overcome suffering.

tamil: எளியேன் நினது திருவருளுக் கெதிர்நோக் குற்றே இரங்குகின்ற
களியேன் எனைநீ கைவிட்டால் கருணைக் கியல்போ கற்பகமே
அளியே தணிகை அருட்சுடரே அடியர் உறவே அருள்ஞானத்
துளியே அமையும் எனக்கெந்தாய் வாஎன் றொருசொல் சொல்லாயே.
translit: eḷiyēṉ niṉatu tiruvaruḷuk ketirnōk kuṟṟē iraṅkukiṉṟa kaḷiyēṉ eṉainī kaiviṭṭāl karuṇaik kiyalpō kaṟpakamē aḷiyē taṇikai aruṭcuṭarē aṭiyar uṟavē aruḷñāṉat tuḷiyē amaiyum eṉakkentāy vā-eṉ ṟorucol collāyē.
translation: I am a humble one looking toward your holy grace and grieving without joy. If you abandon me, is that the true nature of compassion, O wish-fulfilling tree? O grace, flame of grace in Thanigai, true kinship of devotees. Just a single drop of your gracious wisdom is enough for me, my father. Please speak the one word, "Come."
commentary: The soul makes a final, intimate appeal to God's fundamental nature of compassion. If the divine is truly compassionate, it cannot abandon a grieving devotee. The speaker does not demand overwhelming revelations to find peace. Just a single drop of divine wisdom, or a single welcoming word, is entirely enough to save him.

sections.title: Ten Verses on What Cannot Be Borne

translit: meyyaruḷ ḷakattiṉ viḷaṅkumniṉ patamām viraimalart tuṇaitamai virumpāp poyyar tam iṭattiv vaṭiyaṉēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy aiyarum iṭappāl ammaiyum varunti aḷittiṭum teḷḷiya amutē taiyalār mayakkaṟ ṟavarkkaruḷ poruḷē taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it, you see, when this devotee enters the homes of deceitful people who do not desire your pair of fragrant flower-feet that shine in the inner hearts of the truthful. O pure ambrosia given with great care by the Lord and the Mother on his left! O Reality who grants grace to those free from infatuation with women! O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai.
commentary: The pain of worldly life includes the forced company of those who have no genuine love for God. Vallalar says he simply cannot bear to be around deceitful people who ignore the divine. He prays to Saravanabhava (Lord Murugan) for deliverance, addressing him as the pure ambrosia given by the supreme Father and Mother. A devoted heart finds the environment of worldly, indifferent people impossible to endure.

translit: naṉmaiya ellām aḷittiṭum uṉatu naḷiṉamā malaraṭi vaḻuttāp puṉmaiyar iṭattiv vaṭiyaṉēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy ciṉmayap poruḷniṉ toṇṭarpāl nāyēṉ cērntiṭat tiruvaruḷ puriyāy taṉmayak kaṟṟōrk karuḷtarum poruḷē taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it, you see, when this devotee enters the space of base people who do not praise your great lotus feet that grant all good things. O Reality of pure consciousness, grant your divine grace so that I, a mere dog, may join your devotees. O Reality who grants grace to those free from the delusion of ego! O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai.
commentary: The only cure for the pain of worldly association is the fellowship of true devotees. Vallalar begs the Lord to rescue him from the spaces of base, ungrateful people and place him among those who possess genuine spiritual love. He asks this of God as the reality of pure consciousness, noting that divine grace flows easily to those who have abandoned the delusion of the ego.

translit: maruḷilā tavarkaḷ vaḻuttumniṉ aṭiyai maṉamuṟa niṉaintakat taṉpām poruḷilā tavarpāl ēḻaiyēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy aruḷelām tiraṇṭa āṉanta uruvē aṉparpāl iruntiṭa aruḷāy taraḷavāṉ maḻaipey tiṭumtirup poḻilcūḻ taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it, you see, when I, a poor soul, approach those who lack the inner wealth of love and do not deeply contemplate your feet praised by those free from delusion. O form of bliss where all grace gathers! Grant your grace so I may reside with your devotees. O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai, surrounded by divine groves where the sky showers pearls of rain.
commentary: True wealth is the inner presence of love. Vallalar finds it unbearable to spend time with those who lack this inner wealth and live without spiritual contemplation. He asks the Lord, whom he calls the gathered form of pure bliss and grace, to place him safely in the company of true seekers. Surrounding oneself with genuine love is essential for spiritual survival.

translit: nilai-aruḷ niṉatu malaraṭik kaṉpu nikaḻntiṭa nāḷtoṟum niṉaiyāp pulaiyartam iṭamip puṉmaiyēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy malai-ara caḷitta marakatak kompar varunti-īṉ ṟeṭuttamā maṇiyē talai-ara caḷikka intiraṉ pukaḻum taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it, you see, when this lowly soul enters the places of base people who do not think of you daily to let love manifest for your flower-feet that grant the eternal state. O great gem brought forth by the emerald branch given by the King of Mountains! O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai, praised by Indra for granting him his sovereign rule.
commentary: Spiritual love does not happen by accident. It must be cultivated through daily devotion. Vallalar expresses his agony at having to mingle with those who never take the time to awaken this love. He addresses Murugan as the precious gem born of the emerald branch (Goddess Parvati, daughter of the mountain king). The eternal state of grace requires constant, loving attention to the divine.

translit: valiruḷ pavamtīr marunteṉum niṉatu malaraṭi maṉamuṟa vaḻuttāp pullartam iṭamip poyyaṉēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy ollaiyiṉ eṉaimīṭ ṭuṉaṭi yavarpāl uṟṟuvāḻn tiṭacceyiṉ uyvēṉ callamaṟ ṟavarkaṭ karuḷtarum poruḷē taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it, you see, when I, a false soul, enter the places of petty people who do not praise your flower-feet from their hearts, the medicine that cures the dark disease of worldly birth. I will be saved if you rescue me swiftly and let me live alongside your devotees. O Reality who grants grace to those free from deceit! O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai.
commentary: The cycle of worldly birth is a dark disease, and divine grace is its only medicine. Vallalar begs for a swift rescue from petty, deceitful people who refuse this cure. He asks to be planted firmly among sincere devotees so his own spiritual life might survive and flourish. The right company is a literal lifeline for the soul.

translit: kaṟpilār eṉiṉum niṉaintiṭil aruḷniṉ karuṇai-am kaḻalaṭik kaṉpām poṟpilā tavarpāl ēḻaiyēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy aṟpilēṉ eṉiṉum eṉpiḻai poṟuttuṉ aṭiyarpāl cērttiṭil uyvēṉ taṟparā paramē caṟkuṇa malaiyē taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: Even if they lack virtue, if they think of you, your grace grants them love for your beautiful, merciful feet wearing anklets. See, I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it when poor me associates with those who lack such golden beauty. Even though I am without love, if you forgive my faults and join me with your devotees, I will be saved. O Supreme Being! O mountain of good qualities! O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai!
commentary: Divine grace responds instantly to a single thought, even from a person with a flawed past. The speaker asks the Divine, addressed here as Saravanabhava (a name for the deity Murugan), to place him among true seekers rather than those who are blind to this mercy. Thanigai refers to the sacred hill shrine of Thanigai. Surrounding oneself with spiritual company is presented as a vital lifeline.

translit: pattikoṇ ṭavaruḷ paraviya oḷiyām parañcuṭar niṉaṭi paṇiyum puttikoḷ ḷalarpāl eḷiyaṉēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy nittiya aṭiyar tammuṭaṉ kūṭṭa niṉaintiṭil uykuvaṉ aracē catticeṅ karattil tarittiṭum amutē taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: You are the supreme flame, the light that spreads within those who possess devotion. See, I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it when poor me associates with those who do not have the mind to bow at your feet. If you intend to unite me with your eternal devotees, I will be saved, O King. O nectar holding the powerful spear in your red hand! O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai!
commentary: The divine presence is an inner light that spreads within a devoted mind. The deepest pain of spiritual life is having to live among people who have no interest in this truth. To cure this isolation, the speaker begs to be united with those who live constantly in divine awareness. The imagery of the nectar holding a spear refers to Murugan's traditional weapon, representing the power of wisdom.

translit: nīṟṟaṇi viḷaṅkum avarkkaruḷ puriyum niṉaṭik kamalaṅkaḷ niṉaintē pōṟṟiṭā tavarpāl poyyaṉēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy āṟṟalkoḷ niṉpoṉ aṭiyaruk kaṭiyaṉ ācceyil uykuvaṉ amutē cāṟṟiṭum perumaik kaḷavilā tōṅkum taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: You grant grace to those who shine wearing the sacred ash. See, I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it when false me associates with those who do not think of and praise your lotus feet. If you make me a servant to your powerful, golden devotees, I will be saved, O nectar. Rising beyond measure in proclaimed greatness, O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai!
commentary: The sacred ash worn on the forehead is a traditional mark of purity and spiritual dedication. The speaker feels completely false when forced to spend time with people who ignore the divine. True safety lies in becoming a servant to the servants of God. By lowering oneself to serve those who already carry divine power, the soul secures its own rescue.

translit: parintiṭum maṉattōrk karuḷceyum niṉatu pātatā maraikaḷuk kaṉpu purintiṭā tavarpāl eḷiyaṉēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy terintiṭum aṉpar iṭamuṟil uyvēṉ tiruvuḷam aṟikilaṉ tēṉē carintiṭum karuttōrk kariyanaṟ pukaḻkoḷ taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: You grant grace to those with compassionate hearts. See, I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it when poor me associates with those who show no love for your lotus feet. If I reach the place of enlightened lovers, I will be saved. I do not know your divine will, O honey. Possessing good fame that is rare for those with faltering minds to attain, O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai!
commentary: Grace is naturally drawn to a compassionate heart. The text directly connects receiving divine help with holding genuine care for others. It is agonizing for a seeker to spend time with people who lack this fundamental love. Finding a community of enlightened people is the only escape from the draining effect of worldly company.

translit: eṇuṟum avarkaṭ karuḷumniṉ aṭiyai ēttiṭā taḻitarum celvap puṇuṟum avarpāl eḷiyaṉēṉ pukutal poṟukkilaṉ poṟukkilaṉ kaṇṭāy kaṇuṟu maṇiyām niṉaṭi yavarpāl kalantiṭil uykuvaṉ karumpē taṇuṟum karuṇait taṉipperuṅ kaṭalē. taṇikaivāḻ caravaṇa pavaṉē.
translation: Your feet grant grace to those who think of you. See, I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it when poor me associates with those who suffer the ulcer of wealth that destroys them because they do not praise your feet. If I mingle with your devotees who are precious as the apple of the eye, I will be saved, O sugarcane. O singular, great ocean of cool mercy! O Saravanabhava who dwells in Thanigai!
commentary: Worldly wealth without a spiritual purpose is described as a destructive disease. People who chase money while ignoring the divine end up consumed by the very things they hoard. The speaker pleads to be rescued from such a hollow society. True shelter is found only by mingling with true seekers who are as precious to God as the pupil is to the eye.

tamil: மன்னே என்றன் உயிர்க்குயிரே மணியே தணிகை மலைமருந்தே
அன்னே என்னை ஆட்கொண்ட அரசே தணிகை ஐயாவே
பொன்னே ஞானப் பொங்கொளியே புனித அருளே பூரணமே
என்னே எளியேன் துயர்உழத்தல் எண்ணி இரங்கா திருப்பதுவே.
translit: maṉṉē eṉṟaṉ uyirkkuyirē maṇiyē taṇikai malaimaruntē aṉṉē eṉṉai āṭkoṇṭa aracē taṇikai aiyāvē poṉṉē ñāṉap poṅkoḷiyē puṉita aruḷē pūraṇamē eṉṉē eḷiyēṉ tuyaruḻattal eṇṇi iraṅkā tiruppatuvē.
translation: O King, life of my life, gem, medicine of Mount Thanigai! O Mother, sovereign who claimed me, Lord of Thanigai! O gold, surging light of wisdom, pure grace, perfection! Why do you not show pity upon seeing the suffering of this poor soul?
commentary: The speaker addresses the divine in the most intimate terms, calling God both mother and the very life within his own life. He asks how a being of pure grace and perfect wisdom can look upon a suffering soul and withhold pity.

tamil: இரங்கா நின்றிங் கலைதரும்இவ் வெளியேன் கனவின் இடத்தேனும்
அரங்கா அரவின் நடித்தோனும் அயனும் காண்டற் கரிதாய
உரங்கா முறும்மா மயில்மேல்நின் உருவம் தரிசித் துவப்படையும்
வரங்கா தலித்தேன் தணிகைமலை வாழ்வே இன்று வருவாயோ.
translit: iraṅkā niṉṟiṅ kalaitarumiv veḷiyēṉ kaṉaviṉ iṭattēṉum araṅkā araviṉ naṭittōṉum ayaṉum kāṇṭaṟ karitāya uraṅkā muṟummā mayilmēlniṉ uruvam taricit tuvappaṭaiyum varaṅkā talittēṉ taṇikaimalai vāḻvē iṉṟu varuvāyō.
translation: I wander here without your pity. I long for the boon to behold your form seated on the great strong peacock and rejoice, at least in the dreams of this poor wretch. Your form is rare even for Brahma and Vishnu who danced on the serpent. O life of Mount Thanigai, will you come today?
commentary: The speaker begs for a glimpse of the Lord mounted on his peacock, asking for this vision if only in a dream. He points out that this direct experience of the divine form is something even the great creator and preserver gods, Brahma and Vishnu, struggle to attain.

tamil: வருவாய் என்று நாள்தோறும் வழிபார்த் திரங்கி மனந்தளர்ந்தேன்
கருவாய் பவன்என் றெனைத்தள்ளக் கருது வாயோ அன்றிஅருள்
உருவாய் வந்து தருவாயோ தணிகா சலத்துள் உற்றமர்ந்த
ஒருவர் உன்றன் திருவுளத்தை உணரேன் என்செய் துய்கேனே.
translit: varuvāy eṉṟu nāḷtōṟum vaḻipārt tiraṅki maṉantaḷarntēṉ karuvāy pavaṉeṉ ṟeṉaittaḷḷak karutu vāyō aṉṟi-aruḷ uruvāy vantu taruvāyō taṇikā calattuḷ uṟṟamarnta oruvar uṉṟaṉ tiruvuḷattai uṇarēṉ eṉcey tuykēṉē.
translation: Trusting you will come, I watched the path every day, wept, and grew weary in heart. Will you cast me away as a creature of worldly birth? Or will you come as the embodiment of grace and give yourself to me? O Peerless One seated on Mount Thanigai, I do not understand your divine will. What shall I do to be saved?
commentary: Waiting endlessly for grace brings the speaker to the point of absolute heartbreak and exhaustion. He is tormented by the fear that his worldly birth makes him unworthy, leaving him entirely dependent on a divine will he cannot yet understand.

tamil: உய்யும் பொருட்டுன் திருப்புகழை உரையேன் அந்தோ உரைக்கடங்காப்
பொய்யும் களவும் அழுக்காறும் பொருளாக் கொண்டேன் புலையேனை
எய்யும் படிவந் தடர்ந்தியமன் இழுத்துப் பறிக்கில் என்னேயான்
செய்யும் வகைஒன் றறியேனே தென்பால் தணிகைச் செஞ்சுடரே.
translit: uyyum poruṭṭuṉ tiruppukaḻai uraiyēṉ antō uraikkaṭaṅkāp poyyum kaḷavum aḻukkāṟum poruḷāk koṇṭēṉ pulaiyēṉai eyyum paṭivan taṭarntiyamaṉ iḻuttup paṟikkil eṉṉēyāṉ ceyyum vakai-oṉ ṟaṟiyēṉē teṉpāl taṇikaic ceñcuṭarē.
translation: I do not speak your divine praise to attain salvation. Alas, I took indescribable falsehood, theft, and envy as my wealth. When the god of death comes striking to attack, drag, and snatch away this degraded wretch, I know no way to escape. O red flame of southern Thanigai!
commentary: The fear of death exposes the emptiness of a life lived without spiritual focus. The speaker confesses that he pursued deceit and envy instead of seeking liberation, leaving him completely defenseless when his final hour arrives.

tamil: செஞ்சொல் சுவையே மெய்ஞ்ஞானச் செல்வப் பெருக்கே தெள்ளமுதே
விஞ்சைப் புலவர் புகழ்தணிகை விளக்கே துளக்கில் வேலோனே
வெஞ்சொல் புகலும் வஞ்சகர்பால் மேவி நின்தாள் மலர்மறந்தே
பஞ்சில் தமியேன் படும்பாட்டைப் பார்த்தும் அருட்கண் பார்த்திலையே.
translit: ceñcol cuvaiyē meyññāṉac celvap perukkē teḷḷamutē viñcaip pulavar pukaḻtaṇikai viḷakkē tuḷakkil vēlōṉē veñcol pukalum vañcakarpāl mēvi niṉtāḷ malarmaṟantē pañcil tamiyēṉ paṭumpāṭṭaip pārttum aruṭkaṇ pārttilaiyē.
translation: O sweetness of perfect words, abounding wealth of true wisdom, clear nectar! O lamp of Thanigai praised by learned poets, wielder of the unswerving spear! I associated with deceitful people who speak cruel words and forgot your lotus feet. I suffer like cotton in the wind. Even seeing the plight of this lonely wretch, you do not look at me with eyes of grace.
commentary: Bad company and harsh words distract the mind and pull it away from the divine. Without that spiritual anchor, the speaker feels fragile and entirely at the mercy of the world, blown about helplessly like loose cotton in the wind.

tamil: பார்க்கின் றிலையே பன்னிருகண் படைத்தும் எளியேன் பாடனைத்தும்
தீர்க்கின் றிலையே என்னேயான் செய்வேன் சிறியேன் சீமானே
போர்க்குன் றொடுசூர் புயக்குன்றும் பொடிசெய் வேற்கைப் புண்ணியனே
சீர்க்குன் றெனும்நல் வளத்தணிகைத் தேவே மயில்ஊர் சேவகனே.
translit: pārkkiṉ ṟilaiyē paṉṉirukaṇ paṭaittum eḷiyēṉ pāṭaṉaittum tīrkkiṉ ṟilaiyē eṉṉēyāṉ ceyvēṉ ciṟiyēṉ cīmāṉē pōrkkuṉ ṟoṭucūr puyakkuṉṟum poṭicey vēṟkaip puṇṇiyaṉē cīrkkuṉ ṟeṉumnal vaḷattaṇikait tēvē mayilūr cēvakaṉē.
translation: Even with your twelve eyes, you do not look at me. You do not end the sufferings of this lowly one. What shall I do? I am insignificant, O Lord. O virtuous one with the spear in hand, which turned the battle-hill and the mountain-like shoulders of Surapadman to dust! O God of Thanigai, a good mountain of glory! O warrior who rides the peacock!
commentary: The poet asks a very human question of the divine deity Murugan: if this God has twelve eyes, why can he not see one devotee's suffering? Vallalar contrasts Murugan's legendary might against demons like Surapadman with his apparent inaction toward a single struggling soul. The appeal relies on the intimate, demanding relationship between the devotee and God.

tamil: சேவற் கொடிகொள் குணக்குன்றே சிந்தா மணியே யாவர்கட்கும்
காவற் பதியே தணிகைவளர் கரும்பே கனியே கற்பகமே
மூவர்க் கிறையே வேய்ஈன்ற முத்தன் அளித்த முத்தேநல்
translit: cēvaṟ koṭikoḷ kuṇakkuṉṟē cintā maṇiyē yāvarkaṭkum kāvaṟ patiyē taṇikaivaḷar karumpē kaṉiyē kaṟpakamē mūvark kiṟaiyē vēyīṉṟa muttaṉ aḷitta muttēnal tēvark karuḷniṉ cēvaṭikkē viḻaintēṉ yātumteriyēṉē.
translation: O mountain of virtue holding the rooster banner! O wish-fulfilling gem! O protecting Lord for all! O sugarcane flourishing in Thanigai, O sweet fruit, O wish-fulfilling tree! O Lord of the triad! O pearl given by the pure Lord! I yearned only for your red feet that bestow grace on the good celestial beings. I know nothing else.
commentary: God is the sole source of protection, sweetness, and fulfillment. Vallalar uses traditional symbols of total abundance, calling Murugan a wish-fulfilling tree and a magical gem that grants all desires. Yet the poet asks for none of these worldly gifts. He yearns only for the grace found at the Lord's feet, knowing no other goal.

tamil: தெரியேன் உனது திருப்புகழைத் தேவே உன்றன் சேவடிக்கே
பரியேன் பணியேன் கூத்தாடேன் பாடேன் புகழைப் பரவசமாய்த்
தரியேன் தணிகை தனைக்காணேன் சாகேன் நோகேன் கும்பிக்கே
translit: teriyēṉ uṉatu tiruppukaḻait tēvē uṉṟaṉ cēvaṭikkē pariyēṉ paṇiyēṉ kūttāṭēṉ pāṭēṉ pukaḻaip paravacamāyt tariyēṉ taṇikai taṉaikkāṇēṉ cākēṉ nōkēṉ kumpikkē uriyēṉ antō etukoṇṭiṅ kuykēṉ yātuceykēṉē.
translation: I do not know your divine glory, O God. I do not love your red feet, I do not bow down, I do not dance, I do not sing your praise, I do not abide in ecstasy. I do not see Thanigai, I do not die of yearning, I do not ache. I am fit only for hell. Alas, with what can I find salvation here? What shall I do?
commentary: The poet confesses a total lack of spiritual feeling and devotion. In the Tamil tradition of ecstatic worship, devotees weep, dance, and ache for God. Vallalar lists all these passionate signs of faith and admits he feels none of them, declaring himself fit only for a hell of suffering. This absolute self-abasement strips the ego bare, leaving nothing but a desperate cry for mercy.

tamil: செய்வ துனது திருவடிக்காம் திறனே சிந்தை நின்பாலே
வைவ துன்னை நினையாத வஞ்ச கரையே வழுத்திநிதம்
உய்வ துனது திருநாமம் ஒன்றைப் பிடித்தே மற்றொன்றால்
எய்வ தறியேன் திருத்தணிகை எந்தாய் எந்தாய் எளியேனே.
translit: ceyva tuṉatu tiruvaṭikkām tiṟaṉē cintai niṉpālē vaiva tuṉṉai niṉaiyāta vañca karaiyē vaḻuttinitam uyva tuṉatu tirunāmam oṉṟaip piṭittē maṟṟoṉṟāl eyva taṟiyēṉ tiruttaṇikai entāy entāy eḷiyēṉē.
translation: My duty is to serve your holy feet. My mind must be placed on you. I must rebuke the deceitful ones who do not think of you. I must find salvation daily by holding onto your holy name alone. I know no other way to reach the goal. O my father of Thanigai, my father, I am but a poor one.
commentary: Salvation comes entirely from holding fast to the name of God. Realizing his own emptiness, the poet sets out the basic duties of a spiritual life: keeping the mind fixed on the divine, rejecting falsehood, and repeating the holy name. He addresses God as a father, placing his absolute trust in this single path of devotion.

tamil: எளியேன் நினது சேவடியாம் இன்ப நறவை எண்ணிஎண்ணி
அளியேன் நெஞ்சம் சற்றேனும் அன்பொன் றில்லேன் அதுசிறிதும்
ஒளியேன் எந்தாய் என்உள்ளத் தொளித்தே எவையும் உணர்கின்றாய்
வளியே முதலாய் நின்றருளும் மணியே தணிகை வாழ்மன்னே.
translit: eḷiyēṉ niṉatu cēvaṭiyām iṉpa naṟavai eṇṇi-eṇṇi aḷiyēṉ neñcam caṟṟēṉum aṉpoṉ ṟillēṉ atuciṟitum oḷiyēṉ entāy eṉuḷḷat toḷittē evaiyum uṇarkiṉṟāy vaḷiyē mutalāy niṉṟaruḷum maṇiyē taṇikai vāḻmaṉṉē.
translation: I am lowly. I do not melt thinking again and again of the sweet nectar of your red feet. My heart has not the slightest love. I will not hide this at all, my father. You hide within my heart and know everything. O gem who stands as the elements beginning with wind and bestows grace! O king dwelling in Thanigai!
commentary: A person cannot hide their true inner state from the divine. The poet confesses his absolute lack of love, but he knows this confession is almost unnecessary because God dwells silently inside the human heart. The same God who exists outward as the vast physical elements of the universe also lives intimately within, witnessing every thought and feeling.

sections.title: The Truth of the Six Letters

tamil: பெருமை நிதியே மால்விடைகொள் பெம்மான் வருந்திப் பெறும்பேறே
அருமை மணியே தணிகைமலை அமுதே உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
இருமை வளனும் எய்தும்இடர் என்ப தொன்றும் எய்தாதே.
translit: perumai nitiyē mālviṭaikoḷ pemmāṉ varuntip peṟumpēṟē arumai maṇiyē taṇikaimalai amutē uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai orumai maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl irumai vaḷaṉum eytumiṭar eṉpa toṉṟum eytātē.
translation: Treasure of greatness! Rare blessing attained with effort by the Lord who rides the great bull! Precious gem! Ambrosia of Thanigai hill! If one chants your six letters here with a unified mind and applies the supreme holy white ash, the wealth of both worlds will be attained. No affliction whatsoever will approach.
commentary: Focused devotion brings rewards in this life and the next. The six letters refer to the traditional Tamil mantra of Murugan, the deity of Thanigai hill. The holy white ash is a sacred powder worn on the forehead as a mark of purity. When a person unites their mind in this chant and wears the ash, they gain the wealth of both the physical and spiritual worlds, and all their troubles disappear.

tamil: எய்தற் கரிய அருட்சுடரே எல்லாம் வல்ல இறையோனே
செய்தற் கரிய வளத்தணிகைத் தேவே உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
வைதற் கில்லாப் புகழ்ச்சிவரும் வன்கண் ஒன்றும் வாராதே.
translit: eytaṟ kariya aruṭcuṭarē ellām valla iṟaiyōṉē ceytaṟ kariya vaḷattaṇikait tēvē uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai uytaṟ poruṭṭiṅ kuccarittē uyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl vaitaṟ killāp pukaḻccivarum vaṉkaṇ oṉṟum vārātē.
translation: Light of grace hard to reach! All-powerful Lord! Deity of fertile Thanigai where rare deeds are done! If one chants your six letters here to attain salvation and applies the supreme holy white ash, flawless praise will come. No cruel sorrow whatsoever will come.
commentary: Chanting the six syllables with a pure intention protects a person from cruelty and brings lasting respect. The spiritual practice described here requires a genuine desire for liberation. When done earnestly, this meditation forms a shield around the devotee, keeping all harsh sorrows away.

tamil: வாரா இருந்த அடியவர்தம் மனத்தில் ஒளிரும் மாமணியே
ஆரா அமுதே தணிகைமலை அரசே உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
ஏரார் செல்வப் பெருக்கிகவா இடும்பை ஒன்றும் இகந்திடுமே.
translit: vārā irunta aṭiyavartam maṉattil oḷirum māmaṇiyē ārā amutē taṇikaimalai aracē uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai ōrā maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl ērār celvap perukkikavā iṭumpai oṉṟum ikantiṭumē.
translation: Great gem shining in the minds of never-departing devotees! Insatiable ambrosia! King of Thanigai hill! If one chants your six letters here with a meditating mind and applies the supreme holy white ash, abundant and beautiful wealth will never leave. Every affliction will depart.
commentary: A meditating mind turns verbal chanting into a powerful spiritual tool. The divine presence is described as an endless source of sweetness that shines directly inside the minds of true devotees. Through this inward focus and the sacred six letters, abundance naturally flows in and all hardship departs.

tamil: இகவா அடியர் மனத்தூறும் இன்பச் சுவையே எம்மானே
அகவா மயில்ஊர் திருத்தணிகை அரசே உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
சுகவாழ் வின்பம் அதுதுன்னும் துன்பம் ஒன்றும் துன்னாதே.
translit: ikavā aṭiyar maṉattūṟum iṉpac cuvaiyē emmāṉē akavā mayilūr tiruttaṇikai aracē uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai ukavā maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl cukavāḻ viṉpam atutuṉṉum tuṉpam oṉṟum tuṉṉātē.
translation: Sweet taste of joy welling up in the minds of inseparable devotees! My Lord! King of holy Thanigai who rides the calling peacock! If one chants your six letters here with an unfailing mind and applies the supreme holy white ash, the bliss of a joyful life will draw near. No sorrow whatsoever will draw near.
commentary: True spiritual joy wells up from within when devotion remains constant. The deity is pictured riding a peacock, a traditional symbol in Tamil poetry for this divine form. Repeating the mantra with steady, unfaltering attention invites a life filled with quiet bliss and free from all sorrow.

tamil: துன்னும் மறையின் முடிவில்ஒளிர் தூய விளக்கே சுகப்பெருக்கே
அன்னை அனையாய் தணிகைமலை அண்ணா உன்றென் ஆறெழுத்தை
சென்னி அணியாய் அடிசேரும் தீமை ஒன்றும் சேராதே.
translit: tuṉṉum maṟaiyiṉ muṭiviloḷir tūya viḷakkē cukapperukkē aṉṉai aṉaiyāy taṇikaimalai aṇṇā uṉṟeṉ āṟeḻuttai uṉṉi maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl ceṉṉi aṇiyāy aṭicērum tīmai oṉṟum cērātē.
translation: Pure lamp shining at the culmination of the enduring Vedas! Flood of bliss! You who are like a mother! Master of Thanigai hill! If one contemplates your six letters in the mind, chants them here, and applies the supreme holy white ash, your feet will join them as an ornament for their head. No evil whatsoever will draw near.
commentary: The highest spiritual reward is total union with the divine. The passage describes the deity as the pure light found at the very end of the Vedas (the ancient sacred scriptures) and as a presence as comforting as a mother. When the mind holds firmly to the six letters, the divine feet rest gently on the devotee's head as a protective crown, ensuring no evil can ever touch them.

tamil: சேரும் முக்கண் கனிகனிந்த தேனே ஞானச் செழுமணியே
யாரும் புகழும் தணிகைஎம தன்பே உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
பாரும் விசும்பும் பதஞ்சாரும் பழங்கண் ஒன்றும் சாராதே.
translit: cērum mukkaṇ kaṉikaṉinta tēṉē ñāṉac ceḻumaṇiyē yārum pukaḻum taṇikai-ema taṉpē uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai ōrum maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl pārum vicumpum patañcārum paḻaṅkaṇ oṉṟum cārātē.
translation: O honey ripened from the three-eyed fruit! O rich gem of wisdom! O our love residing in Thanigai, praised by all! If one chants your six letters with a focused mind and applies the exalted holy white ash here, they will attain the realms of earth and heaven. Old sorrows will never approach them.
commentary: The core of this devotion is the quiet, focused recitation of Murugan's six-lettered mantra (Sa-ra-va-na-ba-va) along with the wearing of holy white ash. Combining deep mental focus with these sacred acts lifts the soul to higher realms and banishes long-standing grief. The text addresses the divine as a sweet fruit born of the 'three-eyed' Lord, a traditional reference to Murugan as the beloved son of Siva.

tamil: சார்ந்த அடியார்க் கருள்அளிக்கும் தருமக் கடலே தற்பரமே
வார்ந்த பொழில்சூழ் திருத்தணிகை மணியே உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
ஆர்ந்த ஞானம் உறும்அழியா அலக்கண் ஒன்றும் அழிந்திடுமே.
translit: cārnta aṭiyārk karuḷaḷikkum tarumak kaṭalē taṟparamē vārnta poḻilcūḻ tiruttaṇikai maṇiyē uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai ōrntu maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl ārnta ñāṉam uṟumaḻiyā alakkaṇ oṉṟum aḻintiṭumē.
translation: O ocean of righteousness who grants grace to the devotees who seek refuge! O Supreme Being! O gem of holy Thanigai surrounded by lush groves! If one contemplates and chants your six letters in the mind and applies the exalted holy white ash here, profound wisdom will arise. Even unyielding sorrows will be completely destroyed.
commentary: Mental chanting of the mantra and applying holy ash serve as acts of deep inward contemplation. When devotion is fully anchored in the mind, it gives rise to deep spiritual wisdom. This inner clarity completely destroys even the most stubborn, deep-rooted sorrows.

tamil: அழியாப் பொருளே என்உயிரே அயில்செங் கரங்கொள் ஐயாவே
கழியாப் புகழ்சேர் தணிகைஅமர் கந்தா உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
பழியா இன்பம் அதுபதியும் பனிமை ஒன்றும் பதியாதே.
translit: aḻiyāp poruḷē eṉuyirē ayilceṅ karaṅkoḷ aiyāvē kaḻiyāp pukaḻcēr taṇikai-amar kantā uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai oḻiyā maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl paḻiyā iṉpam atupatiyum paṉimai oṉṟum patiyātē.
translation: O imperishable reality! O my life! O Lord holding the sharp spear in your red hand! O Skanda seated in Thanigai of unfading fame! If one chants your six letters ceaselessly in the mind and applies the exalted holy white ash here, flawless joy will take root. Trembling fear will never take hold.
commentary: Unceasing remembrance of the divine replaces worldly anxieties with a flawless, lasting joy. The sacred spear in the Lord's hand acts as a classic symbol of spiritual knowledge piercing through ignorance. By fixing the mind entirely on this imperishable reality, the devotee becomes completely free from trembling fear.

tamil: பதியே எங்கும் நிறைந்தருளும் பரம சுகமே பரஞ்சுடரே
கதியே அளிக்கும் தணிகைஅமர் கடம்பா உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
துதிஏர் நினது பதந்தோன்றும் துன்பம் ஒன்றும் தோன்றாதே.
translit: patiyē eṅkum niṟaintaruḷum parama cukamē parañcuṭarē katiyē aḷikkum taṇikai-amar kaṭampā uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai utiyēr maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl tuti-ēr niṉatu patantōṉṟum tuṉpam oṉṟum tōṉṟātē.
translation: O Lord! O supreme bliss filling everywhere with grace! O Supreme Light! O Kadamba seated in Thanigai, granting liberation! If one chants your six letters with an awakened mind and applies the exalted holy white ash here, your praiseworthy feet will manifest. No sorrow will ever appear.
commentary: An awakened mind is essential for true worship. By chanting the sacred syllables with vivid awareness and wearing the holy ash, the devotee experiences the direct presence of the divine, traditionally described as seeing the Lord's feet. The title Kadamba links the divine to the Kadamba tree, a favored symbol in ancient Tamil devotion.

tamil: தோன்றா ஞானச் சின்மயமே தூய சுகமே சுயஞ்சுடரே
ஆன்றார் புகழும் தணிகைமலை அரசே உன்றன் ஆறெழுத்தை
ஈன்றாள் நிகரும் அருள்அடையும் இடுக்கண் ஒன்றும் அடையாதே.
translit: tōṉṟā ñāṉac ciṉmayamē tūya cukamē cuyañcuṭarē āṉṟār pukaḻum taṇikaimalai aracē uṉṟaṉ āṟeḻuttai ūṉṟā maṉattiṉ uccarittiṅ kuyarnta tiruveṇṇīṟiṭṭāl īṉṟāḷ nikarum aruḷaṭaiyum iṭukkaṇ oṉṟum aṭaiyātē.
translation: O embodiment of unmanifest pure consciousness! O pure bliss! O self-luminous light! O king of Mount Thanigai, praised by the wise! If one chants your six letters with a firmly anchored mind and applies the exalted holy white ash here, they will receive grace equal to a mother's love. No distress will ever reach them.
commentary: The ultimate reward of a perfectly anchored mind is receiving divine grace that equals the boundless, tender love of a mother. The divine is described here as a self-luminous light and pure consciousness, entirely free of physical form. When the mind is steady and fixed on this light through the mantra and the holy ash, no worldly distress can ever touch the soul.

tamil: கற்கி லேன்உன தருட்பெயர் ஆம்குக கந்தஎன் பவைநாளும்
நிற்கி லேன்உன தாகம நெறிதனில் நீசனேன் உய்வேனோ
சொற்கி லேசமில் அடியவர் அன்பினுள் தோய்தரு பசுந்தேனே
அற்கி லேர்தரும் தணிகைஆர் அழுதமே ஆனந்த அருட்குன்றே.
translit: kaṟki lēṉuṉa taruṭpeyar āmkuka kanta-eṉ pavaināḷum niṟki lēṉuṉa tākama neṟitaṉil nīcaṉēṉ uyvēṉō coṟki lēcamil aṭiyavar aṉpiṉuḷ tōytaru pacuntēṉē aṟki lērtarum taṇikai-ār aḻutamē āṉanta aruṭkuṉṟē.
translation: I do not recite your gracious names of Guha and Skanda every day. I do not stand in the path of your Agamas. Will I, a base one, ever be saved? O fresh honey soaking in the love of devotees whose words are free of affliction! O nectar filling Thanigai of unceasing beauty! O hill of blissful grace!
commentary: Vallalar speaks here as a seeker who has failed at basic religious duties. He admits he does not recite the names of God or follow the rules of the scriptures (Agamas). Looking at his own shortcomings, he wonders if a person so deeply flawed can ever hope to be saved.

tamil: பாவ வாழ்க்கையில் பாவியேன் செய்திடும் பண்பிலாப் பிழைநோக்கித்
தேவ ரீர்மன திரக்கமுற் றேஅருள் செய்திடா திருப்பீரேல்
காவ லாகிய கடும்பிணித் துயரம்இக் கடையனேன் தனக்கின்னும்
யாவ தாகுமோ என்செய்கோ என்செய்கோ இயலும்வேல் கரத்தீரே.
translit: pāva vāḻkkaiyil pāviyēṉ ceytiṭum paṇpilāp piḻainōkkit tēva rīrmaṉa tirakkamuṟ ṟē-aruḷ ceytiṭā tiruppīrēl kāva lākiya kaṭumpiṇit tuyaramik kaṭaiyaṉēṉ taṉakkiṉṉum yāva tākumō eṉceykō eṉceykō iyalumvēl karattīrē.
translation: Seeing the uncultured faults this sinner commits in this sinful life, if you do not feel compassion in your heart and bestow your grace upon me, what will become of the severe affliction of disease that keeps me imprisoned? What will happen to this lowest one? What shall I do? What shall I do? O Lord holding the mighty spear!
commentary: The poet feels completely trapped by his own faults and the miseries of physical life. He says that unless God steps in with pure compassion, he has no way to break free from this suffering. His repeated cry asking what he should do shows a mind at the end of its own strength, relying entirely on grace.

tamil: சேவி யாதஎன் பிழைகளை என்னுளே சிறிதறி தரும்போதோ
பாவி யேன்மனம் பகீலென வெதும்பியுள் பதைத்திடக் காண்கின்றேன்
ஆவி யேஅருள் அமுதமே நின்திரு வருள்தனக் கென்னாமோ
பூவில் நாயகன் போற்றிடும் தணிகையம் பொருப்பமர்ந் திடுவாழ்வே.
translit: cēvi yāta-eṉ piḻaikaḷai eṉṉuḷē ciṟitaṟi tarumpōtō pāvi yēṉmaṉam pakīleṉa vetumpiyuḷ pataittiṭak kāṇkiṉṟēṉ āvi yē-aruḷ amutamē niṉtiru varuḷtaṉak keṉṉāmō pūvil nāyakaṉ pōṟṟiṭum taṇikaiyam poruppamarn tiṭuvāḻvē.
translation: Whenever I realize within myself even a fraction of my faults in failing to serve you, I see my sinful mind burn with sudden shock and throb in distress. O my life! O nectar of grace! What will become of your holy grace? O life abiding on the beautiful Thanigai hill, praised by the lord seated on the lotus!
commentary: Even a brief glimpse of his own mistakes fills the poet with burning shock and distress. He turns the question back on the divine, asking what the true measure of holy grace really is if it cannot save someone in such desperate need. He suggests that God's compassion must be vast enough to heal even the worst failures.

tamil: துன்பி னால்அகம் வெதும்பிநைந் தயர்ந்துநின் துணைஅடி மலர்ஏத்தும்
அன்பி லாதஇப் பாவியேன் செய்பிழை அனைத்தையும் பொறுப்பாயேல்
வன்பி லாதநின் அடியவர் தம்திரு மனத்தினுக் கென்னாமோ
இன்பி னால்சுரர் போற்றிடும் தணிகைவாழ் இறைவனே எம்மானே.
translit: tuṉpi ṉālakam vetumpinain tayarntuniṉ tuṇai-aṭi malarēttum aṉpi lāta-ip pāviyēṉ ceypiḻai aṉaittaiyum poṟuppāyēl vaṉpi lātaniṉ aṭiyavar tamtiru maṉattiṉuk keṉṉāmō iṉpi ṉālcurar pōṟṟiṭum taṇikaivāḻ iṟaivaṉē emmāṉē.
translation: If you forgive all the faults committed by this sinner who lacks the love to praise your twin lotus feet even as my mind burns, wastes away, and grows weary from sorrow, what will happen to the holy minds of your devotees who are free of harshness? O God living in Thanigai, praised with joy by the celestials! O my Lord!
commentary: Vallalar wonders aloud if forgiving someone as flawed as himself would seem unfair to the true devotees. He feels he lacks the deep love needed to praise God, even when sorrow is wearing him down. By asking this question, he appeals to a mercy that goes beyond human ideas of fairness and strict justice.

tamil: என்செய் கேன்இனும் திருவருள் காண்கிலேன் எடுக்கரும் துயர்உண்டேன்
கன்செய் பேய்மனக் கடையனேன் என்னினும் காப்பதுன் கடன்அன்றோ
பொன்செய் குன்றமே பூரண ஞானமே புராதனப் பொருள்வைப்பே
மன்செய் மாணிக்க விளக்கமே தணிகைவாழ் வள்ளலே மயிலோனே.
translit: eṉcey kēṉiṉum tiruvaruḷ kāṇkilēṉ eṭukkarum tuyaruṇṭēṉ kaṉcey pēymaṉak kaṭaiyaṉēṉ eṉṉiṉum kāppatuṉ kaṭaṉaṉṟō poṉcey kuṉṟamē pūraṇa ñāṉamē purātaṉap poruḷvaippē maṉcey māṇikka viḷakkamē taṇikaivāḻ vaḷḷalē mayilōṉē.
translation: What shall I do? I still do not see your holy grace. I suffer sorrow that is hard to bear. Even if I am the lowest one with a demonic mind made of stone, is it not your duty to protect me? O hill of gold! O perfect wisdom! O ancient treasure of reality! O firmly established ruby lamp! O benefactor living in Thanigai! O rider of the peacock!
commentary: After confessing all his flaws, Vallalar makes a bold claim. He tells God that protecting him is simply a divine duty, no matter how hard or stubborn his own mind might be. He addresses the divine with radiant images of light and wisdom, trusting that supreme grace must naturally care for the lowest beings.

tamil: மண்ணில் நண்ணிய வஞ்சகர் பால்கொடு வயிற்றினால் அலைப்பட்டேன்
கண்ணில் நண்ணரும் காட்சியே நின்திருக் கடைக்கண்ணோக் கருள்நோக்கி
புண்ணில் நண்ணிய வேல்எனத் துயர்உறில் புலையன்என் செய்கேனே.
translit: maṇṇil naṇṇiya vañcakar pālkoṭu vayiṟṟiṉāl alaippaṭṭēṉ kaṇṇil naṇṇarum kāṭciyē niṉtiruk kaṭaikkaṇṇōk karuḷnōkki eṇṇi eṇṇineñ caḻintukaṇṇīrkoḷum ēḻaiyēṉ taṉakkiṉṉum puṇṇil naṇṇiya vēleṉat tuyaruṟil pulaiyaṉeṉ ceykēṉē.
translation: I suffered, tossed about for the sake of my stomach while approaching deceitful men on earth. O vision rarely grasped by the eyes. Hoping for the grace of your holy side-glance, I am a poor wretch weeping tears, my heart breaking as I think and think of it. If I suffer further like a spear thrust into a wound, what will this base one do?
commentary: The need to feed the physical body often forces a person into humiliating dependence on cruel and deceitful people. This struggle for survival breaks the heart. The poet begs for a single glance of divine grace, warning that any further worldly pain would be like thrusting a spear into an open wound.

tamil: மலங்கி வஞ்சகர் மாட்டிரந் தையகோ வருந்திநெஞ் சயர்வுற்றே
கலங்கி நின்திருக் கருணையை விழையும்என் கண்அருள் செய்யாயோ
இலங்கி எங்கணும் நிறைந்தருள் இன்பமே எந்தையே எந்தாயே
நலங்கி ளர்ந்திடும் தணிகையம் பதியமர் நாயக மணிக்குன்றே.
translit: malaṅki vañcakar māṭṭiran taiyakō varuntineñ cayarvuṟṟē kalaṅki niṉtiruk karuṇaiyai viḻaiyumeṉ kaṇaruḷ ceyyāyō ilaṅki eṅkaṇum niṟaintaruḷ iṉpamē entaiyē entāyē nalaṅki ḷarntiṭum taṇikaiyam patiyamar nāyaka maṇikkuṉṟē.
translation: Bewildered, I begged from deceitful men. Alas, I grieve, my heart exhausted. I am confused. Will you not bestow grace upon me, who longs for your holy compassion? O shining bliss of grace filling everywhere. O my Father. O my Mother. O Lord, the mountain of gems abiding in the sacred city of Thanigai where goodness flourishes.
commentary: Worldly survival drains the spirit and brings utter confusion. Seeking help from dishonest people yields only grief. Turning away from human reliance, the poet addresses the divine presence in the sacred city of Thanigai as both Father and Mother, pleading for pure compassion.

tamil: சைவ நாயக சம்பந்தன் ஆகிய தமிழ்அருட் குன்றேஎன்
தெய்வ மேநினை அன்றிஓர் துணையிலேன் திருவருள் அறியாதோ
வைவ தேகொளும் வஞ்சகர் தம்இடை வருந்திநெஞ் சழிகின்றேன்
செய்வ தோர்கிலேன் கைவிடில் என்செய்கேன் தெளிவிலாச் சிறியேனே.
translit: caiva nāyaka campantaṉ ākiya tamiḻaruṭ kuṉṟē-eṉ teyva mēniṉai aṉṟi-ōr tuṇaiyilēṉ tiruvaruḷ aṟiyātō vaiva tēkoḷum vañcakar tamiṭai varuntineñ caḻikiṉṟēṉ ceyva tōrkilēṉ kaiviṭil eṉceykēṉ teḷivilāc ciṟiyēṉē.
translation: O mountain of Tamil grace who appeared as Sambandar, the master of Saivism. O my God. I have no refuge other than you. Does your holy grace not know this? I grieve, my heart ruined among deceitful men who only know how to hurl abuse. I do not know what to do. If you abandon me, what will this ignorant, little one do?
commentary: The text praises the divine as taking the form of Sambandar, a revered master of the Saiva faith. Surrounded by abusive and deceitful people, the poet confesses absolute helplessness. He declares that God is his only refuge, leaving him nowhere else to turn if abandoned.

tamil: வாழ்வில் ஆம்சிறு களிப்பினால் உன்றனை மறந்திறு மாக்கின்றேன்
தாழ்வி லேசிறி தெண்ணிநொந் தயர்வன்என் தன்மைநன் றருளாளா
கேழ்வி மேவிய அடியவர் மகிழ்வுறக் கிடைத்தருள் பெருவாழ்வே
வேழ்வி ஓங்கிய தணிகைமா மலைதனில் விளங்கிவீற் றிருப்போனே.
translit: vāḻvil āmciṟu kaḷippiṉāl uṉṟaṉai maṟantiṟu mākkiṉṟēṉ tāḻvi lēciṟi teṇṇinon tayarvaṉeṉ taṉmainaṉ ṟaruḷāḷā kēḻvi mēviya aṭiyavar makiḻvuṟak kiṭaittaruḷ peruvāḻvē vēḻvi ōṅkiya taṇikaimā malaitaṉil viḷaṅkivīṟ ṟiruppōṉē.
translation: Through the petty joys of worldly life, I forget you and grow arrogant. In times of decline, I think of you a little and grow exhausted from suffering. Truly my nature is excellent, O merciful one! O great life of grace obtained so that learned devotees rejoice. O Lord who sits in splendor on the great mountain of Thanigai where sacred rites flourish.
commentary: Human devotion is frequently fickle and selfish. In times of worldly comfort, people grow arrogant and forget God entirely. When hardship hits, they remember the divine just a little bit and complain about their suffering. The poet uses sharp sarcasm to call this selfish behavior excellent, knowing fully well how poor it is, while begging the Lord of Thanigai for a truer spiritual life.

tamil: என்றும் மாதர்மேல் இச்சைவைத் துன்றனை எண்ணுவேன் துயருற்றால்
கன்று நெஞ்சகக் கள்வனேன் அன்பினைக் கருத்திடை எணில்சால
நன்று நன்றெனக் கெவ்வணம் பொன்அருள் நல்குவை அறிகில்லேன்
துன்று மாதவர் போற்றிடும் தணிகைவாழ் சோதியே சுகவாழ்வே.
translit: eṉṟum mātarmēl iccaivait tuṉṟaṉai eṇṇuvēṉ tuyaruṟṟāl kaṉṟu neñcakak kaḷvaṉēṉ aṉpiṉaik karuttiṭai eṇilcāla naṉṟu naṉṟeṉak kevvaṇam poṉaruḷ nalkuvai aṟikillēṉ tuṉṟu mātavar pōṟṟiṭum taṇikaivāḻ cōtiyē cukavāḻvē.
translation: Forever placing my desire on women, I think of you only when I am stricken with sorrow. I am a thief with a troubled heart. If you weigh my love in your mind, it is truly great! I do not know how you will ever grant me your golden grace. O Jothi who abides in Thanigai, praised by gathered great sages. O life of bliss.
commentary: Chasing physical desires, a person usually remembers God only when disaster strikes. The poet calls himself a thief for offering such shallow, conditional love. Knowing his own flaws, he wonders how the divine light (Jothi) residing in Thanigai could ever grant him its golden grace.

sections.title: Praying for the Blessing of Service

tamil: நண்ணேனோ மகிழ்வினொடும் திருத்தணிகை மலைஅதனை நண்ணி என்றன்
கண்ணேநீ அமர்ந்தஎழில் கண்குளிரக் காணேனோ கண்டு வாரி
உண்ணேனோ ஆனந்தக் கண்ணீர்கொண் டாடிஉனக் குகப்பாத் தொண்டு
பண்ணேனோ நின்புகழைப் பாடேனோ வாயாரப் பாவி யேனே.
translit: naṇṇēṉō makiḻviṉoṭum tiruttaṇikai malai-ataṉai naṇṇi eṉṟaṉ kaṇṇēnī amarnta-eḻil kaṇkuḷirak kāṇēṉō kaṇṭu vāri uṇṇēṉō āṉantak kaṇṇīrkoṇ ṭāṭi-uṉak kukappāt toṇṭu paṇṇēṉō niṉpukaḻaip pāṭēṉō vāyārap pāvi yēṉē.
translation: Will I not reach the mountain of Thanigai with joy? Reaching it, O my Eye, will I not see your seated beauty, cooling my eyes? Seeing it, will I not scoop and drink it in? Will I not dance with tears of bliss and perform service that delights you? Will I not sing your praises with all my voice, I, a poor sinner?
commentary: The physical climb to the sacred hill is only the beginning of a total spiritual surrender. Seeing the divine presence is described as something so deeply felt that a person can scoop it up and drink it in like water, leading naturally to joyful service.

tamil: பாவியேன் படுந்துயருக் கிரங்கிஅருள் தணிகையில்என் பால்வா என்று
கூவிநீ ஆட்கொளஓர் கனவேனும் காணேனோ குணப்பொற் குன்றே
ஆவியே அறிவேஎன் அன்பேஎன் அரசேநின் அடியைச் சற்றும்
சேவியேன் எனினும்எனைக் கைவிடேல் அன்பர்பழி செப்பு வாரே.
translit: pāviyēṉ paṭuntuyaruk kiraṅki-aruḷ taṇikaiyileṉ pālvā eṉṟu kūvinī āṭkoḷa-ōr kaṉavēṉum kāṇēṉō kuṇappoṟ kuṉṟē āviyē aṟivē-eṉ aṉpē-eṉ aracēniṉ aṭiyaic caṟṟum cēviyēṉ eṉiṉumeṉaik kaiviṭēl aṉparpaḻi ceppu vārē.
translation: Taking pity on the suffering of this sinner, will I not see even a single dream where you call out, "Come to me in Thanigai of grace," and claim me? O golden hill of virtue! My life, my wisdom, my love, my King! Even if I have not served your feet in the slightest, do not abandon me. Your devotees will blame you if you do.
commentary: The yearning for a sign is so intense that even a single dream of invitation would bring comfort. The final plea is a traditional feature of deep devotion, where the speaker gently reminds the divine that ignoring a helpless soul will ruin God's own reputation for boundless mercy.

tamil: வாரேனோ திருத்தணிகை வழிநோக்கி வந்தென்கண் மணியே நின்று
பாரேனோ நின்அழகைப் பார்த்துலக வாழ்க்கைதனில் படும்இச் சோபம்
தீரேனோ நின்அடியைச் சேவித்தா னந்தவெள்ளம் திளைத்தா டேனோ
சாரேனோ நின்அடியர் சமுகம்அதைச் சார்ந்தவர்தாள் தலைக்கொள் ளேனோ.
translit: vārēṉō tiruttaṇikai vaḻinōkki vanteṉkaṇ maṇiyē niṉṟu pārēṉō niṉaḻakaip pārttulaka vāḻkkaitaṉil paṭumic cōpam tīrēṉō niṉaṭiyaic cēvittā ṉantaveḷḷam tiḷaittā ṭēṉō cārēṉō niṉaṭiyar camukamataic cārntavartāḷ talaikkoḷ ḷēṉō.
translation: Will I not come, seeking the path to Thanigai? Reaching there, O apple of my eye, will I not stand and gaze at your beauty? Gazing at it, will I not cure the exhaustion I suffer in this worldly life? Serving your feet, will I not revel and bathe in the flood of bliss? Will I not join the gathering of your devotees? Joining them, will I not bear their feet upon my head?
commentary: True rest from the exhaustion of worldly life comes from immersing oneself entirely in divine beauty. The highest honor envisioned here is not just reaching God, but humbly placing the feet of God's devotees upon one's own head in an act of total surrender.

tamil: கொள்ளேனோ நீஅமர்ந்த தணிகைமலைக் குறஎண்ணம் கோவே வந்தே
அள்ளேனோ நின்அருளை அள்ளிஉண்டே ஆனந்தத் தழுந்தி ஆடித்
துள்ளேனோ நின்தாளைத் துதியேனோ துதித்துலகத் தொடர்பை எல்லாம்
தள்ளேனோ நின்அடிக்கீழ்ச் சாரேனோ துணைஇல்லாத் தனிய னேனே.
translit: koḷḷēṉō nī-amarnta taṇikaimalaik kuṟa-eṇṇam kōvē vantē aḷḷēṉō niṉaruḷai aḷḷi-uṇṭē āṉantat taḻunti āṭit tuḷḷēṉō niṉtāḷait tutiyēṉō tutittulakat toṭarpai ellām taḷḷēṉō niṉaṭikkīḻc cārēṉō tuṇai-illāt taṉiya ṉēṉē.
translation: Will I not hold the thought of Thanigai mountain where you sit, O King? Coming there, will I not scoop up your grace? Scooping and drinking it in, will I not immerse in bliss, dancing and leaping? Will I not praise your feet? Praising them, will I not cast off all worldly ties? Will I not take refuge beneath your feet, I who am solitary and without support?
commentary: Grace is described as a living reality that can be consumed to fill the soul with physical joy. It is this direct experience of bliss that naturally causes all ordinary worldly attachments to fall away.

tamil: தனியேஇங் குழல்கின்ற பாவியேன் திருத்தணிகா சலம்வாழ் ஞானக்
கனியேநின் சேவடியைக் கண்ஆரக் கண்டுமனம் களிப்பு றேனோ
துனியேசெய் வாழ்வில்அலைந் தென்எண்ணம் முடியாது சுழல்வேன் ஆகில்
இனிஏது செய்வேன்மற் றொருதுணையும் காணேன்இவ் வேழை யேனே.
translit: taṉiyē-iṅ kuḻalkiṉṟa pāviyēṉ tiruttaṇikā calamvāḻ ñāṉak kaṉiyēniṉ cēvaṭiyaik kaṇārak kaṇṭumaṉam kaḷippu ṟēṉō tuṉiyēcey vāḻvilalain teṉeṇṇam muṭiyātu cuḻalvēṉ ākil iṉi-ētu ceyvēṉmaṟ ṟorutuṇaiyum kāṇēṉiv vēḻai yēṉē.
translation: I am a sinner wandering here alone. O fruit of wisdom residing on Mount Thanigai! Will I not see your perfect feet to the fullness of my eyes and let my heart rejoice? Wandering in this sorrowful life, if I spin endlessly without fulfilling my intent, what will I do hereafter? I see no other support, poor wretch that I am.
commentary: The feeling of wandering completely alone in the world brings a desperate need for a true anchor. Without the direct experience of divine wisdom, life feels like an endless and pointless spinning with no other shelter to lean on.

tamil: இவ்வேளை அருள்தணிகை அமர்ந்தருளும் தேவைஎன திருகண் ஆய
எவ்வேளை யும்பரவி ஏத்தேனோ அவன்பணிகள் இயற்றி டேனோ
தெவ்வேளை அடர்க்கவகை தெரியாமல் உழல்தருமிச் சிறிய னேனே.
translit: ivvēḷai aruḷtaṇikai amarntaruḷum tēvai-eṉa tirukaṇ āya cevvēḷai maṉaṅkaḷippac ceṉṟupukaḻn tāṉantat teḷitēṉuṇṭē evvēḷai yumparavi ēttēṉō avaṉpaṇikaḷ iyaṟṟi ṭēṉō tevvēḷai aṭarkkavakai teriyāmal uḻaltarumic ciṟiya ṉēṉē.
translation: I am a lowly person wandering in confusion, not knowing how to overcome hostile forces. Will I go right now with a joyful heart to praise the red-hued Lord who is my very vision, the God who graciously resides in holy Thanigai? Will I drink the clear honey of bliss? Will I worship and praise him at all times? Will I perform his sacred service?
commentary: The struggle against life's hostile forces leaves the mind wandering and confused. Relief comes from turning directly toward the divine. The poet longs to visit Thanigai, a sacred hill shrine dedicated to Murugan, the red-hued Lord. Serving God there transforms daily confusion into the clear honey of bliss.

tamil: சிறியேன்இப் போதேகித் திருத்தணிகை மலைஅமர்ந்த தேவின் பாதம்
குறியேனோ ஆனந்தக் கூத்தாடி அன்பர்கள்தம் குழாத்துள் சென்றே
முறியேனோ உடல்புளகம் மூடேனோ நன்னெறியை முன்னி இன்றே.
translit: ciṟiyēṉip pōtēkit tiruttaṇikai malai-amarnta tēviṉ pātam kuṟiyēṉō āṉantak kūttāṭi aṉparkaḷtam kuḻāttuḷ ceṉṟē aṟiyēṉō poruḷnilaiyai aṟinteṉateṉpataiviṭuttivvakilamāyai muṟiyēṉō uṭalpuḷakam mūṭēṉō naṉṉeṟiyai muṉṉi iṉṟē.
translation: Will I, a lowly person, go right now to focus on the feet of the God seated on holy Mount Thanigai? Will I join the gathering of devotees, dance in bliss, and realize the ultimate truth? Realizing it, will I let go of the sense of 'mine' and shatter this worldly illusion? Setting forth on the good path today, will my body thrill with joy?
commentary: Spiritual awakening requires letting go of the ego and the possessive sense of 'mine'. Dancing in joy with a community of devotees helps shatter the illusion of worldly life. Once the mind is freed from this illusion, the physical body itself thrills with the joy of walking the good path.

tamil: முன்னேனோ திருத்தணிகை அடைந்திடநின் சந்நிதியின் முன்னே நின்று
மன்னேனோ அடியருடன் வாழேனோ நின்அடியை வாழ்த்தி டேனோ
உன்னேனோ நன்னிலையை உலகத்தோர் எல்லீரும் உங்கே வாரும்
என்னேனோ நின்பெயரை யார்கூறி னாலும்அவர்க் கிதங்கூ றேனோ.
translit: muṉṉēṉō tiruttaṇikai aṭaintiṭaniṉ cannitiyiṉ muṉṉē niṉṟu maṉṉēṉō aṭiyaruṭaṉ vāḻēṉō niṉaṭiyai vāḻtti ṭēṉō uṉṉēṉō naṉṉilaiyai ulakattōr ellīrum uṅkē vārum eṉṉēṉō niṉpeyarai yārkūṟi ṉālumavark kitaṅkū ṟēṉō.
translation: Will I step forward to reach holy Thanigai? Will I stand firm in your presence? Will I live among your devotees? Will I praise your feet? Will I contemplate the supreme state? Will I call out, "O people of the world, all of you come here"? Will I speak sweet words to anyone who speaks your name?
commentary: The joy of standing in the divine presence naturally overflows into a desire to share it with everyone. The devotee actively calls out to the whole world to come and experience this supreme state together. True devotion creates a deep bond of affection, inspiring sweet words for anyone else who speaks the Lord's name.

tamil: கூறேனோ திருத்தணிகைக் குற்றுன்அடிப் புகழதனைக் கூறி நெஞ்சம்
தேறேனோ நின்அடியர் திருச்சமுகம் சேரேனோ தீராத் துன்பம்
ஆறேனோ நின்அடியன் ஆகேனோ பவக்கடல்விட் டகன்றே அப்பால்
ஏறேனோ அருட்கடலில் இழியேனோ ஒழியாத இன்பம் ஆர்ந்தே.
translit: kūṟēṉō tiruttaṇikaik kuṟṟuṉaṭip pukaḻataṉaik kūṟi neñcam tēṟēṉō niṉaṭiyar tiruccamukam cērēṉō tīrāt tuṉpam āṟēṉō niṉaṭiyaṉ ākēṉō pavakkaṭalviṭ ṭakaṉṟē appāl ēṟēṉō aruṭkaṭalil iḻiyēṉō oḻiyāta iṉpam ārntē.
translation: Reaching holy Thanigai, will I proclaim the glory of your feet and will my heart grow clear? Will I join the sacred gathering of your devotees? Will my endless sorrow heal? Will I become your servant? Leaving the ocean of worldly birth behind, will I ascend beyond? Will I plunge into the ocean of grace and be filled with unending bliss?
commentary: Worldly life is an ocean of endless sorrow. Proclaiming God's glory clears the confused heart and heals this deep pain. By leaving the heavy ocean of worldly existence behind, the soul is free to plunge into a very different expanse: the vast ocean of divine grace and unending bliss.

tamil: தேடேனோ என்நாதன் எங்குற்றான் எனஓடித் தேடிச் சென்றே
நாடேனோ தணிகைதனில் நாயகனே நின்அழகை நாடி நாடிக்
கூடேனோ அடியருடன் கோவேஎம் குகனேஎம் குருவே என்று
பாடேனோ ஆனந்தப் பரவசம்உற் றுன்கமலப் பதம்நண் ணேனோ.
translit: tēṭēṉō eṉnātaṉ eṅkuṟṟāṉ eṉa-ōṭit tēṭic ceṉṟē nāṭēṉō taṇikaitaṉil nāyakaṉē niṉaḻakai nāṭi nāṭik kūṭēṉō aṭiyaruṭaṉ kōvē-em kukaṉē-em kuruvē eṉṟu pāṭēṉō āṉantap paravacamuṟ ṟuṉkamalap patamnaṇ ṇēṉō.
translation: Will I search, crying, "Where is my Lord?" Running and searching, will I seek him? O Lord of Thanigai, seeking your beauty again and again, will I join your devotees? Will I sing, "O King! Our Guha! Our Guru!"? Attaining blissful ecstasy, will I reach your lotus feet?
commentary: Finding the divine requires an active, passionate search. The seeker runs and cries out for the Lord, longing to see his beauty and sing his praises as King, Guha (the deity who dwells in the heart's cave), and Guru (the spiritual teacher). This intense longing eventually culminates in ecstatic union at the Lord's feet.

tamil: வாவா என்ன அருள்தணிகை மருந்தை என்கண் மாமணியைப்
பூவாய் நறவை மறந்தவநாள் போக்கின் றதுவும் போதாமல்
மூவா முதலின் அருட்கேலா மூட நினைவும் இன்றெண்ணி
ஆவா நெஞ்சே எனைக்கெடுத்தாய் அந்தோ நீதான் ஆவாயோ.
translit: vāvā eṉṉa aruḷtaṇikai maruntai eṉkaṇ māmaṇiyaip pūvāy naṟavai maṟantavanāḷ pōkkiṉ ṟatuvum pōtāmal mūvā mutaliṉ aruṭkēlā mūṭa niṉaivum iṉṟeṇṇi āvā neñcē eṉaikkeṭuttāy antō nītāṉ āvāyō.
translation: You forgot the healing medicine of Thanigai that calls out "Come, come" to bestow grace, the great gem of my eyes, the flower's fresh honey. As if wasting my days in vain by forgetting Him were not enough, today you also harbor foolish thoughts unfit for the grace of the ageless Primal Lord. Alas, O heart, you have ruined me! Oh, will you ever survive?
commentary: The speaker speaks directly to his own mind, frustrated that it ignores the welcoming grace of the divine. Instead of focusing on God, the mind clings to foolish, worldly distractions and ruins his spiritual progress.

tamil: வாயாத் துரிசற் றிடும்புலவோர் வழுத்தும் தணிகை மலைஅமுதைக்
காயாக் கனியை மறந்தவநாள் கழிக்கின் றதுவும் போதாமல்
ஈயாக் கொடியர் தமக்கின்றி ஏலா நினைவும் இன்றெண்ணி
