மாயா என்றன் வாழ்வழித்தாய் மனமே நீதான் வாழ்வாயோ.
translit: vāyāt turicaṟ ṟiṭumpulavōr vaḻuttum taṇikai malai-amutaik kāyāk kaṉiyai maṟantavanāḷ kaḻikkiṉ ṟatuvum pōtāmal īyāk koṭiyar tamakkiṉṟi ēlā niṉaivum iṉṟeṇṇi māyā eṉṟaṉ vāḻvaḻittāy maṉamē nītāṉ vāḻvāyō.
translation: You forgot the nectar of Thanigai mountain praised by faultless poets whose words never fail. You forgot the fruit that was never unripe. As if wasting my days in vain by forgetting Him were not enough, today you also harbor unfit thoughts of approaching cruel misers who give nothing. You destroyed my life without perishing yourself. O mind, will you ever truly live?
commentary: It is easier for the mind to seek favors from cruel, selfish people than to rest in divine grace. The speaker asks how his mind expects to survive when it wastes its energy chasing worldly patrons who give nothing.

tamil: வாழும் படிநல் அருள்புரியும் மருவுந் தணிகை மலைத்தேனைச்
சூழும் கலப மயில்அரசைத் துதியாப் பவமும் போதாமல்
வீழும் கொடியர் தமக்கன்றி மேவா நினைவும் மேவிஇன்று
தாழும் படிஎன் தனைஅலைத்தாய் சவலை மனம்நீ சாகாயோ.
translit: vāḻum paṭinal aruḷpuriyum maruvun taṇikai malaittēṉaic cūḻum kalapa mayilaracait tutiyāp pavamum pōtāmal vīḻum koṭiyar tamakkaṉṟi mēvā niṉaivum mēvi-iṉṟu tāḻum paṭi-eṉ taṉai-alaittāy cavalai maṉamnī cākāyō.
translation: You fail to praise the honey of beautiful Thanigai mountain who bestows good grace so we may live well. You fail to praise the king who rides the majestic peacock with spreading plumage. As if this sin were not enough, today you harbor improper thoughts of seeking out cruel, fallen misers. You made me wander and sink low. O feeble mind, will you not die?
commentary: Forgetting to praise God is framed here as a spiritual failure. Adding to this failure, the mind degrades itself further by longing for the approval of wealthy but morally empty people.

tamil: காயோம் எனநின் றவர்க்கினிய கனியாம் தணிகைக் கற்பகத்தைப்
போய்ஓர் கணமும் போற்றுகிலாய் புன்மை புரிந்தாய் புலங்கெட்டாய்
பேயோ எங்கும் திரிந்தோடிப் பேணா என்பைப் பேணுகின்ற
நாயோ மனமே நீஉனைநான் நம்பி வாளா நலிந்தேனே.
translit: kāyōm eṉaniṉ ṟavarkkiṉiya kaṉiyām taṇikaik kaṟpakattaip pōyōr kaṇamum pōṟṟukilāy puṉmai purintāy pulaṅkeṭṭāy pēyō eṅkum tirintōṭip pēṇā eṉpaip pēṇukiṉṟa nāyō maṉamē nī-uṉaināṉ nampi vāḷā nalintēṉē.
translation: You do not go and praise even for a moment the wish-fulfilling tree of Thanigai, the sweet fruit for those who stand firmly without anger. You committed base deeds. You lost your senses. Are you a ghost running around everywhere? Are you a dog chewing on a useless bone? O mind, I trusted you and I have withered in vain.
commentary: The restless mind is compared to a ghost wandering aimlessly or a dog chewing on a useless bone. Trusting this undisciplined mind has left the devotee spiritually withered.

tamil: தேனும் கடமும் திகழ்தணிகைத் தேவை நினையாய் தீநரகம்
மானும் நடையில் உழல்கின்றாய் மனமே உன்றன் வஞ்சகத்தால்
நானும் இழந்தேன் பெருவாழ்வை நாய்போல் அலைந்திங் கவமேநீ
தானும் இழந்தாய் என்னேஉன் தன்மை இழிவாம் தன்மையதே.
translit: tēṉum kaṭamum tikaḻtaṇikait tēvai niṉaiyāy tīnarakam māṉum naṭaiyil uḻalkiṉṟāy maṉamē uṉṟaṉ vañcakattāl nāṉum iḻantēṉ peruvāḻvai nāypōl alaintiṅ kavamēnī tāṉum iḻantāy eṉṉē-uṉ taṉmai iḻivām taṉmaiyatē.
translation: You do not think of the Lord of Thanigai where honey and forests shine. You wander in paths resembling a cruel hell. O mind, because of your deceit I have lost the great life. You wandered uselessly like a dog and lost yourself as well. What is this? Your nature is truly a degraded one.
commentary: The mind's deceitful nature creates a hellish reality, dragging the soul away from a life of deep grace. By wandering after false desires, the mind destroys both itself and the person who trusts it.

tamil: தன்னால் உலகை நடத்தும்அருட் சாமி தணிகை சாராமல்
பொன்னால் மண்ணால் பூவையரால் புலம்பி வருந்தும் புல்நெஞ்சே
உன்னால் என்றன் உயர்விழந்தேன் உற்றார் இழந்தேன் உன்செயலைச்
சொன்னால் நகைப்பர் எனைவிட்டும் தொலையாய் இங்கு நிலையாயே.
translit: taṉṉāl ulakai naṭattumaruṭ cāmi taṇikai cārāmal poṉṉāl maṇṇāl pūvaiyarāl pulampi varuntum pulneñcē uṉṉāl eṉṟaṉ uyarviḻantēṉ uṟṟār iḻantēṉ uṉceyalaic coṉṉāl nakaippar eṉaiviṭṭum tolaiyāy iṅku nilaiyāyē.
translation: Oh petty heart, you do not approach Thanigai of the gracious Lord who directs the world by Himself. Instead, you lament and suffer for gold, land, and women. Because of you, I lost my high state and lost my kin. If I speak of your deeds, others will laugh. You do not leave me and perish, but remain fixed right here.
commentary: The mind constantly chases wealth, property, and physical pleasure instead of turning to the divine presence that sustains the world. This obsession with worldly things brings spiritual ruin and public shame, yet the stubborn heart refuses to let go of its attachments.

tamil: நிலைக்கும் தணிகை என்அரசை நீயும் நினையாய் நினைப்பதையும்
கலைக்கும் தொழில்கொண் டெனைக்கலக்கம் கண்டாய் பலன்என் கண்டாயே
முலைக்கும் கலைக்கும் விழைந்தவமே முயங்கும் மூட முழுநெஞ்சே
அலைக்கும் கொடிய விடம்நீஎன் றறிந்தேன் முன்னர் அறிந்திலனே.
translit: nilaikkum taṇikai eṉaracai nīyum niṉaiyāy niṉaippataiyum kalaikkum toḻilkoṇ ṭeṉaikkalakkam kaṇṭāy palaṉeṉ kaṇṭāyē mulaikkum kalaikkum viḻaintavamē muyaṅkum mūṭa muḻuneñcē alaikkum koṭiya viṭamnī-eṉ ṟaṟintēṉ muṉṉar aṟintilaṉē.
translation: You do not think of my King in enduring Thanigai. You make it your work to scatter my thoughts of Him, and you watch my confusion. What benefit did you find in this? Oh completely foolish heart, you uselessly desire and embrace breasts and garments. I know now you are a tormenting cruel poison. I did not know this before.
commentary: The wandering mind actively interrupts thoughts of God and scatters a person's spiritual focus. Recognizing this inner sabotage is a painful realization, revealing the mind's obsession with physical intimacy to be a destructive poison rather than a source of joy.

tamil: இலதை நினைப்பாய் பித்தர்கள்போல் ஏங்கா நிற்பாய் தணிகையில்என்
குலதெய் வமுமாய்க் கோவாய்சற் குருவாய் நின்ற குகன்அருளே
நலதென் றறியாய் யான்செய்த நன்றி மறந்தாய் நாணாதென்
வலதை அழித்தாய் வலதொடுநீ வாழ்வாய் கொல்லோ வல்நெஞ்சே.
translit: ilatai niṉaippāy pittarkaḷpōl ēṅkā niṟpāy taṇikaiyileṉ kulatey vamumāyk kōvāycaṟ kuruvāy niṉṟa kukaṉaruḷē nalateṉ ṟaṟiyāy yāṉceyta naṉṟi maṟantāy nāṇāteṉ valatai aḻittāy valatoṭunī vāḻvāy kollō valneñcē.
translation: You think of unreal things. You stand yearning like a madman. You do not understand the goodness of the grace of Guhan, who stands in Thanigai as my family deity, my King, and my true Guru. You forgot the favors I did for you. Without shame, you destroyed my strength. Oh hard heart, will you continue to live in strength?
commentary: The mind wastes its energy yearning for illusions instead of seeking the grace of Guhan (a name for Lord Murugan, the divine presence worshipped at Thanigai). By constantly chasing unreal things, the ungrateful heart drains a person's spiritual strength and leaves them completely exhausted.

tamil: நெஞ்சே உகந்த துணைஎனக்கு நீஎன் றறிந்தே நேசித்தேன்
மஞ்சேர் தணிகை மலைஅமுதை வாரிக் கொளும்போ தென்னுள்ளே
நஞ்சே கலந்தாய் உன்உறவு நன்றே இனிஉன் நட்பகன்றால்
உய்ஞ்சேன் இலையேல் வன்னரகத் துள்ளேன் கொள்ளேன் ஒன்றையுமே.
translit: neñcē ukanta tuṇai-eṉakku nī-eṉ ṟaṟintē nēcittēṉ mañcēr taṇikai malai-amutai vārik koḷumpō teṉṉuḷḷē nañcē kalantāy uṉuṟavu naṉṟē iṉi-uṉ naṭpakaṉṟāl uyñcēṉ ilaiyēl vaṉṉarakat tuḷḷēṉ koḷḷēṉ oṉṟaiyumē.
translation: Oh heart, I loved you, thinking you were a fitting companion for me. As I scoop up the nectar of the cloud-capped Thanigai mountain, you mix poison inside me. Your kinship is truly wonderful! If I abandon your friendship now, I am saved. Otherwise, I fall into a fierce hell and I will gain absolutely nothing.
commentary: People usually trust their own thoughts and treat the mind as a reliable companion on the spiritual path. Yet at the exact moment a person begins to experience divine joy, the mind introduces toxic desires and ruins the experience. The only way to avoid absolute ruin is to break completely with these worldly mental habits.

tamil: கொள்ளும் பொழில்சூழ் தணிகைமலைக் கோவை நினையா தெனைநரகில்
தள்ளும் படிக்கோ தலைப்பட்டாய் சகத்தின் மடவார் தம்மயலாம்
கள்ளுண் டந்தோ வெறிகொண்டாய் கலைத்தாய் என்னைக் கடந்தோர்கள்
எள்ளும் படிவந் தலைக்கின்றாய் எனக்கென் றெங்கே இருந்தாயோ.
translit: koḷḷum poḻilcūḻ taṇikaimalaik kōvai niṉaiyā teṉainarakil taḷḷum paṭikkō talaippaṭṭāy cakattiṉ maṭavār tammayalām kaḷḷuṇ ṭantō veṟikoṇṭāy kalaittāy eṉṉaik kaṭantōrkaḷ eḷḷum paṭivan talaikkiṉṟāy eṉakkeṉ ṟeṅkē iruntāyō.
translation: Without thinking of the King of Thanigai mountain surrounded by captivating groves, did you set out just to push me into hell? Alas, you drank the liquor of infatuation for the women of this world and went mad. You scattered my being. You come and torment me so that passing strangers mock me. Where were you waiting just to afflict me?
commentary: Lust acts like an intoxicating liquor that shatters a person's focus and dignity. Drunk on physical infatuation, the mind acts like a hidden enemy waiting in ambush to drag the seeker away from God and into public humiliation.

tamil: இருந்தாய் இங்கு கண்டவிடத் தேகா நின்றாய் அவ்விடத்தும்
பொருந்தாய் மீண்டும் புகுவாய்பின் போவாய் வருவாய் புகழ்த்தணிகை
மருந்தாய் நின்ற குகன்அடியை வழுத்தாய் எனையும் வலிக்கின்றாய்
திருந்தாய் நெஞ்சே நின்செயலைச் செப்ப எனக்குத் திடுக்கிடுமே.
translit: iruntāy iṅku kaṇṭaviṭat tēkā niṉṟāy avviṭattum poruntāy mīṇṭum pukuvāypiṉ pōvāy varuvāy pukaḻttaṇikai maruntāy niṉṟa kukaṉaṭiyai vaḻuttāy eṉaiyum valikkiṉṟāy tiruntāy neñcē niṉceyalaic ceppa eṉakkut tiṭukkiṭumē.
translation: O heart, you stay here. You wander wherever you look and stand there. You find no peace there either. You enter again, then leave, and return. You do not praise the feet of Guhan, who stands as the healing medicine in renowned Thanigai. You drag me along with you. You refuse to mend your ways. Speaking of your actions makes me shudder.
commentary: The restless human mind constantly wanders from place to place and refuses to find peace. Instead of focusing on God, it drags the speaker along in its endless cycle of desires. The speaker urges the mind to worship Guhan (Lord Murugan), who waits at the sacred hill of Thanigai (Thanigai) as a healing medicine for this spiritual sickness. The sheer chaotic energy of the unguided heart makes the speaker shudder.

translit: mañcaṭ pūcciṉ miṉukkili ḷaiñarkaḷ mayaṅka vēceyum vāḷviḻi mātarpāl keñcik koñci niṟai-aḻin tuṉaruṭ kiccai nīttuk kiṭantaṉaṉ āyiṉēṉ mañcuṟ ṟōṅkum poḻiltaṇi kācala vaḷḷal eṉviṉai māṟṟutal nītiyē tañcat tālvan taṭaintiṭum aṉparkaḷ tammaik kākkum taṉi-aruṭ kuṉṟamē.
translation: I begged and dallied with sword-eyed women who make young men swoon with the glow of their turmeric paste. Losing my dignity, I lay ruined, abandoning all desire for Your grace. O mountain of peerless Grace who protects the devotees who come seeking refuge! O benevolent Lord of Thanigachalam with cloud-touching groves! It is only just that You dissolve my karma.
commentary: The pursuit of fleeting physical pleasure drains a person of both dignity and the desire for spiritual growth. Seduced by outward beauty, the mind forgets the lasting joy of grace. Vallalar cries out to the Lord of Thanigachalam (the sacred hill of Thanigai), pleading for release from the burden of past actions (karma) that keep the soul trapped in these worldly habits.

translit: mulaiyaik kāṭṭi mayakki-eṉ āruyir muṟṟum vāṅkuṟum muṇṭaikaḷ naṉmati kulaiyak kāṭṭum kalavikki caintuniṉ kōlaṅ kāṇak kuṟippilaṉ āyiṉēṉ nilaiyaik kāṭṭumnal āṉanta veḷḷamē nēca neñcakam niṉṟoḷir tīpamē kalaiyaik kāṭṭum matitavaḻ naṟṟaṇi kāca lattamarn tōṅkati kāraṉē.
translation: Base women bewitched me by baring their breasts, draining away my precious life entirely. Yielding to the sexual union they displayed to shatter my good sense, I lost all intention to see Your divine form. O flood of good bliss that reveals the true state! O lamp shining within the loving heart! O supreme Lord seated in good Thanigachalam where the phase-revealing moon glides!
commentary: Physical lust shatters a person's good sense and drains their vital energy. By yielding to raw sexual desire, the mind loses all intention to seek a higher divine reality. In contrast to these exhausting worldly passions, the divine presence is described as a flood of true bliss and a steady, guiding lamp within a loving heart.

translit: vañca mēkuṭi koṇṭu viḷaṅkiya maṅkai yarkku mayaluḻan tē-avar nañcam mēvu nayaṉattil cikkiya nāyi ṉēṉuṉai nāṭuva teṉṟukāṇ kañcam mēvum ayaṉpukaḻ cōtiyē kaṭappa māmalark kantacu kantaṉē tañca mē-eṉa vantavar tammai-āḷ taṇikai māmalaic caṟkuru nātaṉē.
translation: I suffered infatuation for women in whom deceit has taken residence. Caught in their poison-filled eyes, I am a dog. When will I ever seek You? O Jothi praised by Brahma seated on the lotus! O fragrant one wearing great kadamba flowers! O true Guru Lord of the great Thanigai mountain, who rules over those who come seeking refuge!
commentary: The poet describes the painful trap of infatuation, comparing seductive eyes to a blinding poison. Caught in this deceitful snare, the soul feels reduced to the state of a wandering street dog, completely disconnected from its spiritual purpose. He calls out to Murugan, the fragrant lord adorned with kadamba flowers, wondering if he will ever find the clarity to seek true refuge.

translit: pāvam ōruru vākiya pāvaiyar paṉṉu kaṇvalaip paṭṭuma yaṅkiyē kōvai vāyitaḻk kiccaiya tākiniṉ kuraika ḻaṟkaṉpu koṇṭilaṉ āyiṉēṉ mēvu vārviṉai nīkki-a ḷittiṭum vēla ṉētaṇi kācala mēlaṉē tēvar tēṭarum cīraruṭ celvaṉē teyva yāṉai tirumaṇa vāḷaṉē.
translation: I was caught and infatuated in the net of the eyes of women who are sin personified. Desiring their red kovai-fruit lips, I failed to cultivate love for Your resounding ankleted feet. O Velan who removes the karma of those who approach You and bestows grace! O Supreme Lord of Thanigachalam! O wealth of excellent grace difficult for the gods to seek! O husband of Deivanai!
commentary: Worldly attraction acts like a net, catching the senses and confusing the mind. Obsessed with physical features like red lips, the soul completely forgets to cultivate love for God. Vallalar addresses the divine as Velan (the spear-wielding deity Murugan), begging this supreme Lord to remove the accumulated consequences of these poor choices.

translit: karattaik kāṭṭiyē kaṇkaḷai nīṭṭiyē kaṭaiya ṉēṉuyir vāṭṭiya kaṉṉiyar urattaik kāṭṭi mayakkama yaṅkiṉēṉ uṉṟaṉ pāta upayattaip pōṟṟilēṉ purattaik kāṭṭu nakaiyiṉe rittatōr puṇṇi yaṟkup pukalkuru nātaṉē varattaik kāṭṭum malaittaṇi kēcaṉē vañca ṉēṟkaruḷ vāḻvuki ṭaikkumō.
translation: Displaying hand gestures and casting long glances, young women withered the life of this lowest wretch. I swooned as they bewitched me by revealing their chests. I did not praise Your pair of feet. O Guru Lord who taught the holy One who burned the three cities with a bright smile! O Lord of Thanigai mountain who reveals boons! Will a deceitful one like me ever attain the life of grace?
commentary: Flirtatious gestures and physical displays easily bewitch the unfocused mind, causing a person to waste their precious life. Caught up in this bodily illusion, the soul fails to praise the divine feet. Here Murugan is praised as the great teacher who imparted wisdom even to Siva, the deity who burned the legendary three flying cities. The verse ends with a desperate question: can someone so deeply trapped in worldly deceit ever hope to experience a life of grace?

translit: kācam mēkam kaṭumpiṇi cūlaimō kāti yāltantu kaṇkalak kamceyum mōca mēnicam eṉṟupeṇ pēykaḷai muṉṉi ṉēṉniṉai muṉṉilaṉ āyiṉēṉ pācam nīkkiṭum aṉparkaḷ pōleṉaip pātu kākkum paramuṉak kaiyaṉē tēcam yāvum pukaḻtaṇi kācalac celva mē-aruṭ ciṟcuka vāriyē.
translation: I pursued demon-like women who bring tuberculosis, asthma, severe diseases, and colic through lust, dimming the eyes. Believing this deception to be the truth, I focused on them and failed to focus on You. O Lord, the burden of protecting me, like the devotees who remove worldly attachments, rests on You. O wealth of Thanigai hill praised by all lands! O ocean of the bliss of divine grace!
commentary: Obsession with physical pleasure brings both bodily disease and spiritual blindness. The poet confesses to mistaking the illusion of lust for ultimate truth, entirely forgetting the divine. He now turns to the Lord of Thanigai, asking for the protective grace that helps true devotees break free from worldly attachments.

translit: aiyam ēṟṟut tiripavar āyiṉum ācai āmporuḷ īntiṭa vallarēl kuyyam kāṭṭumma ṭantaiyar vāyppaṭṭuṉ kōla māmalarp pātamku ṟittilēṉ mai-u lāmpoḻil cūḻumta ṇikaivāḻ vaḷḷa lēvaḷḷi nāyaka ṉēpuvic caiya ṟumpara ñāṉikaḷ pōṟṟiṭum cāmi yē-eṉaik kāppatuṉ taṉmaiyē.
translation: Falling into the trap of women who reveal their secret parts to any wandering beggar capable of giving them the wealth they desire, I failed to meditate on Your beautiful great lotus feet. O benevolent Lord residing in Thanigai surrounded by dark groves! O Lord of Valli! O Deity praised by supreme sages who have cast off worldly doubts! Protecting me is Your true nature.
commentary: Sexual desire can reduce human connection to a transactional trap. By chasing fleeting physical relationships built on wealth, the speaker has neglected to meditate on God. He reminds himself that the divine nature is to protect even those who have strayed, a truth recognized by the highest sages who have shed all their worldly doubts.

translit: kaṇṇaik kāṭṭi irumulai kāṭṭimō kattaik kāṭṭi akattaikkoṇ ṭē-aḻi maṇṇaik kāṭṭiṭum māya vaṉitaimār mālaip pōkkiniṉ kālaip paṇivaṉō paṇṇaik kāṭṭi urukuma ṭiyartam pattik kāṭṭimut tipporuḷ īteṉa viṇṇaik kāṭṭum tiruttaṇi kācala vēla ṉē-umai yāḷaruḷ pālaṉē.
translation: Deceptive women display their eyes, display their two breasts, and display lust to capture the heart, ultimately leading one to the dirt of ruin. Will I ever cast off my infatuation with them and bow at Your feet? You reveal the devotion of melting devotees who sing musical hymns, and You reveal the supreme heaven, declaring it to be the true substance of liberation. O Velan of the holy Thanigai hill! O gracious son of Uma!
commentary: The physical allure of the human body is a temporary illusion that in the end ends in the dust of the grave. The poet wonders if he will ever break free from this infatuation to seek true liberation. He contrasts the destructive pull of lust with the deep devotion of true seekers, who sing with melting hearts and are shown the supreme path by God.

translit: paṭiyiṉ mākkaḷai vīḻttum paṭukuḻi pāvam yāvum paḻakuṟum pāḻṅkuḻi kuṭikoḷ nāṟṟak kuḻiciṟu nīrtarum koṭiya ūṟṟuk kuḻipuḻuk koḷkuḻi kaṭima lakkuḻi ākum karukkuḻik kaḷḷa mātaraik kaṇṭuma yaṅkiṉēṉ oṭivil cīrttaṇi kācala niṉpukaḻ ōti lēṉeṉak kuṇṭukol uṇmaiyē.
translation: I became infatuated with deceitful women who carry the womb, a deadly pit that fells the ignorant people of the earth. It is a ruined pit where all sins are practiced, a pit where foul stench resides, a cruel spring yielding urine, a pit harboring worms, and a foul-smelling pit of excrement. O Lord of the unendingly glorious Thanigai hill, I failed to chant Your praise. Is there any true redemption left for me?
commentary: To break the spell of physical obsession, the poet describes the human body in the harshest possible biological terms. In traditional ascetic poetry, focusing intensely on the foulness of flesh, fluids, and the womb is a mental exercise used to cultivate lasting dispassion. By stripping away the romantic illusion, he exposes how clinging to the physical body prevents the soul from praising God and finding redemption.

translit: kaccuk kaṭṭi maṇaṅkaṭṭik kāmukar kaṇṇaik kaṭṭi maṉaṅkaṭṭi vañcakam vaccuk kaṭṭiya vaṉkaḻaṟ kaṭṭiyum maṇṇiṉ kaṭṭiyum māṉummu laikkaṭṭik kiccaik kaṭṭi-i ṭumpai-e ṉumcumai ēṟak kaṭṭiya eṟkaruḷ vāykolō piccaik kaṭṭiya pittaṉ putalvaṉē perumai kaṭṭum peruntaṇi kēcaṉē.
translation: Women tie their bodices, apply fragrances, and bind the eyes and minds of lustful men, harboring deceit within. I attached my desire to their bound breasts, which resemble hard seeds and clods of earth, and loaded myself with the heavy burden of suffering. Will You ever grant Your grace to me? O son of the mad Lord who wanders for alms! O great Lord of Thanigai adorned with immense glory!
commentary: Artificial adornments like perfumes and tightly bound clothing create a psychological snare for the unwary mind. The poet views his past desires as a heavy, self-imposed burden of suffering based on nothing more than flesh and dirt. He pleads for mercy from the Lord of Thanigai, affectionately identifying him as the son of Siva, the supreme God who wanders like a mad beggar for alms.

sections.title: Longing to Bear the Sacred Feet

tamil: தேனார் அலங்கல் குழல்மடவார் திறத்தின் மயங்காத் திறல்அடைதற்
கானார் கொடிஎம் பெருமான்தன் அருட்கண் மணியே அற்புதமே
கானார் பொழில்சூழ் திருத்தணிகைக் கரும்பே கருணைப் பெருங்கடலே
வானார் அமுதே நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: tēṉār alaṅkal kuḻalmaṭavār tiṟattiṉ mayaṅkāt tiṟalaṭaitaṟ kāṉār koṭi-em perumāṉtaṉ aruṭkaṇ maṇiyē aṟputamē kāṉār poḻilcūḻ tiruttaṇikaik karumpē karuṇaip peruṅkaṭalē vāṉār amutē niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O pupil of the gracious eye of our Lord who bears the bull banner! O wonder! O sugarcane of holy Thanigai surrounded by fragrant groves! O vast ocean of compassion! O heavenly nectar! Grant me the strength to remain unbewildered by the wiles of women whose hair is adorned with honey-dripping garlands. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant.
commentary: The spiritual path requires a mind free from the distraction of physical lust. The poet prays to Lord Murugan, the deity of the Thanigai hill, asking for the clarity to see past these worldly illusions. Receiving the Lord's sacred feet on one's head is a traditional symbol of total surrender and the ultimate granting of divine grace.

tamil: தாழும் கொடிய மடவியர்தம் சழக்கால் உழலாத் தகைஅடைந்தே
ஆழும் பரமா னந்தவெள்ளத் தழுந்திக் களிக்கும் படிவாய்ப்ப
ஊழ்உந் தியசீர் அன்பர்மனத் தொளிரும் சுடரே உயர்தணிகை
வாழும் பொருளே நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: tāḻum koṭiya maṭaviyartam caḻakkāl uḻalāt takai-aṭaintē āḻum paramā ṉantaveḷḷat taḻuntik kaḷikkum paṭivāyppa ūḻun tiyacīr aṉparmaṉat toḷirum cuṭarē uyartaṇikai vāḻum poruḷē niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O flame shining in the minds of excellent devotees guided by ripe past deeds! O reality residing in high Thanigai! Grant me the state of never wandering in confusion through the falsehoods of base and cruel women. Give me the chance to immerse myself and rejoice in the deep flood of supreme bliss. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant.
commentary: Worldly desires create a cycle of confusion and falsehood that pulls the mind away from the truth. The poet asks to trade this shallow existence for a deep flood of supreme spiritual bliss. This bliss is only found when the mind is turned entirely toward the divine flame shining in the hearts of true devotees.

tamil: மின்னுண் மருங்குல் பேதையர்தம் வெளிற்று மயக்குள் மேவாமே
உன்னும் பரம யோகியர்தம் உடனே மருவி உனைப்புகழ்வான்
பின்னும் சடைஎம் பெருமாற்கோர் பேறே தணிகைப் பிறங்கலின்மேல்
மன்னும் சுடரே நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: miṉṉuṇ maruṅkul pētaiyartam veḷiṟṟu mayakkuḷ mēvāmē uṉṉum parama yōkiyartam uṭaṉē maruvi uṉaippukaḻvāṉ piṉṉum caṭai-em perumāṟkōr pēṟē taṇikaip piṟaṅkaliṉmēl maṉṉum cuṭarē niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O peerless treasure of our Lord with braided matted hair! O enduring flame upon the mountain peak of Thanigai! Keep me from entering the empty delusion of foolish women with waists like lightning. Let me join the company of supreme meditating yogis to sing your praises. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant.
commentary: Physical attraction is described here as an empty delusion that passes as quickly as a flash of lightning. Instead of chasing fleeting worldly attachments, the poet longs for the lasting company of meditating yogis. True spiritual progress is sustained by surrounding oneself with those whose minds are already fixed on God.

tamil: ஆறாத் துயரம் தருங்கொடியார்க் காளாய் உழன்றிங் கலையாதே
கூறாப் பெருமை நின்அடியார் கூட்டத் துடன்போய்க் குலாவும்வண்ணம்
தேறாப் பொருளாம் சிவத்தொழுகும் தேனே தணிகைத் திருமலைவாழ்
மாறாச் சுகமே நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: āṟāt tuyaram taruṅkoṭiyārk kāḷāy uḻaṉṟiṅ kalaiyātē kūṟāp perumai niṉaṭiyār kūṭṭat tuṭaṉpōyk kulāvumvaṇṇam tēṟāp poruḷām civattoḻukum tēṉē taṇikait tirumalaivāḻ māṟāc cukamē niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O honey flowing from Siva, the supreme reality beyond ordinary comprehension! O unchanging joy living on the holy mountain of Thanigai! Keep me from wandering here in distress as a slave to cruel women who cause unending sorrow. Let me go and mingle joyfully with the gathering of your devotees of indescribable greatness. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant.
commentary: Submitting to worldly lust leads directly to unending sorrow and a life spent wandering without purpose. The poet seeks refuge from this suffering by joining the gathering of devoted seekers. He describes the divine presence as a pure, unchanging joy that flows directly from the supreme reality.

tamil: விரதம் அழிக்கும் கொடியார்தம் விழியால் மெலியா துனைப்புகழும்
சரதர் அவையில் சென்றுநின்சீர் தனையே வழுத்தும் தகைஅடைவான்
பரதம் மயில்மேல் செயும்தணிகைப் பரனே வெள்ளிப் பருப்பதம்வாழ்
வரதன் மகனே நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: viratam aḻikkum koṭiyārtam viḻiyāl meliyā tuṉaippukaḻum caratar avaiyil ceṉṟuniṉcīr taṉaiyē vaḻuttum takai-aṭaivāṉ paratam mayilmēl ceyumtaṇikaip paraṉē veḷḷip paruppatamvāḻ varataṉ makaṉē niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O supreme Lord of Thanigai dancing upon your peacock! O son of the supreme benefactor residing on the silver mountain! Keep me from weakening before the glances of cruel women who destroy spiritual vows. Let me enter the assembly of the truthful and attain the state of praising only your glories. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant.
commentary: Worldly temptations have the power to weaken and destroy even carefully maintained spiritual vows. The poet asks the Lord, who is depicted traditionally as dancing on a peacock, for the strength to stand firm against these distractions. He desires only to sit among truthful seekers and spend his life praising the divine glories.

tamil: வெயில்மேல் கீடம் எனமடவார் வெய்ய மயற்கண் வீழாமே.
குயில்மேல் குலவும் திருத்தணிகைக் குணப்பொற் குன்றே கொள்கலப
மயில்மேல் மணியே நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: veyilmēl kīṭam eṉamaṭavār veyya mayaṟkaṇ vīḻāmē. ayilmēl karaṅkoḷ niṉaippukaḻum aṭiyārcavaiyiṉ aṭaiyumvakaik kuyilmēl kulavum tiruttaṇikaik kuṇappoṟ kuṉṟē koḷkalapa mayilmēl maṇiyē niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O golden mountain of virtue in Thanigai where cuckoos sing. O gem seated upon the magnificent peacock. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant so that I may join the assembly of devotees who praise you as the one wielding a spear. Let me reach them without falling into the cruel delusion of women, like a worm burning in the hot sun.
commentary: Vallalar asks for the touch of the divine feet as a refuge from the burning torments of worldly lust. He compares the pain of this delusion to a helpless worm scorching in the hot sun. He prays to Lord Murugan of Thanigai to place his sacred feet on his head, granting him the safety and fellowship of true devotees.

tamil: தனமும் கடந்தே நாரியர்மால் தனையும் கடந்தே தவம்அழிக்கும்
சினமும் கடந்தே நினைச்சேர்ந்தோர் தெய்வச் சபையில் சேர்ந்திடவே
வனமும் கடமும் திகழ்தணிகை மலையின் மருந்தே வாக்கினொடு
மனமும் கடந்தோய் நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: taṉamum kaṭantē nāriyarmāl taṉaiyum kaṭantē tavamaḻikkum ciṉamum kaṭantē niṉaiccērntōr teyvac capaiyil cērntiṭavē vaṉamum kaṭamum tikaḻtaṇikai malaiyiṉ maruntē vākkiṉoṭu maṉamum kaṭantōy niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O medicine of the Thanigai mountain shining with forests and groves. O Lord who transcends word and mind. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant so that I may join the divine assembly of those who have reached you by overcoming the desire for wealth, overcoming the lust for women, and overcoming the anger that destroys penance.
commentary: To join the assembly of the divine, a seeker must first conquer the desires for wealth and flesh, along with the anger that destroys spiritual progress. Vallalar describes the Lord as the ultimate medicine who cures these worldly attachments. He prays for the Lord's feet to crown his head, lifting him completely beyond the limits of ordinary speech and thought.

tamil: கல்லாக் கொடிய மடவார்தம் காமக் குழிக்கண் வீழாமே
நல்லார்க் கெல்லாம் நல்லவநின் நாமம் துதிக்கும் நலம்பெறவே
சொல்லாற் புனைந்த மாலையொடும் தொழுது தணிகை தனைத்துதிக்க
வல்லார்க் கருளும் நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: kallāk koṭiya maṭavārtam kāmak kuḻikkaṇ vīḻāmē nallārk kellām nallavaniṉ nāmam tutikkum nalampeṟavē collāṟ puṉainta mālaiyoṭum toḻutu taṇikai taṉaittutikka vallārk karuḷum niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O Lord who is completely good to all good people. You bestow grace upon those who can worship and praise Thanigai with garlands woven of words. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant, so that I may attain the blessing of praising your name without falling into the pit of lust for ignorant, cruel women.
commentary: Sincere praise is presented as a woven garland of words offered to the divine. Vallalar asks the Lord to bless him with the ability to sing these praises continuously. He seeks the physical touch of the Lord's feet to keep his mind focused on grace and safely away from the traps of worldly desires.

tamil: கள்ளக் கயற்கண் மடவார்தம் காமத் துழலா துனைநினைக்கும்
உள்ளத் தவர்பால் சேர்ந்துமகிழ்ந் துண்மை உணர்ந்தங் குற்றிடுவான்
அள்ளற் பழனத் திருத்தணிகை அரசே ஞான அமுதளீக்கும்
வள்ளற் பெருமான் நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பாயே.
translit: kaḷḷak kayaṟkaṇ maṭavārtam kāmat tuḻalā tuṉainiṉaikkum uḷḷat tavarpāl cērntumakiḻn tuṇmai uṇarntaṅ kuṟṟiṭuvāṉ aḷḷaṟ paḻaṉat tiruttaṇikai aracē ñāṉa amutaḷīkkum vaḷḷaṟ perumāṉ niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippāyē.
translation: O King of Thanigai surrounded by fertile fields. O great benefactor who grants the nectar of wisdom. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant. Let me join and rejoice with those whose hearts dwell on you, realizing the truth and abiding there, without wandering in lust for women with deceitful, fish-like eyes.
commentary: Divine wisdom is a sweet nectar granted directly by the Lord. Vallalar seeks the company of pure-hearted devotees who have already realized this ultimate truth. He asks the Lord to claim him by placing his sacred feet on his head, saving him from the deceitful distractions of physical desire.

tamil: பாகைப் பொருவும் மொழியுடையீர் என்று மடவார்ப் பழிச்சாமல்
ஓகைப் பெறும்நின் திருத்தொண்டர் உடன்சேர்ந் துண்மை யுணர்ந்திடுவான்
தோகைப் பரிமேல் வருந்தெய்வ சூளா மணியே திருத்தணிகை
வாகைப் புயனே நின்திருத்தாள் அடியேன் முடிமேல் வைப்பபாயே.
translit: pākaip poruvum moḻiyuṭaiyīr eṉṟu maṭavārp paḻiccāmal ōkaip peṟumniṉ tiruttoṇṭar uṭaṉcērn tuṇmai yuṇarntiṭuvāṉ tōkaip parimēl varunteyva cūḷā maṇiyē tiruttaṇikai vākaip puyaṉē niṉtiruttāḷ aṭiyēṉ muṭimēl vaippapāyē.
translation: O divine crest-jewel who arrives riding your peacock steed. O Lord of Thanigai with victorious shoulders. Place your sacred feet upon the head of this servant. Let me join your joyous holy devotees and realize the truth, without flattering women by telling them their words are as sweet as syrup.
commentary: The poet rejects the empty flattery of worldly romance, refusing to waste his words praising physical beauty. He asks instead to join the joyful company of true devotees and realize the eternal truth. To achieve this, he prays for the Lord, arriving on his magnificent peacock, to place his sacred feet upon his head as a sign of grace.

tamil: தணிகை மலையைச் சாரேனோ சாமி அழகைப் பாரேனோ
பிணிகை யறையைப் பேரேனோ பேரா அன்பு கூரேனோ
அணிசெய் அருள்நீர் ஆரேனோ ஆறாத் தாகம் தீரேனோ
பணிசெய் தொழும்பில் சேரேனோ பார்மீ திரங்கும் நீரேனே.
translit: taṇikai malaiyaic cārēṉō cāmi aḻakaip pārēṉō piṇikai yaṟaiyaip pērēṉō pērā aṉpu kūrēṉō aṇicey aruḷnīr ārēṉō āṟāt tākam tīrēṉō paṇicey toḻumpil cērēṉō pārmī tiraṅkum nīrēṉē.
translation: Will I not reach Thanigai mountain? Will I not see the Lord's beauty? Will I not escape the prison of disease? Will I not feel unwavering love? Will I not drink deeply the beautiful water of grace? Will I not quench my endless thirst? Will I not join the devoted service? I am just a wretch weeping in sorrow upon this earth.
commentary: The speaker yearns to travel to Thanigai, a sacred hill town dedicated to the divine youth Murugan. She feels trapped in the physical suffering of the world and begs to trade her misery for a life of loving service. She wonders if she will ever be allowed to drink the water of divine grace and finally quench her spiritual thirst.

tamil: எளியேன் என்ன இருப்பாரோ ஏழைக் கிரங்கும் விருப்பாரோ
அளியேன் பேர்நெஞ் சிருப்பாரோ அழியாக் காமம் திருப்பாரோ
களியேன் என்ன உருப்பாரோ கருதும் அருட்குக் கருப்பாரோ
தெளியேன் யான்என் செய்கேனே தென்பால் தணிகைப் பொருப்பாரே.
translit: eḷiyēṉ eṉṉa iruppārō ēḻaik kiraṅkum viruppārō aḷiyēṉ pērneñ ciruppārō aḻiyāk kāmam tiruppārō kaḷiyēṉ eṉṉa uruppārō karutum aruṭkuk karuppārō teḷiyēṉ yāṉeṉ ceykēṉē teṉpāl taṇikaip poruppārē.
translation: Will he consider me a lowly wretch? Will he wish to pity this poor girl? Will he dwell in my vast heart? Will he resolve my indestructible passion? Will he grow angry, thinking I am devoid of joy? Is he the source of the grace I seek? I have no clarity. What shall I do? He is the Lord of the southern Thanigai mountain.
commentary: The poet takes on the voice of a young woman longing for her divine lover, expressing deep insecurity about her own worth. She wonders if the Lord looks down on her or if his heart holds enough pity to take her in. Overwhelmed by her own passionate devotion, she admits she is entirely lost and does not know what to do to win his grace.

tamil: செய்கொள் தணிகை நாடேனோ செவ்வேள் புகழைப் பாடேனோ
கைகள் கூப்பி ஆடேனோ கருணைக் கடலில் நீடேனோ
மெய்கொள் புளகம் மூடேனோ மெய்அன் பர்கள்பால் கூடேனோ
பொய்கொள் உலகோ டூடேனோ புவிமீ திருகால் மாடேனே.
translit: ceykoḷ taṇikai nāṭēṉō cevvēḷ pukaḻaip pāṭēṉō kaikaḷ kūppi āṭēṉō karuṇaik kaṭalil nīṭēṉō meykoḷ puḷakam mūṭēṉō meyaṉ parkaḷpāl kūṭēṉō poykoḷ ulakō ṭūṭēṉō puvimī tirukāl māṭēṉē.
translation: Will I not seek out flourishing Thanigai? Will I not sing the praises of the Red Lord? Will I not dance with folded hands? Will I not immerse myself deeply in the ocean of grace? Will my body not be covered in thrilled goosebumps? Will I not join the company of true devotees? Will I not quarrel with this false world? I am but a two-legged beast upon this earth.
commentary: True devotion is shown here as an intensely physical and emotional experience. The speaker longs to sing the praises of the Red Lord, a traditional name for the vibrant deity Murugan, and to feel her body break out in thrilled goosebumps among a community of true believers. Compared to the ecstatic joy of this divine love, she views ordinary human life as a false world and calls herself nothing more than an animal walking on two legs.

tamil: வந்தென் எதிரில் நில்லாரோ மகிழ ஒருசொல் சொல்லாரோ
முந்தம் மதனை வெல்லாரோ மோகம் தீரப் புல்லாரோ
கந்தன் எனும்பேர் அல்லாரோ கருணை நெஞ்சம் கல்லாரோ
சந்தத் தணிகை இல்லாரோ சகத்தில் எல்லாம் வல்லாரே.
translit: vanteṉ etiril nillārō makiḻa orucol collārō muntam mataṉai vellārō mōkam tīrap pullārō kantaṉ eṉumpēr allārō karuṇai neñcam kallārō cantat taṇikai illārō cakattil ellām vallārē.
translation: Will he not come and stand before me? Will he not say a single word to make me rejoice? Did he not conquer the ancient god of love? Will he not embrace me to quench my desire? Is his name not Skandan? Is his compassionate heart made of stone? Is beautiful Thanigai not his home? He is the all-powerful one in this world.
commentary: The speaker questions why the all-powerful Lord refuses to offer even a single word of comfort. She addresses him as Skandan, a beloved name for the youthful god, and wonders if his heart has turned to stone. Since he has the power to conquer Kama, the ancient god of romantic passion, she pleads with him to intervene and relieve her agonizing desire for him.

tamil: நாட்டும் தணிகை நண்ணேனோ நாதன் புகழை எண்ணேனோ
கூட்டும் தொழும்பு பண்ணேனோ குறையா அருள்நீர் உண்ணேனோ
சூட்டும் மயக்கை மண்ணேனோ தொழும்பர் இடத்தை அண்ணேனோ
காட்டும் அவர்தாள் கண்ணேனோ கழியா வாழ்க்கைப் புண்ணேனே.
translit: nāṭṭum taṇikai naṇṇēṉō nātaṉ pukaḻai eṇṇēṉō kūṭṭum toḻumpu paṇṇēṉō kuṟaiyā aruḷnīr uṇṇēṉō cūṭṭum mayakkai maṇṇēṉō toḻumpar iṭattai aṇṇēṉō kāṭṭum avartāḷ kaṇṇēṉō kaḻiyā vāḻkkaip puṇṇēṉē.
translation: Will I not reach established Thanigai? Will I not meditate on the Lord's praises? Will I not perform the devoted service that brings us together? Will I not drink the unceasing water of grace? Will I not bury this enveloping illusion in the earth? Will I not approach the dwelling of his devotees? Will I not see his revealed feet? I am wounded by this miserable life.
commentary: The final verse gathers the speaker's deepest hopes into a clear path forward. She wants to leave behind the illusions of worldly life, join the company of sincere devotees, and dedicate herself entirely to loving service. Her ultimate goal is to see the Lord's holy feet, a traditional symbol of final refuge and saving grace, to heal the deep wounds of earthly existence.

tamil: காமப் பயலைத் தடுப்பாரோ கடப்ப மலர்த்தார் கொடுப்பாரோ
ஏமத் தனத்தைக் கடுப்பாரோ என்மேல் அன்பை விடுப்பாரோ
மாமற் றொருவீ டடுப்பாரோ மனத்தில் கோபம் தொடுப்பாரோ
தாமத் தாழ்வைக் கெடுப்பாரோ தணிகை தனில்வேல் எடுப்பாரே.
translit: kāmap payalait taṭuppārō kaṭappa malarttār koṭuppārō ēmat taṉattaik kaṭuppārō eṉmēl aṉpai viṭuppārō māmaṟ ṟoruvī ṭaṭuppārō maṉattil kōpam toṭuppārō tāmat tāḻvaik keṭuppārō taṇikai taṉilvēl eṭuppārē.
translation: He holds the spear in Thanigai. Will he stop this boy called Lust? Will he give me his garland of Kadamba flowers? Will he make my golden breasts ache? Will he abandon his love for me? Will he approach another great house? Will he harbor anger in his heart? Will he destroy my base delay?
commentary: The devotee speaks here in the voice of a young woman longing for her divine lover, the Lord of Thanigai. She wonders if he will save her from worldly desires and offer his sacred garland of flowers as a sign of his grace. In this poetic tradition, the physical ache of love represents the soul's deep yearning for God.

tamil: காவி மலைக்கண் வதியேனோ கண்ணுள் மணியைத் துதியேனோ
ஓவில் அருளைப் பதியேனோ உயர்ந்த தொழும்பில் கதியேனோ
தாவில் சுகத்தை மதியேனோ சற்றும் பயனில் ஓதியேனே.
translit: kāvi malaikkaṇ vatiyēṉō kaṇṇuḷ maṇiyait tutiyēṉō pāvi mayalai mitiyēṉō paramāṉantat tutiyayēṉō ōvil aruḷaip patiyēṉō uyarnta toḻumpil katiyēṉō tāvil cukattai matiyēṉō caṟṟum payaṉil ōtiyēṉē.
translation: I babble utterly useless words. Will I not dwell on the ochre mountain? Will I not praise the Lord who is the pupil of my eye? Will I not trample this sinful delusion? Will I not rise in supreme bliss? Will I not secure his ceaseless grace? Will I not find my refuge in exalted service? Will I not cherish flawless joy?
commentary: The focus shifts from romantic longing to a clear cry for spiritual transformation. The speaker asks when she will stop wasting her words and finally reach the sacred mountain shrine. The Lord is described beautifully as the pupil of the eye, showing that the divine is intimately present within our own awareness.

tamil: வருந்தும் தனிமுன் மன்னாரோ வருத்தம் உனக்கேன் என்னாரோ
இருந்தென் இடத்தே துன்னாரோ இணைத்தாள் ஈய உன்னாரோ
பொருந்திங் கயலார் அன்னாரோ பொருள்ஈ தென்று பன்னாரோ
செருந்தி மலரும் திருத்தணிகைத் தேவர் எவர்க்கும் முன்னாரே.
translit: varuntum taṉimuṉ maṉṉārō varuttam uṉakkēṉ eṉṉārō irunteṉ iṭattē tuṉṉārō iṇaittāḷ īya uṉṉārō poruntiṅ kayalār aṉṉārō poruḷī teṉṟu paṉṉārō cerunti malarum tiruttaṇikait tēvar evarkkum muṉṉārē.
translation: He stands before all others as the Lord of holy Thanigai where the Serundhi flowers bloom. Will he not appear before me as I suffer alone? Will he not ask why I suffer? Will he not stay and draw close to me? Will he not intend to give me his twin feet? Will he act like a stranger here? Will he not teach me the ultimate truth?
commentary: The soul feels entirely alone in its suffering and asks the Lord to step forward as a comforting guide. She wonders if he will act like a distant stranger or draw close to teach the ultimate truth. Surrendering to the Lord's twin feet is the traditional way of asking for final spiritual refuge.

tamil: தணிகா சலம்போய்த் தழையேனோ சாமி திருத்தாள் விழையேனோ
பணிகா தலித்துப் பிழையேனோ பாடி மனது குழையேனோ
திணிகாண் உலகை அழையேனோ சேர்ந்தவ் வீட்டுள் நுழையேனோ
பிணிகாண் உலகில் பிறந்துழன்றே பேதுற் றலையும் பழையேனே.
translit: taṇikā calampōyt taḻaiyēṉō cāmi tiruttāḷ viḻaiyēṉō paṇikā talittup piḻaiyēṉō pāṭi maṉatu kuḻaiyēṉō tiṇikāṇ ulakai aḻaiyēṉō cērntav vīṭṭuḷ nuḻaiyēṉō piṇikāṇ ulakil piṟantuḻaṉṟē pētuṟ ṟalaiyum paḻaiyēṉē.
translation: I am an ancient soul wandering in confusion, born and suffering in this diseased world. Will I not go to the Thanigai hills and flourish? Will I not long for the Master's holy feet? Will I not love his service and be saved? Will I not sing until my heart melts? Will I not call out to this dense world? Will I not enter that house of liberation and unite with him?
commentary: The speaker feels she is an ancient, exhausted soul wandering through endless worldly births. The cure for this long confusion is an ecstatic devotion that melts the heart completely. She longs to enter the final house of liberation and to call the rest of the world to join her in that divine service.

tamil: மன்னும் குவளை ஈயாரோ மதவேள் மதத்தைக் காயாரோ
இன்னும் கோபம் ஓயாரோ என்தாய் தனக்குத் தாயாரோ
துன்னும் இரக்கம் தோயாரோ துகளேன் துயரை ஆயாரோ
பன்னும் வளங்கள் செறிந்தோங்கும் பணைகொள் தணிகைத் தூயாரே.
translit: maṉṉum kuvaḷai īyārō matavēḷ matattaik kāyārō iṉṉum kōpam ōyārō eṉtāy taṉakkut tāyārō tuṉṉum irakkam tōyārō tukaḷēṉ tuyarai āyārō paṉṉum vaḷaṅkaḷ ceṟintōṅkum paṇaikoḷ taṇikait tūyārē.
translation: He is the pure Lord of Thanigai, surrounded by fertile fields where celebrated riches gather and grow. He is the mother to my own mother. Will he not give me his enduring blue lotus garland? Will he not burn the arrogance of the god of lust? Will his anger still not subside? Will he not be steeped in deep compassion? Will he not examine my sorrow, though I am full of flaws?
commentary: God is addressed with intense tenderness as the mother to the devotee's own mother, highlighting a care deeper than the closest human bond. The speaker asks the Lord to burn away worldly lust and look upon her with divine compassion. Even though the soul is full of flaws, she trusts that his pure grace will answer her sorrow.

tamil: தேனே உளங்கொள் தெளிவே அகண்ட சிதம்மேவி நின்ற சிவமே
கோனே கனிந்த சிவபோத ஞான குருவே விளங்கு குகனே
தானே தனக்கு நிகராய் விளங்கு தணிகா சலத்தெம் அரசே
நானே ழைஇங்கு மனம்நொந்து நொந்து நலிகின்ற செய்கை நலமோ.
translit: tēṉē uḷaṅkoḷ teḷivē akaṇṭa citammēvi niṉṟa civamē kōṉē kaṉinta civapōta ñāṉa kuruvē viḷaṅku kukaṉē tāṉē taṉakku nikarāy viḷaṅku taṇikā calattem aracē nāṉē ḻai-iṅku maṉamnontu nontu nalikiṉṟa ceykai nalamō.
translation: O honey. O clarity held in the heart. O Sivam standing in the infinite space of consciousness. O King. O ripe Guru of divine wisdom. O radiant Guhan. O our King of Thanigachalam, who shines with no equal but yourself. Is it right that I, a helpless one, suffer here with a repeatedly breaking heart?
commentary: God is addressed as sweet honey and clear wisdom, showing a bond of great sweetness and intimacy. The poet calls on the ultimate reality (Sivam) and the perfect divine teacher (Guru). He then asks a very human question: is it right for the supreme Lord to let a helpless soul suffer with a broken heart? This plea reveals a relationship close enough that the devotee feels permitted to challenge God's silence.

tamil: நலமேவு தொண்டர் அயன்ஆதி தேவர் நவைஏக நல்கு தணிகா
சலமேவி உன்றன் இருதாள் புகழ்ந்து தரிசிப்ப தென்று புகலாய்
நிலமேவு கின்ற சிவயோகர் உள்ளம் நிகழ்கின்ற ஞான நிறைவே
வலமேவு வேல்கை ஒளிர்சேர் கலாப மயில்ஏறி நின்ற மணியே.
translit: nalamēvu toṇṭar ayaṉāti tēvar navai-ēka nalku taṇikā calamēvi uṉṟaṉ irutāḷ pukaḻntu taricippa teṉṟu pukalāy nilamēvu kiṉṟa civayōkar uḷḷam nikaḻkiṉṟa ñāṉa niṟaivē valamēvu vēlkai oḷircēr kalāpa mayilēṟi niṉṟa maṇiyē.
translation: O fullness of wisdom manifesting in the hearts of Sivayogis on earth. O gem who stands mounted on the radiant, plumed peacock, holding the powerful spear in your right hand. You reside in Thanigachalam, which removes the flaws of virtuous devotees and gods starting with Brahma. Tell me, when will I praise and behold your two feet?
commentary: The divine presence takes many forms, appearing as vast wisdom in the hearts of enlightened sages (Sivayogis) and as a personal Lord riding a peacock. The poet longs for a direct vision of this grace. He asks when his time will finally come to see the divine presence that already protects the highest celestial gods.

tamil: மணியே கலாப மலைமேல் அமர்ந்த மதியே நினைச்சொல் மலரால்
அணியேன் நல்அன்பும் அமையேன் மனத்தில் அடியார் அடிக்கண் மகிழ்வாய்ப்
பணியேன் நினைந்து பதையேன் இருந்து பருகேன் உவந்த படியே
எணியே நினைக்கில் அவமாம்இவ் வேழை எதுபற்றி உய்வ தரசே.
translit: maṇiyē kalāpa malaimēl amarnta matiyē niṉaiccol malarāl aṇiyēṉ nalaṉpum amaiyēṉ maṉattil aṭiyār aṭikkaṇ makiḻvāyp paṇiyēṉ niṉaintu pataiyēṉ iruntu parukēṉ uvanta paṭiyē eṇiyē niṉaikkil avamāmiv vēḻai etupaṟṟi uyva taracē.
translation: O gem. O moon seated on the plumed mountain. I do not adorn you with flowers of words. I do not establish true love in my mind. I do not bow joyfully at the feet of devotees. I do not tremble thinking of you. I do not sit and drink the nectar of your grace as I please. When I think of it, I am useless. By grasping what will this helpless one be saved, O King?
commentary: True devotion is traditionally shown through offering beautiful poetry, feeling deep love, and trembling with awe before God. The poet confesses he lacks every single one of these qualities. Stripped of all spiritual achievements, he asks what is left to save a helpless person who has absolutely nothing to offer.

tamil: உய்வண்ணம் இன்றி உலகா தரத்தில் உழல்கின்ற மாய மடவார்
பொய்வண்ணம் ஒன்றின் மனமாழ்கி அன்மை புரிதந்து நின்ற புலையேன்
மெய்வண்ணம் ஒன்று தணிகா சலத்து மிளிர்கின்ற தேவ விறல்வேல்
கைவண்ண உன்றன் அருள்வண்ணம் ஆன கழல்வண்ணம் நண்ணல் உளதோ.
translit: uyvaṇṇam iṉṟi ulakā tarattil uḻalkiṉṟa māya maṭavār poyvaṇṇam oṉṟiṉ maṉamāḻki aṉmai puritantu niṉṟa pulaiyēṉ meyvaṇṇam oṉṟu taṇikā calattu miḷirkiṉṟa tēva viṟalvēl kaivaṇṇa uṉṟaṉ aruḷvaṇṇam āṉa kaḻalvaṇṇam naṇṇal uḷatō.
translation: Without a way to be saved, my mind sinks into the false beauty of delusory women who wander in worldly attachments, and I stand as a base person committing evil. O God shining in the truly beautiful Thanigachalam, holding the mighty spear in your beautiful hand. Is it possible for me to attain the beauty of your ankleted feet, which are the very form of your grace?
commentary: The mind easily sinks into worldly desires and fleeting physical attractions. The poet contrasts his own false, temporary attachments with the true, lasting beauty of God's grace. Even while feeling utterly base and unworthy, he still longs to reach the pure reality of the divine.

tamil: நண்ணாத வஞ்சர் இடம்நாடி நெஞ்சம் நனிநொந்து நைந்து நவையாம்
புண்ணாகி நின்ற எளியேனை அஞ்சல் புரியாது நம்பொன் அடியை
எண்ணாத பாவி இவன்என்று தள்ளின் என்செய்வ துய்வ தறியேன்
தண்ணார் பொழிற்கண் மதிவந் துலாவு தணிகா சலத்தி றைவனே.
translit: naṇṇāta vañcar iṭamnāṭi neñcam naṉinontu naintu navaiyām puṇṇāki niṉṟa eḷiyēṉai añcal puriyātu nampoṉ aṭiyai eṇṇāta pāvi ivaṉeṉṟu taḷḷiṉ eṉceyva tuyva taṟiyēṉ taṇṇār poḻiṟkaṇ mativan tulāvu taṇikā calatti ṟaivaṉē.
translation: Seeking out the places of deceitful people who should not be approached, my heart aches intensely, withers, and becomes a festering wound. If you do not offer refuge to this lowly one, but push me away saying, "He is a sinner who does not think of our golden feet," I do not know what to do or how to be saved. O Lord of Thanigachalam, where the moon wanders among cool groves.
commentary: Seeking help from deceitful people in the world only leaves the heart deeply wounded. The poet begs God not to turn him away for being a sinner who forgot to pray. Without this final divine refuge, a broken soul has no other way to be saved.

tamil: இறையேனும் உன்றன் அடிஎண்ணி அங்கி இழுதென்ன நெஞ்சம் இளகேன்
மறைஓதும் உன்றன் அருள்பெற்ற தொண்டர் வழிபட் டலங்கல் அணியேன்
குறையோடும் இங்கு மயல்கொண்டு நின்ற கொடியேனை ஆளல் உளதோ
நிறையோர் வணங்கு தணிகா சலத்தில் நிலைபெற் றிருக்கும் அவனே.
translit: iṟaiyēṉum uṉṟaṉ aṭi-eṇṇi aṅki iḻuteṉṉa neñcam iḷakēṉ maṟai-ōtum uṉṟaṉ aruḷpeṟṟa toṇṭar vaḻipaṭ ṭalaṅkal aṇiyēṉ kuṟaiyōṭum iṅku mayalkoṇṭu niṉṟa koṭiyēṉai āḷal uḷatō niṟaiyōr vaṇaṅku taṇikā calattil nilaipeṟ ṟirukkum avaṉē.
translation: O Lord who abides eternally in Thanigachalam, worshipped by the perfect ones. I do not melt in my heart like butter in the fire by thinking of your feet even for a moment. I do not worship the devotees who chant the Vedas and have received your grace, nor do I wear their garlands. Will you rule over this cruel one who stands here full of flaws and delusion?
commentary: A true devotee's heart melts like butter in a fire at the thought of the divine. The speaker confesses that he feels nothing of this warmth and fails even to honor those who do. He asks if the Lord of Thanigachalam, a sacred hill shrine, will still take in someone so hardened and flawed.

tamil: அவம்நாள் கழிக்க அறிவேன் அலாதுன் அடிபேணி நிற்க அறியேன்
தவம்நாடும் அன்ப ரொடுசேர வந்து தணிகா சலத்தை அடையேன்
எவன்நான் எனக்கும் அவண்நீ இருக்கும் இடம்ஈயில் உன்றன் அடியார்
இவன்ஆர் இவன்றன் இயல்பென்ன என்னில் எவன்என் றுரைப்பை எனையே.
translit: avamnāḷ kaḻikka aṟivēṉ alātuṉ aṭipēṇi niṟka aṟiyēṉ tavamnāṭum aṉpa roṭucēra vantu taṇikā calattai aṭaiyēṉ evaṉnāṉ eṉakkum avaṇnī irukkum iṭamīyil uṉṟaṉ aṭiyār ivaṉār ivaṉṟaṉ iyalpeṉṉa eṉṉil evaṉeṉ ṟuraippai eṉaiyē.
translation: I only know how to waste my days in vain. I do not know how to cherish your feet and stand firm. I do not come to Thanigachalam to join the devotees who seek penance. Who am I? If you give even me a place where you reside, your devotees will ask, "Who is this man? What is his nature?" How will you describe me to them?
commentary: The speaker admits he spends his life wasting time rather than seeking spiritual growth. He feels so unworthy that he imagines a scene in the divine presence: if God were to grant him a place, the true seekers would ask who he is, and God would have no good way to explain his presence there.

tamil: எனையான் அறிந்துன் அடிசேர உன்னை இறையேனும் நெஞ்சி னிதமாய்
நினையேன் அயர்ந்து நிலையற்ற தேகம் நிசம்என் றுழன்று துயர்வேன்
தனையே நின்அன்பன் எனவோதி லியாவர் தகும்என் றுரைப்பர் அரசே
வனைஏர் கொளுஞ்செய் தணிகா சலத்து மகிழ்வோ டமர்ந்த அமுதே.
translit: eṉaiyāṉ aṟintuṉ aṭicēra uṉṉai iṟaiyēṉum neñci ṉitamāy niṉaiyēṉ ayarntu nilaiyaṟṟa tēkam nicameṉ ṟuḻaṉṟu tuyarvēṉ taṉaiyē niṉaṉpaṉ eṉavōti liyāvar takumeṉ ṟuraippar aracē vaṉai-ēr koḷuñcey taṇikā calattu makiḻvō ṭamarnta amutē.
translation: O Nectar seated in joy at Thanigachalam, surrounded by beautiful fields. To know myself and reach your feet, I do not think of you sweetly in my heart even for a moment. I grow weary, wandering in sorrow, believing this transient body to be true. If I call myself your devotee, who will say I am fit for it, O King?
commentary: The core illusion of human life is mistaking the temporary physical body for ultimate reality. Caught up in the physical world, the speaker forgets to seek the divine or understand his own true nature. He feels that claiming the title of a devotee would be entirely unconvincing to anyone watching his actions.

tamil: முதுவோர் வணங்கு தணிகா சலத்து முதலேஇவ் வேழை முறியேன்
மதுவால் மயங்கும் அளிபோல் மயங்கி மதியாது நின்ற பிழையால்
விதுவாகி அன்பர் உளம்மேவும் நீகை விடில்ஏழை எங்கு மெலிவேன்
இதுநீதி அல்ல எனஉன் றனக்கும் எவர்சொல்ல வல்லர் அரசே.
translit: mutuvōr vaṇaṅku taṇikā calattu mutalē-iv vēḻai muṟiyēṉ matuvāl mayaṅkum aḷipōl mayaṅki matiyātu niṉṟa piḻaiyāl vituvāki aṉpar uḷammēvum nīkai viṭilēḻai eṅku melivēṉ itunīti alla eṉa-uṉ ṟaṉakkum evarcolla vallar aracē.
translation: O Primal Lord of Thanigachalam, worshipped by the wise elders. I am a poor wretch who does not break away from the fault of lacking understanding, intoxicated like a bee drunk on honey. If you, who abide as the moon in the hearts of your devotees, abandon me, where will this poor one languish? Who has the power to tell you that this is unjust, O King?
commentary: Worldly distractions intoxicate the mind just as honey intoxicates a bee. The speaker confesses he is lost in this blindness and relies entirely on God for rescue. Because God is the absolute sovereign, there is no higher authority to appeal to if that grace is denied.

translit: aṭuttilēṉ niṉaṭiyar avaikkuṭ caṟṟum aṉpilēṉ niṉtoḻumpaṉ ākēṉ vañcam taṭuttilēṉ taṇikaitaṉil ceṉṟu niṉṉait taricaṉamcey tēmaturat tamiḻccol mālai toṭuttilēṉ aḻutuniṉ taruḷai vēṇṭit toḻututoḻu tāṉantat tūynīr āṭēṉ eṭuttilēṉ nallaṉeṉum peyarai antō ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I did not join the assembly of your devotees. I have no love in me at all. I did not become your servant. I did not stop my deceit. I did not go to Thanigai to see you and string a garland of sweet Tamil words. I do not weep, beg for your grace, worship you endlessly, and bathe in the pure waters of bliss. I did not earn the name of a good man. Alas, why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: A life without love, service, and devotion is an empty one. The poet looks back with bitter regret at his failure to seek grace, serve others, or sing out in worship, feeling that his existence has been nothing but a burden to the world.

translit: tirappaṭuvēṉ maiyalpuri māya vāḻvil tiyaṅkuvēṉ ciṟitēṉum teḷivoṉ ṟillēṉ marappaṭuvēṉ citaṭaruṭaṉ tirivēṉ vīṇē maṅkaiyartam kaṇkaḷeṉum valaikkuḷ vīḻvēṉ karappavarkku muṟpaṭuvēṉ karuṇai illēṉ kaṇaṉaiyāy niṉtaṇikai malaiyaik kāṇēṉ irappavarkkōr aṇuvaḷavum īyēṉ pēyēṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I suffer and stay confused in this illusory life of infatuation. I have no clarity at all. I stand stiff like a tree and wander endlessly with fools. I fall into the net of women's eyes. I stand first among those who hoard wealth. I lack compassion. O Lord who is like an eye, I do not look upon your Thanigai hill. I do not give even an atom to those who beg. I am a demon. Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: Hoarding wealth and chasing physical desires leave the soul spiritually barren. The poet points to his refusal to give even an atom to the poor as his greatest failure, marking a total lack of Jeevakarunyam (compassion for all living beings). Without this basic compassion, a human being becomes blind to divine grace.

translit: . ceytilēṉ niṉtoṇṭar aṭikkuṟ ṟēval tiruttaṇikai malaiyaivalañ ceytu kaṇṇīrp peytilēṉ pulaṉaintum oṭukki vītal piṟattaleṉum kaṭalnīntēṉ peṇkaḷ tammai vaitilēṉ malarkoyyēṉ mālai cūṭṭēṉ maṇiyēniṉ tiruppukaḻai vaḻuttēṉ niṉpāl eytilēṉ ivvuṭalkoṇ ṭēḻai yēṉyāṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I did not perform menial service at the feet of your devotees. I did not circumambulate the holy Thanigai hill and shed tears. I do not control my five senses and swim across the ocean of birth and death. I did not shun women. I do not pluck flowers and offer you garlands. O radiant gem, I do not praise your holy glory. I do not reach you. I am a poor wretch bearing this body. Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: The five physical senses trap the mind in an endless cycle of birth and death when they are left unchecked. True freedom comes from turning those senses away from worldly indulgences and directing them toward humble acts of worship, like gathering flowers and serving the devoted.

translit: cīrkoṇṭār pukaḻtaṇikai malaiyiṟ cērēṉ civaperumāṉ peṟṟaperuñ celva mēniṉ pērkoṇṭār tamaivaṇaṅki makiḻēṉ pittēṉ peṟṟatē amaiyumeṉap piṟaṅkēṉ mātar vārkoṇṭār mulaimalaivīḻn turuḷvēṉ nāḷum vañcamē ceytiṭuvēṉ mati-oṉ ṟillēṉ ērkoṇṭār ikaḻntiṭa-iṅ kēḻai yēṉyāṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I do not reach the Thanigai hill praised by virtuous people. O great wealth begotten by Lord Siva, I do not bow before those who bear your name and rejoice. I am a madman. I do not shine with contentment, accepting what I have received as enough. I fall and roll upon the mountain-like breasts of women wearing tight bodices. I commit deceit every day. I lack all sense. While good people despise me, I linger here as a poor wretch. Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: Endless chasing after physical pleasure breeds discontent and deceit. When a person cannot find peace in what they already possess, they lose their moral sense and miss the joy found in the company of spiritual seekers.

translit: kāmānta kāriyāy mātar alkul kaṭalvīḻntēṉ matitāḻntēṉ kavalai cūḻntēṉ nāmānta kaṉai-utaitta nātaṉ īṉṟa nāyakamā maṇiyēnal nalamē uṉṟaṉ pūmāntaṇ cēvaṭiyaip pōṟṟēṉ ōṅkum poḻilkoḷtaṇi kācalattaip pukaḻntu pāṭēṉ ēmānta pāviyēṉ antō antō ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: Blinded by lust, I fell into the ocean of women's loins. My mind degraded and sorrow surrounded me. O supreme gem begotten by the Lord who kicked the fearsome god of death, O absolute goodness, I do not praise your beautiful, cool lotus feet. I do not sing the praises of Thanigai hill with its towering groves. I am a deluded sinner. Alas, alas, why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: Surrendering completely to physical lust ruins the mind and brings only sorrow. The poet contrasts this dark state with the absolute goodness of the divine, recalling the traditional story that God conquered death itself. True peace lies in seeking that deathless grace rather than fleeting earthly thrills.

translit: naṉṟaṟiyēṉ tīṅkaṉaittum paṟiyēṉ pollā naṅkaiyartam kaṇmāya navaiyaic caṟṟum veṉṟaṟiyēṉ koṉṟaṟivār tammaik kūṭum vēṭaṉēṉ tiruttaṇikai veṟpiṉ niṉpāl ceṉṟaṟiyēṉ ilaiyeṉpa taṟivēṉ oṉṟum ceytaṟiyēṉ civatarumam ceyvōr nallōr eṉṟaṟiyēṉ veṟiyēṉiṅ kantō antō ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I know no good. I do not uproot my many evils. I have never conquered the illusory affliction of the eyes of wicked women, even a little. I am a hunter who associates with killers. I have never approached you on the mountain of Thanigai. I only know how to refuse others. I have never done a single good deed. I do not recognize that those who perform Siva's righteous acts are good people. I am a madman here. Alas, alas! Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: A person separated from grace lives entirely for themselves. The verse describes a state of total selfishness, where one refuses to help others and associates only with cruelty. A life lived without doing a single good deed becomes nothing but a heavy burden on the earth.

translit: allārkkum kuḻalārmēl ācai vaippēṉ aiyāniṉ tiruttāḷmēl aṉpu vaiyēṉ cellārkkum poḻiltaṇikai eṅkē eṉṟu tēṭiṭēṉ niṉpukaḻaic cintai ceyyēṉ kallārkkum kaṭumaṉattēṉ vaṉka ṇēṉpuṉ kaṇṇiṉēṉ utavāta kaiyēṉ poyyēṉ ellārkkum pollāta pāvi yēṉyāṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I place my desire on women with hair dark as night. O Lord, I place no love upon your holy feet. I do not seek out where Thanigai is with its cloud-capped groves. I do not think of your glory. I have a harsh mind harder than stone. I am cruel. I have wretched eyes. My hands offer no help. I am a liar. I am a wicked sinner to everyone. Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: Worldly obsession hardens the heart. When a person's focus is fixed entirely on physical pleasure, their mind becomes like a stone and their hands offer no help to anyone else. Without compassion and love for the divine, a person feels they are only taking up space in the world.

translit: arumpāya nakaimaṭavārk kāḷāy vāḷā alaikiṉṟēṉ aṟiveṉpa taṟiyēṉ niṉpāl tirumpāta pātakaṉēṉ tiru-oṉ ṟillēṉ tiruttaṇikai malaikkēkac cintai ceyyēṉ karumpāya veṟuttuvēm paruntum pollāk kākkai-ottēṉ caṟṟēṉum kaṉital illā irumpāya vaṉneñcak kaḷva ṉēṉyāṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: Enslaved to young women whose smiles are like blooming buds, I wander pointlessly. I know no true wisdom. I am a great sinner who will not turn to you. I possess no sacred wealth. I never think of going to the mountain of Thanigai. Like a wicked crow that rejects sweet sugarcane to eat bitter neem, I am a thief with a hard iron heart that never softens even a little. Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: People routinely choose things that harm them over things that heal them. The verse compares the distracted mind to a crow that ignores sweet sugarcane to eat the bitter leaves of the neem tree. Chasing empty pleasures leaves the heart like iron, unable to soften or receive divine grace.

translit: ampātal neṭuṅkaṇṇārk kiccai koḷvēṉ akamalara mukamalarvō ṭaruḷcey uṉṟaṉ cempāta malarēttēṉ ilavu kāttēṉ tiruttaṇikai yēnamatu celvam eṉṟē nampāta koṭiyēṉnal lōraik kaṇṭāl nāṇilēṉ naṭuṅkilēṉ nāyiṟ pollēṉ empāta kattai-eṭut tiyārkkuc colvēṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I lust after women whose long eyes are like arrows. I do not praise your red lotus feet that bestow grace with a joyous heart and a blossoming face. I waited in vain. I am a cruel person who does not believe that Thanigai is our true wealth. When I see good people, I feel no shame and I do not tremble. I am worse than a dog. To whom can I recount my grave sins? Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: Spending a lifetime on fleeting physical desires in the end leaves a person empty-handed. The admission of having waited in vain captures the uselessness of expecting lasting joy from worldly things. Encountering truly good people only brings intense shame to someone who realizes they have wasted their true spiritual wealth.

translit: paṇṇēṉniṉ pukaḻcolvōr tamakkup pūcai pāṭēṉniṉ tiruccīraip paramaṉ īṉṟa kaṇṇēniṉ taṇikaitaṉaik kaṇṭu pōṟṟēṉ kaikuviyēṉ meykuḷirēṉ kaṇṇīr pāyēṉ uṇṇēṉnal āṉanta amutai aṉpar uṭaṉākēṉ ēkāntat tuṟa-ōr eṇṇam eṇṇēṉvaṉ tuyarmaṇṇēṉ maṉañcem puṇṇēṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ puviccumaiyā irukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I do not worship those who speak your glory. I do not sing of your holy excellence. O precious eye begotten by the supreme Lord, I do not go to see and praise your Thanigai. I do not fold my hands in reverence. My body does not thrill with devotion. I do not shed flowing tears. I do not drink the good nectar of bliss. I do not join with your devotees. I do not form a single thought of abiding in solitude. I do not wash away my severe sorrow. My mind is a raw wound. Why was I born? I remain a burden to the earth.
commentary: Real devotion transforms the entire body and mind. It is felt physically in folded hands, flowing tears, and a thrilling sense of joy. Without this deep emotional connection to the divine and a community of devotees, the human mind is left suffering like an open wound.

sections.title: Ten Verses on Failing to See

tamil: வரங்கொள் அடியர் மனமலரில் மகிழ்வுற் றமர்ந்த மாமணியே
திரங்கொள் தணிகை மலைவாழும் செல்வப் பெருக்கே சிற்பரமே
தரங்கொள் உலக மயல்அகலத் தாழ்ந்துள் உருக அழுதழுது
கரங்கொள் சிரத்தோ டியான்உன்னைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: varaṅkoḷ aṭiyar maṉamalaril makiḻvuṟ ṟamarnta māmaṇiyē tiraṅkoḷ taṇikai malaivāḻum celvap perukkē ciṟparamē taraṅkoḷ ulaka mayalakalat tāḻntuḷ uruka aḻutaḻutu karaṅkoḷ cirattō ṭiyāṉuṉṉaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O great gem joyously seated in the lotus hearts of blessed devotees. O flood of wealth residing on the steadfast Thanigai mountain. O supreme consciousness. I have not bowed down, melted within, wept repeatedly to dispel the delusion of this world, joined my hands above my head, and seen you to my eyes' content.
commentary: This verse captures the deep regret of a seeker who feels they have not tried hard enough to reach God. The divine presence already lives like a bright gem in the hearts of true devotees. To see it, a person must let go of worldly delusion through sincere, melting devotion.

tamil: வல்லி ஒருபால் வானவர்தம் மகளாண் டொருபால் வரமயில்மேல்
எல்லின் இலங்கு நெட்டிலைவேல் ஏந்தி வரும்என் இறையவனே
சொல்லி அடங்காத் துயர்இயற்றும் துகள்சேர் சன்னப் பெருவேரைக்
கல்லி எறிந்து நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: valli orupāl vāṉavartam makaḷāṇ ṭorupāl varamayilmēl elliṉ ilaṅku neṭṭilaivēl ēnti varumeṉ iṟaiyavaṉē colli aṭaṅkāt tuyariyaṟṟum tukaḷcēr caṉṉap peruvēraik kalli eṟintu niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O my Lord. You come riding the excellent peacock, wielding the long leaf-shaped spear shining like the sun, with Valli on one side and the daughter of the celestials on the other. I have not dug up and thrown away the great impure root of birth that brings unspeakable sorrow, and I have not seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: True vision of the divine requires clearing away the deep causes of human suffering. The "root of birth" refers to the stubborn cycle of worldly attachments that leads to endless lifetimes of sorrow. Until this root is completely dug up, the ultimate reality remains hidden.

tamil: உருத்துள் இகலும் சூர்முதலை ஒழித்து வானத் தொண்பதியைத்
திருத்தும் அரைசே தென்தணிகைத் தெய்வ மணியே சிவஞானம்
அருத்தும் நினது திருவருள்கொண் டாடிப் பாடி அன்பதனால்
கருத்துள் உருகி நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: uruttuḷ ikalum cūrmutalai oḻittu vāṉat toṇpatiyait tiruttum araicē teṉtaṇikait teyva maṇiyē civañāṉam aruttum niṉatu tiruvaruḷkoṇ ṭāṭip pāṭi aṉpataṉāl karuttuḷ uruki niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O King who destroyed the fiercely angry Surapadman and restored the radiant heavenly realm. O divine gem of southern Thanigai who nourishes us with divine wisdom. I have not received your divine grace, danced, sung, melted inwardly with love, and seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: God is described here as the source of true spiritual wisdom (civajñāṉam, the highest knowledge of reality). This wisdom is not earned through quiet study alone. It comes as an outpouring of grace to those who sing, dance, and melt inwardly with total love.

tamil: போதல் இருத்தல் எனநினையாப் புனிதர் சனனப் போரோடு
சாதல் அகற்றும் திருத்தணிகைச் சைவக் கனியே தற்பரமே
ஓதல் அறியா வஞ்சகர்பால் உழன்றே மாதர்க் குள்ளுருகும்
காதல் அகற்றி நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: pōtal iruttal eṉaniṉaiyāp puṉitar caṉaṉap pōrōṭu cātal akaṟṟum tiruttaṇikaic caivak kaṉiyē taṟparamē ōtal aṟiyā vañcakarpāl uḻaṉṟē mātark kuḷḷurukum kātal akaṟṟi niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O pure fruit of Thanigai who ends the battle of birth and death for the pure ones who transcend thoughts of going and staying. O supreme being. I have wandered among deceitful people ignorant of true learning. I have not cast away my melting lust for women and seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: The pure ones mentioned here are those who have stopped worrying about worldly gains or losses. They live freely beyond the changing tides of life. Everyday desires and the bad company we keep trap us in the cycle of birth and death, and only by dropping these desires can the mind become clear enough to see God.

tamil: வீட்டைப் பெறுவோர் உள்அகத்து விளங்கும் விளக்கே விண்ணோர்தம்
நாட்டை நலஞ்செய் திருத்தணிகை நகத்தில் அமர்ந்த நாயகமே
கேட்டைத் தருவஞ் சகஉலகில் கிடைத்த மாய வாழ்க்கைஎனும்
காட்டைக் கடந்து நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: vīṭṭaip peṟuvōr uḷakattu viḷaṅkum viḷakkē viṇṇōrtam nāṭṭai nalañcey tiruttaṇikai nakattil amarnta nāyakamē kēṭṭait taruvañ caka-ulakil kiṭaitta māya vāḻkkai-eṉum kāṭṭaik kaṭantu niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O lamp shining within the hearts of those who attain liberation. O Lord seated on the mountain of Thanigai, bringing prosperity to the realm of the celestials. I have not crossed the forest of this illusory life found in this deceitful world that brings ruin, and I have not seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: Worldly life is compared to a dark, confusing forest where it is easy to get lost in illusions. The divine is the inner lamp that guides those seeking true freedom. We must deliberately walk out of this deceptive forest of daily survival to finally see that guiding light clearly.

tamil: மட்டித் தளறு படக்கடலை மலைக்கும் கொடிய மாஉருவைச்
சட்டித் தருளும் தணிகையில்எந் தாயே தமரே சற்குருவே
எட்டிக் கனியாம் இவ்வுலகத் திடர்விட் டகல நின்பதத்தைக்
translit: maṭṭit taḷaṟu paṭakkaṭalai malaikkum koṭiya mā-uruvaic caṭṭit taruḷum taṇikaiyilen tāyē tamarē caṟkuruvē eṭṭik kaṉiyām ivvulakat tiṭarviṭ ṭakala niṉpatattaik kaṭṭit taḻuviniṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: You destroyed the cruel mango tree form that terrified the expansive ocean into mud. O my Mother, my kin, my true Guru residing in Thanigai! To escape the sorrow of this world, which is like a bitter etti fruit, I have not tightly embraced your feet and seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: Worldly life is like the etti fruit, a plant known for its intense, poisonous bitterness. Seeking comfort, the speaker looks to the Lord of Thanigai as a mother, family, and guiding teacher. He recalls the ancient story of Murugan destroying a great demon who took the shape of a massive mango tree in the ocean. Desiring escape from the world's harshness, the soul longs to hold tightly to the divine feet and see the Lord clearly.

tamil: இலக்கம் அறியா இருவினையால் இம்மா னிடம்ஒன் றெடுத்தடியேன்
விலக்கம் அடையா வஞ்சகர்பால் வீணாட் போக்கி மேவிமனத்
தலக்கண் இயற்றும் பொய்வாழ்வில் அலைந்தேன் தணிகை அரசேஅக்
கலக்கம் அகன்று நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: ilakkam aṟiyā iruviṉaiyāl immā ṉiṭamoṉ ṟeṭuttaṭiyēṉ vilakkam aṭaiyā vañcakarpāl vīṇāṭ pōkki mēvimaṉat talakkaṇ iyaṟṟum poyvāḻvil alaintēṉ taṇikai aracē-ak kalakkam akaṉṟu niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: Driven by the countless twin deeds of karma, I took this human birth. Wasting my days among unyielding deceivers, I wandered in this false life that brings sorrow to the mind. O King of Thanigai! Dispelling that confusion, I have not seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: Human birth is driven by the twin forces of good and bad karma. The poet expresses deep regret for wasting his days among deceitful people and pursuing false worldly goals. This kind of living only brings sorrow and distraction to the mind. He longs to clear away this deep confusion so his eyes can finally take in the Lord's true form.

tamil: விரைவாய் கடப்பந் தார்அணிந்து விளங்கும் புயனே வேலோனே
தரைவாய் தவத்தால் தணிகைஅமர் தருமக் கடலே தனிஅடியேன்
திரைவாய் சனனக் கடற்படிந்தே தியங்கி அலைந்தேன் சிவஞானக்
கரைவாய் ஏறி நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: viraivāy kaṭappan tāraṇintu viḷaṅkum puyaṉē vēlōṉē taraivāy tavattāl taṇikai-amar tarumak kaṭalē taṉi-aṭiyēṉ tiraivāy caṉaṉak kaṭaṟpaṭintē tiyaṅki alaintēṉ civañāṉak karaivāy ēṟi niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O Lord whose shoulders shine with the fragrant kadamba garland! O wielder of the spear! O ocean of dharma seated in Thanigai through the penance of the earth! I, your lonely servant, plunged into the wavy ocean of birth and wandered in bewilderment. Climbing onto the shore of supreme wisdom, I have not seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: The endless cycle of birth and death is like a violent, wavy ocean. Lost in this dark sea, the soul wanders in deep bewilderment. To survive this drowning, the seeker must reach the safe shore of supreme spiritual wisdom. Only from that solid ground can one truly see the Lord, who wears a fragrant flower garland and holds the spear of knowledge.

tamil: பள்ள உலகப் படுகுழியில் பரிந்தங் குழலா தானந்த
வெள்ளத் தழுந்தும் அன்பர்விழி விருந்தே தணிகை வெற்பரசே
உள்ளம் அகல அங்கும்இங்கும் ஓடி அலையும் வஞ்சநெஞ்சக்
கள்ளம் அகற்றி நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: paḷḷa ulakap paṭukuḻiyil parintaṅ kuḻalā tāṉanta veḷḷat taḻuntum aṉparviḻi viruntē taṇikai veṟparacē uḷḷam akala aṅkumiṅkum ōṭi alaiyum vañcaneñcak kaḷḷam akaṟṟi niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O feast for the eyes of devotees who immerse themselves in the flood of bliss without wandering in sorrow in the deep pit of this worldly life! O King of the Thanigai hills! Removing the deceit of this treacherous heart that runs here and there displacing true feeling, I have not seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: True devotees experience a flood of spiritual joy because they avoid the deep, sorrowful pit of ordinary worldly attachments. By contrast, the untrained human mind is a tricky thief that runs constantly from one distraction to another. The poet asks the Lord of Thanigai to strip away this inner deceit. A wandering mind must become quiet and honest before it can hold the vision of the divine.

tamil: அடலை அணிந்தோர் புறங்காட்டில் ஆடும் பெருமான் அளித்தருளும்
விடலை எனமூ வரும்புகழும் வேலோய் தணிகை மேலோயே
நடலை உலக நடைஅளற்றை நண்ணா தோங்கும் ஆனந்தக்
கடலை அடுத்து நின்உருவைக் கண்கள் ஆரக் கண்டிலனே.
translit: aṭalai aṇintōr puṟaṅkāṭṭil āṭum perumāṉ aḷittaruḷum viṭalai eṉamū varumpukaḻum vēlōy taṇikai mēlōyē naṭalai ulaka naṭai-aḷaṟṟai naṇṇā tōṅkum āṉantak kaṭalai aṭuttu niṉuruvaik kaṇkaḷ ārak kaṇṭilaṉē.
translation: O brave youth given by the Great Lord who smears himself with ash and dances in the cremation ground! O wielder of the spear praised by the three gods! O Supreme Lord of Thanigai! Shunning the muddy paths of this deceptive world and reaching the rising ocean of bliss, I have not seen your form to my eyes' content.
commentary: Lord Siva is the supreme dancer who smears himself with ash in the cremation ground, a powerful reminder that all material things eventually burn away. Murugan is his brave son, praised by the cosmic trinity of creator, preserver, and destroyer. To see his divine form, the soul must leave behind the muddy, deceptive paths of ordinary life. The ultimate goal is to trade the world's illusions for a rising ocean of pure spiritual bliss.

translit: vañcakap pētaiyar mayakkil āḻntuḻal neñcakap pāviyēṉ niṉainti lēṉaiyō veñcakap pōriṉai viṭṭu ḷōrpukaḻ tañcakat taṇikaivāḻ taruma vāṉaiyē.
translation: Alas, a sinner at heart who sinks and wanders in the delusion of deceitful women, I did not think of the sky of Dharma living in Thanigai, the refuge praised by those who have abandoned fierce earthly strife.
commentary: The poet expresses deep regret for forgetting the divine, lost in the pull of worldly delusion. He contrasts the fleeting nature of sensory attachments with the enduring peace found in Lord Murugan at Thanigai, known here as the "sky of Dharma" (taruma vāṉ) who offers refuge to those who leave behind earthly conflict.

translit: vāṉnikar kūntalār vaṉka ṇālmika mālnikaḻ pētaiyēṉ matitti lēṉ aiyō tāṉirum pukaḻkoḷum taṇikai mēlaruḷ tēṉirun toḻukiya ceṅka rumpaiyē.
translation: Alas, an ignorant fool completely caught in the illusion caused by the harsh glances of women with hair like the dark sky, I did not revere the red sugarcane dripping with the honey of grace upon highly renowned Thanigai.
commentary: Sensory attraction has an overwhelming power that blinds the mind to spiritual truth. The divine presence in Thanigai is pictured as sweet red sugarcane dripping with the honey of grace, a deep sweetness that the ignorant mind completely misses while chasing worldly illusions.

translit: karuṅkaṭu nikarneṭuṅ kaṇṇi ṉārmayal oruṅkuṟu maṉattiṉēṉ uṉṉi lēṉaiyō tarumpukaḻ mikuntiṭun taṇikai māmalai maruṅkamarn taṉparuḷ maṉṉum vāḻvaiyē.
translation: Alas, my mind entirely consumed by infatuation for women with long eyes like black poison, I did not meditate on the true Life who rests upon the great and highly renowned mountain of Thanigai and abides within the hearts of devotees.
commentary: Sensual infatuation acts like a dark poison that consumes the mind entirely. This destructive obsession stands in sharp contrast to the true, life-giving presence of the Lord, who rests on the great mountain of Thanigai and lives eternally in the pure hearts of his devotees.

translit: vaivaḷar vāṭkaṇār mayakkil vīḻntaṟāp poyvaḷar neñciṉēṉ pōṟṟi lēṉaiyō meyvaḷar aṉparkaḷ mēvi ēttuṟum ceyvaḷar taṇikaiyil ceḻikkum tēṉaiyē.
translation: Alas, falling into the delusion of women with sharp sword-like eyes, my heart grew full of endless lies and I did not praise the flourishing honey in fertile Thanigai, whom true devotees approach and exalt.
commentary: Worldly delusion breeds endless falsehoods within the heart, pulling it away from the truth. Instead of falling into this deceit, true devotees gather at fertile Thanigai to praise the divine, which is described here as a flourishing, sweet honey.

translit: ceḻippaṭum maṅkaiyar tīya māyaiyil paḻippaṭum neñciṉēṉ paravi lēṉaiyō vaḻippaṭum aṉparkaḷ vaṟumai nīkkiyē poḻiṟpaṭum taṇikaiyil potinta poṉṉaiyē.
translation: Alas, trapped in the wicked illusion of beautiful women, my heart became blameworthy and I did not worship the hidden gold in grove-filled Thanigai, who dispels the poverty of the devotees following his path.
commentary: When the mind gets trapped by superficial beauty, it falls into spiritual poverty and feels unworthy. The divine presence in Thanigai is actually a hidden treasure of gold, ready to banish the poverty of any seeker who earnestly walks the path of grace.

translit: potitarum maṅkaiyar puḷakak koṅkaimēl vatitarum neñciṉēṉ matitti lēṉaiyō matitarum aṉpartam maṉattil eṇṇiya katitarum taṇikaivāḻ kaṟpa kattaiyē.
translation: Alas, my heart dwells upon the thrilling breasts of beautiful women. I have not revered the wish-fulfilling tree residing in Thanigai, who grants the liberation desired in the minds of wise devotees.
commentary: The mind is easily trapped by physical desire, causing deep regret when it ignores the divine. Vallalar compares the Lord at Thanigai (a sacred hill town) to a heavenly wish-fulfilling tree that grants ultimate liberation to devoted seekers. He laments that while wise people focus their minds on this lasting freedom, his own attention remains caught up in passing sensual pleasures.

translit: vāṉpiṟantār pukaḻtaṇikai malaiyaik kaṇṭu vaḷḷalē niṉpukaḻai makiḻntu kūṟēṉ tēṉpiṟanta malarkkuḻalārk kāḷā vāḷā tirikiṉṟēṉ purikiṉṟēṉ tīmai nāḷum ūṉpiṟanta uṭalōmpi avamē vāḻnāḷ oḻikkiṉṟēṉ paḻikkāḷāy uṟṟēṉ antō ēṉpiṟantēṉ ēṉpiṟantēṉ pāvi yēṉyāṉ eṉkuṟaiyai evarkkeṭuttiṅ kiyampu kēṉē.
translation: I do not look at Thanigai hill, praised by the celestials, and joyfully speak your praise, O benevolent Lord. Enslaved to women with honey-laden flower-decked hair, I wander aimlessly. I commit evil every day. Cherishing this flesh-born body, I waste my days in vain. Alas, I have become a subject of blame. Why was I born? Why was I born, sinner that I am? To whom can I express my shortcomings here?
commentary: The speaker asks why he was even born if his life is spent entirely on bodily desires. He feels trapped by his pursuit of physical beauty and comfort, realizing that these daily distractions keep him from looking toward the divine. In his despair, he brings his deep vulnerability directly to the Lord, knowing no one else can hear his failings.

translit: meyyāvō naṟṟaṇikai malaiyaic cārntu mēṉmaiyuṟum niṉpukaḻai virumpi ēttēṉ uyyāvō valneṟiyēṉ payaṉpa ṭāta ōti-aṉaiyēṉ eṭṭitaṉai ottēṉ aṉpar poyyā-ō ṭeṉamaṭavār pōkam vēṭṭēṉ pulaiyaṉēṉ caṟṟēṉum puṉitam illēṉ aiyāvō nāṇāmal pāvi yēṉyāṉ yārkkeṭutteṉ kuṟaitaṉṉai aṟaiku vēṉē.
