Precious son of the Lord who swallowed poison out of loving compassion, rare ambrosia. You bestowed grace when the creator, the preserver, and the destroyer of the universe praised you. O companion who destroys the cruel birth that breeds sorrow, O dawn of bliss. O great flame appearing on the beautiful peacock, you wielded the spear to save the lives of the celestial gods when they fell exhausted by affliction. O Saiva gem abiding in the shrine of Thanigachalam! O Shanmuga!
commentary: The world often feels harsh and full of cruel-hearted people, and Vallalar laments getting lost in this painful environment. He seeks rescue from a God defined by absolute self-sacrifice. He recalls the traditional story of Lord Siva swallowing lethal poison to save the universe, showing that true divine power is rooted in loving compassion. By appealing to this same mercy, he hopes to be lifted out of worldly sorrow and the cycle of rebirth.

tamil: மாலும் அயனும் உருத்திரனும் வானத் தவரும் மானிடரும்
மாவும் புள்ளும் ஊர்வனவும் மலையும் கடலும் மற்றவையும்
ஆலும் கதியும் சதகோடி அண்டப் பரப்புந் தானாக
அன்றோர் வடிவம் மேருவிற்கொண் டருளுந் தூய அற்புதமே
வேலும் மயிலும் கொண்டுருவாய் விளையாட் டியற்றும் வித்தகமே
வேதப் பொருளே மதிச்சடைசேர் விமலன் தனக்கோர் மெய்ப்பொருளே
சாலும் சுகுணத் திருமலையே தவத்தோர் புகழும் தற்பரனே
தணிகா சலமாம் தலத்தமர்ந்த சைவ மணியே சண்முகனே.
translit: mālum ayaṉum uruttiraṉum vāṉat tavarum māṉiṭarum māvum puḷḷum ūrvaṉavum malaiyum kaṭalum maṟṟavaiyum ālum katiyum catakōṭi aṇṭap parappun tāṉāka aṉṟōr vaṭivam mēruviṟkoṇ ṭaruḷun tūya aṟputamē vēlum mayilum koṇṭuruvāy viḷaiyāṭ ṭiyaṟṟum vittakamē vētap poruḷē maticcaṭaicēr vimalaṉ taṉakkōr meypporuḷē cālum cukuṇat tirumalaiyē tavattōr pukaḻum taṟparaṉē taṇikā calamām talattamarnta caiva maṇiyē caṇmukaṉē.
translation: Vishnu, Brahma, Rudra, celestials, humans, beasts, birds, reptiles, mountains, oceans, and all other things, their destinies, and the expanse of a billion universes all became you when you graciously assumed that singular form upon Mount Meru long ago. O pure wonder. O wise Lord who takes form with the spear and the peacock to enact your divine play. You are the essence of the Vedas. You are the supreme truth taught to the flawless Lord whose matted hair holds the moon. O holy mountain of abundant virtues, O Supreme Being praised by ascetics. O Saiva gem abiding in the shrine of Thanigachalam! O Shanmuga!
commentary: The divine is revealed here as the vast, all-encompassing reality that contains every universe and every living creature. Vallalar describes a cosmic vision where gods, humans, animals, and entire worlds merge into a single divine form. Even though the Lord takes on specific appearances like a warrior with a spear and peacock, he remains the supreme truth that transcends all shapes. He is the original source who even teaches the highest wisdom to the other gods.

tamil: ஏதம் நிறுத்தும் இவ்வுலகத் தியல்பின் வாழ்க்கை யிடத்தெளியேன்
எண்ணி அடங்காப் பெருந்துயர்கொண் டெந்தாய் அந்தோ இளைக்கின்றேன்
வேதம் நிறுத்தும் நின்கமல மென்தாள் துணையே துணைஅல்லால்
வேறொன் றறியேன் அஃதறிந்திவ் வினையேற் கருள வேண்டாவோ
போத நிறுத்தும் சற்குருவே புனித ஞானத் தறிவுருவே
பொய்யர் அறியாப் பரவெளியே புரம்மூன் றெரித்தோன் தரும்ஒளியே
சாதல் நிறுத்தும் அவருள்ளத் தலம்தாள் நிறுத்தும் தயாநிதியே
தணிகா சலமாம் தலத்தமர்ந்த சைவ மணியே சண்முகனே.
translit: ētam niṟuttum ivvulakat tiyalpiṉ vāḻkkai yiṭatteḷiyēṉ eṇṇi aṭaṅkāp peruntuyarkoṇ ṭentāy antō iḷaikkiṉṟēṉ vētam niṟuttum niṉkamala meṉtāḷ tuṇaiyē tuṇai-allāl vēṟoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ aḵtaṟintiv viṉaiyēṟ karuḷa vēṇṭāvō pōta niṟuttum caṟkuruvē puṉita ñāṉat taṟivuruvē poyyar aṟiyāp paraveḷiyē purammūṉ ṟerittōṉ tarumoḷiyē cātal niṟuttum avaruḷḷat talamtāḷ niṟuttum tayānitiyē taṇikā calamām talattamarnta caiva maṇiyē caṇmukaṉē.
translation: Living in this worldly nature that breeds affliction, I am a poor soul. Bearing immeasurable great sorrow, O my father, alas, I grow weary. I know no other support than the true refuge of your soft lotus feet established by the Vedas. Knowing this, should you not bestow grace upon me, burdened by karma? O true Guru who establishes wisdom, O embodiment of pure spiritual knowledge. O supreme space unknown to the deceitful, O light given by the Lord who burned the three cities. O treasure of compassion who plants your feet in the hearts of those who conquer death. O Saiva gem abiding in the shrine of Thanigachalam! O Shanmuga!
commentary: Ordinary worldly life drains the spirit and brings deep exhaustion. Vallalar cries out for help, knowing that the only lasting refuge is the wisdom offered by the true spiritual guide. He describes God as a pure, vast space of spiritual knowledge that deceitful minds can never enter or understand. For those who live in truth, this divine grace takes root in their hearts and offers the power to conquer death itself.

tamil: முருகா எனநின் றேத்தாத மூட ரிடம்போய் மதிமயங்கி
முன்னும் மடவார் முலைமுகட்டின் முயங்கி அலைந்தே நினைமறந்தேன்
உருகா வஞ்ச மனத்தேனை உருத்தீர்த் தியமன் ஒருபாசத்
துடலும் நடுங்க விசிக்கில்அவர்க் குரைப்ப தறியேன் உத்தமனே
பருகா துள்ளத் தினித்திருக்கும் பாலே தேனே பகர்அருட்செம்
பாகே தோகை மயில்நடத்தும் பரமே யாவும் படைத்தோனே
தருகா தலித்தோன் முடிகொடுத்த தரும துரையே தற்பரனே
தணிகா சலமாந் தலத்தமர்ந்த சைவ மணியே சண்முகனே.
translit: murukā eṉaniṉ ṟēttāta mūṭa riṭampōy matimayaṅki muṉṉum maṭavār mulaimukaṭṭiṉ muyaṅki alaintē niṉaimaṟantēṉ urukā vañca maṉattēṉai uruttīrt tiyamaṉ orupācat tuṭalum naṭuṅka vicikkilavark kuraippa taṟiyēṉ uttamaṉē parukā tuḷḷat tiṉittirukkum pālē tēṉē pakararuṭcem pākē tōkai mayilnaṭattum paramē yāvum paṭaittōṉē tarukā talittōṉ muṭikoṭutta taruma turaiyē taṟparaṉē taṇikā calamān talattamarnta caiva maṇiyē caṇmukaṉē.
translation: I went to fools who do not stand and praise you saying "Murugan." Utterly deluded, I wandered about, embracing the breasts of women, and forgot you. I have an unmelting, deceitful heart. When the god of death angrily destroys my form and binds me with his noose, making my body tremble, I do not know what to say to him, O supreme Lord. O milk, honey, and praised red syrup of grace that tastes sweet in the heart even without being drunk. O Supreme Lord who rides the beautiful peacock, creator of all. O Lord of dharma who gave the crown to Indra who loved the celestial tree. O Supreme Being. O Saiva gem abiding in the shrine of Thanigachalam! O Shanmuga!
commentary: Looking back at human frailty, Vallalar expresses deep regret for chasing fleeting physical pleasures and seeking the company of worldly fools. He fears the final moment of death, knowing that a hard, deceitful heart will have no defense when the end comes. Yet he finds hope in the overwhelming sweetness of divine grace, which he describes as milk and honey that can be tasted directly in the heart without ever drinking it physically. This inner sweetness is the soul's ultimate salvation.

translit: ulakiyaṟ kaṭuñcurat tuḻaṉṟu nāḷtoṟum alakilven tuyarkiḷait taḻuṅku neñcamē ilakuciṟ parakuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil kalakamil iṉpamām katiki ṭaikkumē.
translation: O mind, wandering daily in the harsh wasteland of worldly life, multiplying endless cruel sorrows! If you apply the sacred ash chanting, "O Guha, the radiant supreme spirit," you will attain the state of undisturbed bliss.
commentary: Worldly life often feels like a dry and exhausting desert that only produces more sorrow. The remedy given here is a physical act of devotion paired with a spiritual one: applying sacred ash to the body while calling on Guha, a name for Lord Murugan, who represents the light of the supreme spirit. This simple practice anchors the wandering mind in steady joy.

translit: maruḷuṟum ulakilām vāḻkkai vēṇṭiyē iruḷuṟu tuyarkkaṭal iḻiyum neñcamē teruḷuṟu nīṟṟiṉaic civa-eṉ ṟuṭkoḷil aruḷuṟu vāḻkkaiyil amartal uṇmaiyē.
translation: O mind, desiring the life of this deluded world and sinking into the dark ocean of sorrow! If you partake of the clarity-giving sacred ash chanting, "Siva," you will truly abide in a life full of grace.
commentary: The mind constantly chases worldly desires, only to drown in sadness when things inevitably fail. Chanting the name of God while partaking of the sacred ash breaks this delusion, shifting the mind's focus from temporary cravings to a lasting life of grace.

translit: valviṉaip pakutiyāl mayaṅki vañcartam kolviṉaik kuḻiyiṭaik kutikkum neñcamē ilviṉaic caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil nalviṉai paḻukkumōr nāṭu vāykkumē.
translation: O mind, deluded by the force of hard karma and leaping into the deadly pits of deceitful people! If you apply the sacred ash chanting, "O Shanmuga who destroys karma," you will attain a realm where good deeds yield their ripe fruit.
commentary: Bad habits and past actions (karma) often drag a person into toxic situations and bad company. Calling on Shanmuga, the six-faced Lord Murugan, cuts through this heavy momentum. It protects the individual from deceit and redirects their path toward a life where goodness can actually thrive.

translit: kaṭumpulaik karuttartam karuttiṉ vaṇṇamē viṭumpuṉal eṉattuyar viḷaikkum neñcamē iṭumpukaḻc caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil naṭuṅkumac camniṉai naṇṇaṟ keṉṟumē.
translation: O mind, yielding to the will of those with cruel intentions and pouring forth sorrow like rushing water! If you apply the sacred ash chanting, "O glorious Shanmuga," trembling fear will never approach you.
commentary: A weak mind easily surrenders to the demands of cruel or selfish people, leading to a flood of misery and anxiety. The physical touch of the sacred ash, paired with the spoken name of God, acts as a shield. It grants an inner strength that banishes fear completely.

translit: aṉpilā vañcartam avalac cūḻalil eṉpilāp puḻu-eṉa iraṅku neñcamē iṉpaṟāc caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil tuṉpuṟāt taṉikkatic cūḻal vāykkumē.
translation: O mind, suffering like a boneless worm in the wretched company of loveless and deceitful people! If you apply the sacred ash chanting, "O Shanmuga of endless joy," you will attain the unique realm of liberation free from sorrow.
commentary: Without love and compassion, human society becomes a miserable trap where people feel as helpless as crushed worms. Turning to God promises a permanent escape from this cruelty. It leads to a state of independent joy, entirely free from the pain inflicted by a loveless world.

translit: . ceṟivilā vañcakac celvar vāyilil aṟivilā tuḻalumeṉ avala neñcamē eṟivilāc caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil maṟivilāc civakati vāyil vāykkumē.
translation: O my sorrowful heart, wandering senselessly at the doors of deceitful and shallow wealthy people. If you wear the sacred ash while chanting "Flawless Shanmuga", you will attain the gateway to the unobstructed state of Siva.
commentary: The poet addresses his own heart, telling it to stop begging at the doors of the wealthy and deceitful. He promises that chanting the name of Shanmuga (the six-faced Lord Murugan) while wearing sacred ash will open the door to the ultimate spiritual freedom of Siva.

translit: maṟitaru kaṇṇiṉār mayakkat tāḻntuvīṇ veṟiyoṭu malaintiṭar viḷaikkum neñcamē neṟiciva caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil muṟikoḷī-i niṉṟa-uṉ mūṭam tīrumē.
translation: O heart, struggling in frenzy and causing affliction by vainly sinking into the delusion of deer-eyed women. If you wear the sacred ash while chanting "Siva Shanmuga, the true path", your deeply rooted ignorance will be destroyed.
commentary: Here the mind is caught in the frenzy of physical desire and sensual distraction. Chanting the divine name and wearing the sacred ash acts as a cure, clearing away deeply rooted ignorance to reveal the true path.

translit: kāyamām kāṉalaik karuti nāḷtoṟum māyamām kāṉiṭai varuntum neñcamē nēyamām caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil tōyamām perumpiṇit tuṉpam nīṅkumē.
translation: O heart, desiring the mirage of this body and suffering daily in the forest of illusion. If you wear the sacred ash while chanting "Beloved Shanmuga", the sorrow of clinging great diseases will depart.
commentary: The physical body is compared to a mirage in a forest of illusion, bringing only suffering to those who cling to it. Devotion to the divine cures the mind of this worldly sickness and removes all sorrow.

translit: caticeyum maṅkaiyar tamatu kaṇvalai matikeṭa aḻuntiyē vaṇaṅkum neñcamē niticiva caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil vatitarum ulakiluṉ varuttam tīrumē.
translation: O heart, losing your sense and sinking down in submission to the ensnaring eyes of deceitful women. If you wear the sacred ash while chanting "Siva Shanmuga, our true wealth", your suffering in this inhabited world will end.
commentary: The heart often loses its reason, surrendering to the trap of worldly attractions and physical beauty. Real wealth is found in the divine, and turning to it brings an end to the suffering of earthly life.

translit: pacaiyaṟu vañcakar pāṟceṉ ṟēṅkiyē vacaipeṟa nāḷtoṟum varuntu neñcamē icaiciva caṇmuka eṉṟu nīṟiṭil ticaipeṟa matipparuṉ ciṟumai nīṅkumē.
translation: O heart, yearning after loveless deceivers and suffering daily to earn only blame. If you wear the sacred ash while chanting "Glorious Siva Shanmuga", people in all directions will respect you and your degradation will vanish.
commentary: Chasing after the favor of loveless worldly people brings only disappointment and blame. True dignity comes from spiritual devotion, washing away all worldly degradation and elevating the soul.

tamil: யாரை யுங்கடு விழியினால் மயக்குறும் ஏந்திழை அவர்வெந்நீர்த்
தாரை தன்னையும் விரும்பிவீழ்த் தாழ்ந்தஎன் தனக்கருள் உண்டேயோ
காரை முட்டிஅப் புறம்செலும் செஞ்சுடர்க் கதிரவன் இவர்ஆழித்
தேரை எட்டுறும் பொழில்செறி தணிகையில் தேவர்கள் தொழும்தேவே.
translit: yārai yuṅkaṭu viḻiyiṉāl mayakkuṟum ēntiḻai avarvennīrt tārai taṉṉaiyum virumpivīḻt tāḻnta-eṉ taṉakkaruḷ uṇṭēyō kārai muṭṭi-ap puṟamcelum ceñcuṭark katiravaṉ ivarāḻit tērai eṭṭuṟum poḻilceṟi taṇikaiyil tēvarkaḷ toḻumtēvē.
translation: O Lord worshipped by the gods in Thanigai, where dense groves reach the wheeled chariot of the red-rayed sun as it pierces the clouds and journeys beyond! Is there grace for me, who fell low by desiring the foul streams of women who wear fine ornaments and bewitch everyone with their piercing glances?
commentary: The towering height of the sacred landscape stands in sharp contrast to the depths of worldly desire. Vallalar describes the shrine of Thanigai as so magnificent that its groves touch the sun. He sees himself, by contrast, as utterly degraded by physical lust, and asks if divine grace is still open to someone who has sunk so low.

tamil: மறிக்கும் வேற்கணார் மலக்குழி ஆழ்ந்துழல் வன்தசை அறும்என்பைக்
கறிக்கும் நாயினும் கடையநாய்க் குன்திருக் கருணையும் உண்டேயோ
குறிக்கும் வேய்மணி களைக்கதிர் இரதவான் குதிரையைப் புடைத்தெங்கும்
தெறிக்கும் நல்வளம் செறிதிருத் தணிகையில் தேவர்கள் தொழும்தேவே.
translit: maṟikkum vēṟkaṇār malakkuḻi āḻntuḻal vaṉtacai aṟumeṉpaik kaṟikkum nāyiṉum kaṭaiyanāyk kuṉtiruk karuṇaiyum uṇṭēyō kuṟikkum vēymaṇi kaḷaikkatir iratavāṉ kutiraiyaip puṭaitteṅkum teṟikkum nalvaḷam ceṟitirut taṇikaiyil tēvarkaḷ toḻumtēvē.
translation: O Lord worshipped by the gods in holy Thanigai, rich with fertility, where pearls springing from tall bamboos strike the horses of the sun's heavenly chariot and scatter everywhere! Is there your holy grace for me, a dog worse than a street dog that gnaws on dry fleshless bones, having sunk and wallowed in the foul pit of women with spear-like eyes?
commentary: Physical lust is compared here to a starving dog gnawing on dry bones. Vallalar uses this harsh image to show how empty and unfulfilling selfish worldly desires actually are. He places his own sense of deep unworthiness against the vibrant purity of Thanigai, where the natural world is so exalted that pearls from its tall bamboos scatter against the horses of the sun.

tamil: பிரியம் மேயவன் மடந்தையர் தங்களைப் பிடித்தலைத் திடுவஞ்சக்
கரிய பேயினும் பெரியபேய்க் குன்திருக் கருணையும் உண்டேயோ
அரிய மால்அயன் இந்திரன் முதலினோர் அமர்உல கறிந்தப்பால்
தெரிய ஓங்கிய சிகரிசூழ் தணிகையில் தேவர்கள் தொழும்தேவே.
translit: piriyam mēyavaṉ maṭantaiyar taṅkaḷaip piṭittalait tiṭuvañcak kariya pēyiṉum periyapēyk kuṉtiruk karuṇaiyum uṇṭēyō ariya mālayaṉ intiraṉ mutaliṉōr amarula kaṟintappāl teriya ōṅkiya cikaricūḻ taṇikaiyil tēvarkaḷ toḻumtēvē.
translation: O Lord worshipped by the gods in Thanigai, surrounded by towering peaks visible even beyond the known heavenly realms of the great Vishnu, Brahma, Indra, and others! Is there your holy grace for me, a great demon worse than a deceitful black demon, as I seize affectionate women and cause them distress?
commentary: The holy peaks of Thanigai rise far above the traditional heavens of Hindu gods like Brahma, Vishnu, and Indra. Looking up at that supreme height, Vallalar feels the crushing weight of his own faults, calling himself a cruel demon for the way his selfish attachments have distressed others. By asking if grace is still available even to him, he makes clear that divine compassion remains his absolute and only hope.

translit: cīrvaḷar kuvaḷait tārvaḷar puyaṉār civaṉārtam pērvaḷar makaṉār kārvaḷar taṇikaip perumāṉār ērvaḷar mayilmēl ūrvaḷar niyamat tiṭaivantāl vārvaḷar mulaiyār ārvaḷar killār mayalammā.
translation: The renowned son of Lord Siva wears flourishing water-lily garlands on his shoulders. He is the Lord of cloud-capped Thanigai. If he comes riding his beautiful peacock through our town's thriving streets, which woman with bound breasts will not succumb to infatuation, O mother?
commentary: In classical Tamil poetry, the divine is often approached through the metaphor of human love. Here, the soul is a young woman watching the Lord process through her town. His beauty is so absolute that all earthly composure vanishes the moment he appears.

translit: mantā ramcēr paimpoḻi liṉkaṇ mayilēṟi vantār antō kaṇṭaṉaṉ aṅkai vaḷaikāṇēṉ cantā ramcūḻ taṇkiḷar cāral taṇikēcar tantār eṉpāl tantār eṉṉait tantārē.
translation: He came riding his peacock to the green grove filled with mandaram trees. Alas, I saw him, and now I cannot find the bangles on my hands. The Lord of Thanigai, whose cool mountain slopes are surrounded by sandalwood trees, gave himself to me. He gave himself, and he gave me back to myself.
commentary: Slipping bangles are an ancient poetic symbol for lovesickness, showing that the body pines and the wrists have grown thin. Yet this divine romance brings deep spiritual fulfillment. By giving himself to her completely, the Lord awakens the soul to its own true nature.

translit: natiyum matiyum potiyum caṭaiyār naviṉmālum vitiyun tuti-aim mukaṉār makaṉār mikucīrum nitiyum patiyum katiyum taruvār neṭuvēlār vatiyum mayiṉmēl varuvār malarē varumāṟē.
translation: He is the son of the five-faced Lord Siva whose matted hair holds the river and the moon, and who is praised by Vishnu and Brahma. He wields the tall spear and grants immense wealth, treasure, a domain, and liberation. He comes riding the peacock where he resides. He comes softly like a flower.
commentary: The poem praises Murugan as the supreme cosmic ruler and as an intimate lover. He wields the power to grant immense earthly wealth and ultimate spiritual liberation. Still, he approaches the devoted soul as softly as a blooming flower.

translit: cantār varaiyuḷ cintā maṇinēr taṇikēcar mantā nilammē vuntār maṟukil mayilēṟi vantār nilavōr centā maraiyiṉ malarvācak kontār kuḻaleṉ nilaiyuṅ kalaiyuṅ koṇṭārē.
translation: The Lord of Thanigai is like a wish-fulfilling gem on the mountain of sandalwood. He wears a mandaram garland and came riding his peacock through the street. He took away my steady composure and my garments, while my thick hair carries the fragrance of red lotuses blooming in the moonlight.
commentary: When the divine enters the soul's awareness, the ego's usual defenses are entirely swept away. The loss of steady composure and garments represents the total surrender of worldly pride and self-control. The devotee is left completely exposed and transformed by grace.

translit: tantē nayamām mātavar pukaḻum taṇikēcar cantē ṉoḻivāy antēṉ moḻiyāy taṉi-iṉṟu vantēṉ iṉimēl vārēṉ eṉṟār maṉamāḻki nontēṉ mulaimī tavvurai eṉṟār nuvaleṉṉē.
translation: The Lord of Thanigai is praised by great sages who practice sweet charity. He said, "O woman whose mouth flows with sweet nectar, whose words are sweet as honey! I came alone today, and I will not come again." My heart melted and ached. Then he playfully spoke that same word to mean he would embrace my breasts. What can I say of this?
commentary: This verse turns on a playful double meaning, matching the poem's theme of subtle and clever gestures. The Lord first causes her distress by seeming to say he will never return. He then playfully shifts the meaning of the spoken Tamil words to an intimate promise of physical embrace, turning her sudden sorrow into delight.

translit: taṇtaṇi kāntaḷorcaṇpaka malariṉ taḷarveytat teṇṭaṇi nīlamorceṅkuva ḷaiyiṉiṟ ṟikaḻvēṉpāl vaṇṭaṇi kēcarum vantaruḷ vārō vārārō toṇṭaṇi vīroru cōtiṭa mēṉum collīrē.
translation: As the cool gloriosa lily and champak flower wither, I shine like the clear blue lotus and red water lily. Will the Lord of Thanigai with bee-adorned hair come to grace me or not? O devoted friends adorned in service, tell me at least an astrological prediction.
commentary: The soul aches for God and looks for any sign of hope. Taking the voice of a lovesick woman, the devotee describes her physical fading through the image of wilting flowers, while her tear-filled eyes shine like water lilies. Desperate for comfort, she begs her companions to consult the stars and predict if the Lord will arrive to save her.

translit: kāmalar naṟavuk kēmalar mūviru kālēnī tēmalar taṇikait tēvar maruṅkil cērvāyēl āmala ruṭaiyāṭ keṉpeyar palavām avaiyuḷḷē ōmalar aṭikēḷ oṉṟiṉai oṉṟeṉ ṟuraiyāyē.
translation: O six-legged bee seeking honey from the forest flowers! If you reach the presence of the Lord of Thanigai rich with sweet blossoms, tell Him that I possess many names like the goddess seated on the lotus. Among those names, O bee at His flower-like feet, speak one name and say that I am united with Him.
commentary: In the tradition of Tamil love poetry, nature itself acts as a bridge between the lonely soul and God. Here, the devotee sends a wandering bee as a messenger to the Lord of Thanigai. She asks the insect to whisper her name at His feet. She hopes this simple reminder will stir His compassion and draw Him back to her.

translit: tēṭuṅ kiḷinī niṉṉai viḷampit tiru-aṉṉār aṭun taṇikaiyil eṉuyir aṉṉār arukēpōyk kūṭum taṉamicai eṉpeyar vaittak kōtaikkē īṭum keṭa-iṉ ṟeṉṉaiyum īntaruḷ eṉpāyē.
translation: O searching parrot! Announce yourself and approach the Lord who is my very life in beautiful Thanigai. Speak to Him on behalf of this garlanded girl who holds His name upon her breasts. Tell Him to banish her distress and grant her His grace today.
commentary: The devotee now asks a parrot to carry her message. She tells the bird to describe how deeply she cherishes the Lord, holding His very name close to her heart like a physical garland. She asks the parrot to beg for His grace and plead with Him to end her spiritual agony today.

translit: poṉṉai iruttum poṉmalar ekiṉap puḷḷēnī aṉṉai ikaḻntē aṅkalar ceyvāṉ aṉurākam taṉṉai aḷikkun taṇṭaṇi kēcar tampāṟpōy eṉṉai ikaḻntāḷ eṉceyal koṇṭāḷ eṉpāyē.
translation: O swan resting on the golden lotus where the goddess of wealth resides! My mother scorns me, and the town gossips about the love the cool Lord of Thanigai has given me. Go to Him and say that she is despised here and that You have completely taken away her agency.
commentary: The longing for God often separates the spiritual seeker from ordinary society. The devotee tells a swan messenger that her mother scorns her and the town gossips about her intense devotion. She asks the bird to tell the Lord that she has completely lost her own will, surrendering her entire agency to His grace.

tamil: வதியும் தணிகையில் வாழ்வுறும் என்கண் மணி அன்னார்
translit: vatiyum taṇikaiyil vāḻvuṟum eṉkaṇ maṇi aṉṉār matiyun taḻalkeṭa māmayiṉ mītivaṇ varuvārēl titiyum puvipukal niṉpeyar neṟiyait terivippāṉ natiyun tuṇavuta vuvaṉaṅ koṭinī naṭavāyē.
translation: O forest creeper thriving by the river! My Lord, the very pupil of my eye, dwells in Thanigai. If He comes here on His great peacock to extinguish the scorching fire of the moon, please walk as a messenger to reveal your renowned path to the world.
commentary: To a person suffering the pain of separation from God, even the cool light of the moon feels like a scorching fire. The devotee begs a forest vine to act as her messenger. She longs for the Lord to arrive on His peacock, bringing His divine presence to cool her burning grief and restore her soul.

translit: maṉṟēr taṇikaiyi ṉiṉṟīr katitara vantīrō eṉṟē ṉacaitaru miṉṟēṉ moḻiyāy yāṉuṉpāl iṉṟē curarula keytiṭa vantē ṉeṉṟārkāṇ kuṉṟēr mulaiyā yeṉṉaṭi yavarcoṟ kuṟitāṉē.
translation: I asked, "You who stand in beautiful Thanigai, have you come to grant me liberation?" He replied, "O girl whose words are like sweet moving honey, I have come to you today so that you may reach the realm of the gods." O friend with breasts like hills, what is the meaning of his words?
commentary: The young woman asks the Lord for ultimate spiritual liberation, but he replies with playful flirtation. By promising to take her to the world of the gods, he uses the language of an earthly suitor. In this poetic tradition, God often speaks in riddles and romantic promises, testing the soul's true devotion and leaving the heroine to guess at his real meaning.

translit: cētaṉa nantār ceṉṟu vaṇaṅkun tiṟalvēlār tātaṉa vaṇṇat tuḷḷoḷir kiṉṟa taṇikēcar mātaṉa muntā vanteṉa vantē vātātā ātaṉa meṉṟā reṉṉaṭi yammā vavarcūtē.
translation: He is the wielder of the mighty spear, whom wise beings of unfailing consciousness go and worship. He is the Lord of Thanigai who shines within a pollen-like hue. He approached me and said, "Give me your great treasure." Then he said, "Come, give, give me a seat." O my friend, what is the trickery behind his words?
commentary: The Lord of Thanigai is Murugan, the divine wielder of the spear of wisdom. Here he acts like a demanding visitor, asking the young woman to hand over her greatest treasure and give him a place to sit. In the language of love poetry, he sounds like a bold suitor. In the language of devotion, the treasure he demands is her pure love, and the seat he wants is a permanent place within her very heart.

tamil: கங்கையஞ் சடைசேர் முக்கட் கரும்பருள் மணியே போற்றி
அங்கையங் கனியே போற்றி அருட்பெருங் கடலே போற்றி
பங்கையன் முதலோர் போற்றும் பரம்பரஞ் சுடரே போற்றி
சங்கைதீர்த் தருளும் தெய்வச் சரவண பவனே போற்றி.
translit: kaṅkaiyañ caṭaicēr mukkaṭ karumparuḷ maṇiyē pōṟṟi aṅkaiyaṅ kaṉiyē pōṟṟi aruṭperuṅ kaṭalē pōṟṟi paṅkaiyaṉ mutalōr pōṟṟum paramparañ cuṭarē pōṟṟi caṅkaitīrt taruḷum teyvac caravaṇa pavaṉē pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the jewel of grace given by the three-eyed Lord whose matted locks hold the Ganges. Praise to the beautiful fruit resting in the palm of the hand. Praise to the great ocean of grace. Praise to the supreme light worshipped by Brahma and the other gods. Praise to the divine Saravanabhava who dispels doubts and grants grace.
commentary: Murugan is celebrated here as the precious son of Siva, the three-eyed Lord who holds the river Ganges in his hair. The image of a fruit resting in the palm of the hand shows that divine grace is not distant or hidden, but something close and entirely accessible to the seeker. Saravanabhava is a sacred name for Murugan, pointing to his legendary birth in a forest of reeds.

tamil: பனிப்பற அருளும் முக்கட் பரஞ்சுடர் ஒளியே போற்றி
இனிப்புறு கருணை வான்தேன் எனக்கருள் புரிந்தாய் போற்றி
துனிப்பெரும் பவந்தீர்த் தென்னைச் சுகம்பெற வைத்தோய் போற்றி
தனிப்பெருந் தவமே போற்றி சண்முகத் தரசே போற்றி.
translit: paṉippaṟa aruḷum mukkaṭ parañcuṭar oḷiyē pōṟṟi iṉippuṟu karuṇai vāṉtēṉ eṉakkaruḷ purintāy pōṟṟi tuṉipperum pavantīrt teṉṉaic cukampeṟa vaittōy pōṟṟi taṉipperun tavamē pōṟṟi caṇmukat taracē pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the supreme, radiant light of the three-eyed Lord who grants grace to dispel trembling fear. Praise to You who granted me the sweet, heavenly honey of compassion. Praise to You who destroyed my intensely sorrowful worldly birth and placed me in bliss. Praise to the singular, supreme penance. Praise to the six-faced King.
commentary: Divine compassion is described as a sweet, heavenly honey that cures the deep sorrow of continuous worldly births. The six-faced King is another traditional title for Murugan, who clears away all trembling fear and establishes the soul in permanent peace.

tamil: மணப்புது மலரே தெய்வ வான்சுவைக் கனியே போற்றி
தணப்பற அடியர்க் கின்பம் தரும்ஒரு தருவே போற்றி
கணப்பெருந் தலைவர் ஏத்தும் கழற்பதத் தரசே போற்றி
குணப்பெருங் குன்றே போற்றி குமரசற் குருவே போற்றி.
translit: maṇapputu malarē teyva vāṉcuvaik kaṉiyē pōṟṟi taṇappaṟa aṭiyark kiṉpam tarumoru taruvē pōṟṟi kaṇapperun talaivar ēttum kaḻaṟpatat taracē pōṟṟi kuṇapperuṅ kuṉṟē pōṟṟi kumaracaṟ kuruvē pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the fragrant fresh flower. Praise to the divine fruit of heavenly sweetness. Praise to the matchless tree that grants unceasing joy to devotees. Praise to the King whose feet, adorned with anklets, are praised by the great leaders of the celestial hosts. Praise to the vast mountain of virtues. Praise to Kumara, the true Guru.
commentary: God is pictured as a sheltering tree that provides unending joy to those who seek refuge. Kumara means the eternal youth, a name for Murugan honoring him as the ultimate teacher, or true Guru, who embodies a vast mountain of virtues.

tamil: பவம்பெறுஞ் சிறியேன் தன்னைப் பாதுகாத் தளித்தோய் போற்றி
நவம்பெறு நிலைக்கும் மேலாம் நண்ணிய நலமே போற்றி
சிவம்பெறும் பயனே போற்றி செங்கதிர் வேலோய் போற்றி.
translit: tavampeṟu muṉivaruḷḷat tāmarai amarntōy pōṟṟi pavampeṟuñ ciṟiyēṉ taṉṉaip pātukāt taḷittōy pōṟṟi navampeṟu nilaikkum mēlām naṇṇiya nalamē pōṟṟi civampeṟum payaṉē pōṟṟi ceṅkatir vēlōy pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to You who sits on the heart-lotus of ascetics rich in penance. Praise to You who protected and saved this lowly one trapped in worldly birth. Praise to the accessible goodness that stands above all attained states. Praise to the supreme fruit of attaining Sivam. Praise to the wielder of the radiant red spear.
commentary: True spiritual realization is found within the heart-lotus of dedicated seekers. Murugan is the wielder of the radiant red spear, a symbol of sharp spiritual wisdom that cuts through ignorance and leads directly to the supreme divine state of Sivam.

tamil: மூவடி வாகி நின்ற முழுமுதற் பரமே போற்றி
மாவடி அமர்ந்த முக்கண் மலைதரு மணியே போற்றி
சேவடி வழுத்தும் தொண்டர் சிறுமைதீர்த் தருள்வோய் போற்றி
தூவடி வேல்கைக் கொண்ட சுந்தர வடிவே போற்றி
translit: mūvaṭi vāki niṉṟa muḻumutaṟ paramē pōṟṟi māvaṭi amarnta mukkaṇ malaitaru maṇiyē pōṟṟi cēvaṭi vaḻuttum toṇṭar ciṟumaitīrt taruḷvōy pōṟṟi tūvaṭi vēlkaik koṇṭa cuntara vaṭivē pōṟṟi
translation: Praise to the whole and supreme reality that stands as the three forms. Praise to the jewel given by the mountain-daughter of the three-eyed Lord who sits beneath the great mango tree. Praise to You who dispels the misery of devotees who praise Your red feet and grants them grace. Praise to the beautiful form holding the pure, sharp spear.
commentary: The divine child is the precious gift of the Goddess Parvati, the mountain-daughter, and Siva, who is traditionally depicted sitting beneath a sacred mango tree. Devotion to this beautiful form and the pure, sharp spear of wisdom brings an end to all misery and opens the door to grace.

tamil: விண்ணுறு சுடரே என்னுள் விளங்கிய விளக்கே போற்றி
கண்ணுறு மணியே என்னைக் கலந்தநற் களிப்பே போற்றி
பண்ணுறு பயனே என்னைப் பணிவித்த மணியே போற்றி
எண்ணுறும் அடியார் தங்கட் கினியதெள் அமுதே போற்றி.
translit: viṇṇuṟu cuṭarē eṉṉuḷ viḷaṅkiya viḷakkē pōṟṟi kaṇṇuṟu maṇiyē eṉṉaik kalantanaṟ kaḷippē pōṟṟi paṇṇuṟu payaṉē eṉṉaip paṇivitta maṇiyē pōṟṟi eṇṇuṟum aṭiyār taṅkaṭ kiṉiyateḷ amutē pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the flame abiding in the sky. Praise to the lamp shining within me. Praise to the pupil of my eye. Praise to the good joy that mingled with me. Praise to the fruit of music. Praise to the gem who made me bow down. Praise to the sweet, clear nectar for the devotees who contemplate you.
commentary: The poem addresses God as a vast cosmic light in the sky and an intimate lamp burning within the heart. The divine is approached here not as a distant ruler, but as the very pupil of the eye and a sweet joy that mingles directly with the soul.

tamil: மறைஎலாம் பரவ நின்ற மாணிக்க மலையே போற்றி
சிறைஎலாம் தவிர்ந்து வானோர் திருவுறச் செய்தோய் போற்றி
குறைஎலாம் அறுத்தே இன்பம் கொடுத்தஎன் குருவே போற்றி
துறைஎலாம் விளங்கு ஞானச் சோதியே போற்றி போற்றி.
translit: maṟai-elām parava niṉṟa māṇikka malaiyē pōṟṟi ciṟai-elām tavirntu vāṉōr tiruvuṟac ceytōy pōṟṟi kuṟai-elām aṟuttē iṉpam koṭutta-eṉ kuruvē pōṟṟi tuṟai-elām viḷaṅku ñāṉac cōtiyē pōṟṟi pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the ruby mountain standing praised by all the scriptures. Praise to the one who removed all captivity and restored wealth to the celestials. Praise to my guru who severed all my flaws and gave me bliss. Praise, praise to the light of wisdom shining in every path.
commentary: This verse honours the divine as a majestic mountain praised by ancient scriptures and as a personal spiritual guide (guru). The grace of this inner teacher clears away the soul's flaws and shines as the light of wisdom across every path.

tamil: தாருகப் பதகன் தன்னைத் தடிந்தருள் செய்தோய் போற்றி
வேருகச் சூர மாவை வீட்டிய வேலோய் போற்றி
ஆருகச் சமயக் காட்டை அழித்தவெங் கனலே போற்றி
போருகத் தகரை ஊர்ந்த புண்ணிய மூர்த்தி போற்றி.
translit: tārukap patakaṉ taṉṉait taṭintaruḷ ceytōy pōṟṟi vērukac cūra māvai vīṭṭiya vēlōy pōṟṟi ārukac camayak kāṭṭai aḻittaveṅ kaṉalē pōṟṟi pōrukat takarai ūrnta puṇṇiya mūrtti pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the one who struck down the wicked Tarukan and bestowed grace. Praise to the wielder of the spear who destroyed the mango tree form of Suran so its roots were crushed. Praise to the fierce fire that destroyed the overgrown forest of religions. Praise to the holy Lord who rode the battle-ready ram.
commentary: The imagery draws on traditional accounts of the god Murugan destroying the demons Tarukan and Suran to represent the defeat of deep-rooted ignorance. Vallalar says plainly that the divine acts as a fierce fire that destroys the overgrown forest of religions. He teaches that sects and dogmas are false divisions that hide the ultimate truth, and only divine grace can burn them away.

tamil: சிங்கமா முகனைக் கொன்ற திறலுடைச் சிம்புள் போற்றி
துங்கவா ரணத்தோன் கொண்ட துயர்தவிர்த் தளித்தாய் போற்றி
செங்கண்மால் மருக போற்றி சிவபிரான் செல்வ போற்றி
எங்கள்ஆர் அமுதே போற்றி யாவர்க்கும் இறைவ போற்றி.
translit: ciṅkamā mukaṉaik koṉṟa tiṟaluṭaic cimpuḷ pōṟṟi tuṅkavā raṇattōṉ koṇṭa tuyartavirt taḷittāy pōṟṟi ceṅkaṇmāl maruka pōṟṟi civapirāṉ celva pōṟṟi eṅkaḷār amutē pōṟṟi yāvarkkum iṟaiva pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the powerful bird who killed the lion-faced demon. Praise to the one who removed the sorrow of the noble elephant and granted protection. Praise to the nephew of red-eyed Vishnu. Praise to the treasure of Lord Siva. Praise to our rare nectar. Praise to the Lord of all.
commentary: Drawing on classic stories of divine protection, the verse praises God for destroying fierce demonic forces and saving those in sorrow. It brings together the names of different deities, like Siva and Vishnu, to show that a single divine presence is the true Lord of all beings.

tamil: முத்தியின் முதல்வ போற்றி மூவிரு முகத்த போற்றி
சத்திவேற் கரத்த போற்றி சங்கரி புதல்வ போற்றி
சித்திதந் தருளும் தேவர் சிகாமணி போற்றி போற்றி
பத்தியின் விளைந்த இன்பப் பரம்பர போற்றி போற்றி.
translit: muttiyiṉ mutalva pōṟṟi mūviru mukatta pōṟṟi cattivēṟ karatta pōṟṟi caṅkari putalva pōṟṟi cittitan taruḷum tēvar cikāmaṇi pōṟṟi pōṟṟi pattiyiṉ viḷainta iṉpap parampara pōṟṟi pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the source of liberation. Praise to the six-faced Lord. Praise to the one holding the spear of power. Praise to the son of Sankari. Praise, praise to the crest-jewel of the gods who graciously grants spiritual attainments. Praise, praise to the supreme Lord of bliss blossoming from devotion.
commentary: The six-faced Lord holding the spear of power is a classic representation of Murugan, here praised as the supreme source of liberation. The passage shows that true spiritual attainments and ultimate bliss blossom naturally from a foundation of pure devotion.

tamil: தெருளுடை யோர்க்கு வாய்த்த சிவானந்தத் தேனே போற்றி
பொருளுடை மறையோர் உள்ளம் புகுந்தபுண் ணியமே போற்றி
மருளுடை மனத்தி னேனை வாழ்வித்த வாழ்வே போற்றி
அருளுடை அரசே எங்கள் அறுமுகத் தமுதே போற்றி.
translit: teruḷuṭai yōrkku vāytta civāṉantat tēṉē pōṟṟi poruḷuṭai maṟaiyōr uḷḷam pukuntapuṇ ṇiyamē pōṟṟi maruḷuṭai maṉatti ṉēṉai vāḻvitta vāḻvē pōṟṟi aruḷuṭai aracē eṅkaḷ aṟumukat tamutē pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the honey of supreme bliss attained by those of clear understanding! Praise to the merit that enters the hearts of those who know the true meaning of the scriptures! Praise to the life that gave life to me, a person whose mind is filled with delusion! Praise to the graceful King, our six-faced nectar!
commentary: The divine offers different gifts depending on a person's state of mind. To those with clear understanding, God is the sweet honey of bliss, and to those who know the scriptures, God is pure merit. Yet even for a mind filled with confusion, God becomes the very breath of life and an immediate source of rescue.

tamil: பொய்யனேன் பிழைகள் எல்லாம் பொறுத்திடல் வேண்டும் போற்றி
கையனேன் தன்னை இன்னும் காத்திடல் வேண்டும் போற்றி
மெய்யனே மெய்யர் உள்ளம் மேவிய விளைவே போற்றி
ஐயனே அப்ப னேஎம் அரசனே போற்றி போற்றி
translit: poyyaṉēṉ piḻaikaḷ ellām poṟuttiṭal vēṇṭum pōṟṟi kaiyaṉēṉ taṉṉai iṉṉum kāttiṭal vēṇṭum pōṟṟi meyyaṉē meyyar uḷḷam mēviya viḷaivē pōṟṟi aiyaṉē appa ṉē-em aracaṉē pōṟṟi pōṟṟi
translation: Praise to you, you must forgive all the faults of this false one! Praise to you, you must continue to protect this worthless one! Praise to the true one, the result that flourishes in the hearts of the truthful! Praise, praise to the Lord, the Father, our King!
commentary: True devotion requires a truthful heart. While God dwells as a living reality in those who are perfectly honest, this verse asks for patient forgiveness for those who still make mistakes. It is a plea for the divine to act as a protecting father and king, continuing to guide the soul despite its human flaws.

tamil: முருகநின் பாதம் போற்றி முளரியங் கண்ணற் கன்பாம்
மருகநின் கழல்கள் போற்றி வானவர் முதல்வ போற்றி
பெருகருள் வாரி போற்றி பெருங்குணப் பொருப்பே போற்றி
தருகநின் கருணை போற்றி சாமிநின் அடிகள் போற்றி.
translit: murukaniṉ pātam pōṟṟi muḷariyaṅ kaṇṇaṟ kaṉpām marukaniṉ kaḻalkaḷ pōṟṟi vāṉavar mutalva pōṟṟi perukaruḷ vāri pōṟṟi peruṅkuṇap poruppē pōṟṟi tarukaniṉ karuṇai pōṟṟi cāminiṉ aṭikaḷ pōṟṟi.
translation: Murugan, praise to your feet! Beloved nephew of the lotus-eyed one, praise to your ankleted feet! Praise to the foremost of the celestials! Praise to the ocean of abundant grace! Praise to the mountain of great qualities! Bestow your compassion upon me, praise to you! Swami, praise to your feet!
commentary: Here the verse names the divine explicitly as Murugan, praising his vast grace and perfect qualities. The lotus-eyed one refers to the god Vishnu, making Murugan his beloved nephew in the traditional family stories of the gods. The central prayer is a direct request for God to bestow pure compassion on the seeker.

tamil: கோதிலாக் குணத்தோய் போற்றி குகேசநின் பாதம் போற்றி
தீதிலாச் சிந்தை மேவும் சிவபரஞ் சோதி போற்றி
போதில்நான் முகனும் காணாப் பூரண வடிவ போற்றி
ஆதிநின் தாள்கள் போற்றி அநாதிநின் அடிகள் போற்றி.
translit: kōtilāk kuṇattōy pōṟṟi kukēcaniṉ pātam pōṟṟi tītilāc cintai mēvum civaparañ cōti pōṟṟi pōtilnāṉ mukaṉum kāṇāp pūraṇa vaṭiva pōṟṟi ātiniṉ tāḷkaḷ pōṟṟi anātiniṉ aṭikaḷ pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to you of flawless qualities! Lord of the heart's cave, praise to your feet! Praise to the supreme Jothi of Siva that abides in blameless minds! Praise to the perfect form unseen even by the four-faced creator seated on the flower! Primal one, praise to your feet! Beginningless one, praise to your feet!
commentary: God dwells deep within the human being as a supreme light, seated in the hidden cave of a pure mind. This divine presence is perfect and without beginning, existing far beyond the reach of traditional creator gods like the four-faced Brahma.

tamil: வேதமும் கலைகள் யாவும் விளம்பிய புலவ போற்றி
நாதமும் கடந்து நின்ற நாதநின் கருணை போற்றி
போதமும் பொருளும் ஆகும் புனிதநின் பாதம் போற்றி
ஆதரம் ஆகி என்னுள் அமர்ந்தஎன் அரசே போற்றி.
translit: vētamum kalaikaḷ yāvum viḷampiya pulava pōṟṟi nātamum kaṭantu niṉṟa nātaniṉ karuṇai pōṟṟi pōtamum poruḷum ākum puṉitaniṉ pātam pōṟṟi ātaram āki eṉṉuḷ amarnta-eṉ aracē pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the scholar who expounded the Vedas and all the arts! Praise to your compassion, O Lord who stands beyond primal sound! Praise to your feet, O pure one who is both knowledge and reality! Praise to my King who became my support and sat within me!
commentary: The divine is the source of all true knowledge, standing beyond even the primal sound that began the universe. Yet this supreme reality does not remain distant. It takes a seat directly inside the seeker as an inner king, offering permanent support and comfort.

tamil: என்னிரு கண்ணின் மேவும் இலங்கொளி மணியே போற்றி
பன்னிரு படைகொண் டோங்கும் பன்னிரு கரத்தோய் போற்றி
மின்னிரு நங்கை மாருள் மேவிய மணாள போற்றி
நின்னிரு பாதம் போற்றி நீள்வடி வேல போற்றி.
translit: eṉṉiru kaṇṇiṉ mēvum ilaṅkoḷi maṇiyē pōṟṟi paṉṉiru paṭaikoṇ ṭōṅkum paṉṉiru karattōy pōṟṟi miṉṉiru naṅkai māruḷ mēviya maṇāḷa pōṟṟi niṉṉiru pātam pōṟṟi nīḷvaṭi vēla pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise to the brightly shining gem resting in my two eyes. Praise to the one towering with twelve hands holding twelve weapons. Praise to the bridegroom united with two ladies of lightning. Praise to your two feet. Praise to the wielder of the long sharp spear.
commentary: This verse invokes the traditional form of Lord Murugan, celebrating his immense power through his twelve weapon-bearing hands and his iconic vel (spear). He is described alongside his two consorts, yet this vast, towering deity is also experienced intimately as a bright, guiding light resting right within the poet's own eyes.

translit: . mativaḷar caṭaimuṭi maṇitaru curarmuṭi maṇi-eṉkō pativaḷar caravaṇa pavanava civakuru pati-eṉkō tutivaḷar tuṇai-aṭi toḻumaṭi yavarpeṟu tuṇai-eṉkō nitivaḷar paracuka nilaipeṟum neṟitaru niṉaiyāṉē.
translation: Shall I call you the gem on the moon-crowned matted hair and the gem on the crowns of the gods? Shall I call you Saravanabhava of the sacred place and the new Lord Siva-Guru? Shall I call you the companion attained by devotees who worship your twin feet flourishing in praise? O Lord, you grant the path to the enduring state of supreme bliss filled with wealth.
commentary: The poet struggles to find a single title grand enough for the divine. He calls Murugan Saravanabhava (born in the reed forest) and the Siva-Guru, recalling the traditional story where the son becomes the teacher to his own father, Lord Siva. Ultimately, the deity is recognized not just by his lofty titles, but as the intimate companion of his devotees and the source of supreme bliss.

translit: murukā caraṇam caraṇameṉ ṟuṉpatam muṉṉi-uḷḷam urukāta nāyaṉai yēṟkuniṉ taṇṇaruḷ uṇṭukolō arukāta pāṟkaṭal mītē aṉantal amarntavaṉṟaṉ marukāmuk kaṇṇavaṉ maintā eḻilmayil vākaṉaṉē.
translation: O nephew of the Lord who rests in slumber upon the unfailing milky ocean. O son of the three-eyed Lord. O rider of the beautiful peacock. Is your cool grace available to me, a lowly dog whose heart fails to melt even while thinking of your feet and crying out for refuge in Murugan?
commentary: The speaker traces Murugan's divine lineage, naming him the son of the three-eyed Lord Siva and the nephew of Lord Vishnu, who rests on the cosmic milky ocean. Beside these grand family connections and his majestic peacock mount, the poet contrasts his own perceived unworthiness, wondering if divine grace can still reach a hardened heart that fails to melt in true devotion.

translit: ulakam paravum orumutalvā teyvat tilakam tikaḻiṭattut tēvē-ilakutirup puḷḷirukku vēḷurp puṉitā aṭiyēṉṟaṉ uḷḷirukkum tuṉpai oḻi.
translation: O single Primal Lord praised by the world. O God of the place shining like a divine mark on the forehead. O holy one of radiant and sacred Pullirukkuvelur. Eradicate the sorrow residing in the heart of your servant.
commentary: The focus shifts to a specific sacred location, placing the deity in the temple town of Pullirukkuvelur. Even as the poet calls upon him as the supreme primal Lord praised by the whole world, the request is deeply personal: a plea to wipe out the lingering sorrow in his own heart.

translit: cekkac civantē tikaḻorupāl paccaiyatāy akkaṭ paritipurat tārntōṅkum-mukkaṇ kuḻaikkarumpīṉ muttuk kumāra maṇiyē-eṉ piḻaikkiraṅki āḷutiyō pēcu.
translation: Radiant with deep red on one side and green on the other, towering high in Parithipuram. O gem Muthukumara born to the tender sugarcane goddess and the three-eyed Lord. Will you take pity on my faults and rule me? Speak.
commentary: The imagery beautifully blends the deity's parents: the deep red of Lord Siva and the vibrant green of the goddess Parvati, who is described as sweet as tender sugarcane. Addressing Murugan here as Muthukumara (the beautiful youth), the poet asks directly if the divine will overlook his human flaws and take him under his loving command.

tamil: திருமாலைப் பணிகொண்டு திகிரிகொண்ட தாருகனைச் செறித்து வாகைப்
பெருமாலை அணிதிணிதோள் பெருமானே ஒருமான்றன் பெண்மேற் காமர்
வருமாலை உடையவர்போல் மணமாலை புனைந்தமுழு மணியே முக்கட்
குருமாலைப் பொருள்உரைத்த குமாரகுரு வேபரம குருவே போற்றி.
translit: tirumālaip paṇikoṇṭu tikirikoṇṭa tārukaṉaic ceṟittu vākaip perumālai aṇitiṇitōḷ perumāṉē orumāṉṟaṉ peṇmēṟ kāmar varumālai uṭaiyavarpōl maṇamālai puṉaintamuḻu maṇiyē mukkaṭ kurumālaip poruḷuraitta kumārakuru vēparama kuruvē pōṟṟi.
translation: O Great Lord whose firm shoulders wear the grand garland of victory. You commanded Thirumal and destroyed the demon Tharukan who wielded a discus. O flawless gem, you wore a wedding garland for the daughter of a deer as if overcome by mortal lust. You explained the meaning of the supreme mantra to the three-eyed Lord. Praise to you, Kumara Guru, Supreme Guru.
commentary: Murugan is praised here in three great roles: the victorious warrior who defeated demons, the eager lover who married a forest maiden born of a deer, and the supreme teacher who instructed his own father, the great god Siva.

tamil: தோடேந்து கடப்பமலர்த் தொடையொடு செங்குவளை மலர்த்தொடையும் வேய்ந்து
பாடேந்தும் அறிஞர்தமிழ்ப் பாவொடுநா யடியேன்சொற் பாவும் ஏற்றுப்
பீடேந்தும் இருமடவார் பெட்பொடும்ஆங் கவர்கண்முலைப் பெரிய யானைக்
கோடேந்தும் அணிநெடுந்தோட் குமாரகுரு வேபரம குருவே போற்றி.
translit: tōṭēntu kaṭappamalart toṭaiyoṭu ceṅkuvaḷai malarttoṭaiyum vēyntu pāṭēntum aṟiñartamiḻp pāvoṭunā yaṭiyēṉcoṟ pāvum ēṟṟup pīṭēntum irumaṭavār peṭpoṭumāṅ kavarkaṇmulaip periya yāṉaik kōṭēntum aṇineṭuntōṭ kumārakuru vēparama kuruvē pōṟṟi.
translation: You wear a garland of petaled kadambu flowers and a garland of red water lilies. You accept the Tamil poems of renowned scholars along with the words of a dog like me. Embracing two glorious women with affection, your beautiful broad shoulders bear their breasts like the tusks of a great elephant. Praise to you, Kumara Guru, Supreme Guru.
commentary: Murugan is traditionally depicted with two wives and adorned with wild mountain flowers. The poet marvels that a majestic god, who receives the perfect poetry of learned scholars, is equally willing to accept the humble words of an ordinary person.

tamil: நீர்வேய்ந்த சடைமுடித்துத் தோலுடுத்து நீறணிந்து நிலவுங் கொன்றைத்
தார்வேய்ந்து விடங்கலந்த களங்காட்டி நுதலிடைஓர் தழற்கண் காட்டிப்
பேர்வேய்ந்த மணிமன்றில் ஆடுகின்ற பெரும்பித்தப் பெருமான் ஈன்ற
கூர்வேய்ந்த வேல்அணிதோள் குமாரகுரு வேபரம குருவே போற்றி.
translit: nīrvēynta caṭaimuṭittut tōluṭuttu nīṟaṇintu nilavuṅ koṉṟait tārvēyntu viṭaṅkalanta kaḷaṅkāṭṭi nutaliṭai-ōr taḻaṟkaṇ kāṭṭip pērvēynta maṇimaṉṟil āṭukiṉṟa perumpittap perumāṉ īṉṟa kūrvēynta vēlaṇitōḷ kumārakuru vēparama kuruvē pōṟṟi.
translation: You were begotten by the great, mad Lord who dances in the renowned hall of gems. He ties up his matted hair holding the river, wears an animal skin, smears himself with holy ash, wears a garland of shining konrai flowers, displays a poison-stained throat, and reveals an eye of fire on his forehead. O Lord whose shoulders are adorned with a sharp spear, praise to you, Kumara Guru, Supreme Guru.
commentary: This passage draws a vivid portrait of Siva as a fierce, wildly dancing god who wears river water in his hair, a throat stained blue by swallowed poison, and a fiery third eye. It praises Murugan as the son who inherits this immense divine power and carries it forward with his own sharp spear.

translit: peṇkuṇattil kaṭaippaṭum ōr pēykkuṇaṅkoḷ nāyēṉṟaṉ piḻaikaḷ ellām eṇkuṇappoṟ kuṉṟēniṉ tiru-uḷattil ciṟitēṉum eṇṇēl kaṇṭāy paṇkuṇattil ciṟantiṭumniṉ pattartamaip purappatupōl pāvi yēṉai vaṇkuṇattil purattiyilai yēṉumeṉaik kaiviṭēl vaṭivē lōṉē.
translation: O golden mountain of eight qualities, do not hold in your divine mind even slightly the faults of this dog possessing demonic traits, the lowest among feminine qualities. You protect your devotees who excel in sacred song. O Lord with the beautiful spear, even if you do not protect this sinner with your generous grace, do not abandon me.
commentary: In a raw expression of humility, the author calls himself an unruly dog burdened with the lowest traits. He begs the perfect god to overlook his deep flaws and never abandon him, even if he does not deserve the active protection given to true saints.

translit: cattivēl karattaniṉ caraṇam pōṟṟimeyp pattiyō ṭaruccaṉai payilum paṇpiṉāl mutticār kuvareṉa moḻital kēṭṭunal puttiyō ṭuṉpatam pukaḻvar puṇṇiyar.
translation: Praise to your feet, O Lord holding the spear of power in your hand. Hearing the teaching that those who practice worship with true devotion will attain liberation, virtuous people praise your feet with a clear mind.
commentary: Liberation is the ultimate spiritual freedom from the cycle of birth and death. The teaching here is simple: sincere, heartfelt devotion is the direct path to this freedom, a promise that guides wise people to seek the divine.

translit: tēṉē amutē civamē tavamē teḷivē-eṅ kōṉē kuruvē kulamē kuṇamē kukaṉēyō vāṉē vaḷiyē aṉalē puṉalē malaiyē-eṉ ūṉē uyirē uṇarvē eṉatuḷ uṟaivāṉē.
translation: O honey! O ambrosia! O Sivam! O penance! O clarity! O our King! O Guru! O lineage! O virtue! O Guha! O sky! O wind! O fire! O water! O mountain! O my flesh! O life! O consciousness! O One who dwells within me!
commentary: God is not just an outside force worshipped from afar. Here, the divine is recognized as the physical elements of the vast universe, the spiritual path itself, and the very flesh, breath, and consciousness of the person praying.

translit: āṟumu kaṅkoṇṭa aiyā-eṉ tuṉpam aṉaittumiṉṉum ēṟumu kaṅkoṇṭa tallāl iṟaṅkumu kamilaiyāl vīṟumu kaṅkoṇṭa kaivēliṉ vīram viḷaṅka-eṉṉaic cīṟumu kaṅkoṇṭa attuṉpam ōṭac celuttukavē.
translation: O Lord with six faces, all my sorrows are still only increasing and show no sign of decreasing. Let the valor of the magnificent spear in your hand shine brilliantly. Throw it to drive away this raging sorrow that attacks me.
commentary: The six-faced Lord Murugan is traditionally depicted holding a spear to defeat demons in battle. In this prayer, that weapon is called upon for an intimate rescue. The magnificent spear is asked to strike down the overwhelming sorrow that attacks the mind.

translit: paṇkoṇṭa caṇmukat taiyā aruḷmikum paṉṉiraṇṭu kaṇkoṇṭa nīcaṟṟuṅ kaṇṭilai yō-eṉ kavalaiveḷḷam tiṇkoṇṭa eṭṭut ticaikoṇṭu nīḷcatta tīvuṅkoṇṭu maṇkoṇṭu viṇkoṇṭu pātāḷaṅ koṇṭu vaḷarkiṉṟatē.
translation: O six-faced Lord praised in song! You have twelve eyes full of grace. Do you not see at all? The flood of my worries swallows the eight firm directions, swallows the seven vast islands, swallows the earth, swallows the sky, swallows the netherworld, and still keeps growing.
commentary: The imagery contrasts the vastness of human anxiety with the all-seeing nature of the divine. A deity with six faces and twelve eyes should miss nothing, yet the speaker feels entirely unseen. This worry feels so absolute that it drowns the entire universe, spreading from the highest sky down to the deep netherworld.

translit: vaṉkulañ cērkaṭaṉ māmutal vēraṟa māṭṭivaṇmai naṉkulañ cērviṇ nakaraḷit tōyaṉṟu naṇṇi-eṉṉai niṉkulañ cērttaṉai iṉṟuvi ṭēluḷam nērntukoṇṭu piṉkulam pēcukiṉ ṟārumuṇ ṭō-ip perunilattē.
translation: You destroyed the great mango tree by the sea right from its roots to ruin that cruel lineage. You then gave the heavenly city back to the good lineage. You approached me back then and brought me into your lineage. Do not abandon me today. Is there anyone in this vast world who willingly accepts a person into their heart and then questions their lineage later?
commentary: The opening recalls a sacred story where Murugan destroyed a demon hiding as a massive mango tree to save the heavenly beings. The plea then turns intensely personal. Once God accepts a soul into the divine family, it is unthinkable to cast them out later by judging their worldly background or past flaws.

tamil: திருமால் ஆதியர் உள்ளம் கொள்ளும்ஓர் செவ்விய வேலோனே
குருமா மணியே குணமணி யேசுரர் கோவே மேலோனே
கருமா மலம்அறு வண்ணம் தண்அளி கண்டே கொண்டேனே
கதியே பதியே கனநிதி யேகற் கண்டே தண்தேனே
அருமா தவர்உயர் நெஞ்சம் விஞ்சிய அண்ணா விண்ணவனே
அரசே அமுதே அறிவுரு வேமுரு கையா மெய்யவனே
உருவா கியபவ பந்தம் சிந்திட ஓதிய வேதியனே
ஒளியே வெளியே உலகமெ லாம் உடை யோனே வானவனே.
translit: tirumāl ātiyar uḷḷam koḷḷumōr cevviya vēlōṉē kurumā maṇiyē kuṇamaṇi yēcurar kōvē mēlōṉē karumā malamaṟu vaṇṇam taṇaḷi kaṇṭē koṇṭēṉē katiyē patiyē kaṉaniti yēkaṟ kaṇṭē taṇtēṉē arumā tavaruyar neñcam viñciya aṇṇā viṇṇavaṉē aracē amutē aṟivuru vēmuru kaiyā meyyavaṉē uruvā kiyapava pantam cintiṭa ōtiya vētiyaṉē oḷiyē veḷiyē ulakame lām uṭai yōṉē vāṉavaṉē.
translation: O Lord with the perfect spear, held in the hearts of Thirumal and other gods! O great gem of a Guru! O gem of virtue! O king of the celestials! O Supreme One! I beheld your cool grace and received it to sever the dark, great impurity. O refuge! O Lord! O vast treasure! O rock sugar! O cool honey! O Lord who overflows in the exalted hearts of rare ascetics! O heavenly One! O King! O ambrosia! O form of knowledge! O Lord Murugan! O True One! O Master who taught the truth to shatter the embodied bonds of birth! O light! O space! O Master of all the worlds! O celestial One!
commentary: This outpouring of praise gathers every aspect of the divine into one sweeping vision. God is hailed as the supreme teacher who cuts away the dark impurities of the mind and breaks the painful cycle of physical birth. More than just a ruler of the heavens, the divine is experienced directly as pure knowledge, pure light, and the boundless space that holds all worlds.

translit: kūḻuk kaḻuvēṉō kōttaṇikaik kōvē-eṉ ūḻuk kaḻuvēṉō ōyāt tuyarppiṟavi ēḻuk kaḻuvēṉō eṉceykēṉ eṉceykēṉ pāḻuk kiṟaittēṉī tuṉceyalō pārkkumiṭam
translation: Shall I weep for mere porridge? O King of beautiful Thanigai! Shall I weep for my karma? Shall I weep for the seven births of unceasing sorrow? What shall I do? What shall I do? I have poured water into a wasteland. When I consider this, is it your doing?
commentary: The speaker is torn between basic physical survival, crying out for simple porridge, and the immense weight of karma (the cycle of past actions and their spiritual consequences). He feels his life has been entirely wasted, pouring water on barren ground, and asks the Lord if this suffering is his divine will.

translit: cintaik kumvaḻi illai-uṉ taṉmaiyait teritaṟ keṉṉum tiruttaṇi kēcaṉē untaik kumvaḻi illai-eṉ ṟālinta ulakil yāvar uṉai-aṉṟi nīrmoḷḷa montaik kumvaḻi illai varattiru muṇṭaik kumvaḻi illai araiyilcāṇ kantaik kumvaḻi illai arakara kañcik kumvaḻi illai-iṅ kaiyaṉē.
translation: There is no way for the mind to know your nature, O Lord of Thanigai. If you say there is no way for your father either, who else is there in this world besides you? I have no pot to draw water. I have no holy ash to adorn my forehead. I have no span of ragged cloth for my waist. Hara Hara! I have no way to get even thin gruel here, O Lord.
commentary: Absolute destitution is laid bare here. The speaker strips away every worldly comfort, lacking a pot for water, a scrap of cloth for his waist, or even holy ash for his forehead. All that remains is his raw dependence on a God whose true nature sits entirely beyond human understanding.

tamil: கறிபிடித்த ஊன்கடையில் கண்டவர்தம் கால்பிடித்துக் கவ்வும் பொல்லா
வெறிபிடித்த நாய்க்கேனும் வித்தைபயிற் றிடலாகும் வேண்டி வேண்டி
மறிபிடித்த சிறுவனைப் போல் வாத்தியார் மனமறுகி வருந்தத் தங்கள்
குறிபிடித்துக் காட்டுவோர்க் கியாவர்படிப் பிக்கவலார் குமர வேளே.
translit: kaṟipiṭitta ūṉkaṭaiyil kaṇṭavartam kālpiṭittuk kavvum pollā veṟipiṭitta nāykkēṉum vittaipayiṟ ṟiṭalākum vēṇṭi vēṇṭi maṟipiṭitta ciṟuvaṉaip pōl vāttiyār maṉamaṟuki varuntat taṅkaḷ kuṟipiṭittuk kāṭṭuvōrk kiyāvarpaṭip pikkavalār kumara vēḷē.
translation: O Lord Kumara! One could even teach skills to a wicked, rabid dog that waits at a meat shop and bites the legs of those it sees. But who has the power to teach those who stubbornly display only their own arrogance, making their teacher's mind suffer like a deeply obstinate child?
commentary: Arrogance makes learning impossible. Vallalar observes that it would be easier to train a vicious, rabid dog than to teach spiritual truths to someone who is stubbornly proud and refuses to listen.

translit: tātātā tātātā tākkuṟaikkeṉ ceykutumiyām ōtā tavamē yuḻaṉeñcē-mītāt tatiti yeṉamayiliṟ ṟāṉāṭi nāḷun tititi taruntaṇikait tē.
translation: O heart that wanders uselessly without chanting! What shall we do for this deficiency? The Lord of Thanigai dances daily on his peacock to the soaring rhythm 'tha thi thi' and grants us protection.
commentary: The wandering mind constantly forgets to think of God. To fix this emptiness, the verse points to the joyful presence of the divine, imagined here as the Lord dancing rhythmically on his peacock and offering constant protection to the world.

translit: ōriraṇṭā naṟṟaṇikai uttamaṉṟaṉ ōṅkaṟṟōḷ tāriraṇṭār pōṉiṉṟa taiyaṉmīr-vāriraṇṭāt toyyi laḻikkun tuṇaimulaiyā ḷuḷḷakattā maiya laḻikku maruntu.
translation: O women who stand like those wearing double garlands on the mountain-like shoulders of the supreme Lord of good Thanigai! The medicine that cures the deep infatuation in the heart of this girl, whose breasts rub away their painted sandalwood patterns, is the Lord himself.
commentary: The soul's intense yearning for God is pictured here as a lovesick young woman. Speaking in the style of classic Tamil love poetry, her companions realize that the only medicine for her deep spiritual fever is the Lord himself.

translit: ēlun tayaṅkeṉṉu mēvaṟ ketirmaṟaitāṉ ālun toḻiṟkēva lākumō-mālunti māṟṟun taṇikaiyarkku māmayiṉmēl nāṭōṟun tōṟṟun taṇikaiyaṉpoṟ ṟōḷ.
translation: Will the negative of the fitting command 'hesitate' become an order for a dancing action? The golden shoulders of the Lord of Thanigai, who dispels rising delusion, appear daily upon the great peacock.
commentary: This verse uses a playful riddle about the Tamil language to praise Lord Murugan, the presiding deity of Thanigai (Thanigai). The Tamil phrase for "do not hesitate" sounds exactly like the rhythmic syllables spoken to direct a dancer on stage. The poetry connects this joyful dancing rhythm to the great peacock that carries the Lord. When divine grace clears away inner confusion, the mind no longer hesitates, and the golden presence of the Lord is revealed in all its active beauty.

sections.title: The Garland of the Divine Gem

translit: tiru-ōṅku puṇṇiyac ceyalōṅki aṉparuḷ tiṟalōṅku celvamōṅkac ceṟivōṅka aṟivōṅki niṟaivāṉa iṉpam tikaḻntōṅka aruḷkoṭuttu maru-ōṅku ceṅkamala malarōṅku vaṇamōṅka vaḷarkaruṇai mayamōṅki-ōr varamōṅku teḷamuta vayamōṅki āṉanta vaṭivāki ōṅkiñāṉa uru-ōṅkum uṇarviṉniṟai oḷi-ōṅki ōṅkummayil ūrntōṅki evvuyirkkum uṟavōṅkum niṉpatameṉ uḷamōṅki vaḷamōṅka uykiṉṟa nāḷentanāḷ taru-ōṅku ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: What day will I attain salvation, the day Your feet, which hold an ever-growing kinship with all souls, rise in my heart and make it flourish? You grant Your grace so that auspicious holy deeds increase, the powerful wealth within devotees' hearts multiplies, focus and wisdom grow, and perfect bliss shines brightly. You flourish in the color of a fragrant red lotus. You flourish as the very form of growing compassion, as the power of clear nectar granting great boons, and as the embodiment of bliss. You flourish as the full light of awareness taking the form of wisdom, riding Your magnificent peacock. O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in Chennai which abounds in trees. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Vallalar longs for the day when the divine presence takes root in his heart and transforms him. He describes God not as a distant ruler, but as the very form of growing compassion and the full light of awareness. It is this compassion that grants true wisdom and spiritual wealth to all living beings.

translit: paramētu viṉaiceyum payaṉētu pati-ētu pacu-ētu pācamētu patti-ē taṭaikiṉṟa muttira taruḷētu pāvapuṇ yaṅkaḷētu varamētu tavamētu viratamē toṉṟumilai maṉamvirum puṇavuṇṭunal vattiram aṇintumaṭa mātartamai nāṭinaṟu malarcūṭi viḷaiyāṭimēl karamēva viṭṭumulai toṭṭuvāḻn tavaroṭu kalantumakiḻ kiṉṟacukamē kaṇkaṇṭa cukamitē kaikaṇṭa palaṉeṉum kayavaraik kūṭātaruḷ taramēvu ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: Grant me the grace never to associate with those base people who declare, "What is the supreme state? What is the fruit of karma? What is God? What is the soul? What is bondage? What is devotion? What is the grace that grants liberation? What are sins and merits? What are boons, penances, and vows? None of these exist! Eating whatever the mind desires, wearing fine clothes, seeking out young women, wearing fragrant flowers, playing together, placing hands upon them, and living in joyous union with them is the only pleasure we can see, and this alone is the tangible fruit we can hold." O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in Chennai where good people live. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: The poet asks for the grace to stay away from those who mock spiritual life and believe only in what they can see and touch. He points out how easily people dismiss the reality of God, the soul, and the spiritual law of cause and effect, choosing instead to live entirely for physical pleasure. Living only for the senses is a dead end that blinds a person to deeper truths.

translit: tuṭi-eṉṉum iṭai-aṉam piṭi-eṉṉum naṭaimukil tuṇai-eṉum piṇaiyalaḷakam cūteṉṉum mulaiceḻun tāteṉṉum alaipuṉal cuḻi-eṉṉa moḻiceyunti vaṭi-eṉṉum viḻiniṟaiyum mati-eṉṉum vataṉameṉa maṅkaiyartam aṅkamuṟṟē maṉameṉṉum orupāvi mayaleṉṉum atumēvi māḻkanāṉ vāḻka-intap paṭi-eṉṉum ācaiyaik kaṭi-eṉṉa eṉcolip paṭi-eṉṉa aṟiyātuniṉ paṭi-eṉṉa eṉmoḻip paṭi-iṉṉa vittainī paṭi-eṉṉum eṉceykuvēṉ taṭituṉṉum matilceṉṉai kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: Fixated on the physical forms of women, describing their waists as the thudi drum, their gait as the swan and the female elephant, their braided hair as a dark cloud, their breasts as mangoes, their navels as whirlpools in rushing water, their eyes as sharp blades, and their faces as the full moon, the sinner known as the mind succumbs to delusion and perishes. If I beg You, "How am I to live? Eradicate this worldly desire," You ignore my plea, asking, "What is your condition?" and then command me, "Learn this knowledge exactly as I tell you." What can I possibly do? O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in Chennai ringed by sturdy walls. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: The human mind is easily trapped by physical beauty and worldly desires. Vallalar shows how traditional poetry often breaks the body down into objects of obsession, comparing a waist to a drum or eyes to sharp blades, which only feeds this delusion. When he begs for this endless craving to be wiped away, the divine response is to patiently redirect him to the pursuit of true spiritual knowledge.

translit: vaḷḷaluṉai uḷḷapaṭi vāḻttukiṉ ṟōrtamai matittiṭuva taṉṟimaṟṟai vāṉavarai mati-eṉṉil nāṉavarai orukaṉaviṉ māṭṭiṉum maṟantummatiyēṉ kaḷḷamaṟum uḷḷamuṟum niṉpatama lālvēṟu kaṭavuḷar patattai-avareṉ kaṇetir aṭuttaiya naṇeṉa aḷippiṉum kaṭu-eṉa veṟuttuniṟpēṉ eḷḷaḷavum immoḻiyi lēcumoḻi aṉṟuṇmai eṉṉai āṇ ṭaruḷpurikuvāy eṉtantai yē-eṉatu tāyē-eṉ iṉpamē eṉṟaṉaṟi vē-eṉaṉpē taḷḷariya ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: I respect those who truly praise You, the great benefactor, but if asked to revere other celestial gods, I will never do so, not even by mistake, and not even in a dream. Other than Your feet which dwell in a heart completely free of deceit, even if other gods were to appear right before my eyes and offer me their divine feet, saying "Accept this," I would stand rejecting it like poison. There is not a sesame seed's worth of falsehood in my words; this is the absolute truth. Take dominion over me and grant Your grace, O my father, my mother, my bliss, my wisdom, my love! O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in the great, indispensable Chennai. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Vallalar declares his absolute, undivided loyalty to the divine presence he knows intimately. He states plainly that he has no interest in seeking favors from other celestial beings, even if they were to appear right in front of him offering their blessings. This fierce devotion comes from recognizing God not as a remote authority, but as his own mother, father, wisdom, and love.

translit: patipūcai mutalanaṟ kiriyaiyāl maṉameṉum pacukaraṇam īṅkacutta pāvaṉai aṟaccutta pāvaṉaiyil niṟkummeyp patiyōka nilaimai-ataṉāṉ matipācam aṟṟatiṉ aṭaṅkiṭum aṭaṅkavē malaivilmeyñ ñāṉamayamāy varavupōk kaṟṟanilai kūṭumeṉa eṉatuḷē vantuṇarvu tantakuruvē tutivāymai peṟucānta patammēvu matiyamē turicaṟu cuyañcōtiyē tōkaivā kaṉamī tilaṅkavaru tōṉṟalē collariya nallatuṇaiyē tatipeṟum ceṉṉaiyila• kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: "Through virtuous actions like the worship of God, the impure tendencies of the soul's instrument, the mind, are eradicated here. Through the state of true divine union established in pure contemplation, the mind severs its bonds and merges into the Divine. Once merged, it becomes the unshakeable embodiment of true wisdom, and the state free from all coming and going is attained." O Guru who entered my heart and granted me this understanding! O moon dwelling in the peaceful state praised for its truth! O flawless self-luminous Jothi! O noble Lord who comes shining upon the peacock mount! O indescribable, perfect companion! O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in Chennai rich in prosperity. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Sincere worship and virtuous actions slowly wash away the mind's impure habits. When the mind settles into pure focus on the divine, it breaks free from its worldly attachments and merges completely into spiritual light. Vallalar explains that in this unbroken union, a person finally steps off the endless wheel of birth and death, becoming one with the flawless, self-luminous truth.

translit: kāma-uṭ pakaivaṉum kōpaveṅ koṭiyaṉum kaṉalōpa muḻumūṭaṉum kaṭumōka vīṇaṉum koṭumatam eṉuntuṭṭa kaṇkeṭṭa āṅkāriyum ēmamaṟu māccariya viḻalaṉum kolai-eṉ ṟiyampupā takaṉumāmiv veḻuvarum ivarkkuṟṟa uṟavāṉa pērkaḷum eṉaippaṟṟi ṭāmalaruḷvāy cēmamiku māmaṟaiyiṉ ōmeṉum aruṭpatat tiṟaṉaruḷi malayamuṉivaṉ cintaṉaiyiṉ vantaṉai-u vantameyñ ñāṉaciva tēcika cikāratṉamē tāmamoḷir ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukar caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: Bestow your grace so that these seven, along with their relatives, do not seize me: the inner enemy of lust, the cruel one of anger, the utter fool of burning greed, the vain one of fierce delusion, the blind egoist of wicked pride, the useless one of joyless envy, and the sinner called murder. O crown jewel among the true, wise Saiva preceptors, you revealed the power of the gracious syllable 'Om' of the supreme, protective Vedas and rejoiced in the worship within the mind of the sage of the Malaya mountain. O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in Chennai where garlands shine. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Vallalar prays to be shielded from seven destructive inner enemies: lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy, and the ultimate act of murder. He asks the divine to keep these forces, and anyone possessed by them, far away from his mind. He directs this prayer to Skanda, another name for the deity Murugan, praising him as the supreme teacher of spiritual truth.

translit: nilai-uṟum nirācaiyām uyarkulap peṇṭiroṭu nikaḻcānta māmputalvaṉum neṟipeṟum utārakuṇam eṉṉumnaṟ poruḷummaruḷ nīkkumaṟi vāmtuṇaivaṉum malaivaṟu nirāṅkāra naṇpaṉum cuttamuṟu maṉameṉṉum nalēvalum varucakala kēvalami lāta-iṭa mumpeṟṟu vāḻkiṉṟa vāḻvaruḷuvāy alai-ilāc civañāṉa vāriyē āṉanta amutamē kumutamalarvāy aṇikoḷpoṟ koṭipacuṅ koṭi-iru puṟampaṭarn taḻakupeṟa varupoṉmalaiyē talaivarpukaḻ ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: Grant me the blessed life of attaining a state free from all worldly involvement and isolation, living together with the high-born wife of enduring desirelessness, the son of manifest peace, the good wealth of a righteous and generous nature, the companion of ignorance-dispelling knowledge, the unwavering friend of egolessness, and the good servant of a pure mind. O waveless ocean of Siva's wisdom! O nectar of bliss! O golden mountain who comes beautifully with the adorned golden creeper and the green creeper spreading on either side, possessing a mouth like the blooming water lily! O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in Chennai praised by leaders. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Vallalar imagines a perfect spiritual household where virtues take the place of human family members. In this state of grace, his wife is desirelessness, his child is peace, his wealth is generosity, and his friends are knowledge and a mind free of ego. He asks God to let him live entirely in this pure state, completely free from the ordinary struggles of worldly attachment and the darkness of spiritual isolation.

translit: orumaiyuṭaṉ niṉatutiru malaraṭi niṉaikkiṉṟa uttamartam uṟavuvēṇṭum uḷoṉṟu vaittup puṟampoṉṟu pēcuvār uṟavukala vāmaivēṇṭum perumaipeṟu niṉatupukaḻ pēcavēṇ ṭumpoymai pēcā tirukkvēṇṭum peruneṟi piṭittoḻuka vēṇṭummata māṉapēy piṭiyā tirukkavēṇṭum maruvupeṇ ācaiyai maṟakkavē vēṇṭumuṉai maṟavā tirukkavēṇṭum mativēṇṭum niṉkaruṇai nitivēṇṭum nōyaṟṟa vāḻvilnāṉ vāḻavēṇṭum tarumamiku ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: I need the fellowship of the pure ones who contemplate your holy lotus feet with one-pointedness of mind. I must not mingle with those who hold one thing in their hearts and speak another outwardly. I must speak your glorious praise. I must remain without speaking lies. I must firmly follow the great path. I must not be seized by the ghost of religious pride. I must entirely forget the desire for alluring women. I must never forget you. I need a clear mind. I need the treasure of your grace. I must live a life free of disease. O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in highly righteous Chennai. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Vallalar lists the core requirements for a pure spiritual life, asking for good health, clear thinking, and the company of sincere seekers. He warns against hypocrisy, insisting that a seeker must avoid those whose inner thoughts contradict their outward words. He specifically prays to be kept safe from the ghost of religious pride, treating attachment to a single religion as a trap that destroys true spiritual progress.

translit: ī-eṉṟu nāṉoruvar iṭamniṉṟu kēḷāta iyalpumeṉ ṉiṭamoruvarī tiṭu-eṉṟa pōtavark kilai-eṉṟu collāmal iṭukiṉṟa tiṟamumiṟaiyām nī-eṉṟum eṉaiviṭā nilaiyumnāṉ eṉṟumuḷa niṉaiviṭā neṟiyumayalār niti-oṉṟum nayavāta maṉamummeyn nilainiṉṟu nekiḻāta tiṭamumulakil cī-eṉṟu pēyeṉṟu nāyeṉṟu piṟar tamait tīṅkucol lātateḷivum tiramoṉṟu vāymaiyum tūymaiyum tantuniṉ tiruvaṭik kāḷākkuvāy tāyoṉṟu ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: Grant me the nature of never standing before anyone to beg for alms, and the ability to give without saying "no" when someone asks me for charity. Grant me the state where you, the Lord, never abandon me, and the path where I never abandon the thought of you. Grant me a mind that does not covet the wealth of others, and the firmness of standing in the true state without wavering. Grant me the clarity of never speaking evil of others in the world by calling them despicable, a ghost, or a dog. Grant me steadfast truthfulness and purity, and make me a servant to your holy feet. O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in motherly Chennai. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: A true spiritual life requires both deep dignity and limitless generosity. Vallalar asks for the grace never to beg from others, alongside the ability to give to anyone in need without ever refusing them. He also prays for total purity of speech, asking to never insult or degrade another living being with cruel words.

translit: karaiyilvīṇ katai-elām utirkaruṅ kākkaipōl kataṟuvār kaḷḷuṇṭatīk kantamnā ṟiṭa-ūttai kātamnā ṟiṭa-uṟu kaṭumpoyiru kātamnāṟa varaiyilvāy koṭutarkka vātamiṭu vārciva maṇaṅkamaḻ malarppoṉvāykku mavuṉamiṭu vārivarai mūṭareṉa ōtuṟu vaḻakkunal vaḻakkeṉiṉumnāṉ uraiyilavar tamaiyuṟā tuṉatupukaḻ pēcumava rōṭuṟavu peṟa-aruḷuvāy uyarteyva yāṉaiyoṭu kuṟavarmaṭa māṉumuḷ uvappuṟu kuṇakkuṉṟamē taraiyiluyar ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: Like shedding black crows, they scream endless, vain tales. The foul stench of the toddy they consumed reeks, their bodily filth reeks for a league, and their severe lies reek for two leagues. They engage in contentious arguments with their boundless mouths, but they impose silence on their golden, flower-like mouths when it comes to radiating the fragrance of Siva. Even though the custom of calling such people fools is a just custom, I will not speak of them or associate with them. Bestow your grace so that I may attain the fellowship of those who speak your praise. O mountain of virtues who brings inner joy to the noble Deivayanai and to Valli, the young deer of the hill tribes! O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in Chennai, which is elevated on this earth. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Vallalar vividly describes people who waste their lives in loud, arrogant arguments while ignoring the divine. He compares their empty talk to the screaming of crows, saying their lies and inner corruption create an overwhelming spiritual stench. Rather than fighting them or insulting them in return, he simply asks God for the grace to stay entirely away from them, seeking only the company of those focused on truth.

translit: nāmpiramam namai-aṉṟi āmpiramam vēṟillai naṉmaitī maikaḷum illai navilkiṉṟa vāki-ān taramiraṇṭiṉumoṉṟa naṭuniṉṟa teṉṟuvīṇāḷ pōmpirama nītikēṭ pōrpiramai yākavē pōtippar cātippartām puṉmaineṟi kaiviṭār tampiramam viṉai-oṉṟu pōntiṭil pōkaviṭuvār cāmpirama māmivarkaḷ tāmpiramam eṉumaṟivu tāmpupām peṉumaṟivukāṇ cattuva akaṇṭaparipuraṇa kāra-upa cāntaciva ciṟpirama nī tāmpirivil ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: "We are Brahman. Other than us, there is no Brahman. Good and evil do not exist." People who say such things waste their days asserting, "It stands in the center, uniting both the spoken external and internal states." They preach such illusory doctrines to their listeners and practice them, yet they never abandon their base ways. If a single karmic reaction strikes them, they quickly let go of their 'Brahman'. The knowledge of these bewildered people claiming "We are Brahman" is exactly like mistaking a rope for a snake. You alone are the undivided, completely perfect, supremely peaceful Siva, the absolute Brahman of consciousness. O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in inseparable Chennai. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Claiming to be God while living a selfish life is a spiritual illusion. People who preach that they are already the supreme reality (Brahman), and that good and evil no longer matter, drop their high philosophy the moment real suffering strikes. Vallalar says their understanding is as false as mistaking a piece of rope for a deadly snake.

translit: pārkoṇṭa naṭaiyilvaṉ pacikoṇṭu vantirap pārmukam pārttiraṅkum paṇpumniṉ tiruvaṭik kaṉpumniṟai āyuḷum patiyumnal nitiyumuṇarvum cīrkoṇṭa niṟaiyumuṭ poṟaiyummeyp pukaḻumnōyt tīmai-oru caṟṟumaṇukāt tiṟamummeyt tiṭamumnal iṭamumniṉ aṭiyarpukaḻ ceppukiṉ ṟōraṭaivarkāṇ kūrkoṇṭa neṭṭilaik katirvēlum mayilumoru kōḻiyaṅ koṭiyumviṇṇōr kōmāṉtaṉ makaḷumoru māmāṉtaṉ makaḷummāl koṇṭaniṉ kōlamaṟavēṉ tārkoṇṭa ceṉṉaiyil kantakōṭ ṭattuḷvaḷar talamōṅku kantavēḷē taṇmukat tuyyamaṇi uṇmukac caivamaṇi caṇmukat teyvamaṇiyē.
translation: Those who speak the praise of your devotees will surely attain all these: the compassion to look upon the faces of those who come begging with fierce hunger in this earthly life and show them pity; love for your holy feet; a full lifespan; a good home; good wealth; true realization; excellent fulfillment; inner patience; true fame; the strength to remain completely untouched by the evil of disease; true stability; and a good state. I will never forget your beautiful form, holding the sharp, long-leafed, radiant spear, accompanied by the peacock, the beautiful rooster banner, the daughter of the celestial king, and the daughter of the great deer who are deeply in love with you. O Lord Skanda whose eminent shrine flourishes in Kandakottam in garlanded Chennai. O pure gem with a cool face, O Saiva gem of the inner face, O divine gem with six faces.
commentary: Honoring those who love God naturally opens the heart to compassion and brings immense blessings in life.
