commentary: The divine is described here as a supreme medicine that cures the darkness of worldly delusion. The verse recalls a traditional story where Lord Vishnu offered his own lotus-like eye as a flower to worship Siva. This imagery points to a supreme reality that is made entirely of love, knowledge, and an endless flood of grace.

tamil: வான நடுவே வயங்குகின்ற மவுன மதியை மதிஅமுதைத்
தேனை அளிந்த பழச்சுவையைத் தெய்வ மணியைச் சிவபதத்தை
ஊனம் அறியார் உளத்தொளிரும் ஒளியை ஒளிக்கும் ஒருபொருளை
ஞான மலையைப் பழமலைமேல் நண்ணி விளங்கக் கண்டேனே.
translit: vāṉa naṭuvē vayaṅkukiṉṟa mavuṉa matiyai mati-amutait tēṉai aḷinta paḻaccuvaiyait teyva maṇiyaic civapatattai ūṉam aṟiyār uḷattoḷirum oḷiyai oḷikkum oruporuḷai ñāṉa malaiyaip paḻamalaimēl naṇṇi viḷaṅkak kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I saw Him approach and shine upon the Ancient Mountain. He is the silent moon shining in the middle of the heavens. He is the nectar of the moon, honey, and the sweet taste of ripe fruit. He is the divine gem and the state of Siva. He is the light shining in the hearts of the flawless, the peerless reality that radiates light, and the mountain of wisdom.
commentary: God is experienced internally as pure sweetness. This sweetness is compared to honey, ripe fruit, and the nectar of a silent moon. This inner reality shines brightly as spiritual light within the hearts of those who have purified their minds of worldly flaws.

tamil: தவள நிறத்துத் திருநீறு தாங்கு மணித்தோள் தாணுவைநம்
குவளை விழித்தாய் ஒருபுறத்தே குலவ விளங்கும் குருமணியைக்
கவள மதமா கரியுரிவைக் களித்த மேனிக் கற்பகத்தைப்
பவள மலையைப் பழமலையிற் பரவி ஏத்திக் கண்டேனே.
translit: tavaḷa niṟattut tirunīṟu tāṅku maṇittōḷ tāṇuvainam kuvaḷai viḻittāy orupuṟattē kulava viḷaṅkum kurumaṇiyaik kavaḷa matamā kariyurivaik kaḷitta mēṉik kaṟpakattaip pavaḷa malaiyaip paḻamalaiyiṟ paravi ēttik kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I worshipped and praised Him, seeing Him on the Ancient Mountain. He is the immovable Lord whose beautiful shoulders bear the white sacred ash. He is the master gem who shines delightfully with our Mother of blue-lily eyes on one side. He is the wish-fulfilling tree whose form rejoices in wearing the skin of the great, fierce rutting elephant. He is the mountain of coral.
commentary: The spiritual vision merges fierce and gentle aspects of the divine form. The Lord is seen wearing the terrifying skin of a wild elephant, yet stands joyfully beside the Mother goddess with beautiful blue-lily eyes. Together they act as a divine wish-fulfilling tree that grants all spiritual boons.

tamil: இளைத்த இடத்தில் உதவிஅன்பர் இடத்தே இருந்த ஏமவைப்பை
வளைத்த மதின்மூன் றெரித்தருளை வளர்த்த கருணை வாரிதியைத்
திளைத்த யோகர் உளத்தோங்கித் திகழுந் துரியா தீதமட்டுங்
கிளைத்த மலையைப் பழமலையிற் கிளர்ந்து வயங்கக் கண்டேனே.
translit: iḷaitta iṭattil utavi-aṉpar iṭattē irunta ēmavaippai vaḷaitta matiṉmūṉ ṟerittaruḷai vaḷartta karuṇai vāritiyait tiḷaitta yōkar uḷattōṅkit tikaḻun turiyā tītamaṭṭuṅ kiḷaitta malaiyaip paḻamalaiyiṟ kiḷarntu vayaṅkak kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I saw Him rise up and shine brightly on the Ancient Mountain. He is the golden treasure who helps devotees in their times of weakness and abides with them. He is the ocean of compassion who burned the three encircling fortresses and fostered grace. He is the mountain that branches out all the way to the supreme state beyond the fourth, rising and shining in the hearts of joyful yogis.
commentary: God is depicted as a faithful golden treasure who stays near devotees to help them in their moments of greatest weakness. The verse mentions turiyātīta (the supreme state beyond the fourth). This is the highest peak of awareness, transcending the ordinary experiences of waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the fourth state known as turiya (pure consciousness).

tamil: மடந்தை மலையாண் மனமகிழ மருவும் பதியைப் பசுபதியை
அடர்ந்த வினையின் தொடக்கைஅறுத் தருளும் அரசை அலைகடன்மேல்
கிடந்த பச்சைப் பெருமலைக்குக் கேடில் அருள்தந் தகம்புறமும்
கடந்த மலையைப் பழமலைமேற் கண்கள் களிக்கக் கண்டேனே.
translit: maṭantai malaiyāṇ maṉamakiḻa maruvum patiyaip pacupatiyai aṭarnta viṉaiyiṉ toṭakkai-aṟut taruḷum aracai alaikaṭaṉmēl kiṭanta paccaip perumalaikkuk kēṭil aruḷtan takampuṟamum kaṭanta malaiyaip paḻamalaimēṟ kaṇkaḷ kaḷikkak kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: My eyes rejoiced to see Him on the Ancient Mountain. He is the Lord who embraces the mountain-born goddess to the delight of her heart. He is the Lord of souls. He is the sovereign who severs the bonds of dense karma and grants grace. He granted imperishable grace to Vishnu, the great green mountain resting on the wavy ocean. He is the mountain that transcends both the inner and outer realms.
commentary: The sovereign Lord releases the soul from the tight bonds of dense karma (the accumulated results of past actions). As the master of all living beings, God exists beyond all boundaries. This divine presence transcends both the inner world of the mind and the outer physical universe.

tamil: துனியும் பிறவித் தொடுவழக்குஞ் சோர்ந்து விடவுந் துரியவெளிக்
கினியும் பருக்குங் கிடையாத இன்பம் அடைந்தே இருந்திடவும்
பனியுந் திமய மலைப்பச்சைப் படர்ந்த பவளப் பருப்பதத்தைக்
translit: tuṉiyum piṟavit toṭuvaḻakkuñ cōrntu viṭavun turiyaveḷik kiṉiyum parukkuṅ kiṭaiyāta iṉpam aṭaintē iruntiṭavum paṉiyun timaya malaippaccaip paṭarnta pavaḷap paruppatattaik kaṉiyuñ cilaiyuṅ kalanta-iṭameṅkē aṅkē kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I saw the coral mountain covered by the green of the snowy Himalayas exactly where the fruit and the stone merge. I saw Him so that sorrow and the ongoing entanglement of birth might fade away, and so I might attain and abide in the bliss of the Turiya space that is beyond reach.
commentary: The divine vision brings an end to sorrow and the endless cycle of rebirth. The poet sees a mountain of red coral draped in Himalayan green, an image of the divine combining ultimate power with nurturing grace. Experiencing this reality allows the soul to enter Turiya, a state of pure spiritual consciousness far beyond ordinary waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.

tamil: கருணைக் கடலை அக்கடலிற் கலந்த அமுதை அவ்வமுதத்
தருணச் சுவையை அச்சுவையிற் சார்ந்த பயனைத் தனிச்சுகத்தை
வருணப் பவளப் பெருமலையை மலையிற் பச்சை மருந்தொருபால்
பொருணச் சுறவே பழமலையிற் பொருந்தி யோங்கக் கண்டேனே.
translit: karuṇaik kaṭalai akkaṭaliṟ kalanta amutai avvamutat taruṇac cuvaiyai accuvaiyiṟ cārnta payaṉait taṉiccukattai varuṇap pavaḷap perumalaiyai malaiyiṟ paccai maruntorupāl poruṇac cuṟavē paḻamalaiyiṟ porunti yōṅkak kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I saw the ocean of compassion, the nectar mingled in that ocean, the fresh taste of that nectar, the reward drawn from that taste, the unique bliss, and the great mountain of radiant coral with the green medicine on one side. I saw Him shining perfectly with true meaning at Pazhamalai.
commentary: Experiencing God is described as diving into an ocean of compassion and tasting its sweet nectar. The vision takes the form of a radiant coral mountain with green medicine on one side, representing the divine as a healing force that cures the soul's ailments. This deep encounter takes place at Pazhamalai, the ancient mountain, revealing the true meaning of spiritual bliss.

tamil: என்னார் உயிரிற் கலந்துகலந் தினிக்கும் கரும்பின் கட்டிதனைப்
பொன்னார் வேணிக் கொழுங்கனியைப் புனிதர்உளத்தில் புகுங் களிப்பைக்
கன்னார் உரித்துப் பணிகொண்ட கருணைப் பெருக்கைக் கலைத்தெளிவைப்
பன்னா கப்பூண் அணிமலையைப் பழைய மலையிற் கண்டேனே.
translit: eṉṉār uyiriṟ kalantukalan tiṉikkum karumpiṉ kaṭṭitaṉaip poṉṉār vēṇik koḻuṅkaṉiyaip puṉitaruḷattil pukuṅ kaḷippaik kaṉṉār urittup paṇikoṇṭa karuṇaip perukkaik kalaitteḷivaip paṉṉā kappūṇ aṇimalaiyaip paḻaiya malaiyiṟ kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I saw the block of sugar that constantly mixes and tastes sweet in my precious life, the rich fruit with golden matted hair, the joy that enters the hearts of the pure ones, the flood of compassion that stripped away my stony nature and took me into service, the clarity of wisdom, and the mountain adorned with serpent ornaments. I saw Him at the ancient mountain.
commentary: God's grace acts directly on the human heart to transform its hard, stubborn nature into pure devotion. The divine presence is experienced as a deep sweetness, like sugar dissolving perfectly into life itself. Stripped of his stony resistance, the poet is flooded with compassion and clarity, drawn permanently into a life of loving service.

tamil: நல்ல மனத்தே தித்திக்க நண்ணும் கனியை நலம்புரிந்தென்
அல்லல் அகற்றும் பெருவாழ்வை அன்பால் இயன்ற அருமருந்தைச்
சொல்ல முடியாத் தனிச்சுகத்தைத் துரிய நடுவே தோன்றுகின்ற
வல்ல மலையைப் பழமலையில் வயங்கி யோங்கக் கண்டேனே.
translit: nalla maṉattē tittikka naṇṇum kaṉiyai nalampurinteṉ allal akaṟṟum peruvāḻvai aṉpāl iyaṉṟa arumaruntaic colla muṭiyāt taṉiccukattait turiya naṭuvē tōṉṟukiṉṟa valla malaiyaip paḻamalaiyil vayaṅki yōṅkak kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I saw the fruit that draws near to taste sweet in a good heart, the great life that grants goodness and removes my sorrows, the rare medicine formed of love, the unique bliss that cannot be spoken, and the mighty mountain appearing in the center of the Turiya state. I saw Him shining and rising high at Pazhamalai.
commentary: A pure and loving heart is the true vessel for receiving divine grace. God appears here as a rare medicine made entirely of love, capable of removing all earthly sorrows and granting a greater life. This supreme joy reveals itself in the center of Turiya, the state of pure consciousness, standing firm like a mighty mountain.

tamil: ஆதி நடுவு முடிவுமிலா அருளா னந்தப் பெருங்கடலை
ஓதி உணர்தற் கரியசிவ யோகத் தெழுந்த ஒருசுகத்தைப்
பாதி யாகி ஒன்றாகிப் படர்ந்த வடிவைப் பரம்பரத்தைச்
சோதி மலையைப் பழமலையிற் சூழ்ந்து வணங்கிக் கண்டேனே.
translit: āti naṭuvu muṭivumilā aruḷā ṉantap peruṅkaṭalai ōti uṇartaṟ kariyaciva yōkat teḻunta orucukattaip pāti yāki oṉṟākip paṭarnta vaṭivaip paramparattaic cōti malaiyaip paḻamalaiyiṟ cūḻntu vaṇaṅkik kaṇṭēṉē.
translation: I encircled, bowed, and saw the great ocean of graceful bliss without beginning, middle, or end. I saw the unique bliss arising from Siva Yoga which is difficult to realize merely by reciting texts, the form that expanded as half and as one, the supreme reality, and the mountain of light at Pazhamalai.
commentary: True spiritual union cannot be achieved simply by reciting scriptures or studying sacred texts. Divine bliss is an endless ocean, and it must be known through direct, lived experience rather than intellectual learning. The ultimate reality reveals itself as a mountain of radiant light, a perfect unity that expands to fill all existence.

sections.title: Is It the Ancient Mountain or an Old Mountain?

translit: ātimalai aṉātimalai aṉpumalai eṅkum āṉamalai ñāṉamalai āṉanta malaivāṉ jōtimalai turiyamalai turiyamuṭik kappāl tōṉṟumalai tōṉṟāta cūtāṉa malaiveṇ pūtimalai cutta aṉu pūtimalai ellām pūttamalai valliyeṉap pukaḻumalai taṉaiyōr pātimalai muttarelām paṟṟumalai eṉṉum paḻamalaiyaik kiḻamalaiyāyp pakaruvateṉ ṉulakē.
translation: It is the first mountain, the beginningless mountain, the mountain of love, the mountain that has become everything, the mountain of wisdom, the mountain of bliss. It is the mountain of the heavenly Jothi, the transcendent mountain, the mountain that appears beyond the peak of transcendence, the subtle unmanifest mountain. It is the mountain of white sacred ash, the mountain of pure spiritual experience, the mountain from which everything blossomed. It is the mountain that holds the Goddess praised as a tender vine as its own half, the mountain that all liberated beings hold fast. Why does the world call this eternal Ancient Mountain an aging mountain?
commentary: God is pictured here as a vast, eternal mountain that is the source of all love, wisdom, and light. The verse plays on a sacred site literally named the Ancient Mountain. The poet asks why people think of the divine as old or aging when it is actually a state of pure, timeless experience. It remains the solid foundation of all existence, completely beyond the reach of time.

translit: cākkiyaṉār eṟintacilai cakittamalai citta cāntar uḷañ cārntōṅkit taṉittamalai capaiyil tūkkiyakā loṭuviḷaṅkum tūyamalai vētam coṉṉamalai colliṟanta turiyanaṭu malaivāṉ ākkiyaḷit taḻikkumalai aḻiyāta malainal aṉparukkiṉ pantarumōr aṟputappoṉ malainaṟ pākkiyaṅka ḷellāmum paḻuttamalai eṉṉum paḻamalaiyaik kiḻamalaiyāyp pakaruvateṉ ṉulakē.
translation: It is the mountain that accepted the stone thrown by Sakkiyanar. It is the unique mountain that dwells and rises high in the hearts of the peaceful. It is the pure mountain that shines with a lifted foot in the hall of dance. It is the mountain proclaimed by the scriptures, the mountain in the center of the transcendent state beyond all words. It is the mountain that creates, sustains, and destroys the heavens. It is the indestructible mountain, the wondrous golden mountain that grants bliss to good devotees, the mountain where all good fortunes ripen. Why does the world call this Ancient Mountain an aging mountain?
commentary: True devotion transforms even violent acts into pure worship. Sakkiyanar was a legendary saint who threw stones at a shrine every day out of intense, focused love, and God gladly accepted those stones as fragrant flowers. The mountain here also represents the dancing form of God lifting a foot in the hall of grace. This divine presence is an indestructible, golden mountain that constantly grants joy to the pure of heart.

translit: āṟu viḷaṅka aṇikiḷartēr ūrnta-ulāp pēṟu viḷaṅka-uḷam peṟṟatumaṉ - kūṟukiṉṟa oṉṟiraṇṭu tāṟupuṭai ōṅkum paḻamalaiyār miṉtiraṇṭu niṉṟacaṭai mēl.
translation: My heart received the glorious blessing of the procession as He rode in the beautifully adorned chariot. The river shines upon the matted hair of the Lord of the Ancient Mountain. His hair stands gathered like a mass of lightning, flanked by one or two towering clusters.
commentary: The imagery shifts from a towering mountain to a joyous festival procession. Traditional stories describe God with a sacred river flowing through His matted hair, shining with bright energy like lightning. Witnessing this grand display of divine grace fills the devotee's heart with ultimate blessing.

translit: uriya nāyaki yōṅkati kaippatit turiya nāyaki tūyavī raṭṭaṟkē piriya nāyaki pēraruḷ nāyaki periya nāyaki peṟṟiyaip pēcuvām.
translation: We shall speak of the greatness of Periyanayaki, the Goddess of great grace, the beloved Goddess of the pure Lord of Veerattanam, the Goddess of the transcendent state, the rightful Goddess of the flourishing town of Athigai.
commentary: The hymn opens with a declaration of intent to praise Goddess Periyanayaki. She is celebrated as the source of great grace, the companion to Siva at the Athigai temple, and the ruler of the highest spiritual states.

tamil: உலகந் தழைக்க உயிர்தழைக்க உணர்வு தழைக்க ஒளிதழைக்க
உருவந் தழைத்த பசுங்கொடியே உள்ளத் தினிக்கும் தெள்ளமுதே
திலகந் தழைத்த நுதற்கரும்பே செல்வத் திருவே கலைக்குருவே
சிறக்கும் மலைப்பெண் மணியேமா தேவி இச்சை ஞானமொடு
வலகந் தழைக்குங் கிரியை இன்பம் வழங்கும் ஆதி பரைஎன்ன
வயங்கும் ஒருபே ரருளேஎம் மதியை விளக்கும் மணிவிளக்கே
அலகந் தழைக்குந் திருவதிகை ஐயர் விரும்பும் மெய்யுறவே
அரிய பெரிய நாயகிப்பெண் ணரசே என்னை ஆண்டருளே.
translit: ulakan taḻaikka uyirtaḻaikka uṇarvu taḻaikka oḷitaḻaikka uruvan taḻaitta pacuṅkoṭiyē uḷḷat tiṉikkum teḷḷamutē tilakan taḻaitta nutaṟkarumpē celvat tiruvē kalaikkuruvē ciṟakkum malaippeṇ maṇiyēmā tēvi iccai ñāṉamoṭu valakan taḻaikkuṅ kiriyai iṉpam vaḻaṅkum āti parai-eṉṉa vayaṅkum orupē raruḷē-em matiyai viḷakkum maṇiviḷakkē alakan taḻaikkun tiruvatikai aiyar virumpum meyyuṟavē ariya periya nāyakippeṇ ṇaracē eṉṉai āṇṭaruḷē.
translation: O green vine who took a verdant form so that the world, living beings, awareness, and light may flourish. O clear nectar sweet to the heart. O sugarcane whose forehead is adorned with a beautiful mark. O goddess of wealth. O guru of the arts. O excellent gem among mountain maidens. O great goddess. O peerless great grace who shines as the primal supreme goddess, granting the bliss of will, wisdom, and action to make the world flourish. O jeweled lamp who illumines our minds. O true companion loved by the Lord of holy, beautiful Athigai. O rare Queen, Periyanayaki, rule over me and grant your grace.
commentary: The goddess is praised as the very life-force that causes the world, living beings, and human awareness to flourish. She embodies the three fundamental divine powers: the will to act, the wisdom to know, and the action itself. The verse uses sweet and vivid imagery, calling her a green vine, sweet nectar, and a jeweled lamp to show her nurturing and illuminating presence.

tamil: தன்னேர் அறியாப் பரவெளியில் சத்தாம் சுத்த அநுபவத்தைச்
சார்ந்து நின்ற பெரியவர்க்கும் தாயே எமக்குத் தனித்தாயே
மின்னே மின்னேர் இடைப்பிடியே விளங்கும் இதய மலர்அனமே
வேதம் புகலும் பசுங்கிளியே விமலக் குயிலே இளமயிலே
பொன்னே எல்லாம் வல்லதிரி புரையே பரையே பூரணமே
புனித மான புண்ணியமே பொற்பே கற்ப கப்பூவே
அன்னே முன்னே என்னேயத் தமர்ந்த அதிகை அருட்சிவையே
அரிய பெரிய நாயகிப்பெண் ணரசே என்னை ஆண்டருளே.
translit: taṉṉēr aṟiyāp paraveḷiyil cattām cutta anupavattaic cārntu niṉṟa periyavarkkum tāyē emakkut taṉittāyē miṉṉē miṉṉēr iṭaippiṭiyē viḷaṅkum itaya malaraṉamē vētam pukalum pacuṅkiḷiyē vimalak kuyilē iḷamayilē poṉṉē ellām vallatiri puraiyē paraiyē pūraṇamē puṉita māṉa puṇṇiyamē poṟpē kaṟpa kappūvē aṉṉē muṉṉē eṉṉēyat tamarnta atikai aruṭcivaiyē ariya periya nāyakippeṇ ṇaracē eṉṉai āṇṭaruḷē.
translation: O Mother even to the great sages who remain established in the pure experience of reality in the incomparable supreme space. O peerless Mother to us. O lightning. O she-elephant with a waist like lightning. O swan in the shining flower of the heart. O green parrot praised by the Vedas. O pure cuckoo. O young peacock. O gold. O omnipotent goddess of the three cities. O supreme goddess. O utter perfection. O sacred merit. O beauty. O wish-fulfilling flower. O Mother. O ancient one. O graceful goddess of Athigai who abides in my love. O rare Queen, Periyanayaki, rule over me and grant your grace.
commentary: Here the goddess is recognized as the universal mother who guides both the most enlightened sages and ordinary seekers alike. She is described through a series of beautiful natural forms, ranging from a swan in the heart to a green parrot and a young peacock. Above all, she is absolute perfection and grace, dwelling directly within the devotee's own love.

sections.title: The Flourishing Flame of Siva That Illuminates Arunagiri

translit: tiruviḷaṅkac civayōka cittiyelām viḷaṅkac civañāṉa nilaiviḷaṅkac civānupavam viḷaṅkat teruviḷaṅku tiruttillait tirucciṟṟam palattē tirukkūttu viḷaṅka-oḷi ciṟantatiru viḷakkē uruviḷaṅka uyirviḷaṅka uṇarcciyatu viḷaṅka ulakamelām viḷaṅka-aru ḷutavuperun tāyām maruviḷaṅku kuḻalvalli makiḻntorupāl viḷaṅka vayaṅkaruṇa kiriviḷaṅka vaḷarntacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O holy lamp of supreme light. You shine so the divine dance manifests in the sacred little hall of Tillai with its illustrious streets. You shine so auspiciousness manifests, so all the attainments of Siva yoga manifest, so the state of supreme wisdom manifests, and so the experience of Siva manifests. O flourishing flame of Siva. You grow to illuminate radiant Arunagiri. The great mother who grants grace, the goddess like a tender vine with fragrant hair, rejoices and shines on your side so physical forms manifest, so souls manifest, so consciousness manifests, and so all the worlds manifest.
commentary: God is the supreme light that makes both spiritual liberation and physical existence possible. Inwardly, this light grants the seeker supreme wisdom and Siva yoga, which is spiritual union with the divine. It is this same light that dances in the sacred hall of Tillai, the holy town of Chidambaram. Outwardly, accompanied by the divine mother who embodies pure grace, this flame brings physical forms, consciousness, and entire worlds into being.

sections.title: Hymn to Sivagnana Desikan of Thiruvothur

translit: ulakiyaliṉ uṟumayaliṉ aṭaivupeṟum eṉatitayam oḷipeṟa viḷaṅkucuṭarē
translation: O shining flame bringing light to my heart caught in the intense delusion of worldly life!
commentary: The spiritual teacher is praised as a radiant flame. This light alone can pierce through the deep confusion and delusion caused by everyday worldly attachments.

translit: utayaniṟai mati-amuta uṇavupeṟa nilavuciva yōkanilai aruḷumalaiyē
translation: O mountain granting the enduring state of Siva Yoga to receive the nectar food of the rising full moon!
commentary: The teacher acts as a steady mountain of grace guiding the disciple into Siva Yoga (the spiritual path of union with the divine). The deep joy of this deep meditation is described as drinking nourishing nectar from a rising full moon.

translit: uṉatuceyal eṉatuceyal uṉatuṭaimai eṉatuṭaimai uṇareṉa uṇarttuniṟaivē
translation: O fullness making me realize that my actions are your actions and my possessions are your possessions!
commentary: True spiritual realization completely erases the ego's sense of control. The guru brings the understanding that every personal action and possession actually belongs to the divine.

translit: uḷa-eṉavum ila-eṉavum urai-upaya vacaṉamaṟa orumoḻiyai utavunitiyē
translation: O treasure offering the one supreme word to end the dualistic talk asserting that things exist or do not exist!
commentary: Intellectuals often debate endlessly over whether spiritual realities exist or do not exist. The guru gives a single word of supreme truth that quiets the mind and ends all this divided, dualistic arguing.

translit: oṉṟuṭaṉ iraṇṭeṉavi taṇṭai-iṭum miṇṭaroṭum oṉṟalaṟa niṉṟanilaiyē
translation: O state standing entirely apart from the stubborn sophists who argue contentiously about one and two!
commentary: Philosophers constantly argue over whether the soul and God are one single entity or two separate things. The state of true spiritual realization stands completely apart from these petty intellectual debates.

translit: uṉṉalaṟa uṉṉunilai iṉṉateṉa eṉṉuṭaiya uḷuṇara uḷḷumatiyē
translation: O wisdom that reflects within so my heart may realize the nature of the state of contemplating without thought.
commentary: True spiritual wisdom reveals a state of deep contemplation that is completely free from active mental thought. The divine awakens this silent, direct awareness from within the heart itself.

translit: uṉnilaiyum eṉnilaiyum aṉṉiyami laicciṟitum uṟṟaṟiti eṉṟaporuḷē
translation: O Supreme Reality who declared that I should intimately know there is not the slightest difference between your state and my state.
commentary: The divine reality reveals to the seeker that there is absolutely no separation between God's state and the soul's state. This ultimate oneness is something to be known intimately through direct experience.

translit: uṇmaineṟi aṇmaitaṉil uṇṭuḷamo ruṅkileṉa ōtumeyp pōtaneṟiyē
translation: O path of true wisdom that teaches that the path of truth is near if the heart becomes unified.
commentary: The realization of ultimate truth is not distant or unreachable. When a person's heart and mind become completely unified and focused, the spiritual path is immediately present.

translit: alakiṉmaṟai moḻiyumoru poruḷiṉmuṭi peṉa-eṉa takanteḷiya aruḷceyteruḷē
translation: O clear wisdom that granted grace so my heart could clearly realize the ultimate conclusion of the One Reality proclaimed by the measureless scriptures.
commentary: Countless spiritual texts all point toward a single, ultimate reality. Reading them is not enough on its own, because only divine grace working within the heart can bring a clear experience of this final truth.

translit: aimpūtam ātinī allai-at tattuva atīta-aṟi veṉṟa-oṉṟē
translation: O Supreme One who declared: "You are not the five elements and the rest. You are the consciousness transcending those principles."
commentary: The divine teaches that the true self is not made of the five physical elements (earth, water, fire, air, space) or any other natural principles, which are known as tattvas. Instead, the soul is pure consciousness that exists entirely beyond the material world.

translit: attuvā āṟaiyum akaṉṟanilai yātaḵtu atītanilai eṉṟanaṉṟē
translation: O supreme goodness who declared that the state transcending all six paths is the transcendent state.
commentary: The six paths (adhvas) are the traditional routes of spiritual progression in Saiva Siddhanta. The ultimate truth is found only by moving past all these established religious paths into a state that transcends them completely.

translit: āṇai-ema tāṇai-emai aṉṟi-oṉ ṟillainī aṟiti-eṉa aruḷumutalē
translation: O primal source of grace who decreed: "By our command, by our command, there is nothing other than us. Know this."
commentary: The Divine asserts with absolute authority that nothing exists apart from God. Every soul and every part of creation is fundamentally inseparable from this one supreme reality.

translit: aṉpeṉpa tēcivam uṇarntiṭuka eṉa-eṉakku aṟivitta cutta-aṟivē
translation: O pure intelligence who taught me: "Love itself is Siva. Realize this."
commentary: God is not a distant figure to be appeased. The divine reality is the very essence of love itself. To experience pure love and compassion for all living beings is to directly experience God.

translit: attuvita nilaituvita nilainiṉṟa piṉṉalatu aṭaintiṭā teṉṟa-iṟaiyē
translation: O Lord who declared that the non-dual state cannot be attained unless one first stands in the dual state.
commentary: The non-dual state is the final realization that the soul and God are completely united. A seeker must first approach God through heartfelt devotion as a separate, humble worshipper before this ultimate union can take place.

translit: āṉanta matucacci tāṉanta mē-iḵtu aṟintaṭaiti eṉṟanalamē
translation: O supreme goodness who told me: "True bliss is existence, consciousness, and bliss. Know this and attain it."
commentary: True joy is a state of eternal existence, pure awareness, and complete bliss (sat-chit-ananda). Realizing this deep state is the true goal of spiritual life, offering a peace far beyond temporary worldly happiness.

translit: aṭṭacit tikaḷumniṉa tēvalceyum nī-avai avāvi-iṭal eṉṟamaṇiyē
translation: O Gem who told me, "The eight mystic powers will do your bidding, so do not desire them."
commentary: The Divine warns Vallalar against chasing occult abilities (aṭṭacitti, the eight mystic powers). Such powers will naturally arrive to serve a realized soul, so one must never desire them as a goal in themselves.

translit: ilakupari pūraṇa vilācamala tilai-aṇṭam eṅkaṇum eṉaccolpatiyē
translation: O Lord who told me, "Everywhere in the universe there is nothing but the radiant and perfect manifestation."
commentary: The entire universe is a continuous expression of divine perfection. The Lord teaches that there is no empty space anywhere, as everything is filled with this radiant manifestation.

translit: iravupakal aṟṟa-iṭamatucakala kēvalam iraṇṭiṉnaṭu eṉṟaparamē
translation: O Supreme who told me, "The place without night and day lies exactly between the two states of sakala and kevala."
commentary: True spiritual awareness exists beyond the ordinary states of human consciousness. The Divine explains that this perfect clarity (a place without night or day) is found exactly between cakala (active involvement in the world) and kēvala (unconscious slumber). It is a state of pure, unbroken light.

translit: iccaimaṉa māyaiyē kaṇṭaṉa elāmavai iruntukāṇ eṉṟatavamē
translation: O Embodiment of Penance who told me, "All things perceived are the illusion of the desiring mind. Remain still and observe them."
commentary: The objects and experiences we chase are often mirages created by our own desires. The instruction here is to remain perfectly still and simply observe the mind's illusions without becoming entangled in them.

translit: yāṉpiṟar eṉumpēta naṭaiviṭut teṉṉōṭu irutti-eṉa uraiceyaraicē
translation: O King who told me, "Abandon the divisive conduct of 'I' and 'others' and remain with me."
commentary: The feeling of being separate from other people is a barrier to grace. The Divine King commands Vallalar to drop all sense of 'I' and 'others' in order to remain forever united with God.

translit: eṉkaḷaika ṇē-eṉatu kaṇṇē-eṉ irukaṇ ilaṅkumaṇi yē-eṉuyirē
translation: My refuge, my eye, the shining pupil of my two eyes, my life!
commentary: The poet addresses God with intense intimacy. The divine is not a distant power, but the very core of his being. God is the pupil of his eye, the very thing that allows him to see, and his life itself.

translit: eṉuyirk kuyirē-eṉ aṟivē-eṉ aṟivūṭu iruntaciva mē-eṉ aṉpē
translation: The life of my life, my knowledge, the Sivam residing within my knowledge, my love!
commentary: God is the deep source that animates all living things. The word Sivam refers to the supreme divine reality, and here that reality lives directly inside human awareness. The divine is both the knowledge a person possesses and the love they feel.

translit: eṉteyva mē-eṉatu tantaiyē eṉai-īṉṟu eṭuttatā yē-eṉuṟavē
translation: My God, my father, the mother who bore and raised me, my kin!
commentary: God fulfills every vital human relationship. The divine is the ultimate parent, holding the protective care of a father and the nurturing love of a mother, alongside being the soul's truest family.

translit: eṉcelva mē-eṉatu vāḻvē-eṉ iṉpamē eṉaruṭ kuruvaṭivamē
translation: My wealth, my life, my bliss, the form of my grace-bestowing Guru!
commentary: True prosperity and happiness are found only in the divine. God appears here in the form of a Guru, a spiritual teacher who guides the soul by giving grace.

translit: kalakamaṉam uṭaiya-eṉ piḻaipoṟut tāṭkoṇṭa karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalamutamē
translation: The nectar from the ocean of grace that forgave the faults of my turbulent mind and claimed me!
commentary: The human mind is often restless and prone to mistakes. The poet acknowledges his own inner turmoil and praises God for looking past those faults. God is an endless ocean of compassion, offering a sweet nectar that heals the mind and accepts the soul completely.

translit: kāḻitaṉil aṉṟucurar muṉivarcit tarkaḷyōkar karutucama yātiparkaḷum
translation: In Sirkali on that day, celestial beings, sages, siddhas, yogis, and the leaders of esteemed religions
commentary: A grand gathering takes place at Sirkali, the birthplace of the child saint Sambandar. Celestial beings, powerful mystics known as siddhas, disciplined yogis, and religious leaders all come together in reverence.

translit: kaikuvit tarukilniṉ ṟēttamū vāṇṭil kaḷittumeyp pōtamuṇṭu
translation: stood nearby with folded hands and offered praise. At three years of age, you rejoiced and consumed true wisdom.
commentary: The gathered crowd stands with folded hands to honor a three-year-old boy. This refers to the famous story where the young Sambandar was fed the milk of true wisdom directly by the Divine Mother, giving him instant spiritual awakening.

translit: kaṉimaturam oḻukucem patikacce ḻumcoṉmaḻai kaṇṇutal pavaḷamalaiyil
translation: You formed a rain of rich words in beautiful verses dripping with fruit-like sweetness for the coral mountain of the Lord with an eye on his forehead.
commentary: Overflowing with this divine wisdom, the child immediately began to sing. His poetry falls like a rain of sweet words over Siva, who is described here as a coral mountain with a third eye on his forehead.

translit: kaṇṭupoḻi aruḷmukil campanta vaḷḷalāṅ kaṭavuḷē ōttūriṉil
translation: You are the cloud of grace who beheld him and showered those words. O divine and benevolent Sambandar! In Othur,
commentary: Sambandar is seen as a cloud of grace that freely showers divine poetry upon the world. The poem now turns its attention to a specific place called Othur to recall the young saint's actions there.

translit: kaviṉuṟa viḷaṅkunaṟ paṇikaḷciva puṇṇiyak kati-ula kaṟintuyyavē
translation: you performed beautifully shining noble services so the world could know the path of merit dedicated to Siva and attain salvation.
commentary: In Othur, Sambandar performed acts of devotion that served as a shining example for everyone else. His beautiful actions showed the whole world how to find salvation through spiritual merit dedicated to Siva.

translit: karai-aṟṟa makiḻviṉoṭu ceytaruḷ purintiṭum kāṭciyē civañāṉiyām
translation: The vision that bestows grace with boundless joy is the sage of Siva.
commentary: True spiritual wisdom is recognized by boundless joy and the outpouring of grace. A sage of Siva (Siva-jnani) is someone whose very presence offers this joyous vision of divine blessing to others.

translit: karutavarum orutirup peyarkoḷmaṇiyē-emaik kāppatuṉ kaṭaṉeṉṟumē.
translation: O gem bearing the unique holy name that arises in thought, protecting us is forever your duty.
commentary: The speaker addresses the Divine with deep intimacy, calling God a precious gem whose holy name naturally arises in the mind. By declaring that protection is God's eternal duty, the verse shows a deep trust and a loving claim placed upon the divine presence.

sections.title: Eight Sacred Verses on Sivajnanadesikar of Thiruvothur

note: Editor's note: the second half of verse 4 and verses 5 to 8 have not been found.
tamil: அணிவா யுலகத் தம்புயனும் அளிக்குந் தொழிற்பொன் அம்புயனும்
அறியா அருமைத் திருவடியை அடியேந் தரிசித் தகங்குளிர
மணிவாய் மலர்ந்தெம் போல்வார்க்கு மறையுண் முடிபை வகுத்தருள
வயங்குங் கருணை வடிவெடுத்து வந்து விளங்கு மணிச்சுடரே
பிணிவாய் பிறவிக் கொருமருந்தே பேரா னந்தப் பெருவிருந்தே
பிறங்கு கதியின் அருளாறே பெரியோர் மகிழ்விற் பெரும்பேறே
திணிவாய் எயிற்சூழ் திருவோத்தூர் திகழ அமர்ந்த சிவநெறியே
translit: aṇivā yulakat tampuyaṉum aḷikkun toḻiṟpoṉ ampuyaṉum aṟiyā arumait tiruvaṭiyai aṭiyēn taricit takaṅkuḷira maṇivāy malarntem pōlvārkku maṟaiyuṇ muṭipai vakuttaruḷa vayaṅkuṅ karuṇai vaṭiveṭuttu vantu viḷaṅku maṇiccuṭarē piṇivāy piṟavik korumaruntē pērā ṉantap peruviruntē piṟaṅku katiyiṉ aruḷāṟē periyōr makiḻviṟ perumpēṟē tiṇivāy eyiṟcūḻ tiruvōttūr tikaḻa amarnta civaneṟiyē tēvar pukaḻuñ civañāṉattēvē ñāṉa cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: The lotus-born Brahma and the golden lotus-eyed Vishnu who performs the work of preservation cannot know your rare sacred feet. You took the shining form of compassion and came as a radiant gem-like flame so that we humble devotees could see them and our hearts could rejoice. You opened your gem-like mouth to grace those like us with the ultimate truths of the Vedas. You are the peerless medicine for the disease of birth. You are the great feast of supreme bliss. You are the river of grace leading to the shining supreme state. You are the great boon in the joy of the great ones. You are the path of Siva, seated in glory in Thiruvothur surrounded by strong walls. O Lord Sivajnanadeva, praised by the celestials! O crest-jewel of wisdom!
commentary: Divine compassion takes human form in the spiritual teacher. The guru is described as a radiant light who brings the ultimate spiritual truths down to earth, curing the endless cycle of birth and death. By taking a form we can see and hear, the divine makes its grace accessible to everyone.

tamil: நின்பால் அறிவும் நின்செயலும் நீயும் பிறிதன் றெமதருளே
நெடிய விகற்ப உணர்ச்சிகொடு நின்றாய் அதனால் நேர்ந்திலைகாண்
அன்பால் உன்பால் ஒருமொழிதந் தனம்இம் மொழியால் அறிந்தொருங்கி
அளவா அறிவே உருவாக அமரென் றுணர்த்தும் அரும்பொருளே
இன்பால் என்பால் தருதாயில் இனிய கருணை இருங்கடலே
இகத்தும் பரத்தும் துணையாகி என்னுள் இருந்த வியனிறைவே
தென்பால் விளங்குந் திருவோத்தூர் திகழும் மதுரச் செழுங்கனியே
தேவர் புகழுஞ் சிவஞானத் தேவே ஞான சிகாமணியே.
translit: niṉpāl aṟivum niṉceyalum nīyum piṟitaṉ ṟemataruḷē neṭiya vikaṟpa uṇarccikoṭu niṉṟāy ataṉāl nērntilaikāṇ aṉpāl uṉpāl orumoḻitan taṉamim moḻiyāl aṟintoruṅki aḷavā aṟivē uruvāka amareṉ ṟuṇarttum arumporuḷē iṉpāl eṉpāl tarutāyil iṉiya karuṇai iruṅkaṭalē ikattum parattum tuṇaiyāki eṉṉuḷ irunta viyaṉiṟaivē teṉpāl viḷaṅkun tiruvōttūr tikaḻum maturac ceḻuṅkaṉiyē tēvar pukaḻuñ civañāṉat tēvē ñāṉa cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: "Your knowledge, your action, and you yourself are nothing other than our grace. You stood with deep dualistic perception, and therefore you did not realize this. Out of love, we have given you a single word. Know this through this word, become unified, and remain as the embodiment of measureless wisdom." Thus you instructed me, O rare treasure! You are sweeter than a mother who feeds me sweet milk. You are the vast ocean of compassion. You are my companion in this world and the next, the wondrous fullness residing within me. You are the sweet, rich fruit shining in glorious Thiruvothur in the south. O Lord Sivajnanadeva, praised by the celestials! O crest-jewel of wisdom!
commentary: The guru reveals a deep truth: the individual soul, its awareness, and its actions are all entirely made of divine grace. The illusion of separation makes people feel disconnected from the divine. Through a single word of instruction, the teacher dissolves this false division and awakens the soul to its boundless nature.

tamil: ஆகும் அதனை எமதருளால் அலவாம் என்றே உலவாமல்
இசையும் விகற்ப நிலையைஒழித் திருந்த படியே இருந்தறிகாண்
என்றென் உணர்வைத் தெளித்தநினக் கென்னே கைம்மா றறியேனே
நசையும் வெறுப்பும் தவிர்ந்தவர்பால் நண்ணும் துணையே நன்னெறியே
நான்தான் என்னல் அறத்திகழ்ந்து நாளும் ஓங்கு நடுநிலையே
திசையும் புவியும் புகழோத்தூர்ச் சீர்கொள் மதுரச் செழும்பாகே
தேவர் புகழுஞ் சிவஞானத் தேவே ஞான சிகாமணியே.
translit: acaiyum paricān tattuvamaṉ ṟavattai-akaṉṟa aṟivēnī ākum ataṉai emataruḷāl alavām eṉṟē ulavāmal icaiyum vikaṟpa nilaiyai-oḻit tirunta paṭiyē iruntaṟikāṇ eṉṟeṉ uṇarvait teḷittaniṉak keṉṉē kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉē nacaiyum veṟuppum tavirntavarpāl naṇṇum tuṇaiyē naṉṉeṟiyē nāṉtāṉ eṉṉal aṟattikaḻntu nāḷum ōṅku naṭunilaiyē ticaiyum puviyum pukaḻōttūrc cīrkoḷ maturac ceḻumpākē tēvar pukaḻuñ civañāṉat tēvē ñāṉa cikāmaṇiyē.
translation: "You are not the moving elements. You are the wisdom that has transcended the states of consciousness. Realize this truth through our grace. Instead of perpetually doubting it, cast off the dualistic state that clings to you, remain exactly as you are, and know the truth." You clarified my awareness in this way. What return can I offer you? I do not know. You are the companion who draws near to those free from desire and aversion. You are the good path. You are the balanced state that flourishes daily, shining entirely devoid of the concepts of "I" and "mine." You are the sweet, rich syrup of prosperous Thiruvothur, praised by the whole earth and all directions. O Lord Sivajnanadeva, praised by the celestials! O crest-jewel of wisdom!
commentary: People often mistake themselves for their physical bodies or their shifting mental states. The spiritual teacher corrects this by showing that the soul is pure wisdom, existing far beyond the physical elements. The instruction is simple but deep: drop the habit of dividing the world into "I" and "mine" and just rest quietly in your true nature.

tamil: கண்மூன் றுடையான் எவன்அவனே கடவுள் அவன்தன் கருணைஒன்றே
கருணை அதனைக் கருதுகின்ற கருத்தே கருத்தாம் அக்கருத்தை
மண்மூன் றறக்கொண் டிருந்தவரே வானோர் வணங்கும் அருந்தவராம்
translit: kaṇmūṉ ṟuṭaiyāṉ evaṉavaṉē kaṭavuḷ avaṉtaṉ karuṇai-oṉṟē karuṇai ataṉaik karutukiṉṟa karuttē karuttām akkaruttai maṇmūṉ ṟaṟakkoṇ ṭiruntavarē vāṉōr vaṇaṅkum aruntavarām ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...
translation: Whoever possesses three eyes, he alone is God. His compassion alone is true compassion. The intention that contemplates it is true intention. Those who hold firmly to that intention, casting off the three earthly desires, are the rare ascetics worshipped by the celestials...
commentary: True spiritual focus means meditating constantly on God's compassion. When a person aligns their own mind with this divine mercy and lets go of worldly cravings, they reach a state of purity that even heavenly beings revere.

note: Editor's note: words in round brackets are conjectures by the editor A. Balakrishna Pillai (Ā. Pā.) where letters in the manuscript could not be read.
tamil: திருத்தகுசீர்த் தமிழ்மறைக்கே முதலாய வாக்கதனால் திருப்பேர் கொண்டு
கருத்தர்நம தேகம்பக் கடவுளையுட் புறங்கண்டு களிக்கின் றோய்நின்
கருத்தறியேன் எனினு(முனைக்) கொடு(முயல்வேன் றனை)யன்பால் காக்க அன்றே.
translit: tiruttakucīrt tamiḻmaṟaikkē mutalāya vākkataṉāl tiruppēr koṇṭu karuttarnama tēkampak kaṭavuḷaiyuṭ puṟaṅkaṇṭu kaḷikkiṉ ṟōyniṉ uruttakucē vaṭikkaṭiyēṉ orukōṭiteṇṭaṉiṭṭē uraikkiṉṟēṉuṉ karuttaṟiyēṉ eṉiṉu(muṉaik) koṭu(muyalvēṉ ṟaṉai)yaṉpāl kākka aṉṟē.
translation: You bear a sacred name drawn from the very first word of the glorious and beautiful Tamil scripture. You rejoice in seeing our Lord, the God of Ekambaram, both within and without. I, your servant, offer ten million prostrations at your beautiful red feet and speak these words. Although I do not know your mind, you must lovingly protect this one who strives by holding fast to you.
commentary: This verse is a highly formal greeting to a revered spiritual guide whose name comes from the opening word of a sacred Tamil text. The recipient is praised as someone who constantly sees God both within their own mind and in the external world. The reference to Ekambaram points to the ancient temple of Siva in Kanchipuram. By asking this spiritually advanced person for loving protection, the speaker shows deep humility and reverence for those who live in direct contact with the divine.

note: Editor's note: a notebook copy records the origin of this pathigam: “Composed by C. Ramalinga Pillai on Friday, the 26th of Chithirai in the year Raktakshi, under the star Karthigai, for the healing of his brother Sabapathi Pillai's illness.” (6 May 1864, Ā. Pā.)
translit: poṉmakaḷvāḻ ciṅkapuri pōtaṉaṟu māmukaṉmēl naṉmaimiku centamiḻppā nāmuraikkac - ciṉmayattiṉ meyvaṭivām naṅkurutāḷ vēḻamukaṉ taṉṉirutāḷ poyyakalap pōṟṟuvamip pōtu.
translation: We wish to compose this highly beneficial pure Tamil song upon the great six-faced Lord, the wise one of Singapuri where the golden goddess of wealth resides. To dispel all falsehood, we now praise the feet of our Guru who is the true form of pure consciousness, and the two feet of the elephant-faced Lord.
commentary: The poet calls upon his spiritual teacher (guru) and the elephant-faced god Ganesha to ensure his song is free from falsehood. Traditional Tamil poetry often begins with such a protective invocation to clear obstacles and ground the work in pure truth.

tamil: சீராரு மறையொழுக்கந் தவிராது நான்மரபு சிறக்க வாழும்
ஏராரு நிதிபதிஇந் திரன்புரமும் மிகநாணும் எழிலின் மிக்க
வாராருங் கொங்கையர்கள் மணவாளர் உடன்கூடி வாழ்த்த நாளும்
தேராரு நெடுவீதிச் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: cīrāru maṟaiyoḻukkan tavirātu nāṉmarapu ciṟakka vāḻum ērāru nitipati-in tiraṉpuramum mikanāṇum eḻiliṉ mikka vārāruṅ koṅkaiyarkaḷ maṇavāḷar uṭaṉkūṭi vāḻtta nāḷum tērāru neṭuvītic ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: O divine mountain seated in Singapuri with its long chariot-filled streets! The people here live ceaselessly following excellent Vedic conduct, making the four lineages flourish. Its abundant beauty puts the cities of Kubera and Indra to great shame. Every day, women wearing snug bodices unite with their husbands and sing your praises.
commentary: The town of Singapuri is described as an ideal earthly city that outshines the wealthy heavens of Kubera (the god of wealth) and Indra (the king of the gods). The poet praises the town as a place of spiritual and material harmony, where the people live disciplined lives and celebrate the divine presence of Murugan.

tamil: உம்பர்துயர் கயிலைஅரற் கோதிடவே அப்பொழுதே உவந்து நாதன்
தம்பொருவில் முகமாறு கொண்டுநுதல் ஈன்றபொறி சரவ ணத்தில்
நம்புமவர் உயவிடுத்து வந்தருளும் நம்குகனே நலிவு தீர்ப்பாய்
திங்கள்தவழ் மதில்சூழும் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: umpartuyar kayilai-araṟ kōtiṭavē appoḻutē uvantu nātaṉ tamporuvil mukamāṟu koṇṭunutal īṉṟapoṟi carava ṇattil nampumavar uyaviṭuttu vantaruḷum namkukaṉē nalivu tīrppāy tiṅkaḷtavaḻ matilcūḻum ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: O divine mountain seated in Singapuri surrounded by walls that touch the moon! When the celestials recounted their sorrow to Siva in Kailash, the Lord immediately rejoiced and assumed six peerless faces. He emitted sparks from his forehead into the Saravana lake. O our Guha, you graciously came forth to save those who trust in you. Please cure my affliction.
commentary: The birth of Murugan is a direct response to a plea for help. When the heavenly beings were suffering, Siva produced sparks of fire that became Murugan (Guha, the hidden one) in a sacred lake. The poet uses this ancient story of divine rescue as the foundation for his own personal plea: he asks the god who was born to save the heavens to heal his human affliction.

tamil: பொல்லாத சூர்க்கிளையைத் தடிந்தமரர் படுந்துயரப் புன்மை நீக்கும்
வல்லானே எனதுபிணி நீநினைந்தால் ஒருகணத்தில் மாறி டாதோ
கல்லாதேன் எனினும்எனை இகழாதே நினதடியார் கழகங் கூட்டாய்
செல்லாதார் வலிஅடக்கும் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: pollāta cūrkkiḷaiyait taṭintamarar paṭuntuyarap puṉmai nīkkum vallāṉē eṉatupiṇi nīniṉaintāl orukaṇattil māṟi ṭātō kallātēṉ eṉiṉumeṉai ikaḻātē niṉataṭiyār kaḻakaṅ kūṭṭāy cellātār vali-aṭakkum ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: O mighty one who destroyed the wicked Surapadman and his clan, removing the base sorrow suffered by the celestials! If you will it, will my disease not vanish in a single moment? Though I am unlearned, do not despise me. Gather me into the assembly of your devotees. O divine mountain seated in Singapuri, a city that subdues the strength of those who stray from the path!
commentary: A god powerful enough to destroy cosmic demons can surely cure a human illness in an instant. The speaker feels unworthy due to his lack of learning, yet he still asks for the highest spiritual prize: to be accepted into the company of genuine devotees. The plea shows that sincere devotion matters far more than formal education in approaching the divine.

tamil: பண்டுறுசங் கப்புலவர் அருஞ்சிறையைத் தவிர்த்தருளும் பகவ னேஎன்
புண்தருஇந் நோய்தணிக்கப் புரையிலியோய் யான்செய்யும் புன்மை தானோ
தண்டைஎழில் கிண்கிணிசேர் சரணமலர்க் கனுதினமும் தமியேன் அன்பாய்த்
தெண்டனிடச் செய்தருள்வாய் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: paṇṭuṟucaṅ kappulavar aruñciṟaiyait tavirttaruḷum pakava ṉē-eṉ puṇtaru-in nōytaṇikkap puraiyiliyōy yāṉceyyum puṉmai tāṉō taṇṭai-eḻil kiṇkiṇicēr caraṇamalark kaṉutiṉamum tamiyēṉ aṉpāyt teṇṭaṉiṭac ceytaruḷvāy ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: O Lord who long ago graciously relieved the harsh imprisonment of the Sangam poets! O flawless one, is it my own baseness that prevents you from curing this disease that wounds me? Grant that this lonely soul may lovingly bow down every day to your lotus feet adorned with beautiful anklets and tinkling bells. O divine mountain seated in Singapuri!
commentary: The poet recalls a legend where Murugan rescued ancient Tamil scholars (Sangam poets) from a literal prison, asking if his own flaws are keeping him locked in the prison of disease. His ultimate request is remarkably simple. He does not ask for complex visions, choosing instead to pray for the daily grace to bow humbly at the deity's feet.

tamil: தாவாத வசியர்குலப் பெண்ணினுக்கோர் கரமளித்த சதுரன் அன்றே
மூவாத மறைபுகலும் மொழிகேட்டுன் முண்டகத்தாள் முறையில் தாழ்ந்து
தேவாதி தேவன்எனப் பலராலும் துதிபுரிந்து சிறப்பின் மிக்க
தீவாய்இப் பிணிதொலைப்பாய் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: tāvāta vaciyarkulap peṇṇiṉukkōr karamaḷitta caturaṉ aṉṟē mūvāta maṟaipukalum moḻikēṭṭuṉ muṇṭakattāḷ muṟaiyil tāḻntu tēvāti tēvaṉeṉap palarālum tutipurintu ciṟappiṉ mikka tīvāyip piṇitolaippāy ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: Are you not the capable one who gave your hand in marriage to the woman of the faultless merchant clan? Hearing the words spoken by the ageless Vedas, I bowed properly at your lotus feet. Many praise you as the God of gods, a lord of great excellence. Destroy this fiery disease, O divine mountain seated in Singapuri!
commentary: The speaker begs the divine to cure a burning illness. They recall the Lord's supreme status in the Vedas (ancient scriptures) and his willingness to step down into the world to marry a human devotee. This history of divine approachability gives the speaker hope for physical healing.

tamil: வானவர்கோன் மேனாளில் தரமறியா திகழ்ந்துவிட விரைவில் சென்று
மானமதில் வீற்றிருந்தே அவன்புரிந்த கொடுமைதனை மாற்றும் எங்கள்
தானவர்தம் குலம்அடர்த்த சண்முகனே இப்பிணியைத் தணிப்பாய் வாசத்
தேனவிழும் பொழில்சூழும் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: vāṉavarkōṉ mēṉāḷil taramaṟiyā tikaḻntuviṭa viraivil ceṉṟu māṉamatil vīṟṟiruntē avaṉpurinta koṭumaitaṉai māṟṟum eṅkaḷ tāṉavartam kulamaṭartta caṇmukaṉē ippiṇiyait taṇippāy vācat tēṉaviḻum poḻilcūḻum ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: In days past, the king of the celestials failed to realize your worth and scorned you. You went swiftly, sat majestically, and reversed the cruelty he had inflicted. O our Shanmuga who destroyed the clan of the Asuras, quell this disease! O divine mountain seated in Singapuri, surrounded by groves dripping with fragrant honey!
commentary: The speaker calls upon Shanmuga (the six-faced Lord) to conquer their physical suffering. He is known for subduing the pride of celestial kings and destroying the Asuras (demons). The speaker asks this same fierce and protective force to destroy their disease.

tamil: மட்டாரும் பொழில்சேரும் பரங்கிரிசெந் தூர்பழனி மருவு சாமி
நட்டாரும் பணிபுரியும் ஆறுதலை மலைமுதலாய் நணுகி எங்கள்
ஒட்டாதார் வலிஅடக்கி அன்பர்துதி ஏற்றருளும் ஒருவ காவாய்
தெட்டாதார்க் கருள்புரியும் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: maṭṭārum poḻilcērum paraṅkiricen tūrpaḻaṉi maruvu cāmi naṭṭārum paṇipuriyum āṟutalai malaimutalāy naṇuki eṅkaḷ oṭṭātār vali-aṭakki aṉpartuti ēṟṟaruḷum oruva kāvāy teṭṭātārk karuḷpuriyum ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: O Lord who dwells in Parangiri, Tiruchendur, and Palani, shrines surrounded by fragrant groves. You reside in Swami Malai and other temples where devotees serve you. You subdue the strength of foes and graciously accept the praises of your devotees. O supreme one, protect me! You bestow grace on those free from deceit, O divine mountain seated in Singapuri!
commentary: The Lord is present across the great sacred shrines of the Tamil land, including Palani and Tiruchendur. Divine presence is vast, but true grace flows specifically to those who keep their hearts completely free from deceit.

tamil: முன்செய்த மாதவத்தால் அருணகிரி நாதர்முன்னே முறையிட் டேத்தும்
புன்செயல்தீர் திருப்புகழை ஏற்றருளும் மெய்ஞ்ஞான புனிதன் என்றே
என்செயலில் இரவுபகல் ஒழியாமல் போற்றியிட இரங்கா தென்னே
தென்திசைசேர்ந் தருள்புரியும் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: muṉceyta mātavattāl aruṇakiri nātarmuṉṉē muṟaiyiṭ ṭēttum puṉceyaltīr tiruppukaḻai ēṟṟaruḷum meyññāṉa puṉitaṉ eṉṟē eṉceyalil iravupakal oḻiyāmal pōṟṟiyiṭa iraṅkā teṉṉē teṉticaicērn taruḷpuriyum ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: Through his great past penance, Arunagirinathar stood before you and sang praises. You graciously accepted his Tiruppugazh, which cures base actions. Knowing you as the pure one of true wisdom, I praise you unceasingly day and night in all my deeds. Why do you not show pity on me? You bestow grace in the southern land, O divine mountain seated in Singapuri!
commentary: The speaker measures their own longing against the famous devotion of Arunagirinathar, a revered Tamil saint. This saint composed the Tiruppugazh (Holy Praise), songs known to cure base actions. The speaker praises the Lord day and night with equal sincerity and wonders aloud why pity is delayed.

tamil: விண்ணவர்கோன் அருந்துயர நீங்கிடவும் மாதுதவ விளைவு நல்கும்
கண்ணகன்ற பேரருளின் கருணையினால் குஞ்சரியைக் காத லோடு
மண்ணுலகோர் முதல்உயிர்கள் மகிழ்ந்திடவும் மணம்புரிந்த வள்ள லேஎன்
திண்ணியதீ வினைஒழிப்பாய் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: viṇṇavarkōṉ aruntuyara nīṅkiṭavum mātutava viḷaivu nalkum kaṇṇakaṉṟa pēraruḷiṉ karuṇaiyiṉāl kuñcariyaik kāta lōṭu maṇṇulakōr mutaluyirkaḷ makiḻntiṭavum maṇampurinta vaḷḷa lē-eṉ tiṇṇiyatī viṉai-oḻippāy ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: To relieve the intense sorrow of the king of the celestials, and to grant the fruit of the lady's penance, you lovingly married Kunjari through the compassion of your vast and boundless grace. You did this so the people of the earth and all living beings would rejoice. O generous one, eradicate my stubborn evil karma! O divine mountain seated in Singapuri!
commentary: The Lord's marriage to Kunjari (the celestial princess Deivayanai) is remembered as an act of vast compassion that brought joy to all living beings. The speaker points to this boundless generosity and asks the Lord to wipe out their deep-rooted karma.

tamil: மாசகன்ற சிவமுனிவர் அருளாலே மானிடமாய் வந்த மாதின்
ஆசில்தவப் பேறளிக்க வள்ளிமலை தனைச்சார்ந்தே அங்குக் கூடி
நேசமிகு மணம்புரிந்த நின்மலனே சிறியேனை நீயே காப்பாய்
தேசுலவு பொழில்சூழும் சிங்கபுரி தனில்அமர்ந்த தெய்வக் குன்றே.
translit: mācakaṉṟa civamuṉivar aruḷālē māṉiṭamāy vanta mātiṉ āciltavap pēṟaḷikka vaḷḷimalai taṉaiccārntē aṅkuk kūṭi nēcamiku maṇampurinta niṉmalaṉē ciṟiyēṉai nīyē kāppāy tēculavu poḻilcūḻum ciṅkapuri taṉilamarnta teyvak kuṉṟē.
translation: O pure one, you went to Vallimalai to grant the boon of flawless penance to the lady who came as a human by the grace of the blemishless Siva sage. You united with her there and married her with boundless love. O divine mountain seated in Singapuri surrounded by radiant groves, you alone must protect lowly me.
commentary: The Lord's deep compassion is shown here through the sacred story of Valli, a devotee born on earth as a hunter girl by the grace of a pure sage. God went directly to her home at Vallimalai (the hill of Valli) to reward her flawless spiritual practice and marry her in an act of boundless love. The speaker asks this same pure Lord, enshrined as a divine mountain in the radiant groves of Singapuri, to offer that exact protection to his own lowly self.

translit: aiṅkaraṉ aṭimalar iṅkuṟa niṉaitiniṉ poṅkuṟu tuyaraṟum maṅkaliṉ maṉaṉaṉē.
translation: O unfading mind, think firmly here upon the lotus feet of the five-handed Lord. Your surging sorrow will be severed.
commentary: Directing the mind steadily toward God is the cure for overwhelming sorrow. The poet tells his own mind to meditate on the feet of the five-handed Lord (Ganesha, the elephant-headed deity who removes obstacles) to find peace.

translit: tirumāl aṟiyāc cēvaṭi yāleṉ karumāl aṟukkuṅ kaṇapati caraṇam.
translation: I take refuge in Ganapati. He severs my dark delusion with his red feet that remain unknown even to Vishnu.
commentary: Divine grace has the power to cut through our darkest spiritual ignorance. The poet notes that even great gods like Vishnu could not find these sacred feet, yet they are freely offered to anyone seeking shelter from delusion.

translit: tutipeṟu kaṇapati iṇaiyaṭi malarum patitaru caravaṇa pavaṉmala raṭiyuṅ katitaru paracivaṉiyalaṇi kaḻalum matiyuṟa maṉaṉiṭai maruvutu mikavē.
translation: May the widely praised twin lotus feet of Ganapati, the lotus feet of Saravanabhava who grants the divine abode, and the beautiful anklet-adorned feet of Parasiva who grants liberation abide firmly and vastly in our clear minds.
commentary: True spiritual clarity comes when the divine takes root in human awareness. The poet calls upon Ganapati (Ganesha), Saravanabhava (the youthful god of wisdom, also known as Murugan), and Parasiva (the supreme form of Lord Siva) to firmly occupy his mind and grant liberation.

translit: aruḷuṟuṅ kayamukat taṇṇal pātamum poruḷuṟu caṇmukap puṉitaṉ tāḷkaḷum teruḷuṟu civapirāṉ cempoṟ kañcamum maruḷaṟa nāṭoṟum vaṇaṅki vāḻttuvām.
translation: To destroy our delusions, let us daily worship and praise the feet of the graceful elephant-faced Lord, the feet of the holy six-faced Lord full of supreme truth, and the pure red golden lotus feet of Lord Siva who grants clarity.
commentary: Daily devotion keeps the mind free from confusion. The poet invites us to join him in praising the graceful elephant-faced God, the six-faced God of truth, and Lord Siva, viewing their sacred feet as the source of true spiritual clarity.

translit: aṟputak kaṇapati amala pōṟṟiyē taṟpara caṇmuka cāmi pōṟṟiyē ciṟpara civamakā tēva pōṟṟiyē poṟpamar kauriniṟ pōṟṟi pōṟṟiyē.
translation: Praise to the wondrous and pure Ganapati. Praise to the supreme Lord Shanmuga. Praise to the supreme consciousness Siva Mahadeva. Praise and praise again to you, beautiful golden Gauri.
commentary: This verse crowns the opening invocation with a unified chant of praise to the entire divine family. It honors Ganapati, Shanmuga (another name for the six-faced god Murugan), Lord Siva, and finally Gauri (the golden Goddess representing divine grace), praising them all as pure expressions of supreme consciousness.

tamil: மாதங்க முகத்தோன்நங் கணபதிதன் செங்கமல மலர்த்தாள் போற்றி
தாதங்க மலர்க்கொன்றைச் சடையுடைய சிவபெருமான் சரணம் போற்றி
சீதங்கொள் மலர்க்குழலாள் சிவகாம சவுந்தரியின் திருத்தாள் போற்றி.
translit: mātaṅka mukattōṉnaṅ kaṇapatitaṉ ceṅkamala malarttāḷ pōṟṟi ētaṅkaḷ aṟuttaruḷuṅ kumarakuruparaṉpāta iṇaikaḷ pōṟṟi tātaṅka malarkkoṉṟaic caṭaiyuṭaiya civaperumāṉ caraṇam pōṟṟi cītaṅkoḷ malarkkuḻalāḷ civakāma cavuntariyiṉ tiruttāḷ pōṟṟi.
translation: Praise the red lotus feet of our Ganapati with the elephant face. Praise the two feet of Kumarakuruparan who cuts away our afflictions and grants grace. Praise and take refuge in Lord Siva whose matted hair bears pollen-filled kondrai flowers. Praise the holy feet of Sivakama Soundari whose tresses are adorned with cool flowers.
commentary: This traditional verse of praise honors the divine family of Lord Siva. It seeks the blessing of the elephant-faced god Ganapati, the graceful teacher Murugan (called Kumarakuruparan here), Lord Siva wearing golden flowers in his matted hair, and the goddess Parvati (Sivakama Soundari). Seeking their protection and refuge grounds the poetry in deep devotion.

translit: kalainiṟai kaṇapati caraṇañ caraṇam kajamuka kuṇapati caraṇañ caraṇam talaivaniṉ iṇaiyaṭi caraṇañ caraṇam caravaṇa pavakuka caraṇañ caraṇam cilaimalai yuṭaiyava caraṇañ caraṇam civaciva civaciva caraṇañ caraṇam ulaivaṟum oruparai caraṇañ caraṇam umaicivai ampikai caraṇañ caraṇam.
translation: Refuge, refuge in Ganapati who is full of the arts. Refuge, refuge in the elephant-faced Lord of noble qualities. Refuge, refuge at your two feet, O Master. Refuge, refuge in Guhan born in the Saravana lake. Refuge, refuge in the Lord who holds the mountain as a bow. Refuge, refuge in Siva, Siva, Siva, Siva. Refuge, refuge in the unfaltering and peerless Supreme Goddess. Refuge, refuge in Uma, Sivai, Ambikai.
commentary: This verse is a rhythmic chant of complete surrender. The repeated call for refuge (caranam) places the soul entirely in the care of Ganapati, Murugan (Guhan), Lord Siva, and the Goddess in her many forms (Uma, Sivai, Ambikai). Surrendering at the feet of the divine is an essential step in spiritual life, marking the moment a person yields their own ego to God.

sections.title: Ten Verses on the Blissful Dance

translit: paracivā ṉantapari pūraṇa catāṉanta pāvaṉā tītamukta paramakai valyacai taṉyaniṣ kaḷapūta pautikā tārayukta carvamaṅ kaḷacacci tāṉanta caupākya cāmpava vinācarakita cāsvata purātara nirātara apētavā cāmakō caranirūpā turuvakaru ṇākara nirantara turantara cukōtaya patitvanimala cuttanit tiyaparō kṣānupava aparōkṣa cōmacē karacorūpā arahara civāyanama eṉṟumaṟai ōlamiṭ ṭaṇuvaḷavum aṟikilāta aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: O embodiment of supreme Siva, completely full of eternal bliss, liberated beyond thought! O pure consciousness of ultimate isolation, formless support of all physical elements! O all-auspicious form of being, consciousness, and bliss, devoid of destruction! O eternal, ancient, unsupported, non-dual reality beyond the reach of words and senses! O steady source of grace, continuous leader, dawn of happiness, lordly and pure! O eternally pure form wearing the moon, experienced directly and indirectly! Though the Vedas cry out your names, they do not know You even a tiny measure. O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: Scriptures and ancient texts cannot capture the ultimate divine reality. Vallalar describes God as a continuous, blissful dance of light happening in the space of wisdom, rather than a static figure found in books. He uses traditional names for the divine here only to show that true grace is vast, formless, and completely beyond the reach of human words.

translit: jōtimaṇi yē-akaṇ ṭāṉanta caitaṉya cuttamaṇiyē ariyanal turiyamaṇi yēturiya muṅkaṭan tappāl tulaṅkumaṇi yē-uyarnta jātimaṇi yēcaiva camayamaṇi yēcacci tāṉanta māṉamaṇiyē cakajanilai kāṭṭiviṉai yōṭṭi-aruḷ nīṭṭi-uyar camaraca cupāvamaṇiyē nītimaṇi yēniru vikaṟpamaṇi yē-aṉpar niṉaivilamar kaṭavuṇmaṇiyē niṉmala cuyampira kācaṅkulavum atvaita nitya-ā ṉantamaṇiyē ātimaṇi yē-eḻil anātimaṇi yē-eṉak kaṉputavum iṉpamaṇiyē aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: O gem of Jothi! O gem of unbroken, blissful, pure consciousness! O rare and good gem of the fourth state! O gem shining beyond the fourth state! O gem of the highest kind! O gem of the Saiva path! O gem that is being, consciousness, and bliss! O gem of the supreme harmonious nature, showing the natural state, driving away karma, and extending grace! O gem of justice! O gem without modifications! O divine gem seated in the thoughts of lovers! O pure, self-luminous, non-dual gem of eternal bliss! O first gem! O beautiful beginningless gem! O gem of happiness granting me love! O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: The divine light is a flawless, radiant gem existing beyond all known states of human consciousness. Vallalar explains that this pure light naturally dissolves past karma (the accumulated burden of past actions) and brings the soul into a state of supreme harmony. This perfect harmony, he says, is directly experienced in the heart by those who approach it with love.

translit: tēṉamar pacuṅkoṉṟai mālaiyā ṭakkaviṉ ceyyumati vēṇiyāṭa ceyyumup purinūlu māṭanaṭu variyuri ciṟantāṭa vēkarattil māṉimirn tāṭa-oḷir maḻuveḻun tāṭamaka vāṉāti tēvarāṭa māmuṉivar urakarkiṉ ṉararviñcai yarumāṭa mālpirama ṉāṭa-uṇmai ñāṉa-aṟi vāḷartiṉa māṭa-ula kaṉṉaiyām naṅkaiciva kāmiyāṭa nākamuṭaṉ ūkamaṉa nāṭi-oru puṟamāṭa nantimaṟai yōrkaḷāṭa āṉaimuka ṉāṭamayi lēṟiviḷai yāṭumuyar āṟumuka ṉāṭamakiḻvāy aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: As the honey-filled fresh konrai garland dances, as the beautifully adorned matted hair bearing the moon dances, as the triple sacred thread dances, as the striped tiger skin dances excellently on Your waist, as the leaping deer dances in Your hand, as the shining battle-axe rises and dances, as Indra and the first gods dance, as the great sages, serpents, celestial musicians, and heavenly beings dance, as Vishnu and Brahma dance, as the knowers of true wisdom dance daily, as the Mother of the world, the lady Sivakami, dances, as the tiger-footed and snake-bodied sages seek You and dance on one side, as Nandi and the Vedic scholars dance, as the elephant-faced Ganesha dances, as the high six-faced Murugan rides the peacock and plays, You joyfully dance. O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: The entire universe is caught up in a single, joyous cosmic dance. Vallalar describes all the traditional gods, sages, and forces of nature moving together in time with the supreme divine light. By showing every deity joining this dance, he teaches that all paths and powers are simply parts of one ultimate, blissful reality expressing itself.

translit: poyyāṉa vāḻkkaiyiṉai meyyāka nampivīṇ pōkkinaṉ ṉāḷaimaṭavār pōkamē periteṉak koṇṭaṟi vaḻintuniṉ poṉṉaṭik kāṉapaṇiyaic ceyyāta pāviyēṉ eṉṉainī kaiviṭil ceyvataṟi yēṉēḻaiyēṉ cēyceyta piḻaiyelām tāypoṟup patupōla cintaitaṉil eṇṇiṭāyō meyyāṉa nilaipeṟak kaiyā laṇaittaruḷa vēṇṭumaṟai yākamattiṉ mēlāṉa cuttacaṉ mārkka-aṉu pavacānta mētaiyarkaḷ paravivāḻttum aiyāṉa ṉaṅkoṇṭa teyvamē kaṅkai-ara vampuliyu māṭamuṭimēl aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: Believing this false life to be true, I wasted my good days. Thinking only worldly pleasure is great, I lost my understanding. I am a sinner who has not served Your golden feet. If You abandon me, I, a poor wretch, do not know what to do. Will You not consider in Your mind to forgive all the faults committed by this child, just as a mother does? You must embrace me with Your hands to grant me the true state. O five-faced God, praised and blessed by peaceful sages who have the experience of the pure Sanmarkkam that is above the scriptures! As the Ganges, the snake, and the moon dance on Your crown, O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: The true spiritual path of Suddha Sanmarkkam stands far above all traditional scriptures and religious texts. Speaking as a lost soul asking a mother for forgiveness, Vallalar begs the divine to pull him out of the illusion of worldly pleasures. He teaches that only direct grace, not learned texts, can grant a person the true state of spiritual peace.

translit: (pōtāru nāṉmukap) puttēḷi ṉāṟperiya pūmiyiṭai vantunamaṉāṟ pōkumuyir kaḷviṉaiyai oḻimiṉeṉ ṟēkuravar pōtikkum uṇmaimoḻiyaik kātāra vēpala taraṅkēṭṭum nūṟkaḷiṟ kaṟṟumaṟi vaṟṟiraṇṭu kaṇkeṭṭa kuṇṭaiyeṉa vīṇē yalaintiṭum kaṭaiyaṉēṉ uyvatennāḷ mātāvu māyñāṉa vuruvumāy aruḷceyum vaḷḷalē uḷḷamutalē mālāti tēvarmuṉi vōrparavi yētoḻutu vāḻttimuṭi tāḻttumuṉṟaṉ ātāra māṉa-am pōrukat taikkāṭṭi yāṇṭaruḷa vēṇṭumaṇicīr aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: Coming to this great earth created by the four-faced god seated on the lotus, the gurus teach the true word, telling us to destroy the karma of souls taken by the god of death. Though I heard this fully with my ears many times and learned it from texts, I lack understanding. Like a blind beast, I wander in vain. On what day will I, the lowest one, be saved? O benevolent Lord who acts as a mother and takes the form of wisdom to bestow grace! O source within my heart! Vishnu, the other gods, and sages praise You, worship You, bless You, and bow their heads. You must show Your foundational lotus feet and rule me. O beautiful gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: Reading spiritual books and listening to teachers is useless without the direct experience of grace. Vallalar says that a person who only memorizes scriptures is like a blind beast wandering aimlessly. To escape the cycle of birth and death, he teaches that the soul must seek the source of wisdom within the heart and surrender entirely to the divine light.

translit: paṇṇāru mūvarcoṟ pāvēṟu kēḷviyiṟ paṇpaṭā ēḻaiyiṉcoṟ pāvaiyum ikaḻntiṭā tēṟṟumaṟai muṭivāṉa paramārtta ñāṉanilaiyai kaṇṇāra nelliyaṅ kaṉiyeṉak kāṭṭinaṟ karuṇaicey tāḷāviṭil kaṭaiyaṉēṉ īṭēṟum vakai-enta nāḷaruṭ kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiceyvāy taṇṇā riḷampiṟai taṅkumuṭi mēṉmēṉi tanta-oru cuntariyaiyum takkavā mattiṉiṭai paccaimayi lāmariya cattiyaiyum vaittumakiḻeṉ aṇṇā-eṉ appā-eṉ aṟivē-eṉ aṉpē-eṉ ṟaṉpar (ep poḻutum) vāḻttum aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: Devotees constantly praise you, crying out, "My Lord, my Father, my Wisdom, my Love!" You placed the beautiful river goddess, who gave her body, on your crown where the cool young crescent rests. You placed the rare energy, the green peacock, on your fitting left side and rejoiced. O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom. You do not despise my words. You accept the poetic words of this poor, uncultured one, placing them alongside the musical verses of the three great saints. If you do not show me the state of supreme wisdom, the crown of the scriptures, as clearly as a gooseberry held in the hand, and if you do not bestow your good grace to rule me, on what day will this lowest one find salvation? O God of Grace, bestow your mercy!
commentary: The speaker marvels that the divine accepts his humble words alongside the celebrated hymns of the great saints. He begs to be shown the ultimate truth of the scriptures as clearly and directly as a gooseberry resting in the palm of a hand. This is a traditional idiom for absolute, unquestionable clarity. Without this direct experience of divine grace, he feels there is no hope for his salvation.

translit: pavamāṉa eḻuvakaip parappāṉa vēlaiyiṟ pacuvāṉa pāvi-iṉṉum paṟṟāṉa kuṟṟamatai uṟṟalai turumpeṉap paṭarātu maṟaiyaṉaittum uvamāṉa muraiceyya aritāṉa civanilaiyai uṟṟataṉai yoṉṟivāḻum uḷavāṉa vaḻiyī teṉakkāṭṭi aruḷceyyil uykuvēṉ muṭivāṉanal tavamāṉa neṟipaṟṟi raṇṭaṟṟa cukavāri taṉṉilniṉai nāṭiyellām tāṉāṉa cuttacaṉ mārkka-aṉu pavacānta taṟpararka ḷakaniṟaintē avamāṉa karuṇaippira kācaniṉ ṉaruḷtaṉai aṭiyaṉuk karuḷceykuvāy aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: In this vast ocean of the sevenfold cycle of birth, I am a bound sinner. I must not drift like a tossing straw caught in worldly attachments and flaws. The scriptures find it hard to offer any comparison for the supreme state of Sivam. If you reveal the true path to reach that state and live united with it, and if you grant your grace, I will be saved. The supreme, peaceful beings who experience pure Sanmarkkam grasp the ultimate path of good penance. They seek you in the ocean of non-dual bliss and become all things, and you fill their hearts completely. O matchless light of compassion, bestow your grace upon this devotee! O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: The soul feels tossed about like a piece of straw in the vast ocean of repeated births and worldly attachments. To escape this drifting, the speaker asks for the direct path to the supreme state of Sivam (the ultimate divine reality). Those who practice pure Sanmarkkam (the true path of spiritual realization) merge into a state of blissful unity, where they find the divine filling their hearts completely as a light of pure compassion.

translit: cantatamum aḻiyāmal orupaṭit tāyilaku cāmiciva kāmiyiṭamār campuvā meṉṉumaṟai ākamat tuṇivāṉa catyamoḻi taṉṉainampi entaiyē eṉṟaṟiñar yāvarum niṉpukaḻai ēttiviṉai taṉaimāṟṟiyē iṉpamaya māyiṉitu vāḻntiṭap puviyiṉiṭai ēḻaiyēṉ oruvaṉantō cintaiyā ṉatukalak kaṅkoṇṭu vāṭaleṉ ceppuvāy vētaṉāti tēvarmuṉi varkaruṭar kāntaruvar viñcaiyar cittarkaḷum ēvalpuriya antaṇarkaḷ palakōṭi mukamaṉā ṭappiṟaṅ karuṇmuka vilācattuṭaṉ aṟputa citākāca ñāṉi-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: Brahma, the primal gods, sages, celestial eagles, heavenly musicians, divine scholars, and perfected beings perform your commands. Crores of pure ones sing praises to the expansive radiance of your gracious face. O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom. Trusting the true words and the firm conclusion of the scriptures, which declare that the Lord shining eternally without change is Shambu who holds Sivakami on his left side, all the wise ones praise your glory. They cry out, "My Father!" They erase their karma and live sweetly in joy on this earth. Alas, why does the mind of this poor one alone wither in confusion? Tell me.
commentary: While wise sages and celestial beings easily trust the scriptures and live in joy, the speaker wonders why his own mind is left to wither in confusion. The wise find peace by praising the divine and erasing their karma (the cycle of action and its lasting consequences). This verse gives voice to the deep, isolating doubt that can arise on the spiritual path when everyone else seems perfectly assured of their salvation.

translit: nīṟaṇin toḷirakka maṇipūṇṭu caṉmārkka neṟiniṟkum aṉparmaṉamām nilamītu vaḷartēva tāruvē nilaiyāṉa niṟaivē (mey yaruṭcattiyām) vīṟaṇin taḻiyāta nitiyamē oḻiyāta viṇṇē akaṇṭacutta veḷiyē viḷaṅkupara oḷiyē varaintiṭā vētamē vētamuṭivē tūṟaṇin talaikiṉṟa pāviyēṉ niṉtirut tuṇaimalart tāṭkuriyaṉāyt tuyartīrn tiḷaippāṟum iṉpa-am pōtiyil tōya-aruḷ puritikaṇṭāy āṟaṇin tiṭuvēṇi aṇṇalē aṇikulavum ammaiciva kāmiyuṭaṉē aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: O divine wish-fulfilling tree growing in the minds of devotees who wear holy ash, adorn themselves with radiant rudraksha beads, and stand firmly in the path of Sanmarkkam! O enduring perfection! O imperishable treasure adorned with the majesty of true graceful energy! O endless heaven! O infinite pure space! O shining supreme Jothi! O unwritten scripture! O crown of the scriptures! I am a sinner wandering covered in dirt. Grant your grace so that I may become worthy of your twin divine lotus feet, end my sorrows, and bathe in the restful ocean of bliss. O Lord with matted hair adorned with the river! O gem of the blissful dance, You dance with the beautifully adorned Mother Sivakami in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: The divine is described as a wish-fulfilling tree growing in the minds of those who walk the path of Sanmarkkam. Devotees traditionally wear holy ash and rudraksha (sacred seeds) as marks of their dedication. Longing to be cleansed of worldly flaws, the speaker asks to bathe in the restful ocean of bliss provided by the supreme Jothi (the divine light of grace), seeking total relief from life's sorrows.

translit: maṇikoṇṭa neṭiya-ula kāyatil taṅkumāṉ mākkaḷāy āṉmākkaḷiṉ malamoḻit taḻiyāta peruvāḻ viṉaittarum vaḷḷalāy māṟāmikat tiṇikoṇṭa muppurā tikaḷeriya nakaikoṇṭa tēvāy akaṇṭañāṉac celvamāy vēlēntu cēyāy kajāṉaṉac cemmalāy aṇaiyākavem paṇikoṇṭa kaṭavuḷāyk kaṭavuḷa relāmtoḻum paramapati yāyeṅkaḷtam paramēṭṭi yāypparama pōtamāy nātamāy paramamō kṣātikkamāy aṇikoṇṭa cutta-aṉu pūtiyāyc cōtiyāy ārntumaṅ kaḷavaṭivamāy aṟputa citākāca ñāṉa-am palamāṭum āṉanta naṭaṉamaṇiyē.
translation: You are this vast world adorned with gems. You are the souls residing within it. You are the benevolent giver who removes the impurities of those souls and grants them the imperishable great life. You are the Lord who smiled to burn down the intensely fortified, unyielding triple cities. You are the infinite wealth of wisdom. You take the forms of the spear-wielding child and the noble elephant-faced god. You are the God who wears a fierce serpent as an ornament. You are the supreme Lord worshipped by all gods. You are our highest master. You are supreme knowledge, the primal sound, and the supreme mastery of liberation. You are the beautifully adorned pure experience. You are the Jothi. You are the fully manifested auspicious form. O gem of the blissful dance, You dance in the wondrous conscious sky of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: The divine reality encompasses absolutely everything. God is the physical world, the souls living within it, and the liberating grace that removes their impurities. While acknowledging traditional deities like the spear-wielding child and the elephant-faced god, the verse points to the ultimate truth. The supreme Lord is pure experience and limitless Jothi, the radiant light that stands as the source of all these forms.

translit: araṅkāya maṉamāyai aḷakkar āḻam aṟiyāmal kāliṭṭiṅ kaḻuntu kiṉṟēṉ iraṅkāyō ciṟitumuyir irakkam illā eṉmaṉamō niṉmaṉamum iṟaivi uṉṟaṉ uraṅkāṇum araciyaṟkōl koṭuṅkōl āṉāl ōṭi-eṅkē pukuntevaruk kuraippa tammā tiraṅkāṇāp piḷḷai-eṉat tāyvi ṭāḷē civakāma valli-eṉum teyvat tāyē.
translation: Without knowing its depth, I stepped into the ocean of the mind's illusion and am sinking here. Will you not show even a little pity? Is your heart devoid of compassion like my own heart, O Goddess? If your powerful royal scepter turns into a cruel scepter, where can I run for refuge, and to whom can I complain, O Mother? A mother does not abandon her child just because it lacks ability, O divine Mother Sivakamavalli.
commentary: The mind's illusions are a treacherous ocean where the seeker is drowning. Vallalar approaches the divine as a mother, reminding her that a true mother never abandons her child simply because they lack skill or merit.

tamil: தனத்தால் இயன்ற தனிச்சபையில் நடிக்கும் பெருமான் தனக்கன்றே
இனத்தால் உயர்ந்த மணமாலை இட்டுக் களித்த துரைப்பெண்ணே
மனத்தான் விளங்கும் சிவகாம வல்லிக் கனியே மாலொடும்ஓர்
அனத்தான் புகழும் அம்மேஇவ் வடியேன் உனக்கே அடைக்கலமே.
translit: taṉattāl iyaṉṟa taṉiccapaiyil naṭikkum perumāṉ taṉakkaṉṟē iṉattāl uyarnta maṇamālai iṭṭuk kaḷitta turaippeṇṇē maṉattāṉ viḷaṅkum civakāma vallik kaṉiyē māloṭumōr aṉattāṉ pukaḻum ammē-iv vaṭiyēṉ uṉakkē aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O noble lady who joyfully placed the distinguished wedding garland on the great Lord who dances in the unique golden hall. O sweet fruit of Sivakamavalli who shines in the mind. O Mother praised by Vishnu and by Brahma upon his swan. This devotee takes refuge in you alone.
commentary: Sivakamavalli is praised as the divine partner of the dancing Lord at Chidambaram. Taking refuge in her shows that divine grace is the active, loving force connecting the seeker directly to God.

tamil: திருவே திகழுங் கலைமகளே திருவே மலையான் திருமகளே
உருவே இச்சை மயமேமெய் உணர்வின் வணமே உயர்இன்பக்
குருவே ஆதித் தனித்தாயே குலவும் பரையாம் பெருந்தாயே
மருவே மலரே சிவகாம வல்லி மணியே வந்தருளே.
translit: tiruvē tikaḻuṅ kalaimakaḷē tiruvē malaiyāṉ tirumakaḷē uruvē iccai mayamēmey uṇarviṉ vaṇamē uyariṉpak kuruvē ātit taṉittāyē kulavum paraiyām peruntāyē maruvē malarē civakāma valli maṇiyē vantaruḷē.
translation: O goddess of wealth, O shining goddess of arts, O auspicious daughter of the mountain. O divine form, O embodiment of will, O nature of true awareness, O guru of supreme bliss. O original unique mother, O great mother celebrated as the supreme power. O fragrance, O flower, O gem of Sivakamavalli, come and bestow your grace.
commentary: All traditional forms of the divine feminine are wrapped into one supreme mother. Whether people call her the goddess of wealth, the goddess of arts, or the daughter of the mountain, Vallalar says she is the single ultimate power of grace that awakens true awareness.

tamil: அருளே அறிவே அன்பேதெள் ளமுதே மாதர் அரசேமெய்ப்
பொருளே தெருளே மாற்றறியாப் பொன்னே மின்னே பூங்கிளியே
இருளேய் மனத்தில் எய்தாத இன்பப் பெருக்கே இவ்வடியேன்
மருளே தவிர்த்த சிவகாம வல்லி நினக்கே வந்தனமே.
translit: aruḷē aṟivē aṉpēteḷ ḷamutē mātar aracēmeyp poruḷē teruḷē māṟṟaṟiyāp poṉṉē miṉṉē pūṅkiḷiyē iruḷēy maṉattil eytāta iṉpap perukkē ivvaṭiyēṉ maruḷē tavirtta civakāma valli niṉakkē vantaṉamē.
translation: O grace, O knowledge, O love, O clear ambrosia, O queen of women. O true reality, O clarity, O pure gold of unmeasured worth, O lightning, O beautiful parrot. O flood of bliss that does not reach a dark mind. O Sivakamavalli who removed this devotee's confusion, I offer my reverence to you alone.
commentary: Divine grace is pure love, clear knowledge, and a flood of joy. This deep bliss cannot enter a mind clouded by ignorance, but once grace removes that inner darkness, only perfect clarity remains.

translit: taruvāy itunal taruṇaṅkaṇ ṭāyeṉṉait tāṅkikkoṇṭa kuruvāy viḷaṅku maṇimaṉṟa vāṇaṉaik kūṭi-iṉpa uruvāyeṉ uḷḷattiṉ uḷḷē amarntuḷḷa uṇmai-elām tiruvāy malarnta civakāma valliniṉ cīraruḷē.
translation: You will bestow your grace, for this is the good moment. O Sivakamavalli, you joined the Lord of the gem-hall who sustained me and shines as the Guru. Taking a form of bliss, you sit deep within my heart and graciously speak all the truths. This is your excellent grace.
